3487:function mcd(a, b)     # Si a o b son 0, se termina el ciclo     if a == 0 || b == 0         return 0     # Si a es igual a b se devuelve a     elseif a == b         return a     # Si a es mayor que b, se devuelve el resultado de la llamada recursiva     elseif a > b         return mcd(a-b, b)     # Si a es menor que b, se devuelve el resultado de la llamada recursiva     elseif a < b         return mcd(a, b-a)     end end

3497:function extended_euclidean_algorithm(a, b)     x0, x1, y0, y1 = 0, 1, 1, 0     while a != 0         q, b, a = div(b, a), a, b % a         y0, y1 = y1, y0 - q * y1         x0, x1 = x1, x0 - q * x1     end     return (b, x0, y0) end

3514:function can_connect_via_site_wire(a_site, a_site_wire, b_site, b_site_wire) # 1: Hard code the wires in each site. # 2: Keep track of the site wires in a dict: #        {site => {wire => Number of connections}} # 3: Have a list of wire connections (source, dest, wire): #        [[1, 2, 1], [2, 3, 1]] # 3: - 1: Have a hash of all the site wires in the site, and the wires that they are connected to #        {1 => [2, 3], 2 => [1], 3 => [1]} # 3: - 2: Have a hash of the connections #        {1 => [1, 2, 3], 2 => [2, 1, 3], 3 => [2, 1, 1]} # 3: - 3: Have a hash of the connections in both directions, so we don't have to go through the list each time #        {1 => [1, 2, 3], 2 => [1, 2, 3], 3 => [1, 2, 3]} # 3: - 4: For each connection, increase the count of each connection in both directions # 3: - 5: Once the count of each connection is greater than 1, it is connected via a site wire     if a_site != b_site         # Not in same site, not connected         return false     end     # Must be connected via the same site wire     return a_site_wire == b_site_wire end

3541:function _merge_and_count_split_inv(left, right)     n, m = length(left), length(right)     # Initialize merged as empty array of length (n + m)     merged = Vector{eltype(left)}(undef, n + m)     # merge the array by comparing the left and right elements     inv_count = 0     i, j, k = 1, 1, 1     while i <= n && j <= m         if left[i] <= right[j]             merged[k] = left[i]             i += 1         else             merged[k] = right[j]             j += 1             # Count inversions             inv_count += n - i + 1         end         k += 1     end     # Append remaining elements of left array     while i <= n         merged[k] = left[i]         i += 1         k += 1     end     # Append remaining elements of right array     while j <= m         merged[k] = right[j]         j += 1         k += 1     end     return merged, inv_count end

3547:function pkg_version_cmp(left::String, right::String)::Int64     # Split strings into (name, version, suffix).     left_parts = split(left, '-')     left_name = string(left_parts[1])     if length(left_parts) >= 2         left_version = left_parts[2]     else         left_version = ""     end     left_suffix = ""     if length(left_parts) == 3         left_suffix = left_parts[3]     end     right_parts = split(right, '-')     right_name = string(right_parts[1])     if length(right_parts) >= 2         right_version = right_parts[2]     else         right_version = ""     end     right_suffix = ""     if length(right_parts) == 3         right_suffix = right_parts[3]     end     # Compare version numbers.     if left_version < right_version         return -1     elseif left_version == right_version         # If the versions are equal, compare names.         if left_name < right_name             return -1         elseif left_name == right_name             # If the names are equal, compare suffixes.             if left_suffix < right_suffix                 return -1             elseif left_suffix == right_suffix                 return 0             else                 return 1             end         else             return 1         end     else         return 1     end end

3551:function isMAGPYABS(filename)     try         lines = readlines(filename)         line = lines[1]         # a file containing a valid MAGPYABS header has to have the first line         # exactly matching the "MAGPYABS" header     catch         return false     end     if !occursin(r"^Miren", line)         return false     end     # check whether the second line contains a valid version number     line = lines[2]     m = match(r"^v([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+)$", line)     if m == nothing         return false     end     version_major = parse(Int, m.captures[1])     version_minor = parse(Int, m.captures[2])     version_patch = parse(Int, m.captures[3])     if !(1 ≤ version_major ≤ 2)         return false     end     if !(0 ≤ version_minor ≤ 9)         return false     end     if !(0 ≤ version_patch ≤ 9)         return false     end     # finally check whether the third line contains a valid number of entries     line = lines[3]     m = match(r"^([0-9]+)$", line)     if m == nothing         return false     end     n = parse(Int, m.captures[1])     if !(0 ≤ n ≤ 2^31 - 1)         return false     end     return true end

3553:function isPow2(num)::Bool     if typeof(num) == Int64         return num != 0 && ((num & (num - 1)) == 0)     elseif typeof(num) == Int16         return num != 0 && ((num & (num - 1)) == 0)     elseif typeof(num) == Int32         return num != 0 && ((num & (num - 1)) == 0)     elseif typeof(num) == Int8         return num != 0 && ((num & (num - 1)) == 0)     elseif typeof(num) == Int128         return num != 0 && ((num & (num - 1)) == 0)     elseif typeof(num) == Float64         return num != 0.0 && ((num & (num - 1.0)) == 0.0)     elseif typeof(num) == Float32         return num != 0.0 && ((num & (num - 1.0)) == 0.0)     elseif typeof(num) == Float16         return num != 0.0 && ((num & (num - 1.0)) == 0.0)     else         error("type is not a valid type: $(typeof(num))")     end end

3592:function draft_anchor(m)::String     # Optimize case where the anchor is of a single character     if length(m) == 1         return string(m[1])     end     # Optimize case where the anchor is a single letter and we can find it in     # the middle of a word.     if length(m) == 2         if length(filter(i -> i == m[1], keys(alphabet))) == 1             if occursin(uppercase(m[1]), uppercase(m[2])) || occursin(uppercase(m[1]), lowercase(m[2]))                 return m[1] * m[2]             end         end     end     # Work out where the anchor is by finding the longest repetition of the     # letters in the string     anchor = ""     for (k, v) in alphabet         anchor = find_longest_repeated(m, k)         if anchor != ""             return anchor         end     end     # If no anchor found, try again with all the letters in the alphabet     anchor = ""     for (k, v) in alphabet         anchor = find_longest_repeated(m, k)         if anchor != ""             return anchor         end     end     return anchor end

3628:function sample_from_config(opt)     if !haskey(opt, "dist")         return opt     end     if isa(opt["dist"], String)         opt["dist"] = JSON.parse(opt["dist"])     end     if !haskey(opt["dist"], "type")         error("Distribution type not provided")     end     dist_type = opt["dist"]["type"]     if dist_type == "uniform"         return rand(Uniform(opt["dist"]["low"], opt["dist"]["high"]))     elseif dist_type == "normal"         return rand(Normal(opt["dist"]["mean"], opt["dist"]["std"]))     elseif dist_type == "lognormal"         return rand(LogNormal(opt["dist"]["mean"], opt["dist"]["std"]))     elseif dist_type == "triangular"         return rand(Triangular(opt["dist"]["low"], opt["dist"]["high"], opt["dist"]["mode"]))     elseif dist_type == "exponential"         return rand(Exponential(opt["dist"]["rate"]))     elseif dist_type == "gamma"         return rand(Gamma(opt["dist"]["shape"], opt["dist"]["scale"]))     elseif dist_type == "beta"         return rand(Beta(opt["dist"]["alpha"], opt["dist"]["beta"]))     elseif dist_type == "discrete"         return rand(DiscreteUniform(opt["dist"]["low"], opt["dist"]["high"]))     elseif dist_type == "poisson"         return rand(Poisson(opt["dist"]["lambda"]))     elseif dist_type == "binomial"         return rand(Binomial(opt["dist"]["n"], opt["dist"]["p"]))     else         error("Distribution type " * dist_type * " not supported")     end end

3635:function minkowski(ratings_1, ratings_2, r)     # Check if ratings_1 and ratings_2 have any common keys     common = intersect(keys(ratings_1), keys(ratings_2))     # Sum of squared differences in ratings     sumSqrs = 0     # Number of common ratings     numCommon = 0     # For all common ratings...     for commonRating in common         # Add the squared difference         sumSqrs += abs(ratings_1[commonRating] - ratings_2[commonRating])^r         numCommon += 1     end     # If there were any common ratings...     if numCommon > 0         # Take the rth root of the sum of squared differences         return sumSqrs^(1/r)     else         # If there were no common ratings, return 0         return 0     end end

3651:function IoU(X, Y)     Xtl = X[1]     Xtr = X[2]     Xbl = X[3]     Xbr = X[4]     Ytl = Y[1]     Ytr = Y[2]     Ybl = Y[3]     Ybr = Y[4]     # Calculate the area of intersection between the two bounding boxes.     # If the boxes do not intersect, they have zero intersection area.     intersection_area = max(0, min(Xbr, Ybr) - max(Xtl, Ytl) + 1) * max(0, min(Xbl, Ybl) - max(Xtr, Ytr) + 1)     # Calculate the area of the union of the two bounding boxes.     # If the boxes do not intersect, their union has zero area.     X_area = (Xbr - Xtl + 1) * (Xbl - Xtr + 1)     Y_area = (Ybr - Ytl + 1) * (Ybl - Ytr + 1)     union_area = X_area + Y_area - intersection_area     return intersection_area / (union_area + eps(Float64)) end

3653:function isprime(n)     if n < 2         return false     end     if n == 2 || n == 3         return true     end     if n % 2 == 0 || n % 3 == 0         return false     end     i = 5     w = 2     while i * i <= n         if n % i == 0             return false         end         i += w         w = 6 - w     end     return true end

3664:function inv_symmetric_3x3(m11, m22, m33, m12, m23, m13)     det = m11 * (m33 * m22 - m23^2) - m12 * (m33 * m12 - m23 * m13) + m13 * (m23 * m12 - m22 * m13)     a11 = m33 * m22 - m23^2     a12 = m13 * m23 - m33 * m12     a13 = m12 * m23 - m13 * m22     a22 = m33 * m11 - m13^2     a23 = m12 * m13 - m11 * m23     a33 = m11 * m22 - m12^2     a11 = a11 / det     a12 = a12 / det     a13 = a13 / det     a22 = a22 / det     a23 = a23 / det     a33 = a33 / det     return a11, a22, a33, a12, a23, a13 end

3707:function count_alive_neighbors(grid, x, y)     #print(x, y)     height = size(grid, 1)     width = size(grid, 2)     alive_count = 0     for i = 1:2         for j = 1:2             neighbor_x = x + i             neighbor_y = y + j             if i == 1 && j == 1                 continue             elseif neighbor_x < 0 || neighbor_y < 0 || neighbor_y > height || neighbor_x > width                 # Edges are considered alive. 3710:function importify_params(param_arg)     if param_arg in (true, false)         return lowercase(string(param_arg))     elseif isa(param_arg, AbstractString)         # For pre-existing data, assume it's a table name         if !startswith(param_arg, "https://")             return param_arg         else             return URI(param_arg)         end     elseif isa(param_arg, Dict)         # Take a dict and convert it to a list of parameters         return [importify_params(k) => importify_params(v) for (k, v) in param_arg]     elseif isa(param_arg, Array)         # Take an array and convert each element         return [importify_params(x) for x in param_arg]     elseif isa(param_arg, URI)         # Nothing to do for URLs (no extra processing)         return param_arg     elseif isa(param_arg, Tuple)         # (col, typ) to (col, (typ, args))         return (param_arg..., ())     elseif isa(param_arg, Number)         # Numbers to Strings         return string(param_arg)     elseif isa(param_arg, Null)         # Nothing to do for nulls         return param_arg     else         error("Can't convert `$(typeof(param_arg))` to Import API parameter")     end end

3717:function _key_nchunks(key, mbits, ndims)     nchunks = zeros(Int, mbits)     mask = (1 << ndims) - 1 # number with all bits set to 1, with ndims bits, e.g. ndims = 3 == 0b111     for i in 1:mbits         nchunks[mbits - i + 1] = (key & mask)         key >>= ndims     end     return nchunks end
3718:function metrics(tp, pred_len, gt_len, labels_num)     tp = round(tp)     pred_len = round(pred_len)     gt_len = round(gt_len)     labels_num = round(labels_num)     fn = gt_len - tp     fp = pred_len - tp     tn = labels_num - tp - fn - fp     if tp == 0         recall, precision, f1 = 0, 0, 0     else         recall = tp / gt_len         precision = tp / pred_len         f1 = 2 * recall * precision / (recall + precision)     end     accuracy = tp / (gt_len + pred_len - tp)     accuracy_balanced = ((tp / (tp + fn)) + (tn / (tn + fp))) / 2     return recall, precision, f1, accuracy, accuracy_balanced end

3779:function ith_bit(x::Int64, i::Int64)::Int64     # Raise an error if the input is negative.     if x < 0         error("Negative input not supported.")     end     # Perform a bitwise AND on the input and the mask.     # The mask has 1's in all the ith-bit positions.     # The mask is shifted to the left to make room for the 1's.     # The mask is shifted to the right to cancel the extra 1's that     # were shifted over when the mask was shifted left.     return ((x & (1 << i)) >> i) end

3890:function lerp(a, b, p)     # We want to be able to interpolate all types of numbers (e.g. Ints, Floats, BigFloats, complex).     # We can't use the built-in Python functions here since they only work on     # numbers that can be converted to a float (e.g. Int/Float/BigInt/BigFloat).     # Instead, we have to do it the long way.     a = convert(Float64, a)     b = convert(Float64, b)     p = convert(Float64, p)     # Return the interpolated value.     a * (1.0 - p) + b * p end

3928:function f3cubic(x, gamma, mu, p12, p23, g13, g23)     if p12 == 0 || p23 == 0         return 1.0     end     d = -p12 * gamma / mu     c = 1.0 + (g23 + g13 / p12) / p23     b = (g23 + g13 / p12 + g13 * g23 / (p12 * p23)) / p23     a = g13 * g23 / (p12 * p23 * p23)     return a * x * x * x + b * x * x + c * x + d end

3944:function euler_problem_1(n)     num_multiples_of_3 = div(n - 1, 3)     num_multiples_of_5 = div(n - 1, 5)     num_shared_multiples = div(n - 1, 15)     sum_one_up_to_k(k) = (k^2 + k) / 2     sum_multiples_of_3 = sum_one_up_to_k(num_multiples_of_3) * 3     sum_multiples_of_5 = sum_one_up_to_k(num_multiples_of_5) * 5     sum_shared_multiples = sum_one_up_to_k(num_shared_multiples) * (3 * 5)     retval = sum_multiples_of_3 + sum_multiples_of_5 - sum_shared_multiples     return retval end

3958:function rolling_hashes(string::String)::String     p = 23     P = 666013     str_rev = string[end:-1:1]     f_foward = 0     f_backward = 0     p_power = 1     max_suffix_palindrome = 0     for index = 1:length(str_rev)         char_idx = Int(str_rev[index]) - Int('a')         f_foward = (f_foward + char_idx * p_power) % P         f_backward = (f_backward * p + char_idx) % P         p_power *= p         if f_foward == f_backward             max_suffix_palindrome = index         end     end     return string * str_rev[max_suffix_palindrome+1:end] end

3986:function lRGB_ACEScg(lRGB)     # The numerical constants are taken from the ACEScg specification     R, G, B = lRGB     # Red     R_to_R =  0.6050374899     G_to_R =  0.3297772590     B_to_R =  0.0652703903     R = R * R_to_R + G * G_to_R + B * B_to_R     # Green     R_to_G =  0.0693938279     G_to_G =  0.9192626515     B_to_G =  0.0113133072     G = R * R_to_G + G * G_to_G + B * B_to_G     # Blue     R_to_B =  0.0207546370     G_to_B =  0.1074133069     B_to_B =  0.8717796985     B = R * R_to_B + G * G_to_B + B * B_to_B     return [R, G, B] end

4062:function iou_bbox(box1, box2)     x1, y1, x2, y2 = box1     x3, y3, x4, y4 = box2     tl = (max(x1, x3), max(y1, y3))     br = (min(x2, x4), min(y2, y4))     # compute the area of intersection rectangle     w, h = br .- tl .+ 1     inter = max(0, w) * max(0, h)     # compute the area of both the prediction and ground-truth     # rectangles     box1Area = (x2 - x1 + 1) * (y2 - y1 + 1)     box2Area = (x4 - x3 + 1) * (y4 - y3 + 1)     # compute the intersection over union     iou = inter / (box1Area + box2Area .- inter)     # return the intersection over union value     return iou end

4074:function compute_iou(box_1, box_2)     # box_1: (top left x, top left y, bottom right x, bottom right y), where the four     #        coordinates are integers     # box_2: (top left x, top left y, bottom right x, bottom right y), where the four     #        coordinates are integers     # if the boxes don't intersect     if box_1[4] < box_2[1] || box_1[1] > box_2[4] || box_1[3] < box_2[2] || box_1[2] > box_2[3]         return 0.0     end     # intersection rectangle     x_left = max(box_1[1], box_2[1])     y_top = max(box_1[2], box_2[2])     x_right = min(box_1[3], box_2[3])     y_bottom = min(box_1[4], box_2[4])     # compute the area of intersection rectangle     intersection_area = (x_right - x_left) * (y_bottom - y_top)     # compute the area of both the prediction and ground-truth     # rectangles     box_1_area = (box_1[3] - box_1[1]) * (box_1[4] - box_1[2])     box_2_area = (box_2[3] - box_2[1]) * (box_2[4] - box_2[2])     # compute the intersection over union by taking the intersection     # area and dividing it by the sum of prediction + ground-truth     # areas - the interesection area     iou = intersection_area / (box_1_area + box_2_area - intersection_area)     return iou end

4143:function reverse(x::Int64)::Int64   # Shorthand   isneg = x < 0   # Get the magnitude of the number (without sign)   sign = (isneg) ? -1 : 1   mag = (x >= 0) ? x : -x   # Set up the reverse number   rev = 0   while mag > 0     rem = mag % 10     mag = div(mag, 10)     rev = 10 * rev + rem   end   # Return the proper result   return isneg ? -rev : rev end

4204:function swap32(x)     # This swaps the order of the bytes in a 32 bit integer.     # This is useful when you have the integer in a different order     # for some reason.     # For example, in MATLAB, integers are represented as a big     # endian 4 byte integer, but in Python the order is little     # endian, so you must swap.     # @param x integer     # @return swapped integer     # @author <NAME>     # @license MIT     ((((x & 0xFF000000) >> 24) & 0x000000FF) |      (((x & 0x00FF0000) >> 8) & 0x0000FF00) |      (((x & 0x0000FF00) << 8) & 0x00FF0000) |      (((x & 0x000000FF) << 24) & 0xFF000000)) end

4208:function is_curious(num, den)     l = []     for c in string(num)         push!(l, parse(Int, c))     end     num = l     l = []     for c in string(den)         push!(l, parse(Int, c))     end     den = l     # the intersection of the digits of the numerator and denominator     common_digits = intersect(num, den)     if length(common_digits) == 0 || length(common_digits) == 2         return false     end     # if the intersection of the digits is zero, the fraction is not curious     if common_digits[1] == 0         return false     end     # remove the common digits from the numerator and denominator     deleteat!(num, findall(in(common_digits), num))     deleteat!(den, findall(in(common_digits), den))     # if the denominator is zero, the fraction is not curious     if den[1] == 0         return false     end     return num[1]/den[1] == num[1]/common_digits[1] end

4220:function bb_iou_dice(boxa, boxb)     a_x1, a_y1, a_x2, a_y2 = boxa     b_x1, b_y1, b_x2, b_y2 = boxb     x_min = max(a_x1, b_x1)     y_min = max(a_y1, b_y1)     x_max = min(a_x2, b_x2)     y_max = min(a_y2, b_y2)     inter_area = (x_max - x_min) * (y_max - y_min)     a_area = (a_x2-a_x1)*(a_y2-a_y1)     b_area = (b_x2-b_x1)*(b_y2-b_y1)     iou = inter_area / float(a_area + b_area - inter_area)     dice = (2 * inter_area) / float(a_area + b_area)     return iou, dice end

4262:function gc_content(dna)     # Initialize the counts to zero     at_count = 0     gc_count = 0     n_count = 0     # Count the number of A's, T's, C's, G's, W's, and S's     for nt in dna         if nt == 'a' || nt == 'A'             at_count += 1         elseif nt == 't' || nt == 'T'             at_count += 1         elseif nt == 'c' || nt == 'C'             gc_count += 1         elseif nt == 'g' || nt == 'G'             gc_count += 1         elseif nt == 'w' || nt == 'W'             gc_count += 1         elseif nt == 's' || nt == 'S'             gc_count += 1         else             n_count += 1         end     end     # Use the general equation to calculate the %GC content     if at_count + gc_count == 0         return 0.0     else         return float(gc_count) / (gc_count + at_count)     end end

4264:function fib(n::Int64)::Int64     if n <= 2         return 1     end     # Time complexity: O(n)     # Space complexity: O(n)     # 2^n => 2^n => n     # n * 2^n => n + n^2 => n^2 => n^2     memo = zeros(Int64, n)     memo[1] = 1     memo[2] = 1     for i in 3:n         memo[i] = memo[i - 1] + memo[i - 2]     end     return memo[n] end

4271:function _trapz_simps_overlap2(dy, dx)     n = length(dy)     if n == 1         return 0     end     if n == 2         return (dx/6)^2 * 12 * dy[1]^2     end     n == 3 && return (dx/6)^2 * 12 * (dy[2]^2 + 4*dy[3]^2)     if isodd(n)         simp = 10*dy[1] + 4*dy[2] + 2*dy[3]         for i = 4:2:n-1             simp += 4*dy[i] + 2*dy[i+1]         end         simp *= dx/3         trap = 2 * (dy[1] + dy[end])         for i = 2:n-1             trap += 2*dy[i]         end         return (dx/6)^2 * (trap^2 + simp^2)     else         simp = 10*dy[1] + 4*dy[2] + 2*dy[3]         for i = 4:2:n             simp += 4*dy[i] + 2*dy[i+1]         end         simp *= dx/3         trap = 2 * (dy[1] + dy[n])         for i = 2:n-1             trap += 2*dy[i]         end         return (dx/6)^2 * (trap^2 + simp^2)     end end

4291:function poly_area_calculation(points)     if length(points) < 3         error("NOT SUFFICIENT POINTS!")     end     sum = [0.0, 0.0]     area = 0     for i in 1:length(points)         j = i + 1         if i == length(points)             j = 1         end         m = points[i][1]*points[j][2] - points[j][1]*points[i][2]         sum[1] += (points[i][1] + points[j][1]) * m         sum[2] += (points[i][2] + points[j][2]) * m         area += m     end     area /= 2     if area != 0         sum[1] /= (6*area)         sum[2] /= (6*area)     end     return [abs(area), (sum[1], sum[2])] end

4429:function convert_dict(my_dict)     # Create new dictionary     new_dict = Dict()     # Loop over old dictionary     for (k, v) in my_dict         # Check if the key is 'host', if so then pop the value and use it as the new key         if k == "host"             new_key = pop!(my_dict, k)             # Create a new key/value pair for 'hostname'             new_dict["hostname"] = new_key         # Check if the key is 'device_type', if so then pop the value and use it as the new key         elseif k == "device_type"             new_key = pop!(my_dict, k)             # Split the device type at the underscore             new_value = split(new_key, "_")[2]             # Create a new key/value pair for 'device_type'             new_dict["device_type"] = new_value         # For all other keys, simply copy the value to the new dictionary         else             new_dict[k] = v         end     end     return new_dict end

4555:function decode(value)     value == '\0' && return nothing     decoded = ""     for char in value         output = char         if char == '\x01'             try                 next_char = iterate(value, nextind(value, 1))                 ordinal = Ordinal(next_char)                 if ordinal >= 0x40 && ordinal <= 0x4f                     output = chr(ordinal ^ 0x40)                 else                     output *= 2                 end             catch                 # ignore             end         end         decoded *= output     end     return decoded end

4565:function _fib_rec(n)     if n == 0         return (1, 0)     end     (f1, f2), i = (1, 0), 31     while i >= 0         if (n >> i) > 0             f1, f2 = f1^2 + f2^2, f2 * (2*f1 - f2)             if (n >> i) % 2 == 1                 f1, f2 = f1 + f2, f1             end         end         i -= 1     end     return f1, f2 end

4582:function is_palindrome_permutation_v2(phrase) 	if(length(phrase) == 1) 		return true 	end 	# Count the number of characters 	char_counts = Dict() 	for char in phrase 		if char in keys(char_counts) 			char_counts[char] += 1 		else 			char_counts[char] = 1 		end 	end 	# If there are an even number of characters, return false 	# otherwise, return true 	odd_count = 0 	for val in values(char_counts) 		if val % 2 == 1 			odd_count += 1 			if odd_count == 2 				return false 			end 		end 	end 	return true end

4603:function string_to_binary(string, to_type) 	if to_type == "b" # Boolean 		return string_to_binary(string, "i") == 0 ? false : true 	elseif to_type == "B" # Byte 		return string_to_binary(string, "h") % 256 	elseif to_type == "h" # Short 		return Int16(string) 	elseif to_type == "i" # Integer 		return Int32(string) 	elseif to_type == "L" # Long 		return Int64(string) 	elseif to_type == "f" # Float 		return Float32(string) 	elseif to_type == "d" # Double 		return Float64(string) 	elseif to_type == "255p" # String 		return string 	else 		println(string("Unsupported type \"", to_type, "\" for value \"", string, "\".")) 		exit(1) 	end 	return nothing end

4742:function gcd(_a, _b)     # Edge Cases:     # 0. gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a) = a if a == b or a == 0 or b == 0     # 1. gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a) = 0 if a == 0 or b == 0     if _a == 0 || _b == 0         return _a + _b     end     if _a > _b         _a, _b = _b, _a     end     while _b > 0         _a, _b = _b, _a % _b     end     return _a end

4798:function _repeatlast(numfields, listin)     # If listin is empty, return a list of N copies of last     if length(listin) == 0         return [last(listin) for i = 1:numfields]     end     # If numfields <= length(listin) return listin     if numfields <= length(listin)         return listin     end     # Otherwise, return a list of length numfields,     # where the last element is repeated numfields - length(listin) times.     append!(copy(listin), [last(listin) for i = 1:(numfields - length(listin))]) end

4896:function naive_square_matrix_product(A, B)     # Check if matrices are square     m, n = length(A), length(A[1])     if m != n         throw(ArgumentError("Matrices A and B must be square."))     end     # Check if matrices can be multiplied     p = length(B[1])     if n != p         throw(ArgumentError("Matrices A and B can be multiplied."))     end     # Multiply matrices     C = [[0 for _ in 1:n] for _ in 1:m]     for i in 1:m         for j in 1:n             for k in 1:p                 C[i][j] += A[i][k] * B[k][j]             end         end     end     return C end

4921:function collide(ri, vi, rj, vj, box)     # rij = ri - rj     # rij = rij - round.(rij) # Separation vector     # rij = rij * box             # Now in sigma=1 units     # vij = vi - vj               # Relative velocity     # factor = dot(rij, vij)     # vij = -factor * rij     # vi = vi + vij     # vj = vj - vij     # virial = dot(vij, rij) / 3.0     # return vi, vj, virial     rij = ri - rj     rij = rij .- round.(rij) # Separation vector     rij = rij .* box             # Now in sigma=1 units     vij = vi - vj               # Relative velocity     factor = sum(rij .* vij)     vij = -factor * rij     vi = vi .+ vij     vj = vj .- vij     virial = sum(vij .* rij) / 3.0     return vi, vj, virial end

4923:function bit_neighbors(bit)     # get the upper and lower bitboard     # and make sure they're positive     upper_bitboard = (bit & 0xFEFEFEFEFEFEFEFE) >> 1     lower_bitboard = (bit & 0x7F7F7F7F7F7F7F7F) << 1     # get the right and left bitboards     right_bitboard = (bit & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFF00) >> 8     left_bitboard = (bit & 0x00FFFFFFFFFFFFFF) << 8     # return the sum of all the neighbor boards     return upper_bitboard + lower_bitboard + right_bitboard + left_bitboard end

5038:function get_longest_substring(a, b) 	longest = 0 	dy_map = Dict{Tuple{Int64, Int64},Int64}() 	for i in 1:length(a) 		for j in 1:length(b) 			if a[i] == b[j] 				key = (i, j) 				dy_map[key] = get(dy_map, (i - 1, j - 1), 0) + 1 				longest = max(longest, dy_map[key]) 			end 		end 	end 	return longest end

5067:function search(dirname, searchKey)     if !isdir(dirname)         error("$(dirname) is not a directory")     end     # use glob to search for files     files = String[]     if searchKey == "*"         files = readdir(dirname, join=true)     elseif searchKey == ".*"         files = String[]         for (root, dirs, fs) in walkdir(dirname)             for f in fs                 if endswith(f, ".*")                     push!(files, joinpath(root, f))                 end             end         end     elseif contains(searchKey, "[") && contains(searchKey, "]")         # range         for (root, dirs, fs) in walkdir(dirname)             for f in fs                 try                     if f in string.(eval(Meta.parse(searchKey)))                         push!(files, joinpath(root, f))                     end                 catch                     # invalid range                     continue                 end             end         end     elseif isfile(joinpath(dirname, searchKey))         # explicit path         push!(files, joinpath(dirname, searchKey))     else         # not a file or explicit path         for (root, dirs, fs) in walkdir(dirname)             for f in fs                 try                     if ismatch(Regex(searchKey), f)                         push!(files, joinpath(root, f))                     end                 catch                     # invalid regex                     continue                 end             end         end     end     return files end
5068:function _scale_to_fit(width, height, max_width, max_height)     # If both dimensions are already less than the maximum,     # nothing needs to be done.     if width <= max_width && height <= max_height         return width, height     end     # Calculate the scale that needs to be applied to get the     # width to fit within the maximum, and do the same for     # height.     scale_x = max_width / width     scale_y = max_height / height     # Apply the smaller scale to both the width and height.     # This will ensure that the image is not stretched.     scale = min(scale_x, scale_y)     return round(Int, width * scale), round(Int, height * scale) end

5083:function _romberg_diff(b, c, k)     #type checking     if isnan(b) || isnan(c)         error("b and c must be numbers")     end     if !isreal(b) || !isreal(c)         error("b and c must be real numbers")     end     if isnan(k)         error("k must be a number")     end     if !isreal(k)         error("k must be a real number")     end     if k<0         error("k must be positive")     end     #end type checking     if k==0         return c     else         tmp = 4.0^k         diff = (tmp*c-b) / (tmp-1.0)         return diff     end end

5098:function calc_s11_s22_s33(s2211, s1133)     s11, s22, s33 = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0     if (s2211 > 0.0) && (s1133 > 0.0)         if (s1133 < 1e-12)             # s11 = 0.5*(s1133+s2211)             s11 = 0.5*s1133             s22 = 0.5*s1133         elseif (s2211 < 1e-12)             # s22 = 0.5*(s1133+s2211)             s22 = 0.5*s2211             s11 = 0.5*s2211         else             # s11 = s2211*s1133 / (s2211+s1133)             # s22 = s11*s2211 / (s1133+s2211)             # s33 = s11*s1133 / (s1133+s2211)             s11 = (s2211*s1133)/(s2211+s1133)             s22 = s11*s2211/(s1133+s2211)             s33 = s11*s1133/(s1133+s2211)         end     elseif (s2211 > 0.0) && (s1133 < 0.0)         # s11 = s2211         s11 = s2211         s22 = 0.0         s33 = 0.0     elseif (s2211 < 0.0) && (s1133 > 0.0)         # s11 = 0.0         s11 = 0.0         s22 = s1133         s33 = 0.0     else         # s11 = s2211 = s1133 = 0.0         s11 = 0.0         s22 = 0.0         s33 = 0.0     end     return s11, s22, s33 end

5118:function _replace_from_end(s, a, b, times)     first = findfirst(isequal(a), s)     if first == nothing         return s     end     last = findlast(isequal(a), s)     if last == nothing         return s     end     replacements = 0     if first == last         if replacements < times             return string(s[1:(last - 1)], b, s[(last + 1):end])         else             return s         end     end     for i in last:-1:first         if replacements >= times             break         end         if s[i] == a             s = string(s[1:(i - 1)], b, s[(i + 1):end])             replacements += 1         end     end     return s end

5183:function iou(box1, box2)     xmin1 = box1[1]     ymin1 = box1[2]     xmax1 = box1[3]     ymax1 = box1[4]     xmin2 = box2[1]     ymin2 = box2[2]     xmax2 = box2[3]     ymax2 = box2[4]     # determine the coordinates of the intersection rectangle     x_overlap = min(xmax1, xmax2) - max(xmin1, xmin2)     y_overlap = min(ymax1, ymax2) - max(ymin1, ymin2)     # check if there is an overlap     if x_overlap >= 0 && y_overlap >= 0         intersection = x_overlap * y_overlap         # calculate the area of each bounding box         box1area = (xmax1 - xmin1) * (ymax1 - ymin1)         box2area = (xmax2 - xmin2) * (ymax2 - ymin2)         # calculate the intersection over union         iou = intersection / (box1area + box2area - intersection)         return iou     end     return 0 end

5207:function findKeyD(phi, e) 	x = 0 	old_x = 1 	y = 1 	old_y = 0 	r = e 	old_r = phi 	while !iszero(r) 		q = div(old_r, r) 		old_r, r = r, old_r - q*r 		old_x, x = x, old_x - q*x 		old_y, y = y, old_y - q*y 	end 	d = mod(old_y, phi) 	if d < 0 		d += phi 	end 	return d end

5247:function naive_log_ctz(x::Int64)::Int64     if x == 0         return 0     end     # We get the number of trailing zero bits in x by counting the number of trailing     # ones in x's binary representation, starting at the highest bit.     # The number of trailing ones is the number of zeros in x,     # so the number of trailing zeros is the number of trailing ones minus 1.     # This algorithm is logarithmic in the number of trailing bits.     count = 0     while x & 1 == 0         count += 1         x >>= 1     end     return count end
5248:function to_base(number::Int64, base::Int64)::String     if base > 36         throw(ErrorException("Bases greater than 36 not handled in base_repr."))     elseif base < 2         throw(ErrorException("Bases less than 2 not handled in base_repr."))     end     if number == 0         return "0"     end     number_is_negative = false     if number < 0         number_is_negative = true         number = abs(number)     end     digits = "0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"     res = ""     while number > 0         res *= digits[number % base+1]         number = div(number, base)     end     if number_is_negative         res *= '-'     end     return reverse(res) end

5260:function sort_module_names(modlst)     # Sort a list of module names in order of subpackage depth     srtlst = sort!(copy(modlst))     # Filter out unwanted modules     srtlst = filter(x -> occursin(r"^[^_].*", x), srtlst)     srtlst = filter(x -> !occursin(r"__init__$", x), srtlst)     # Get list of unique prefixes     prfxlst = sort(unique(map(x -> split(x, ".")[1], srtlst)))     # Get prefix depths     prfdpls = map(x -> count(y -> y == x, prfxlst), srtlst)     # Assign depths in descending order     prfdpls = sort(prfdpls, rev=true)     # Create tuple of name, depth     name_depths = collect(zip(srtlst, prfdpls))     # Sort tuple in order of depth, then alphabetically     srtlst = map(x -> x[1], sort(name_depths, by=x -> x[2], rev=true))     return srtlst end

5331:function baryocentric_coords(pts, pt)   (p1, p2, p3) = pts   # We use the barycentric coordinate system to express the coordinates of the   # point (x, y) in terms of the coordinates of the three points (x1, y1),   # (x2, y2) and (x3, y3). The formula is:   #   # x = x1 * (1 - γ - β) + x2 * γ + x3 * β   # y = y1 * (1 - γ - β) + y2 * γ + y3 * β   #   # which is equivalent to:   #   # x = (x1 - x3) * γ + (x2 - x3) * β + x3   # y = (y1 - y3) * γ + (y2 - y3) * β + y3   #   # where γ and β are the coordinates of the point in the triangle.   (x1, y1) = p1   (x2, y2) = p2   (x3, y3) = p3   x, y = pt   γ = ((x2 - x3) * (y - y3) + (y2 - y3) * (x - x3)) / ((x2 - x3) * (y1 - y3) + (y2 - y3) * (x1 - x3))   β = ((x3 - x1) * (y - y3) + (y3 - y1) * (x - x3)) / ((x2 - x3) * (y1 - y3) + (y2 - y3) * (x1 - x3))   return γ, β, 1 - γ - β end

5431:function compute_iou(rec1, rec2)     y0 = rec1[1]     x0 = rec1[2]     y1 = rec1[3]     x1 = rec1[4]     y2 = rec2[1]     x2 = rec2[2]     y3 = rec2[3]     x3 = rec2[4]     # compute area of each rectangle     S_rec1 = (x1 - x0) * (y1 - y0)     S_rec2 = (x3 - x2) * (y3 - y2)     # compute the sum_area     sum_area = S_rec1 + S_rec2     # find the each edge of intersect rectangle     left_line = max(x0, x2)     right_line = min(x1, x3)     top_line = max(y0, y2)     bottom_line = min(y1, y3)     # judge if there is an intersect     if left_line >= right_line || top_line >= bottom_line         return 0     else         intersect = (right_line - left_line) * (bottom_line - top_line)         # print(intersect,sum_area)         return (float(intersect) / float(sum_area - intersect)) * 1.0     end end

5525:function xgcd(b, n)     x, lastx, y, lasty = 0, 1, 1, 0     while n != 0         q, b, n = div(b, n), n, mod(b, n)         x, lastx = lastx - q * x, x         y, lasty = lasty - q * y, y     end     return b, lastx, lasty end
5526:function get_iou(box1, box2)     # Calculate the (y1, x1, y2, x2) coordinates of the intersection of box1 and box2. Calculate its Area.     xi1 = max(box1[1], box2[1])     yi1 = max(box1[2], box2[2])     xi2 = min(box1[3], box2[3])     yi2 = min(box1[4], box2[4])     inter_area = max(xi2 - xi1, 0) * max(yi2 - yi1, 0)     # Calculate the Union area by using Formula: Union(A,B) = A + B - Inter(A,B)     box1_area = (box1[3]-box1[1]) * (box1[4]-box1[2])     box2_area = (box2[3]-box2[1]) * (box2[4]-box2[2])     union_area = box1_area + box2_area - inter_area     # compute the IoU     iou = inter_area / union_area     return iou end

5555:function aai_seq(seq1, seq2)   # calculate length of the longest sequence   # i.e. maximum number of mismatches   # aaa_seq("abcdefghi", "agttactgg")   # > 3   longest_sequence = max(length(seq1), length(seq2))   # calculate the number of mismatches   # between the 2 sequences   # aaa_seq("abcdefghi", "agttactgg")   # > 6   number_of_mismatches = 0   for (i,j) in zip(seq1, seq2)     number_of_mismatches += i != j   end   # return the percentage of identity   # aaa_seq("abcdefghi", "agttactgg")   # > 0.8   return 1 - (number_of_mismatches / longest_sequence) end

5640:function quantize(x)     # Unpack the 4 LSBs from the byte, and remove them.     # This returns a 4-bit number, from 0 to 15.     top = x & 0b11110000     # Determine the number of quantized values within 0 and 15.     # The & 0b1111 ensures we don't have a negative number.     num_quantized = top & 0b1111     # We need to determine the distance between each quantized value.     # This is equivalent to the number of quantized values per byte.     # The 0b11111111 is a mask that ensures that we don't have an overflow     # by pulling the byte into the first bit of the next byte.     quantized_distance = (num_quantized * 255) & 0b11111111     # Determine the lower bound of our quantization.     # This is equivalent to the first quantized value.     lower_bound = top - quantized_distance     # The upper bound is the lower bound plus 8 quantized values.     upper_bound = lower_bound + quantized_distance * 8     # Calculate the quantized value.     quantized = quantized_distance * (x - lower_bound)     # We can now return the quantized value, from 0 to 255.     return quantized end
5641:function fuzzy_equal(x, y, z)     if length(x) != length(y)         throw(DomainError("x and y must be the same length"))     end     if length(x) != length(z)         throw(DomainError("x and z must be the same length"))     end     return (y .< (x .+ z)) .& (y .> (x .- z)) end
5642:function is_palindrome(s)     # check if the given input is a string     if typeof(s) != String         error("is_palindrome: input needs to be a string!")     end     # check if the length of the input is 1 or less     if length(s) < 2         # return True, because a palindrome is a word with 1 letter or less         return true     end     # check if the first letter of the string is the last letter of the string     # case is not taken into consideration     if uppercase(s[1]) == uppercase(s[end])         # if the input is a palindrome, then we can assume the second letter         # is the second last letter of the string and so on         # case is not taken into consideration         return is_palindrome(lowercase(s[2:end-1]))     else         # otherwise we know the input is not a palindrome         return false     end end

5644:function grad_logp(p, alpha0, x)     n = length(alpha0)     d = length(p)     if n > 1         J = zeros(n, d)         for j in 1:d             J[1,j] = (alpha0[1] - 1 - x[j]) / p[1]             for i in 2:n                 J[i,j] = (alpha0[i] - alpha0[i-1] - x[j]) / p[i]             end         end         return J     else         return (alpha0[1] - 1 - x[1]) / p[1]     end end

5651:function extended_euclidean(a, b)     r = (a, b)     s = (1, 0)     t = (0, 1)     while r[2] != 0         q = floor(Int, r[1]/r[2])         new_r = (r[2], r[1] % r[2])         s = (s[2], s[1] - q*s[2])         t = (t[2], t[1] - q*t[2])         r = new_r     end     return r[1], s[1], t[1] end

5683:function orientation(a, b, c)     # Return a value less than zero if c is clockwise     # from point a, greater than zero if counterclockwise.     # Note that we use the cross product formula     #     (1) (y2 - y1) (z - x1)     #     (2) (x2 - x1) (y - y1)     #     (3) (x2 - x1) (z - x1)     # which is the determinant of the matrix     #     | y2 - y1 |     # M = | z - x1 |     #     | y - y1 |     # and is equivalent to the signed volume of the parallelepiped     # determined by the vectors (x1, y1, z), (x2, y2, z) and (x, y, c).     (b[2] - a[2]) * (c[1] - a[1]) - (b[1] - a[1]) * (c[2] - a[2]) end

5746:function iou(obj_proposal, annot_rect)     # find the coordinates of the intersection box     xi1 = max(obj_proposal[1], annot_rect[1])     yi1 = max(obj_proposal[2], annot_rect[2])     xi2 = min(obj_proposal[3], annot_rect[3])     yi2 = min(obj_proposal[4], annot_rect[4])     # compute the area of intersection     inter_area = (yi2 - yi1) * (xi2 - xi1)     # compute the area of each box     obj_proposal_area = (obj_proposal[3] - obj_proposal[1]) * (obj_proposal[4] - obj_proposal[2])     annot_rect_area = (annot_rect[3] - annot_rect[1]) * (annot_rect[4] - annot_rect[2])     # compute the area of union     union_area = obj_proposal_area + annot_rect_area - inter_area     # compute the intersection over union     iou = inter_area / union_area     return iou end

5754:function saponificationIndex(sample_weight, HCl_molarity, HCl_fc, HCl_spent, blank_volume)     # We can write the result in terms of a function of the blank volume, since     # the proportion of KOH spent is just the ratio of the final volume to the     # initial volume.     V_HCl = blank_volume - HCl_spent     mols_KOH = HCl_molarity * HCl_fc * V_HCl     KOH_mass = mols_KOH * 56 # 56 is the molecular weight of the KOH     saponification_index = KOH_mass / sample_weight     return saponification_index end

5794:function rosenbrock(args) 	if length(args) < 1 		return 100000 	end 	x = args 	inner = 0 	for i in 1:(length(x) - 1) 		inner += 100 * (x[i] * x[i] - x[i + 1]) * (x[i] * x[i] - x[i + 1]) + (1 - x[i]) * (1 - x[i]) 	end 	return inner end

5799:function dispatch_strategy(declaration)     if !declaration["abstract"] && declaration["derivative"] == nothing         return "use_type"     end     if !declaration["abstract"] && declaration["derivative"] != nothing         # use the derived version for performance reasons         if declaration["derivative"] == "generic_derivative"             # this function is a factory function that we want to call on Type             return "use_type"         elseif declaration["derivative"] == "scalar_to_tensor"             # this function should not be called from differentiable code             # and should always return a differentiable tensor             return "use_type"         elseif declaration["derivative"] == "view_as_real"             # this function is used in differentiable code to perform             # conversions between real and complex.  We want to call it             # on the Type dispatch path because it is implemented             # concretely and the underlying complex functions are             # differentiable (e.g., imag())             return "use_type"         end         # this is a function that is implemented concretely.         # we want to call it on the derived Type dispatch path to ensure         # that we don't need to unpack and pack Tensors         return "use_derived"     end     # abstract functions that are not implemented on at::Type should     # not be differentiable.  They should be wrapped in a Variable.     # We want to call them on the derived Type dispatch path to ensure     # that we don't need to unpack and pack Tensors.     return "use_derived" end

5810:function convert_bboxm_to_bboxcen(bbox)     # Given the bounding box in the form     # [label, xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax]     # return the bounding box in the form     # [label, xcen, ycen, w, h]     # where:     #   xcen, ycen = center of bounding box     #   w, h = width and height of bounding box     # Isolate the class of the bounding box     label = bbox[1]     # Isolate the corners of the bounding box     x = bbox[2]     y = bbox[3]     xb = bbox[4]     yb = bbox[5]     # Compute the dimensions of the bounding box     w = xb - x     h = yb - y     # Compute the center of the bounding box     xcen = x + w/2     ycen = y + h/2     return [label, xcen, ycen, w, h] end

5861:function _mat_mat_sub_fp(x, y)     # Check that the dimensions of the matrices match.     m = size(x, 1)     n = size(x, 2)     if size(y, 1) != m         throw(DimensionMismatch("x and y must have the same number of rows."))     end     if size(y, 2) != n         throw(DimensionMismatch("x and y must have the same number of columns."))     end     # Create an empty matrix to store the result.     z = similar(x)     # Loop over the rows and columns of the matrices.     for i in 1:m         for j in 1:n             z[i, j] = x[i, j] - y[i, j]         end     end     # Return the result.     return z end

5990:function modular_inverse(a, mod)     # Initialize values     r_prev, u_prev, v_prev, r, u, v = a, 1, 0, mod, 0, 1     # Loop while r is not 0     while r != 0         q = r_prev ÷ r         r_prev, u_prev, v_prev, r, u, v = (             r,             u,             v,             r_prev - q * r,             u_prev - q * u,             v_prev - q * v,         )     end     return u_prev end
5991:function is_valid_sa_id_no(sa_id_no)     # len(sa_id_no) == 13     if length(sa_id_no) != 13         return false     end     # Every character should be between '0' and '9'     for c in sa_id_no         if c < '0' || c > '9'             return false         end     end     # First character should not be '0'     if sa_id_no[1] == '0'         return false     end     # Second character should not be '0'     if sa_id_no[2] == '0'         return false     end     # Last character should not be '0'     if sa_id_no[13] == '0'         return false     end     # First 7 characters should not be '0'     for c in sa_id_no[1:7]         if c == '0'             return false         end     end     # Second 7 characters should not be '0'     for c in sa_id_no[8:14]         if c == '0'             return false         end     end     # Calculate the checksum     cs = 0     for i = 1:length(sa_id_no)         if i % 2 == 0             cs += parse(Int, sa_id_no[i])         else             cs += parse(Int, sa_id_no[i]) * 3         end     end     # The checksum should be divisible by 10     return cs % 10 == 0 end

6003:function struct_size(items)     member_sum = 0     pad = 0     most_aligned = 1     for (elem, align) in items         most_aligned = max(most_aligned, align)         pad = (align - member_sum % align) % align         member_sum = member_sum + pad + elem         pad = (most_aligned - member_sum % most_aligned) % most_aligned         member_sum += pad     end     return [member_sum, most_aligned] end

6013:function parse_signing_keys(raw)     lines = split(raw, '\n')     count = 1     keys = Dict{AbstractString, AbstractString}()     next_fingerprint = nothing     while count <= length(lines)         if startswith(lines[count], "fingerprint")             if next_fingerprint !== nothing                 error("File has not the expected format")             else                 next_fingerprint = split(lines[count], ' ')[2]             end         elseif lines[count] == "dir-signing-key"             count += 1             key = lines[count] * '\n'             count += 1             while lines[count] != "-----END RSA PUBLIC KEY-----"                 key *= lines[count] * '\n'                 count += 1             end             key *= "-----END RSA PUBLIC KEY-----"             keys[next_fingerprint] = key             next_fingerprint = nothing         end         count += 1     end     return keys end

6015:function weakest_cipher(supported_ciphers)     if length(supported_ciphers) == 0         return nothing     end     # find lowest cipher bits supported     lowest_cipher_bits = 4000000000  # suitably large number     for c in supported_ciphers         cipher_bits = parse(Int, c["bits"])         if cipher_bits < lowest_cipher_bits             lowest_cipher_bits = cipher_bits         end     end     # find the highest cipher order with the lowest cipher bits     # assumes the supported_ciphers list is already sorted     # by cipher order     highest_order_lowest_bit_cipher = nothing     for c in supported_ciphers         cipher_bits = parse(Int, c["bits"])         if cipher_bits == lowest_cipher_bits             highest_order_lowest_bit_cipher = c             break         end     end     result = nothing     if !isnothing(highest_order_lowest_bit_cipher)         result = [             string(highest_order_lowest_bit_cipher["bits"], "-bit ", highest_order_lowest_bit_cipher["cipher"]),             highest_order_lowest_bit_cipher["strength"]         ]     end     result end

6025:function compute_line_intersection_point(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, x4, y4)     D = (x1 - x2) * (y3 - y4) - (y1 - y2) * (x3 - x4)     Dx = (x1*y2 - y1*x2) * (x3 - x4) - (x1 - x2) * (x3*y4 - y3*x4)     Dy = (x1*y2 - y1*x2) * (y3 - y4) - (y1 - y2) * (x3*y4 - y3*x4)     if D != 0         x = Dx / D         y = Dy / D         return x, y     else         return false     end end

6050:function snake_to_screaming_snake_case(text::String)::String     # We can't just call `uppercase` on the whole string because we'd end up     # with a SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE_SNAKE_CASE, which is ugly. Instead, we'll     # construct the SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE as we go.     output = IOBuffer()     first_char = true     for c in text         if first_char             write(output, uppercase(c))             first_char = false         elseif c === '_'             write(output, '_')             first_char = true         else             write(output, uppercase(c))         end     end     return String(take!(output)) end

6146:function scale(val, src, dst)     # Scale value from src range to dst range.     # If value outside bounds, it is clipped and set to     # the low or high bound of dst.     # Ex:     #     scale(0, (0.0, 99.0), (-1.0, 1.0)) == -1.0     #     scale(-5, (0.0, 99.0), (-1.0, 1.0)) == -1.0     (src_low, src_high) = src     (dst_low, dst_high) = dst     # Clamp value to src range     if val < src_low         val = src_low     elseif val > src_high         val = src_high     end     # Calculate dst value     dst_low + (val - src_low) / (src_high - src_low) * (dst_high - dst_low) end

6156:function _sortnodesellipsis(store, nodes, cl, lookup)     # Ellipses serving mode.     #     # In a perfect world, we'd generate better ellipsis-ified graphs     # for non-changelog revlogs. In practice, we haven't started doing     # that yet, so the resulting DAGs for the manifestlog and filelogs     # are actually full of bogus parentage on all the ellipsis     # nodes. This has the side effect that, while the contents are     # correct, the individual DAGs might be completely out of whack in     # a case like 882681bc3166 and its ancestors (back about 10     # revisions or so) in the main hg repo.     #     # The one invariant we *know* holds is that the new (potentially     # bogus) DAG shape will be valid if we order the nodes in the     # order that they're introduced in dramatis personae by the     # changelog, so what we do is we sort the non-changelog histories     # by the order in which they are used by the changelog.     key = Rev -> begin         if Rev in keys(lookup)             return cl.rev(lookup[Rev])         else             return cl.rev(Rev)         end     end     return sort(nodes, by=key) end

6190:function decay(rho, beta, progress)     if rho >= 0 && rho <= 1         if rho == 0             return beta         elseif rho > 0 && rho < 0.5             return beta * (1 - (progress) ^ (1 / (2 * rho)))         elseif rho == 0.5             return beta * (1 - progress)         elseif rho > 0.5 && rho < 1             return beta * (1 - progress) ^ (1 / (2 * (1 - rho)))         elseif rho == 1             return 0         end     else         throw(DomainError(rho, "Rho must be in [0,1]"))     end end

6192:function estimate_p_value(observed_value, random_distribution)     num_permutations = length(random_distribution)     num_exceedances = length([score for score in random_distribution             if score >= observed_value])      if num_exceedances > 10         return num_exceedances / num_permutations     else         # This is the expected number of exceedances for a random         # value drawn from the distribution, assuming that the random         # value is a typical value.         N = length(random_distribution)         expected_num_exceedances = num_permutations *             N / (N - 1)         # The estimated p-value is simply M / N, where M is the number         # of exceedances, and M > 10, and N is the number of         # permutations performed to this point (rather than the total         # number of permutations to be performed, or possible). For         # further details, see Knijnenburg et al. [1]         p_value = num_exceedances / num_permutations         return min(p_value, expected_num_exceedances)     end end
6193:function union(left, right)     result = Dict()     for (key, value) in left         if key in keys(right)             if length(value) < length(right[key])                 result[key] = value             else                 result[key] = right[key]             end         else             result[key] = value         end     end     for (key, value) in right         if !(key in keys(left))             result[key] = value         end     end     return result end

6323:function splitdrive(path)     if any(path .== "/")         # OS X, Windows, and other systems with a single-character root         drive = "/"         path = path[2:end]     elseif any(path .== "\\")         # Windows, but with a drive specification.         if length(path) < 2             return ("", path)         end         drive = path[1]         if drive in 'a':'z' || drive in 'A':'Z'             path = path[3:end]         elseif drive == '/' || drive == '\\'             path = path[2:end]         else             return ("", path)         end     else         # No drive specification.         drive = ""     end     return (drive, path) end

6435:function auto_refresh_cached(n_intervals)     # This is the slow cache.     # The dash callbacks will call the functions in this cache in intervals.     # The result is that these functions will run without user interaction.     # The sleep() ensures that the functions are called a little bit after     # the cache expires. Thus, the slow cache should always be populated     # and no user should ever need to have to wait for the expensive functions     # to run.     SLOW_CACHE = Dict{Symbol,Any}()     function get_map_data()         # sleep(10)         # logging.debug("Auto-refreshing slow cache...")         # get_map_data()         # get_map_traces()         # logging.debug(f"Auto-refresh {n_intervals} finished.")         return n_intervals     end     function get_map_traces()         # sleep(10)         # logging.debug("Auto-refreshing slow cache...")         # get_map_data()         # get_map_traces()         # logging.debug(f"Auto-refresh {n_intervals} finished.")         return n_intervals     end     # This is the fast cache.     # The dash callbacks will call the functions in this cache in intervals.     # The result is that these functions will run without user interaction.     # The dash callbacks will call the functions in this cache in intervals.     # The result is that these functions will run without user interaction.     # The sleep() ensures that the functions are called a little bit after     # the cache expires. Thus, the slow cache should always be populated     # and no user should ever need to have to wait for the expensive functions     # to run.     FAST_CACHE = Dict{Symbol,Any}()     function get_map_data()         # sleep(10)         # logging.debug("Auto-refreshing slow cache...")         # get_map_data()         # get_map_traces()         # logging.debug(f"Auto-refresh {n_intervals} finished.")         return n_intervals     end     function get_map_traces()         # sleep(10)         # logging.debug("Auto-refreshing slow cache...")         # get_map_data()         # get_map_traces()         # logging.debug(f"Auto-refresh {n_intervals} finished.")         return n_intervals     end     # The interval component fires a callback that makes these calls to the     # functions in the SLOW_CACHE. The result is that these expensive functions     # are called periodically without user interaction. The sleep() delay ensures     # that the functions are called a little bit after the cache expires. Thus, the     # slow cache should always be populated and no user should ever need to have to     # wait for the expensive functions to run.     return minimum([get_map_data(), get_map_traces()]) end

We have to include a mapping from 'graph_attrs' to     # the dictionary of values in args that are in the set graphattr_set     pass_args = Dict()     for (key, value) in pairs(args)         # If the key is in map_args         if key in map_args             # Add the key and value to pass_args             pass_args[key] = value         else             # Else if the key is 'graph_attrs' and the value is in graphattr_set             if key == "graph_attrs" && value in graph_attrs                 # Add the key and value to graph_attrs                 graph_attrs[key] = value             end         end     end     # Add graph_attrs to pass_args     pass_args["graph_attrs"] = graph_attrs     return pass_args end

6522:function SetFieldValue(regValue, lsb, fsize, fieldValue)     if fieldValue < 0 then         error("field value '%d' must be positive", fieldValue)     end     if fieldValue > ((1 << fsize) - 1) then         error("field value '%d' exceeds range of %d bits", fieldValue, fsize)     end     msb = lsb + fsize     mask = ~((1 << msb) - 1 & ~((1 << lsb) - 1))     return regValue & mask | (fieldValue << lsb) end

6545:function estimate_cudnn_parameter_size(input_size, hidden_size, direction)     # To use CuDNN RNN, we need to keep the length of the sequence the same for each batch.     # If we feed variable length sequences, CuDNN RNN will return an error.     # If we feed a fixed length sequence, the first element of the sequence is used for all the batches.     # This can result in losing information.     # This is why we pad the inputs to have the same length.     # Moreover, when using CuDNN RNN, the number of layers of the network must be one.     # Therefore, we use two networks: one for the forward pass and one for the backward pass.     # In principle, it is possible to do it in one network but it requires recurrent layers     # that can operate on sequences of different lengths, which is not supported by CuDNN.     direction == :forward && return hidden_size * (input_size + hidden_size + 3)     direction == :backward && return hidden_size * (input_size + hidden_size + 2) end
6546:function check_string(input_string)     replace_words = Dict(" " => "_",                          "," => "_",                          ";" => "_",                          ":" => "_",                          "\"" => "_",                          "=" => "_equal_",                          ">" => "_greater_",                          "<" => "_smaller_",                          "&" => "_and_",                          "|" => "_or_")     replace_chars = Dict('!' => "_exclamation_",                          '?' => "_question_",                          '$' => "_dollar_",                          '%' => "_percent_",                          '^' => "_caret_",                          '&' => "_and_",                          '*' => "_asterisk_",                          '(' => "_open_par_",                          ')' => "_close_par_",                          '-' => "_minus_",                          '+' => "_plus_",                          '=' => "_equal_",                          '{' => "_open_curly_",                          '}' => "_close_curly_",                          '[' => "_open_bracket_",                          ']' => "_close_bracket_",                          '<' => "_less_",                          '>' => "_greater_",                          ';' => "_semicolon_",                          ':' => "_colon_",                          '"' => "_double_quote_",                          '\'' => "_single_quote_",                          '/' => "_forward_slash_",                          '\\' => "_backward_slash_",                          '.' => "_period_",                          ',' => "_comma_",                          '#' => "_hash_",                          '@' => "_at_",                          '~' => "_tilde_")     # replace characters     for (old, new) in replace_chars         input_string = replace(input_string, old => new)     end     # replace words     for (old, new) in replace_words         input_string = replace(input_string, old => new)     end     return input_string end

6561:function Hubble(Om, z)     if z > 0.55         return (Om * (1 + z)^3 + 1 - Om)^0.5     end     if z < -0.55         return (Om * (1 + z)^3 + 1 - Om)^0.5     end     H0 = 100. * Om * (1 + z)^3 / (2.9979e10 * 3.086e18)^2     H = 100. * Om * (1 + z)^3 / (2.9979e10 * 3.086e18 * (1 + z)^3 * (1 + z)^-3)^2     D = 0.005 * Om * (1 + z)^3 / (1 + z)^2     H1 = H0 * (1 + 0.65 * D * (1 + z)^2 / (1 + 0.65 * (1 + z)^2))     H2 = H0 * (1 + 0.3 * D * (1 + z)^2 / (1 + 0.3 * (1 + z)^2))     if z >= -0.01 && z <= 0.01         return H     end     if z >= 0.01 && z <= 0.55         return H1     end     if z >= 0.55 && z <= 1.25         return H2     end     if z >= 1.25 && z <= 2.05         return H2     end     if z >= 2.05 && z <= 5.0         return H2     end     return H2 end

6625:function min_edit_distance(word1::String, word2::String)::Int64     word1 = lowercase(word1)     word2 = lowercase(word2)     if length(word1) == 0         return length(word2)     elseif length(word2) == 0         return length(word1)     end     dp = zeros(Int64, length(word1) + 1, length(word2) + 1)     for i in 0:length(word1)         dp[i + 1, 1] = i     end     for i in 0:length(word2)         dp[1, i + 1] = i     end     for i in 1:length(word1)         for j in 1:length(word2)             if word1[i] == word2[j]                 dp[i + 1, j + 1] = dp[i, j]             else                 insert = dp[i, j + 1]                 remove = dp[i + 1, j]                 replace = dp[i, j]                 dp[i + 1, j + 1] = min(insert + 1, remove + 1, replace + 1)             end         end     end     return dp[end, end] end

6666:function detxy2kxy(xdet, ydet, xstart, ystart, x0, y0, fx, fy, xstep, ystep)     # check input     if !haskey(ENV, "JULIA_DEBUG") && (x0 > 1 || x0 < 0 || y0 > 1 || y0 < 0)         throw(DomainError(x0, "x0 must be between 0 and 1"))     end     if !haskey(ENV, "JULIA_DEBUG") && (fx < 0 || fy < 0)         throw(DomainError(fx, "fx and fy must be positive"))     end     if !haskey(ENV, "JULIA_DEBUG") && (xstep < 1 || ystep < 1)         throw(DomainError(xstep, "xstep and ystep must be positive"))     end     # calculate determinant     xdet0 = xstart + xstep * x0     ydet0 = ystart + ystep * y0     kx = fx * ((xdet - xdet0) / xstep)     ky = fy * ((ydet - ydet0) / ystep)     return kx, ky end
6667:function assess_difficulty(parsed_text)     # initialise graded_parsed_text     graded_parsed_text = copy(parsed_text)     # for each word in parsed_text     for word_index in 1:length(parsed_text)         # check to see if we've reached the end of the text         if word_index == length(parsed_text)             # if so, then we want to skip this word             continue         end         # check to see if this word has been identified as translatable         if parsed_text[word_index][:to_translate] == true             # if so, find the translation from the english_to_spanish dictionary             translation = english_to_spanish[parsed_text[word_index][:word]]             # if we can't find the translation, set the difficulty score to 0             if translation == nothing                 graded_parsed_text[word_index][:difficulty_score] = 0             else                 # if we can find the translation, then find the length of the translation                 # and set the difficulty score to the difference between the word length                 # and the translation length                 graded_parsed_text[word_index][:difficulty_score] = length(parsed_text[word_index][:word]) - length(translation)             end         end     end     # return the graded parsed text     return graded_parsed_text end

6751:function frequency_p(tol_str, tar_str)     len_tol_str = length(tol_str)     len_tar_str = length(tar_str)     if len_tol_str < len_tar_str         return 0     end     tar_count, tar1_count, tar2_count, tar3_count = 0, 0, 0, 0     i = 1     while i <= len_tol_str - len_tar_str + 1         if tol_str[i:i+len_tar_str-1] == tar_str             tar_count += 1             i += len_tar_str             if (                     i) % 3 == 1                 # judge the position of last base of kmer in corresponding codon. pay attention to "i + 1"                 tar1_count += 1             elseif (i) % 3 == 2                 tar2_count += 1             else                 tar3_count += 1             end         else             i += 1         end     end     return (tar_count, tar1_count, tar2_count, tar3_count) end

6770:function DensHumid(tempc, pres, e)     tempk = tempc + 273.15     Rs_v = 461.52  # Specific gas const for water vapour, J kg^{-1} K^{-1}     Rs_da = 287.05  # Specific gas const for dry air, J kg^{-1} K^{-1}     pres_da = pres * 100.0 - e * 100.0     rho_da = pres_da / (Rs_da * tempk)     rho_wv = e / (Rs_v * tempk)     return rho_da + rho_wv end

6788:function catmull_rom_one_point(x, v0, v1, v2, v3)     # Values for Catmull-Rom spline.     # Can be pre-computed.     c1 = 1.0 * v1     c2 = -0.5 * v0 + 0.5 * v2     c3 = 1.0 * v0 + -2.5 * v1 + 2.0 * v2 - 0.5 * v3     c4 = -0.5 * v0 + 1.5 * v1 + -1.5 * v2 + 0.5 * v3     return ((c4 * x + c3) * x + c2) * x + c1 end

6790:function _evenly_distribute(ys)     # Initialize counters for number of ones and zeros.     ones = zeros = 0     # Loop through array, counting the number of ones and zeros.     for y in ys         y == 0 ? zeros += 1 : ones += 1     end     # Assert that there are no ones and zeros in the input array.     @assert ones + zeros == length(ys)     # Return the original array if there are no ones or zeros.     if ones == 0 || zeros == 0         return ys     end     # Calculate the ratio of ones to zeros.     ratio = ones / zeros     # Initialize an empty array for the result.     result = []     # Loop through the input array.     for y in ys         # If there are more zeros than ones, append a zero to the result.         if zeros > ones             push!(result, 0)             zeros -= 1         # If there are more ones than zeros, append a one to the result.         elseif ones > zeros             push!(result, 1)             ones -= 1         # If there are more zeros than ones, append a zero to the result.         else             push!(result, round(y / ratio))             if y % ratio == 1                 ones -= 1             else                 zeros -= 1             end         end     end     # Assert that there are no more zeros or ones in the result.     @assert zeros == 0 || ones == 0     return result end

6885:function hermiteInterpolate(v0, v1, v2, v3, alpha, tension, bias)     alpha2 = alpha * alpha     alpha3 = alpha2 * alpha     m0 = (((v1 - v0) * (1 - tension)) * (1 + bias)) / 2.0     m0 += (((v2 - v1) * (1 - tension)) * (1 - bias)) / 2.0     m1 = (((v2 - v1) * (1 - tension)) * (1 + bias)) / 2.0     m1 += (((v3 - v2) * (1 - tension)) * (1 - bias)) / 2.0     a0 = 2 * alpha3 - 3 * alpha2 + 1     a1 = alpha3 - 2 * alpha2 + alpha     a2 = alpha3 - alpha2     a3 = -2 * alpha3 + 3 * alpha2     return a0 * v1 + a1 * m0 + a2 * m1 + a3 * v2 end

6922:function sir(s, v, i, i_v, r, vaccination_rate, beta, gamma_unvaccinated, gamma_vaccinated, vaccine_efficacy, n)     s_n = -beta * s * i * vaccination_rate - beta * s * i_v + vaccination_rate * s     v_n = vaccination_rate * s - beta * (1 - vaccine_efficacy) * v * i - beta * (1 - vaccine_efficacy) * v * i_v + v     i_n = beta * s * i * vaccination_rate + beta * s * i_v - gamma_unvaccinated * i + i     i_v_n = beta * (1 - vaccine_efficacy) * v * i + beta * (1 - vaccine_efficacy) * v * i_v - gamma_vaccinated * i_v + i_v     r_n = gamma_vaccinated * i_v + gamma_unvaccinated * i + r     scale = n / (s_n + v_n + i_n + i_v_n + r_n)     s = s_n * scale     v = v_n * scale     i = i_n * scale     i_v = i_v_n * scale     r = r_n * scale     return s, v, i, i_v, r end

6976:function quick_remove_equivalent_partitions(partitions)     partition_set = Set()     for part in partitions         if length(part) < 2             push!(partition_set, part)             continue         end         for subset in partition_set             if length(union(subset, part)) == length(subset)                 break             elseif length(union(subset, part)) == length(part)                 # return the partition that is in the larger subset                 if length(subset) > length(part)                     return subset                 else                     return part                 end             end         end         push!(partition_set, part)     end     return sort!(collect(partition_set)) end

6998:function search(str1, str2)     max_correct = 0     max_seq = "No match"     len_str1 = length(str1)     len_str2 = length(str2)     if len_str1 == 0 || len_str2 == 0         return max_seq     end     for i = 1:len_str1-len_str2+1         correct = 0         for j = 1:len_str2             if str1[i+j-1] == str2[j]                 correct += 1             end         end         if correct > max_correct             max_correct = correct             max_seq = str1[i:i+len_str2-1]         end     end     return max_seq end

7100:function zimmermann(x)     x0, x1 = x     f8 = 9 - x0 - x1     c0, c1, c2, c3 = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0     if x0 < 0.0         c0 = -100.0 * x0     end     if x1 < 0.0         c1 = -100.0 * x1     end     xx =  (x0-3.0)*(x0-3.0) + (x1-2.0)*(x1-2.0)     if xx > 16.0         c2 = 100.0 * (xx-16.0)     end     if x0 * x1 > 14.0         c3 = 100.0 * (x0*x1-14.0)     end     return max(f8,c0,c1,c2,c3) end
7101:function boarding_pass_to_seat_id(boarding_pass::String)::Int64     seat_id::Int64 = 0     # Iterate over boarding pass, one character at a time     for i in 1:length(boarding_pass)         if boarding_pass[i] == 'F' || boarding_pass[i] == 'L'             # Character is F or L (0), so drop the 0 to the left             # Example: 'FBFBBFFRLR' at index 1 => 0101100101             seat_id <<= 1         else             # Character is B or R (1), so raise the 0 to the left             # Example: 'FBFBBFFRLR' at index 1 => 1101100101             seat_id <<= 1             seat_id += 1         end     end     # Return the seat ID     return seat_id end

7112:function canConstruct_v4(ransomNote::String, magazine::String)::Bool     # We need to make sure the count of letters in the ransom note is less than or equal to the count of letters in the magazine.     # For this, we build a dictionary of the letters of the magazine and use the letter as a key and count as the value.     # We use the dictionary's "get" function to check if the letter exists in the dictionary.     # If it does, we add 1 to the current count.     # If it does not, we initialize the letter's count as 1 and add the letter to the dictionary.     # If the value of the current letter in the dictionary is greater than or equal to the value of the letter in the ransom note, we remove the current letter from the dictionary.     # Otherwise, we return False.     # If we finish iterating over the ransom note, we return True.     d = Dict{Char,Int}()     for letter in magazine         d[letter] = get(d, letter, 0) + 1     end     for letter in ransomNote         val = get(d, letter, 0)         val -= 1         val == 0 && delete!(d, letter)         val < 0 && return false     end     return true end
7113:function linearRegression(xyList)     (xs, ys) = (first.(xyList), last.(xyList))     (avgX, avgY, avgX2, avgXY) = (sum(xs)/length(xs), sum(ys)/length(ys), sum(xs.^2)/length(xs), sum(xs .* ys)/length(xs))     a = (avgXY - avgX * avgY) / (avgX2 - avgX^2)     b = avgY - a * avgX     return (a, b) end

7256:function belong_to_the_same_package(first_module_import_path::String, second_module_import_path::String)::Bool     # if one of the import paths is empty, then return false     if length(first_module_import_path) == 0 || length(second_module_import_path) == 0         return false     end     # if one of the import paths is empty, then return false     if first_module_import_path[end] == '.'         first_module_import_path = first_module_import_path[1:end-1]     end     if second_module_import_path[end] == '.'         second_module_import_path = second_module_import_path[1:end-1]     end     # first_chunks and second_chunks are the list of domain packages that each module belongs to.     first_chunks = split(first_module_import_path, '.')     second_chunks = split(second_module_import_path, '.')     # domain packages can only be of length 0, 1 or 2.     # length(first_chunks) must be 1 <= length(first_chunks) <= 2     # length(second_chunks) must be 1 <= length(second_chunks) <= 2     # there are only two valid cases for the domain packages:     # 1. first_chunks is of length 1, in which case it is a domain package itself.     # 2. second_chunks is of length 1, in which case it is a domain package itself.     # 3. first_chunks and second_chunks are of length 2, in which case they are both domain packages.     # the cases 1 and 2 are already covered by this code.     # case 3 is also already covered by this code.     # the only case that is left is when first_chunks and second_chunks are of length 2     # which means that both first_chunks[1] and second_chunks[1] must be the same     # and that there must exist a third domain package     # which is common to both first_chunks and second_chunks     # which in this case will be third_chunks[1]     # note that this implies that first_chunks and second_chunks must be of the same length.     # and that the first domain package is the same for both import paths.     # thus we only need to check whether first_chunks[2] == second_chunks[2]     if length(first_chunks) != length(second_chunks)         return false     end     if first_chunks[1] != second_chunks[1]         return false     end     return first_chunks[2] == second_chunks[2] end

7342:function split_nth(string, count)     # Create an empty list of length equal to the number of chunks     chunks = []     # Get the string length     str_len = length(string)     # Range of the length of the string, with the chunk size as step size     range = 1:count:str_len     # Iterate over the range     for i in range         # Get the next chunk         chunk = string[i:min(i + count - 1, str_len)]         # Add the chunk to the list         push!(chunks, chunk)     end     return chunks end

7375:function predict(hypothesis, example)     # if the number of elements in the example is different     # than the number of elements in the hypothesis, then the     # length of the hypothesis must be one greater than the length     # of the example, since a one-element hypothesis implies a binary     # outcome.     if length(hypothesis) != length(example) + 1         return false     end     # For each element in the example     for element in example         # if the corresponding element in the hypothesis is ?         # or if it is different from the example         if hypothesis[end] == '?' || hypothesis[end] != element             # return false             return false         end         # otherwise, drop the last element from the hypothesis         # and move on to the next element         pop!(hypothesis)     end     # if we are here, all the elements in the example were equal     # to the corresponding elements in the hypothesis, so return true     return true end

7460:function decimal_to_base2(dec)     # Push remainders into stack.     rem_stack = []     while dec > 0         dec, rem = divrem(dec, 2)         push!(rem_stack, rem)     end     # Pop remainders and concat them into binary number string.     bin_num = ""     while !isempty(rem_stack)         bin_num = bin_num * string(pop!(rem_stack))     end     return bin_num end

7514:function default_k_rdm(n_rdm)     # minimum number of subjects is k_rdm. We switch to more groups whenever     # the groups all contain more rdms, e.g. we make 3 groups of 2 instead of     # 2 groups of 3. We follow this scheme until we reach 5 groups of 4.     # From there on this function returns 5 groups forever.     #bootstrapped crossvalidation also uses this function to set k, but scales     #n_rdm to the expected proportion of samples retained when bootstrapping     # (1-np.exp(-1))     if n_rdm < 6         k_rdm = 2     elseif n_rdm < 12         k_rdm = 3     elseif n_rdm < 20         k_rdm = 4     else         k_rdm = 5     end     return k_rdm end
