7540:function quadratic(a, b, c)     discrim = b^2 - 4 * a * c     if discrim < 0         return (false, 0, 0)     end     rootd = discrim^(1/2)     if b < 0         q = -0.5*(b - rootd)     else         q = -0.5*(b + rootd)     end     t0 = q / a     t1 = c / q     if t1 > t0         tmp = t1         t1 = t0         t0 = 1     end     return (true, t0, t1) end

RNA will not be transcribed."     end     #map of nucleotides to complement, accounting for T->U in RNA     #replace key with value will transcribe DNA -> RNA     transcription_map = Dict('C' => 'G',                             'G' => 'C',                             'T' => 'A',                             'A' => 'U')     #Force all seqs to be capitalized     seq = uppercase(seq)     #new_seq will be built by the loop     new_seq = ""     #iterate through seq to generate new_seq     for base in seq         #get replacement complement         complement = transcription_map[base]         #add replacement complement to new_seq         new_seq = string(new_seq, complement)     end     return new_seq end

7621:function unique_paths(rows::Int64, columns::Int64)::Int64     # If there are no rows or columns, there is one path     if rows == 1 || columns == 1         return 1     end     # Otherwise, the answer is the sum of the number of paths to each     # adjacent cell. 7646:function chan_id(access_address)     # Addresses are 24-bit, and the channel ID is 16-bit.     # The high 16 bits of the 24-bit address are zero.     # It's a good idea to take the low-order 16 bits and treat it as a 16-bit number,      # because the bits in the address are actually reversed.     # Combine the high order 16 bits with the low order 16 bits,     # and reverse the bits so the output is a 16-bit number.     return ((access_address & 0xffff0000) >> 16) ⊻ (access_address & 0x0000ffff) end

7648:function order(alpha, p)     # Some initial parameters and checks     x = alpha     if p == 2         return 2     end     if x == 1         return 1     end     if gcd(x, p) != 1         throw(DomainError(alpha, "Element is not invertible modulo p"))     end     # Calculate order     order = 1     while x != 1         x = (x * alpha) % p         order += 1     end     return order end

7675:function _format_line(headers, fields)     # Check that the number of headers and fields are equal.     if length(headers) != length(fields)         throw(ArgumentError("headers and fields should have the same length"))     end     # Build a string by putting each field at the right position.     #   max(0, len(header) - len(field))     #     > 0 if field is wider than the header (eg "is_teacher" vs "t")     #     == 0 if the field is the same width as the header     #     < 0 if the header is wider than the field (eg "username" vs "usr")     return join(         " " * max(0, length(h) - length(f)) * " " * string(f)         for (h, f) in zip(headers, fields)     ) end

7706:function gauss(A)     n = length(A)     for i in 1:n         maxRow = i         for k in i+1:n             if abs(A[k][i]) > abs(A[maxRow][i])                 maxRow = k             end         end         A[i], A[maxRow] = A[maxRow], A[i] # swap rows         for k in i+1:n             c = -A[k][i] / A[i][i]             for j in i:n                 if i == j                     A[k][j] = 0                 else                     A[k][j] += c * A[i][j]                 end             end         end     end     x = fill(0, n)     for i in n:-1:1         x[i] = A[i][end] / A[i][i]         for k in i-1:-1:1             A[k][end] -= A[k][i] * x[i]         end     end     return x end

7717:function merge_successors(strings)     to_remove = Set()     for (i, string) in enumerate(strings)         same_beginnings = filter(x -> startswith(x, string) && x != string, strings)         # count how many different successor letters there are after the following         successors = Set(map(s -> s[length(string)], same_beginnings))         # only merge if there is one successor         # e.g. tak -> taka but not k -> ka/ki         if length(successors) == 1             to_remove = push!(to_remove, i)         end     end     # rebuild the list with only the 'merged' successor strings     merged_strings = [string for (i, string) in enumerate(strings) if i ∉ to_remove]     return merged_strings end

7758:function rotate_inplace(matrix)     rows, cols = length(matrix), length(matrix[1])     for i in 1:div(rows, 2)         for j in 1:div(cols, 2)             t = matrix[i][j]             matrix[i][j] = matrix[rows - j + 1][i]             matrix[rows - j + 1][i] = matrix[rows - i + 1][cols - j + 1]             matrix[rows - i + 1][cols - j + 1] = matrix[j][rows - i + 1]             matrix[j][rows - i + 1] = t         end     end     return nothing end

7774:function deduped_table(table)     tmp_table_1 = copy(table)     # Remove all except the _last_ entries for code points U+2550, U+255E,     # U+2561, U+256A, U+5341, and U+5345.     tmp_table_1 = reverse(tmp_table_1)     tmp_table_2 = []     seen = Set{UInt32}()     for (index, codepoint) in tmp_table_1         if codepoint ∉ seen             if codepoint in [0x2550, 0x255E, 0x2561, 0x256A, 0x5341, 0x5345]                 push!(seen, codepoint)             end             push!(tmp_table_2, (index, codepoint))         end     end     tmp_table_2 = reverse(tmp_table_2)     # For the rest, remove all except the _first_ entries.     new_table = []     seen = Set{UInt32}()     for (index, codepoint) in tmp_table_2         if codepoint ∉ seen             push!(seen, codepoint)             push!(new_table, (index, codepoint))         end     end     new_table end

7782:function redshift_num2str(z::Float64)     # convert to string     z_str = string(z)     # find the decimal point     decimal_point_index = findfirst(x -> x == '.', z_str)[1]     # split the string at decimal point     integer_part = z_str[1:decimal_point_index-1]     decimal_part = z_str[decimal_point_index+1:length(z_str)]     # pad the integer part     if length(integer_part) < 3         integer_part = "0"^(3-length(integer_part)) * integer_part     end     # pad the decimal part     if length(decimal_part) < 3         decimal_part = decimal_part * "0"^(3-length(decimal_part))     end     # create the full string     return "z"*integer_part*"p"*decimal_part end

7858:function is_valid_directed_joint_degree(in_degrees, out_degrees, nkk)     if length(in_degrees) != length(out_degrees)         return false     end     V = Dict{Tuple{Int,Int},Int}()     forbidden = Dict{Tuple{Int,Int},Int}()     for idx in 1:length(in_degrees)         i = in_degrees[idx]         o = out_degrees[idx]         V[(i, 0)] = get(V, (i, 0), 0) + 1         V[(o, 1)] = get(V, (o, 1), 0) + 1         forbidden[(o, i)] = get(forbidden, (o, i), 0) + 1     end     S = Dict{Tuple{Int,Int},Int}()     for k in keys(nkk)         for l in keys(nkk[k])             val = nkk[k][l]             if !isinteger(val)                 return false             elseif val > 0                 S[(k, 1)] = get(S, (k, 1), 0) + val                 S[(l, 0)] = get(S, (l, 0), 0) + val                 # condition 3                 if val + get(forbidden, (k, l), 0) > V[(k, 1)] * V[(l, 0)]                     return false                 end             end         end     end     for s in keys(S)         if !isapprox(S[s] / s[1], V[s])             # condition 2             return false         end     end     # if all conditions abive have been satisfied then the input nkk is     # realizable as a simple graph.     return true end

7969:function replace_last(string, old, new)     # find the index of the first occurrence of old in string and     # the index of its last occurrence     first_occurrence_index = findfirst(old, string)     last_occurrence_index = findlast(old, string)     # return string if old is not found     if isnothing(first_occurrence_index) || isnothing(last_occurrence_index)         return string     end     # return string if old is found at the first or the last     # position     if first_occurrence_index == 1         return string[1:end-length(old)]*new*string[end]     elseif last_occurrence_index == length(string)         return string[1:end-length(old)]*new*string[end]     end     # replace old by new     return string[1:first_occurrence_index-1]*new*string[first_occurrence_index+length(old)-1:end] end

7982:function convert_identifier(identifier)     if split(identifier, ",") |> length |> (x -> x > 1)         return identifier     end     # remove special characters     identifier = replace(identifier, r"[^\w\s\d\.\-\+\(\)]+" => "")     # remove consecutive special characters     identifier = replace(identifier, r"\s+" => " ")     # remove trailing and leading whitespace     identifier = replace(identifier, r"^\s+" => "")     identifier = replace(identifier, r"\s+$" => "")     # remove leading and trailing ( and )     identifier = replace(identifier, r"^\(" => "")     identifier = replace(identifier, r"\)$" => "")     # remove trailing ,     identifier = replace(identifier, r"\s*,\s*$" => "")     # remove trailing .     identifier = replace(identifier, r"\s*\.\s*$" => "")     # remove trailing -     identifier = replace(identifier, r"\s*-\s*$" => "")     # remove trailing +     identifier = replace(identifier, r"\s*\+\s*$" => "")     # remove trailing )     identifier = replace(identifier, r"\s*\)\s*$" => "")     # remove trailing (     identifier = replace(identifier, r"\s*\(\s*$" => "")     if split(identifier, " ") |> length |> (x -> x > 1)         return identifier     end     if split(identifier, "-") |> length |> (x -> x > 1)         first, rest = split(identifier, "-")         try             first = parse(Int, first)             identifier = string(first)         catch             return identifier         end         for el in split(rest, "-")             try                 el = parse(Int, el)                 identifier = string(identifier, "-", el)             catch                 return identifier             end         end         return identifier     end     return identifier end

8028:function build_mapping(triples, entity_path, relation_path)     entity2id = Dict{String, Int}()     relation2id = Dict{String, Int}()     for triple in triples         head, rel, tail = triple[1], triple[2], triple[3]         if head ∉ keys(entity2id)             entity2id[head] = length(entity2id)         end         if tail ∉ keys(entity2id)             entity2id[tail] = length(entity2id)         end         if rel ∉ keys(relation2id)             relation2id[rel] = length(relation2id)         end     end     open(entity_path, "w") do f_e         write(f_e, "$(length(entity2id))\n")         for (entity, idx) in entity2id             write(f_e, "$entity $idx\n")         end     end     open(relation_path, "w") do f_r         write(f_r, "$(length(relation2id))\n")         for (relation, idx) in relation2id             write(f_r, "$relation $idx\n")         end     end     id2entity = Dict{Int, String}()     for (entity, idx) in entity2id         id2entity[idx] = entity     end     id2relation = Dict{Int, String}()     for (relation, idx) in relation2id         id2relation[idx] = relation     end     return entity2id, id2entity, relation2id, id2relation end

8053:function non_repeating_substring(str1::String)::Int64     left_index = 1     right_index = 1     max_length = 0     max_right_index = 0     seen = Dict{Char, Int64}()     while right_index <= length(str1)         character = str1[right_index]         if haskey(seen, character)             left_index = max(left_index, seen[character] + 1)         end         seen[character] = right_index         max_length = max(max_length, right_index - left_index + 1)         max_right_index = max(max_right_index, right_index)         right_index += 1     end     return max_length end

8070:function is_partitioned_line_blank(indent::String, text::String)::Bool     # Solution 1     # 1. Strip the leading indent and the following newline.     # 2. If there's text following the newline, it's not blank.     if length(text) != 0         return false     end     # Solution 2     # 1. Use `strip` to remove the newline character.     # 2. If there's text remaining, it's not blank.     if length(strip(text)) != 0         return false     end     # Solution 3     # 1. Use `rstrip` to remove trailing white space.     # 2. If there's text remaining, it's not blank.     if length(rstrip(text)) != 0         return false     end     # Solution 4     # 1. Use `isempty` to test for empty strings.     # 2. If there's text remaining, it's not blank.     if isempty(text)         return true     end     # Solution 5     # 1. Use `length` to check for non-zero length.     # 2. If there's text remaining, it's not blank.     return length(text) == 0 end

8093:function kepler_parabolic(B)     B0 = B     p = (1/3)*B^3     p0 = 1.0     max_iter = 1000     diff = 10.0     if B0 == 0.0         return 0.0     end     if B0 > 1000.0         return B0 + 0.1 * B0^3     end     for i in 1:max_iter         B1 = B0 - p0 / p         p0 = p         B0 = B1         p = (1/3)*B0^3         diff = abs(B1-B0)         if diff < 1.0e-10             break         end     end     if diff > 1.0e-10         return NaN     end     return B0 + 0.1 * B0^3 end

8175:function compare_sitemaps(latest_sitemap_urls, previous_sitemap_urls) 	# We only need the `loc` attribute for each URL, so we convert all to strings 	# to match the list of URLs in the previous sitemap 	latest_sitemap_urls = map(string, latest_sitemap_urls) 	previous_sitemap_urls = map(string, previous_sitemap_urls) 	# Use the built-in set difference to find the differences 	removed_urls = setdiff(previous_sitemap_urls, latest_sitemap_urls) 	new_urls = setdiff(latest_sitemap_urls, previous_sitemap_urls) 	return [new_urls, removed_urls] end

8188:function returnListWithoutOutliers(data, outlierRange)     data = deepcopy(data)     data = sort(data)     dataPointsBefore = length(data)     Q1 = data[round(Int, dataPointsBefore/4)]     Q3 = data[round(Int, 3*dataPointsBefore/4)]     IQR = Q3 - Q1     lowerFence = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR * outlierRange     upperFence = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR * outlierRange     filteredData = [i for i in data if i >= lowerFence && i <= upperFence]     dataPointsAfter = length(filteredData)     println("Removed $((dataPointsBefore - dataPointsAfter)) outliers")     return filteredData end
8189:function append(base, suffix)     # Do nothing if the base is missing or empty     if base == ""         return base     end     # Return the base string if the suffix is missing or empty     if suffix == ""         return base     end     # Return the original string if the suffix is already present     if occursin(suffix, base)         return base     end     # Append the suffix to the base string     return base * suffix end
8190:function solution(A)   # Read input   n = length(A)   if n==1     return 0   end   if n==2     if A[1] == A[2]       return 1     end     return -1   end   # Precompute the sums for A[0] to A[n-1]   sums = zeros(Float64, n)   sums[1] = A[1]   for i in 2:n     sums[i] = sums[i-1] + A[i]   end   # Find the equilibrium index   for i in 1:n     # Compute the sums of elements to the left and right of A[i].     sum_left  = sums[1]     sum_right = sums[n] - sums[i]     # If both sums are equal, then we have a match!     if sum_left == sum_right       return i     end   end   # No match found   return -1 end

8212:function ce(actual, predicted)     # Check the actual and predicted parameters     if(isempty(actual))         return NaN;     end     if(isempty(predicted))         return NaN;     end     if(typeof(actual) != typeof(predicted))         return NaN;     end     if(isa(actual, AbstractArray) != isa(predicted, AbstractArray))         return NaN;     end     # Compute the classification error     if(isa(actual, AbstractArray) && length(actual) != length(predicted))         return NaN;     end     result = 0.0     for i = 1:length(actual)         if(actual[i] != predicted[i])             result += 1.0         end     end     return result / length(actual) end

8224:function alpha(algorithm_period_return, treasury_period_return, benchmark_period_returns, beta)     return algorithm_period_return - (treasury_period_return + beta * (benchmark_period_returns - treasury_period_return)) # Trading Strategies # ================== # Expectiminimax # --------------- # Expectiminimax is an algorithmic method used to determine the best move in a game. This algorithm is used in computer chess, go, backgammon, and other board games. It was introduced by <NAME> in 1940. It is a recursive algorithm with a time complexity of O(n^2), where n is the number of moves in the game. # # The algorithm is as follows: # # Take an initial state and a depth n. # # If the depth is 0, return the value of the state. # # For each of the possible moves from the given state, perform the following steps: # # If the state resulting from the move is a win, the algorithm returns a positive score for the move. # # If the state resulting from the move is a loss, the algorithm returns a negative score for the move. # # If the state resulting from the move is a draw, the algorithm returns 0 for the move. # # Otherwise, the algorithm recursively calls itself with depth n-1 to find out the best score from that state, and adds that score to the score for the move. # # For example, for n = 3 in the following state diagram: # # # .. image:: ../images/example_expectiminimax_state.png #    :width: 400px #    :alt: Example Expectiminimax State # # # If the algorithm is given to move A, the best move it can make is to move C. The value of this move is (2 + 6) + (7 - 2) = 11. However, if the algorithm is given to move B, it can make moves A and D. Both have a score of (2 + 6) + (7 + 3) = 13, so the best score is 11. # # In the example above, the algorithm is given to move A, the best move it can make is to move C. The value of this move is (2 + 6) + (7 - 2) = 11. # # In the example above, the algorithm is given to move B, the best move it can make is to move A or D. The value of move A is (2 + 6) + (7 + 3) = 13, while the value of move D is (2 + 6) + (7 - 3) = 11. # # The values of moves A and D are the same, so the algorithm makes move C. # # The values of moves B and C are the same, so the algorithm makes move A. # # The values of moves C and A are the same, so the algorithm makes move D. # # The values of moves D and B are the same, so the algorithm makes move B. # # Now that the algorithm has made its move, the resulting state is: # # .. image:: ../images/example_expectiminimax_state_after_move.png #    :width: 400px #    :alt: Example Expectiminimax State After Move # # # At this point, the algorithm has given itself the maximum number of moves it can make (depth = 0), so the value of the state is 10. # # # The Python code for the Expectiminimax algorithm is: # # :: # #     def expectiminimax(state, depth, maxplayer, player): #         if depth == 0: #             return value(state) #         value = -1000 #         for state in possible_states(state, player): #             value = max(value, -expectiminimax(state, depth - 1, -maxplayer, -player)) #         return value # # To determine the best move for a given state, we loop through the possible moves and determine the maximum value of the resulting state. # # The Expectimax algorithm also has a variant called “alphabeta” where the algorithm uses a parameter called alpha to help it find the best move. # # The alpha-beta pruning algorithm is a form of minimax algorithm in which the search is abandoned if at any point the maximum possible value end

8316:function bs_cost(bw, bf, nodes, depth, max_depth, total)     # Base case: full tree is reached.     if depth == max_depth         return total     end     # Recursively evaluate left subtrees.     left_nodes = nodes * bf     left_cost = 0     if left_nodes < bw         left_cost = bs_cost(bw, bf, left_nodes, depth + 1, max_depth, total)     end     # Recursively evaluate right subtrees.     right_nodes = nodes * (bf + 1)     right_cost = 0     if right_nodes < bw         right_cost = bs_cost(bw, bf, right_nodes, depth + 1, max_depth, total)     end     # The cost of a node is the sum of left and right subtrees.     total += max(left_cost, right_cost)     return total end

8331:function substitute(expr, d)     if expr isa Number         return expr     elseif expr isa Parameter         return haskey(d, expr) ? d[expr] : expr     else         op = expr.op         args = map(e -> substitute(e, d), expr.args)         if op isa Add             return foldl((x,y) -> add(x,y), args)         elseif op isa Sub             return foldl((x,y) -> sub(x,y), args)         elseif op isa Mul             return foldl((x,y) -> mul(x,y), args)         elseif op isa Div             return div(args[1], args[2])         elseif op isa Power             return pow(args[1], args[2])         elseif op isa Exponent             return exp(args[1])         elseif op isa Log             return log(args[1])         elseif op isa Abs             return abs(args[1])         elseif op isa Sin             return sin(args[1])         elseif op isa Cos             return cos(args[1])         elseif op isa Sqrt             return sqrt(args[1])         elseif op isa Literal             return literal(args[1])         else             return expr         end     end end

8363:function uniformSegmentAlignment(alignment, subLabelsOut)     @assert length(alignment) == length(subLabelsOut)     alignmentOut = []     numSubLabels = length(subLabelsOut)     for (labelStartTime, labelEndTime, label, subAlignment) in alignment         @assert subAlignment === nothing         durMult = (labelEndTime - labelStartTime) * 1.0 / numSubLabels         subAlignmentOut = []         for subLabelIndex = 1:numSubLabels             startTime =                 Int(round(durMult * (subLabelIndex - 1) + 0.5)) + labelStartTime             endTime = Int(round(durMult * subLabelIndex + 0.5)) + labelStartTime             subAlignmentOut =                 push!(subAlignmentOut, (startTime, endTime, subLabelsOut[subLabelIndex], nothing))         end         push!(alignmentOut, (labelStartTime, labelEndTime, label, subAlignmentOut))     end     return alignmentOut end

8384:function step_lr_generator(step_size, epochs, lr, lr_decay_milestones)   total_steps = epochs * step_size   milestones = zeros(Int64, lr_decay_milestones)   learning_rates = zeros(Float64, lr_decay_milestones)   for i in range(1, lr_decay_milestones)     milestones[i] = Int(total_steps * i / lr_decay_milestones)   end   milestones[end] = total_steps   learning_rates[1] = lr   for i in range(2, lr_decay_milestones)     learning_rates[i] = lr*0.5^(i - 1)   end   return milestones, learning_rates end

8476:function grad_beta_logpdf(p::Float64, alpha::Float64, beta::Float64)::Float64     # gradient of the log-density function of the Beta distribution     # Args:     #   p: A point on the unit interval at which to evaluate the density.     #   alpha: Beta distribution 'success' parameter.     #   beta: Beta distribution 'failure' parameter.     # Returns:     #   out: The gradient of the log-density of the Beta distribution.     # alpha - 1.0     left_term = (alpha - 1.0)     # beta - 1.0     right_term = (beta - 1.0)     # 1.0 - p     one_minus_p = (1.0 - p)     # (alpha - 1.0) / p     left_term /= p     # (beta - 1.0) / (1.0 - p)     right_term /= one_minus_p     # (alpha - 1.0) / p - (beta - 1.0) / (1.0 - p)     out = left_term - right_term     return out end

8567:function lookup_discrete(x, xs, ys)     # Note: We must also handle the last two points.     # Solution: Check if we are at the end. If so, return the final value. Otherwise, check if we are less than the first value. If so, return the first value. Otherwise, return the value associated with the next lower x-coordinate.     # Out-of-range values are the same as the closest endpoint (i.e, no extrapolation is performed).     if x == xs[end]         return ys[end]     elseif x < xs[1]         return ys[1]     elseif x < xs[end]         for index in 1:length(xs)             if x < xs[index]                 return ys[index-1]             end         end     end     return ys[length(ys)] end

8582:function fib(n::Int64)::Int64     if n < 0         return -fib(-n)     end     a, b, p, q = 1, 0, 0, 1     while n > 0         if n % 2 == 0             p, q = (p ^ 2 + q ^ 2), (q ^ 2 + 2 * p * q)             n //= 2         else             a, b = (b * q + a * p + a * q), (b * p + a * q)             n -= 1         end     end     return b end
8583:function calculate_bending_moments_ring(force, r, theta)     if theta == 0         # See http://www.ics.uci.edu/~eppstein/numth/frap.pdf         moment = force * r * r / 2         return moment     elseif theta == pi/2         # See http://www.ics.uci.edu/~eppstein/numth/frap.pdf         moment = force * r * (1 - r) / 2         return moment     elseif theta == pi         # See http://www.ics.uci.edu/~eppstein/numth/frap.pdf         moment = force * r * r / 2         return moment     else         # See http://www.ics.uci.edu/~eppstein/numth/frap.pdf         # and https://www.math.ubc.ca/~israel/SCS/Notes/CurvedSurfaces.pdf         moment = force * r * (1 - cos(theta)) / 2         return moment     end end

8605:function jaccard_similarity(doc1::String, doc2::String)::Float64     # split the words of both documents     words_doc1 = Set(split(lowercase(doc1), ' '))     words_doc2 = Set(split(lowercase(doc2), ' '))     # find the intersection of the words list of doc1 & doc2     intersection = words_doc1 ∩ words_doc2     # find the union of the words list of doc1 & doc2     union = words_doc1 ∪ words_doc2     # Calculate Jaccard similarity score     # using length of intersection set divided by length of union set     return length(intersection) / length(union) end

8615:function square_root(num)     square = 0     guess = 1     while square < num         square = guess * guess         guess = guess + 1     end     if square == num         return guess - 1     end     low = guess - 1     high = guess     while low <= high         mid = (low + high) / 2         square = mid * mid         if square > num             high = mid - 1         elseif square == num             return mid         else             low = mid + 1         end     end     return low - 1 end

8650:function extended_gcd(phi, e)     d = 1     top1 = phi     top2 = phi     while e != 1         k = div(top1, e)         oldTop1 = top1         oldTop2 = top2         top1 = e         top2 = d         e = oldTop1 - k * e         d = oldTop2 - k * d         d = mod(d, phi)     end     return d end

8675:function bigram_similarity(word1::String, word2::String)::Float64   word1 = lowercase(word1)   word2 = lowercase(word2)   word1_length = length(word1)   word2_length = length(word2)   pairs1 = Vector{String}()   pairs2 = Vector{String}()   for i in 1:word1_length     if i == word1_length       continue     end     pairs1 = push!(pairs1, word1[i] * word1[i + 1])   end   for i in 1:word2_length     if i == word2_length       continue     end     pairs2 = push!(pairs2, word2[i] * word2[i + 1])   end   similar = Vector{String}()   for word in pairs1     if word in pairs2       push!(similar, word)     end   end   return float(length(similar)) / float(max(length(pairs1), length(pairs2))) end

8693:function ghc_cc_program_args(cc)     args = String[]     push!(args, "-pgma")     push!(args, cc)     push!(args, "-pgmc")     push!(args, cc)     push!(args, "-pgml")     push!(args, cc)     # Setting -pgm* flags explicitly has the unfortunate side effect     # of resetting any program flags in the GHC settings file. So we     # restore them here. See     # https://ghc.haskell.org/trac/ghc/ticket/7929.     #     # Since GHC 8.8 the semantics of `-optP` have changed and these flags     # are now also forwarded to `cc` via `-Xpreprocessor`, which breaks the     # default flags `-E -undef -traditional`. GHC happens to word split the     # argument to `-pgmP` which allows to pass these flags to `gcc` itself     # as the preprocessor. See     # https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/ghc/issues/17185#note_261599.     push!(args, "-pgmP")     push!(args, cc * " -E -undef -traditional")     push!(args, "-optc-fno-stack-protector")     return args end

8697:function planeNorm(vect1, vect2, vect3)     v1 = [vect1[1] - vect2[1], vect1[2] - vect2[2], vect1[3] - vect2[3]]     v2 = [vect2[1] - vect3[1], vect2[2] - vect3[2], vect2[3] - vect3[3]]     # Take the cross product     normal = [v1[2] * v2[3] - v1[3] * v2[2], v1[3] * v2[1] - v1[1] * v2[3], v1[1] * v2[2] - v1[2] * v2[1]]     # Normalize     length = sqrt(normal[1] * normal[1] + normal[2] * normal[2] + normal[3] * normal[3])     if length < eps()         return [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]     else         return [normal[1] / length, normal[2] / length, normal[3] / length]     end end

8700:function _diff_env(a, b)     # difference of two envs     # returns:     #   (d1, d2)     #       where d1: variables in a but not in b     #       where d2: variables in b but not in a     #     # works by diff'ing sets of (key, value) pairs     #     # note: for efficiency, should return dicts of strings, not char arrays     #     # note: requires that the values are equal for pairs of keys to be considered equal     #       otherwise, dicts are inconsistent     a_keys = Set(keys(a))     b_keys = Set(keys(b))     d1 = Dict{String, String}()     d2 = Dict{String, String}()     for k in a_keys         if !haskey(b, k)             d1[k] = a[k]         end     end     for k in b_keys         if !haskey(a, k)             d2[k] = b[k]         end     end     return (d1, d2) end

8725:function model_trapezoidal_pulses(pileup_time, energy1, energy2, cfg)     # First case:     if pileup_time <= cfg["filter"]["gap"] - cfg["signal"]["rise_time"]         return energy1 + energy2     # Second case:     elseif pileup_time <= cfg["filter"]["gap"]         x = pileup_time + cfg["signal"]["rise_time"] - cfg["filter"]["gap"]         y = x * energy2 / cfg["signal"]["rise_time"]         a = x * y / 2         return energy1 + (energy2 * cfg["filter"]["length"] - a) / cfg["filter"]["length"]     # Third case:     elseif cfg["filter"]["gap"] < pileup_time <= cfg["filter"]["gap"] + cfg["filter"]["length"] - cfg["signal"]["rise_time"]         return energy1 + (cfg["filter"]["length"] + cfg["filter"]["gap"] - pileup_time - 0.5 * cfg["signal"]["rise_time"]) * energy2 / cfg["filter"]["length"]     # Fourth case:     elseif cfg["filter"]["gap"] + cfg["filter"]["length"] - cfg["signal"]["rise_time"] < pileup_time <= cfg["filter"]["gap"] + cfg["filter"]["length"]         x = cfg["filter"]["length"] + cfg["filter"]["gap"] - pileup_time         y = x * energy2 / cfg["signal"]["rise_time"]         return energy1 + x * y * 0.5 / cfg["filter"]["length"]     else         throw(error("Pileup time out of range!"))     end end

8732:function average_accuracy(y_true, y_pred)     # Check if the data is in the correct format.     n = length(y_true)     m = length(y_pred)     if n == 0         throw(ErrorException("Number of true labels cannot be zero."))     elseif n != m         throw(ErrorException("Number of true labels must be equal to number of predicted labels."))     end     # Calculate the number of true positives, true negatives, false positives, and false negatives.     true_positives = sum(y_true .== y_pred)     true_negatives = n - true_positives     false_positives = sum(y_pred .!= y_true)     false_negatives = m - true_positives     # Calculate and return the accuracy.     (true_positives + true_negatives) / (true_positives + true_negatives + false_positives + false_negatives) end

8755:function equals(a, b)     # if the types don't match, return false     if typeof(a) != typeof(b)         return false     end     # if the types match but the values don't, return false     if a != b         return false     end     # if the types and values match, check for special cases     if typeof(a) in [Bool, Missing]         return true     end     if typeof(a) == Dict         # the dict values must be equal, so make a new dict with the         # same keys, but compare each value         keys = collect(keys(a))         values = map(keys) do key             equals(a[key], b[key])         end         return all(values)     end     if typeof(a) == Array         # the array values must be equal, so make a new array with the         # same values, but compare each value         values = map(enumerate(a)) do (index, value)             equals(value, b[index])         end         return all(values)     end     true end

8764:function basicStats(data)   # mean   sum = 0   for val in data     sum += val   end   mean = sum/length(data)   # median   if length(data)%2 == 1     median = data[round(Int, (length(data) + 1)/2)]   else     median = (data[round(Int, length(data)/2)] + data[round(Int, length(data)/2)+1])/2   end   # standard deviation   sum = 0   for val in data     sum += (val - mean)^2   end   std = sqrt(sum/length(data))   # variance   sum = 0   for val in data     sum += (val - mean)^2   end   var = sum/length(data)   # min/max   max = data[1]   min = data[1]   for val in data     if val > max       max = val     end     if val < min       min = val     end   end   return (mean, median, std, var, max, min) end

8831:function jacobi(n, m)     acc = 1     while true         n %= m         if n == 0             return 0         end         while n & 1 == 0             n >>= 1             if (m & 7) ∉ (1, 7)                 acc *= -1             end         end         if n == 1             return acc         end         if n & 3 == 3 && m & 3 == 3             acc *= -1         end         n, m = m, n     end end

8844:function vdowham(eta, vel_entrain, e_eff, r_eff)     # PROBLEM STATEMENT     # Find the velocity parameter for a given velocity of entrainment.     # This is a correction to the constant-velocity approach.     # The velocity parameter is the ratio of velocity and radius of     # entrainment.     # The velocity parameter represents the average velocity of the     # lubricant relative to the entrained fluid.     # The velocity parameter is a function of the radius of entrainment     # and the effective modulus and is used to determine how much of the     # lubricant is entrained in the contact.     # Parameters     # eta: dynamic viscosity of the lubricant     # vel_entrain: the entrainment velocity of the contact problem     # e_eff: the effective modulus of the contact problem     # r_eff: the effective radius of the contact problem     # Calculate the velocity parameter     param_velocity = (eta * vel_entrain / (e_eff * r_eff))     return param_velocity end

8907:function weight_distrib(full, weights)     if full == 0         return Array{Int}(undef, length(weights))     elseif isempty(weights)         return Int[]     end     sw = sum(weights)     fr = full .* weights ./ sw     r, rem = Int[], 0.0     for i in fr         i, lrem = divrem(i, 1.0)         inc, rem = divrem(rem + lrem, 1.0)         push!(r, Int(i + inc))     end     # Rounding errors.     if 0 < rem <= 1 && sum(r) + 1 == full         r[end] += 1     end     return r end

8926:function is_valid_shape(shape)     # special case, if you want a 1D array, then return (1,)     if isnothing(shape) || (shape == ())         return (1,)     end     # special case, if you want a 2D array, then return (1,1)     if shape == (1,)         return (1,1)     end     # else, the shape should be a tuple, with the first element being the length     # the second element being the height     # the third element, if it exists, is the width     # if the third element doesn't exist, it defaults to the second element     # which means you can only have 2D or 3D shapes     if length(shape) == 1         shape = (shape[1], shape[1])     elseif length(shape) == 2         shape = (shape[1], shape[2], shape[2])     end     # make sure that the first element is the length     if shape[1] <= 0         return false     end     # make sure that the second element is the height     if shape[2] <= 0         return false     end     # make sure that the third element, if it exists, is the width     if shape[3] <= 0         return false     end     # make sure that the third element is the same as the second element     if shape[3] != shape[2]         return false     end     # if we made it this far, then it's a valid shape!     return true end

9052:function map_onto_scale(p1, p2, s1, s2, v)     @assert p1 <= p2 "p1, p2 must be specified in ascending order"     @assert s1 <= s2 "s1, s2 must be specified in ascending order"     if p1 == p2         @assert s1 == s2 "s1, s2 must be the same if p1 == p2"         return s1     else         f = (v-p1) / (p2-p1)         r = f * (s2-s1) + s1         return r     end end
9053:function fib_dp_tbl(n::Int64)::Int64     # Base case: 0 and 1 are the only Fibonacci numbers.     if n <= 1         return n     end     # Array to store the Fibonacci numbers so far.     # Note: In Julia, arrays are stored in column-major order,     # so index n starts from the beginning of a row.     # The first row is initialized with 0 and 1.     # Other rows are initialized with zeros.     # For example, in an 8x8 array, row 4 column 2 is the 11th element.     fibs = zeros(Int64, n+1, n+1)     fibs[1,1] = 0     fibs[2,1] = 1     # Fill in the remaining numbers.     for i in 2:n+1         # The first number in each row is the previous row's last number.         fibs[1,i] = 0         # The second number in each row is the previous row's second number.         fibs[2,i] = 1         for j in 3:i             # The rest of each row is the sum of the previous two numbers.             fibs[j,i] = fibs[j-1,i-1] + fibs[j-2,i-1]         end     end     # Return the last number in the last row.     return fibs[n+1, n+1] end

9117:function greedy_hire(lambs)   # Edge case I: we can pay only to the junior.   if lambs < 1     return 0   end   # Edge case II: we can pay only to the first two juniors.   if lambs < 2     return 1   end   # Store payments   payments = [1, 1]   # Hire two juniors.   while true     # Check the rest of sum.     rest = lambs - sum(payments)     # Try to "hire" new henchman, paying him the "minimum".     next = payments[end] + payments[end-1]     # If the next henchman is too much for us to pay.     if next > rest       # Print the result.       return length(payments)     else       # Hire!       push!(payments, next)     end   end end

9135:function abc_q2d(n, m)     D = (4 * n^2 - 1)*(m+n-2)*(m+2*n-3)     A = ((2*n-1)*(m+2*n-2)*(4*n*(m+n-2)+(m-3)*(2*m-1)))/D     B = (-2*(2*n-1)*(m+2*n-3)*(m+2*n-2)*(m+2*n-1)) / D     C = (n*(2*n-3)*(m+2*n-1)*(2*m+2*n-3)) / D     return A, B, C end

9149:function _reduce_xyfp(x, y)     # Right-hand coordinate system with origin at the centre of the field, +x to the left, +y to the top.     # Assuming the field is 1024 mm in diameter     #     #        [0.0, 1024.0]     #         (0.0, 0.0)     #        [1024.0, 0.0]     #     # [y_mm, -x_mm]     #     # Convert xy_mm to xy_fp, where xy_fp is relative to the FP origin     #     # [y_fp, -x_fp]     #     # FP origin is at the centre of the field, aka the +x/+y axes.     # This is unlike the +y axis, which is at the top of the field.     #     # For this reason, we "rotate" the FP so it's +y goes to the top.     # This means we "flip" the FP so it's +x goes to the left.     #     #          [0.0, 1024.0]     #           (0.0, 0.0)     #          [1024.0, 0.0]     #     # [1024.0 -y_mm, x_mm]     #     # Convert xy_fp to xy_mm, where xy_mm is relative to the origin at the centre of the field, aka the origin of the +x/+y axes.     #     # [-x_mm, 1024.0 -y_mm]     #     # Rotate back by 180 deg to get back to the correct orientation.     #     # [-x_mm, y_mm]     #     # (NB: y_mm = 1024.0 - y_fp)     #     # Convert xy_mm back to x and y_mm, which will be relative to the top left of the field, aka the origin of the +y axis.     #     # [x, y]     #     # Note: that we didn't need to do this rotation for the y axis because it's at the top.     a = 1024.0 #mm     return (x/a, y/a) end

9170:function egcd(a, m)     lastremainder, remainder = a % m, m     x, lastx, y, lasty = 0, 1, 1, 0     while remainder != 0         lastremainder, (quotient, remainder) = remainder, divrem(lastremainder, remainder)         x, lastx = lastx - quotient * x, x         y, lasty = lasty - quotient * y, y     end     return lastremainder, lastx * (a < 0 ? -1 : 1), lasty * (m < 0 ? -1 : 1) end

9294:function case_sort(string::String)::String     # code goes here     # uppercase characters go before lowercase characters     # handle case of empty string     if length(string) == 0         return ""     end     # convert to an array of char     char_array = collect(string)     upper_array = Vector{Char}()     lower_array = Vector{Char}()     for char in char_array         if isuppercase(char)             push!(upper_array, char)         elseif islowercase(char)             push!(lower_array, char)         end     end     # sort     upper_array = sort(upper_array)     lower_array = sort(lower_array)     # combine     output_array = Vector{Char}()     for char in char_array         if isuppercase(char)             push!(output_array, upper_array[1])             popfirst!(upper_array)         elseif islowercase(char)             push!(output_array, lower_array[1])             popfirst!(lower_array)         end     end     return join(output_array) end

9350:function sample_labels(model, wkrs, imgs)     n_samples = size(wkrs, 1) * size(imgs, 1)     labels = Vector{Any}(undef, n_samples)     # i is the current index of the labels array, which is the     # linear combination of imgs and wkrs indices, so that     # i = imgs[j] + n_imgs * wkrs[k], where j, k are indices into     # those lists.  imgs and wkrs will be traversed in parallel.     j = 1     k = 1     for i = 1:n_samples         if i > (j-1)*size(imgs,1) + size(wkrs,1)             j += 1             k = 1         end         labels[i] = model.sample_label(wkrs[k], imgs[j])         k += 1     end     return labels end

9357:function district_margins(state_lines)     if isempty(state_lines)         return Dict()     else         # Find indices of the rows containing the state's districts         state_district_rows = findall(x -> !isempty(x["D"]), state_lines)         # Find indices of the rows containing the state's margins         state_margin_rows = findall(x -> !isempty(x["M"]), state_lines)         state_margins = Dict()         # Get the winner and second-place districts for each state         for row_winner in state_district_rows             district_winner = parse(Int, state_lines[row_winner]["D"])             # Find the row containing the second-place districts             row_second = findfirst(state_lines[row_winner+1:end]) do x                 !isempty(x["D"])             end             # Skip if no second-place districts             if isnothing(row_second)                 continue             end             district_second = parse(Int, state_lines[row_second]["D"])             # Get the margin in percentage             margin = parse(Float64, strip(replace(state_lines[row_margin_rows[district_winner]][M], "%" => "")))             # Add the district, if it has a margin of at least 1             if margin > 0                 state_margins[district_winner] = margin - margin_from_winner(district_winner, district_second)             end         end         return state_margins     end end

9384:function min_cost(costs)     n = length(costs)     R = zeros(Int, n)     G = zeros(Int, n)     B = zeros(Int, n)     R[1] = costs[1][1]     G[1] = costs[1][2]     B[1] = costs[1][3]     for i in 2:n         R[i] = min(G[i - 1], B[i - 1]) + costs[i][1]         G[i] = min(R[i - 1], B[i - 1]) + costs[i][2]         B[i] = min(R[i - 1], G[i - 1]) + costs[i][3]     end     return min(R[n], G[n], B[n]) end

9442:function clean_site_name_for_path(site_name::String)::String     # Step 1: Make lowercase     site_name_lower = lowercase(site_name)     # Step 2: Remove leading and trailing spaces     site_name_strip = lstrip(rstrip(site_name_lower))     # Step 3: replace spaces with dashes     site_name_replace_spaces = replace(site_name_strip, r"\s" => "-")     # Step 4: replace & with 'and'     site_name_replace_ampersand = replace(site_name_replace_spaces, r"&" => "and")     # Step 5: replace / with '-'     site_name_replace_slash = replace(site_name_replace_ampersand, r"/" => "-")     # Step 6: replace ( with '-'     site_name_replace_open_paren = replace(site_name_replace_slash, r"\(" => "-")     # Step 7: replace ) with '-'     site_name_replace_close_paren = replace(site_name_replace_open_paren, r"\)" => "-")     # Step 8: replace { with '-'     site_name_replace_open_brace = replace(site_name_replace_close_paren, r"\{" => "-")     # Step 9: replace } with '-'     site_name_replace_close_brace = replace(site_name_replace_open_brace, r"\}" => "-")     # Step 10: return cleaned string     return site_name_replace_close_brace end

9444:function transform_json_from_studio_to_vulcan(studio_json)     vulcan_json = []     for studio_image in studio_json["images"]         vulcan_pred = Dict(             "outputs" => [                 Dict(                     "labels" => Dict(                         "discarded" => [],                         "predicted" => [],                     ),                 ),             ],         )         predicted = []         discarded = []         for (metadata, val) in pairs(studio_image)             if metadata in ["location", "data"]                 vulcan_pred[metadata] = val             end         end         for studio_pred in studio_image["annotated_regions"]             annotation = Dict(                 "label_name" => studio_pred["tags"][1],                 "score" => studio_pred["score"],                 "threshold" => studio_pred["threshold"],             )             if studio_pred["region_type"] == "Box"                 annotation["roi"] = Dict(                     "bbox" => Dict(                         "xmin" => studio_pred["region"]["xmin"],                         "xmax" => studio_pred["region"]["xmax"],                         "ymin" => studio_pred["region"]["ymin"],                         "ymax" => studio_pred["region"]["ymax"],                     ),                 )             end             if annotation["score"] >= annotation["threshold"]                 push!(predicted, annotation)             else                 push!(discarded, annotation)             end         end         # Sort by prediction score of descending order         predicted = sort(predicted, by=x->x["score"], rev=true)         discarded = sort(discarded, by=x->x["score"], rev=true)         vulcan_pred["outputs"][1]["labels"]["predicted"] = predicted         vulcan_pred["outputs"][1]["labels"]["discarded"] = discarded         # Update vulcan json         push!(vulcan_json, vulcan_pred)     end     return vulcan_json end

9470:function jaccard_index_pair_counts(a, b, c)     # Returns jaccard index, where b = number of pairs of elements that are     # clustered in first but not second partition     # c = number of pairs of elements that are clustered in second but not first partition     # d = number of pairs of elements that are clustered in neither partition     # a = number of pairs of elements that are clustered in both partitions     # (a+b+c+d) = number of pairs of elements that are clustered in either partition     if a + b + c != 0         return a / (a + b + c)     else         return 1.0     end end

9485:function iou(box1, box2)     # intersect_x1 = max(box1[0], box2[0])     # intersect_y1 = max(box1[1], box2[1])     # intersect_x2 = min(box1[2], box2[2])     # intersect_y2 = min(box1[3], box2[3])     # intersect_w = max(intersect_x2 - intersect_x1, 0)     # intersect_h = max(intersect_y2 - intersect_y1, 0)     #     # box1_area = (box1[2] - box1[0]) * (box1[3] - box1[1])     # box2_area = (box2[2] - box2[0]) * (box2[3] - box2[1])     #     # return intersect_w * intersect_h / (box1_area + box2_area - intersect_w * intersect_h)     intersect_x1 = max(box1[1], box2[1])     intersect_y1 = max(box1[2], box2[2])     intersect_x2 = min(box1[3], box2[3])     intersect_y2 = min(box1[4], box2[4])     intersect_w = max(intersect_x2 - intersect_x1, 0)     intersect_h = max(intersect_y2 - intersect_y1, 0)     box1_area = (box1[3] - box1[1]) * (box1[4] - box1[2])     box2_area = (box2[3] - box2[1]) * (box2[4] - box2[2])     return intersect_w * intersect_h / (box1_area + box2_area - intersect_w * intersect_h) end

9529:function suzuki_trotter(trotter_order, trotter_steps)     order_slices = []     p1 = p2 = p4 = p5 = 1.0 / (4 - (4 ^ (1.0 / 3)))     p3 = 1.0 - 4 * p1     if trotter_order == 1         order_slices = [(1, 0), (1, 1)]     elseif trotter_order == 2         order_slices = [(0.5, 0), (1, 1), (0.5, 0)]     elseif trotter_order == 3         order_slices = [(7.0 / 24, 0), (2.0 / 3.0, 1), (3.0 / 4.0, 0), (-2.0 / 3.0, 1),                         (-1.0 / 24, 0), (1.0, 1)]     elseif trotter_order == 4         order_slices = [(p5 / 2, 0), (p5, 1), (p5 / 2, 0),                         (p4 / 2, 0), (p4, 1), (p4 / 2, 0),                         (p3 / 2, 0), (p3, 1), (p3 / 2, 0),                         (p2 / 2, 0), (p2, 1), (p2 / 2, 0),                         (p1 / 2, 0), (p1, 1), (p1 / 2, 0)]     else         error("Invalid trotter_order")     end     order_slices = repeat(order_slices, outer=trotter_steps)     return order_slices end

9756:function eec(u, v)     u1 = 1     u2 = 0     u3 = u     v1 = 0     v2 = 1     v3 = v     while v3 != 0         quotient = u3 ÷ v3         tmp1 = u1 - quotient * v1         tmp2 = u2 - quotient * v2         tmp3 = u3 - quotient * v3         (u1, u2, u3) = (v1, v2, v3)         (v1, v2, v3) = (tmp1, tmp2, tmp3)     end     return u3, u1, u2 end

9770:function problem_5_1(n, m, i, j)     # We can only use bitwise operations on integers, so let's convert M to     # an integer.     m = convert(Int, m)     # We use a mask that contains the bits that we want to keep from N.     mask = ((2^j-1) << (j+1)) + (2^i-1)     # We perform the bitwise AND operation on N with the mask to clear the     # bits between i and j.     n = n & mask     # We perform the bitwise OR operation on N with M << i to set the bits     # between i and j to M.     n = n | (m << i)     return n end

9901:function edit_diff(start, goal, limit)     if start == goal         return 0     elseif limit == 0 #stop when reach the limit!         return 1     elseif start == ""         return length(goal)     elseif goal == ""         return length(start)     elseif start[1] == goal[1]         return edit_diff(start[2:end], goal[2:end], limit)     else         add_char = 1 + edit_diff(goal[1:1] * start, goal, limit-1)         remove_char = 1 + edit_diff(start[2:end], goal, limit-1)         substitute_char = 1 + edit_diff(goal[1:1] * start[2:end], goal, limit-1)         return min(add_char, remove_char, substitute_char)     end end

9936:function read_calibration_file(calib_filename)     # if file does not exist, return nothing     if !isfile(calib_filename)         return nothing     end     # get the data level and format     # data level is the first line in the file     # format is the third line in the file     data_level = 0     format = "f32"     open(calib_filename, "r") do f         first_line = readline(f)         data_level = parse(Int32,first_line)         format = readline(f)     end     # if this is a data level 1 file, return nothing     if data_level == 1         return nothing     end     # if this is a data level 2 file, try to read the calibration file     # if it does not exist, return nothing     if data_level == 2         calib_filename = replace(calib_filename,".f32","_cal.f32")         if !isfile(calib_filename)             return nothing         end     end     # if the file exists, return it     return calib_filename end

9941:function compute_iou(bbox0, bboxes0)     ious = Vector{Float64}(undef, length(bboxes0))     for (i, bbox) in enumerate(bboxes0)         cx0, cy0, scale0, _, x0, y0, h0, w0 = bbox0         cx, cy, scale, _, x, y, h, w = bbox         area0 = scale0 * scale0 * h0 * w0         area = scale * scale * h * w         x1 = max(x0, x)         y1 = max(y0, y)         x2 = min(x0 + w0, x + w)         y2 = min(y0 + h0, y + h)         w = x2 - x1         h = y2 - y1         inter_area = max(w, 0) * max(h, 0)         union_area = area0 + area - inter_area         ious[i] = inter_area / union_area     end     return ious end

9952:function skew_area(col, n)     # Skew area: number of elements in the lower-left triangle     # including the diagonal     # Proof: https://stackoverflow.com/a/40673998/128761     # This function returns the area of the lower-left triangle of     # the matrix, excluding the diagonal     # The area of the lower-left triangle including the diagonal     # is 2 * area_of_lower_triangle - the diagonal area     # area_of_lower_triangle = skew_area(col)     # The area of the diagonal = col * (2 * n - col - 1) // 2     # which is equivalent to the area of the lower-left triangle     # without the diagonal     return col * (2 * n - col - 1) // 2 end

9959:function unrationalize(fraction)     # We only need to handle the case of negative numbers,     # the positive case can be handled by converting the fraction     # string to a positive number, and then applying the same     # logic as for the positive case.     if fraction[1] == "-"         # Just negate the whole string         return unrationalize("-" * fraction[2:end])     end     # Split the fraction into its numerator and denominator     numerator, denominator = split(fraction, "/")     # Convert the numerator and denominator to base 10     numerator = parse(BigInt, numerator, base = 10)     denominator = parse(BigInt, denominator, base = 10)     # To find the decimal equivalent of a fraction,     # we can just divide the numerator by the denominator     # and then convert the result to a decimal     decimal = numerator / denominator     # Return the decimal number     return decimal end

9964:function kgtk_lqstring(x)   if (typeof(x) != "string")     return false   end   # First, strip off any trailing '@'   local len = length(x)   if (x[len] == '@')     x = x[1:end-1]     len -= 1   end   # Next, check that it begins with "'".   if (x[1] != '\'')     return false   end   # Next, scan the string for unescaped single quotes.   local count = 1   local i = 2   while (i < len)     local c = x[i]     if (c == '\'')       if ((i < len-1) && (x[i+1] == '\''))         # The string contains an escaped single quote, so skip it.         i += 2         continue       else         # The string is finished, so the character is not escaped.         count += 1         break       end     end     i += 1   end   # If the count is not even, we found an unescaped single quote.   if ((count % 2) != 0)     return true   end   return false end

9966:function calculate_plane_point(plane, point)     @assert length(plane) == 4     @assert length(point) == 3     if point[1] == nothing && point[2] == nothing         x, y = calculate_plane_point(plane, [point[3], 1])         return [x, y, point[3]]     elseif point[2] == nothing && point[3] == nothing         x, y, z = calculate_plane_point(plane, [point[1], 1, 1])         return [x, y, z]     elseif point[1] == nothing         x = -(plane[1]*point[2] + plane[2]*point[3] + plane[4]) / plane[3]         return [x, point[2], point[3]]     elseif point[2] == nothing         y = -(plane[1]*point[1] + plane[2]*point[3] + plane[4]) / plane[3]         return [point[1], y, point[3]]     elseif point[3] == nothing         z = -(plane[1]*point[1] + plane[2]*point[2] + plane[4]) / plane[3]         return [point[1], point[2], z]     end end

10043:function is_anagram(w1, w2)     if length(w1) !== length(w2)         return false     end     # Count letters in w1 and w2     counts1 = Dict{Char,Int}()     counts2 = Dict{Char,Int}()     for c in w1         counts1[c] = get(counts1, c, 0) + 1     end     for c in w2         counts2[c] = get(counts2, c, 0) + 1     end     # Check whether the counts are equal     for (c, count) in counts1         if !haskey(counts2, c)             return false         elseif counts2[c] != count             return false         end     end     # All keys in counts1 were also in counts2, so the words are anagrams     return true end

10063:function id_toa_line(line)     # If the line starts with '#' or 'C', we will skip it     if line[1] == '#' || line[1] == 'C'         return false     end     # If the line starts with 'FORMAT' or 'MODE', we will skip it     if startswith(line, "FORMAT") || startswith(line, "MODE")         return false     end     # split the line into its tokens, separated by whitespace     tokens = split(line)     # If there aren't enough tokens, then this isn't a TOA line     if length(tokens) < 3         return false     end     # If the third token is 5 digits long, then it's probably MJD.     mjd = split(tokens[2], '.')     if length(mjd) == 2 && length(mjd[1]) == 5         return true     end     # Otherwise, we'll say that this is not a TOA line.     return false end

10078:function pkg_version_cmp(left::String, right::String)::Int64     left = strip(left)     right = strip(right)     if length(left) == 0 || length(right) == 0         throw(ErrorException("version numbers cannot be empty"))     end     if left[end] == 'v' || right[end] == 'v'         throw(ErrorException("version numbers cannot have a leading 'v'"))     end     left = replace(left, r"[^0-9\.]" => "")     right = replace(right, r"[^0-9\.]" => "")     left, right = split(left, "."), split(right, ".")     max_length = max(length(left), length(right))     left, right = lpad.(left, max_length, "0"), lpad.(right, max_length, "0")     for i in 1:max_length         l = parse(Int64, left[i])         r = parse(Int64, right[i])         if l < r             return -1         elseif l > r             return 1         end     end     return 0 end
10079:function edges_intersect(a1, a2, b1, b2)     a = Dict(:x=>a2[1] - a1[1], :y=>a2[2] - a1[2])     b = Dict(:x=>b2[1] - b1[1], :y=>b2[2] - b1[2])     u = Dict(:x=>a1[1] - b1[1], :y=>a1[2] - b1[2])     a_dot_b = (b[:y] * a[:x]) - (b[:x] * a[:y])     if a_dot_b == 0         return false     end     b_dot_u = (b[:x] * u[:y]) - (b[:y] * u[:x])     a_dot_u = (a[:x] * u[:y]) - (a[:y] * u[:x])     ua = b_dot_u / a_dot_b     ub = a_dot_u / a_dot_b     return 0 <= ua <= 1 && 0 <= ub <= 1 end

10083:function segment_point_distance_sq(x1, y1, x2, y2, px, py)     pd2 = (x1 - x2)^2 + (y1 - y2)^2     if pd2 == 0         # Points are coincident.         x = x1         y = y2     else         # parameter of closest point on the line         u = ((px - x1) * (x2 - x1) + (py - y1) * (y2 - y1)) / pd2         if u < 0             # off the end             x = x1             y = y1         elseif u > 1.0             # off the end             x = x2             y = y2         else             # interpolate             x = x1 + u * (x2 - x1)             y = y1 + u * (y2 - y1)         end     end     return (x - px)^2 + (y - py)^2 end

10173:function bfs(x, n, res)     # If our stepping number is smaller than the range we can just append it and return     if x <= n         push!(res, x)         return res     end     # The stepping number is divided into 10 parts     number = []     number = split(string(x), "")     # For each of the parts, we create a new stepping number using the range given     # and append it to the queue     q = []     for i in 1:length(number)         val = number[i]         if val == "0"             q.append(x*10 + (val+1))         elseif val == "9"             q.append(x*10 + (val-1))         else             q.append(x*10 + (val+1))             q.append(x*10 + (val-1))         end     end     # We recursively call bfs for each of the stepping numbers in the queue     while q         p = popfirst!(q)         bfs(p, n, res)     end     return res end

10256:function is_power_of_two(value::Int64)::Bool     if value <= 0         return false     end     # If value is a power of two, its highest bit that is set to 1 will toggle to 0 when subtracting 1 because all     # other bits are 0; all other bits will thus be flipped to 1. Therefore, value and (value - 1) don't have any     # bits in common and the bitwise AND will return 0.     # On the other hand, if value is not a power of two, the highest bit set to 1 will not be flipped when subtracting     # 1 and thus, value and (value - 1) will have bits in common and the bitwise AND will not return 0.     # Therefore, if the result is 0, value is a power of two.     return (value & (value - 1)) == 0 end

10263:function fulfillsHairpinRule(s)     bracket_indices = [i for i = 1:length(s) if s[i] in ('(', '[', '{', '<')]     stack = []     stack_last_opening_char = []     last_opening_char = 0     for i in bracket_indices         if s[i] == '('             stack = push!(stack, i)             stack_last_opening_char = push!(stack_last_opening_char, last_opening_char)         elseif s[i] == ')'             if stack_last_opening_char[end] == last_opening_char                 pop!(stack)                 pop!(stack_last_opening_char)             else                 return false             end         elseif s[i] == '['             stack = push!(stack, i)             stack_last_opening_char = push!(stack_last_opening_char, last_opening_char)         elseif s[i] == ']'             if stack_last_opening_char[end] == last_opening_char                 pop!(stack)                 pop!(stack_last_opening_char)             else                 return false             end         elseif s[i] == '{'             stack = push!(stack, i)             stack_last_opening_char = push!(stack_last_opening_char, last_opening_char)         elseif s[i] == '}'             if stack_last_opening_char[end] == last_opening_char                 pop!(stack)                 pop!(stack_last_opening_char)             else                 return false             end         elseif s[i] == '<'             stack = push!(stack, i)             stack_last_opening_char = push!(stack_last_opening_char, last_opening_char)         elseif s[i] == '>'             if stack_last_opening_char[end] == last_opening_char                 pop!(stack)                 pop!(stack_last_opening_char)             else                 return false             end         end         last_opening_char = i     end     if length(stack) > 0         return false     else         return true     end end

10398:function bb_IoU(boxA, boxB)     # determine the (x, y)-coordinates of the intersection rectangle     xA = max(boxA[1], boxB[1])     yA = max(boxA[2], boxB[2])     xB = min(boxA[3], boxB[3])     yB = min(boxA[4], boxB[4])     # compute the area of intersection rectangle     interArea = max(0, xB - xA + 1) * max(0, yB - yA + 1)     # compute the area of both the prediction and ground-truth     # rectangles     boxAArea = (boxA[3] - boxA[1] + 1) * (boxA[4] - boxA[2] + 1)     boxBArea = (boxB[3] - boxB[1] + 1) * (boxB[4] - boxB[2] + 1)     # compute the intersection over union by taking the intersection     # area and dividing it by the sum of prediction + ground-truth     # areas - the interesection area     iou = interArea / float(boxAArea + boxBArea - interArea)     # return the intersection over union value     return iou end

10410:function lengthOfLongestSubstring(s::String)::Int64     # Create an empty hash table to store all the chars and their indices in the string.     char_indices = Dict{Char, Int64}()     # Keep track of the longest substring length     longest = 0     # Keep track of the window start and end indices     window_start = 1     window_end = 1     # Iterate through each character in the string     for letter in s         # Check if the letter is already in the hash table.         if letter ∈ keys(char_indices)             # If so, move the window to the position after the last occurrence of the letter in the string.             window_start = max(window_start, char_indices[letter]+1)         end         # Update the hash table with the current letter and its index in the string.         char_indices[letter] = window_end         # Move the window end forward in the string.         window_end += 1         # Update the length of the longest substring if needed.         longest = max(longest, window_end - window_start)     end     return longest end

10430:function Mc_eta_m1_m2(m1, m2) 	# Mc = (m1*m2)**(3./5.)/(m1+m2)**(1./5.) 	Mc = (m1*m2/3) / (m1+m2) 	# eta = m1*m2/(m1+m2)**2 	eta = (m1*m2) / (m1+m2)^2 	return Mc, eta end
10431:function iou(box1, box2)     x1min, y1min, x1max, y1max = box1[1], box1[2], box1[3], box1[4]     x2min, y2min, x2max, y2max = box2[1], box2[2], box2[3], box2[4]     x1min > x2max && return 0.0     y1min > y2max && return 0.0     x1max < x2min && return 0.0     y1max < y2min && return 0.0     intersection = (min(x1max, x2max) - max(x1min, x2min)) * (min(y1max, y2max) - max(y1min, y2min))     box1area = (x1max - x1min) * (y1max - y1min)     box2area = (x2max - x2min) * (y2max - y2min)     return intersection / (box1area + box2area - intersection) end

10459:function calc_z_dropoff(theta, t_min, t_max)     # if theta > t_max:     #     return 1.0     # else:     #     d = (t_min - t_max) ** 2     #     z_mult = -1 / d * theta ** 2 + 2 * t_max / d * theta + (t_min ** 2 - 2 * t_min * t_max) / d     #     return clamp(z_mult, 0.0, 1.0)     z_mult = 1.0     if theta > t_max         z_mult = 1.0     else         if t_min < theta && theta < t_max             # Apply the following quadratic to get faster falloff closer to the poles:             # y = -1/(min_z - max_z)^2 * x*2 + 2 * max_z / (min_z - max_z) ^2 * x + (min_z^2 - 2 * min_z * max_z) / (min_z - max_z) ^2             d = (t_min - t_max) ^ 2             z_mult = -1 / d * theta ^ 2 + 2 * t_max / d * theta + (t_min ^ 2 - 2 * t_min * t_max) / d         elseif theta < t_min             z_mult = 0.0         end     end     return clamp(z_mult, 0.0, 1.0) end

10534:function calc_reward(p_i, winning_price, n_winning_price, reservation_price, m_consumer)     # If the agents charges a price above reservation price, he comes home with zero.     # If he plays the winning price, he shares the market with the others who played     # the winning price.     # If his price is above the winning price, he also goes home with zero.     if p_i > reservation_price         return 0     elseif p_i == winning_price         return (1 / n_winning_price) * p_i * m_consumer     else         return 0     end end

10555:function rotate_clockwise(shape)     # This solution uses a swapping technique     # When rotate a matrix clockwise, switch the value of each row with the first element and the last element     # And switch the value of each column with the first element and the last element     # Time complexity: O(n^2)     # Space complexity: O(1)     # return reverse(transpose(shape))     # This solution uses four transpositions     # Time complexity: O(n^2)     # Space complexity: O(1)     shape = transpose(shape)     shape = transpose(shape)     shape = transpose(shape)     return transpose(shape) end

10589:function pgnum_from_pgint(pgint) 	# Table of translations from the international pointgroup names 	# to the number. 	# 	# In the table, the keys are the international pointgroup names, 	# and the values are the number of the pointgroup (from 1 to 32). 	# 	# See: http://www.cryst.ehu.es/cgi-bin/cryst/programs/nph-norma?pgint=C1 	# 	# Note that some of the keys are also valid in the International 	# Tables for Crystallography (http://it.iucr.org/A/) where they 	# are named as: 	# 	#   [C1, Ci, Cs, D2, C2v, C4v, C3v, T, O, Th, Oh, D4h, D2h, C4h, D3h, C3h, D6h, C2h, C6h] 	# 	# See: http://it.iucr.org/A/articles/n/notes/2014/12/notes121/index.html 	# 	# The table entries below do not include all these names, because 	# the international names are not used in the International Tables 	# for Crystallography. 	# 	# In the table below, the entries with 2 in them refer to the 	# degenerated pointgroups. 	pgnum_from_pgint = Dict{String, Int64}( 		"C1" => 1, 		"C2" => 3, 		"C2h" => 5, 		"C2v" => 7, 		"C3" => 16, 		"C3h" => 22, 		"C3i" => 17, 		"C3v" => 19, 		"C4" => 9, 		"C4h" => 11, 		"C4v" => 13, 		"C6" => 21, 		"C6h" => 23, 		"C6v" => 25, 		"Ci" => 2, 		"Cs" => 4, 		"D2" => 6, 		"D2d" => 14, 		"D2h" => 8, 		"D3" => 18, 		"D3d" => 20, 		"D3h" => 26, 		"D4" => 12, 		"D4h" => 15, 		"D6" => 24, 		"D6h" => 27, 		"O" => 30, 		"Oh" => 32, 		"S4" => 10, 		"T" => 28, 		"Td" => 31, 		"Th" => 29 	) 	# Check if the input is valid. 	if (pgint in keys(pgnum_from_pgint)) 		pgnum = pgnum_from_pgint[pgint] 		return pgnum 	else 		error("Invalid input, pgint=$pgint.") 	end end

10620:function distance_to_buffer(distance)     # The 1078.599717114 comes from taking the distance from the equator to     # the pole (or other extreme) and dividing by the circumference of the     # Earth (1000km). It is roughly equal to 1000km / (2 * pi * 6378).     #     # The goal here is to take a point with lat/lon and convert it to a     # circle of a given radius. The formula for a circle in Euclidean     # coordinates is:     # x = r * cos(theta)     # y = r * sin(theta)     # Where theta is the angle between the point and the center of the circle.     #     # The Euclidean distance between two points is given by:     # d = sqrt((x1 - x2)^2 + (y1 - y2)^2)     # Which can be written in terms of theta as:     # d = r * theta     #     # Since we are given a radius and distance, we can compute the angle     # between the point and the center of the circle:     # theta = d / r     #     # Since we want to buffer a point with a circle, the formula for the     # buffer is:     # r_buffer = sqrt(d^2 + r^2)     #     # To make this work, we need to convert the theta to a number of pixels.     # We know that 1 pixel = 1 degree (latitude). We can compute the number     # of pixels based on this:     # 1 degree = pi / 180     # 1 pixel = pi / (180 * 6378)     #     # This gives us the equation:     # pixels = d / (pi / (180 * 6378))     theta = distance / 1078.599717114  # km     return round(theta / (pi / (180 * 6378)), digits = 2) end

10631:function _log1_p(log_p::Float64)     # The first branch is for x > 0.5     # The second branch is for x <= 0.5     # for x > 0.5, (1 - exp(-x)) = exp(x) / (1 + exp(x))     # for x <= 0.5, (1 - exp(-x)) = exp(x) / (exp(x) + 1)     return ifelse(log_p > 0, log1p(-exp(log_p)), log_p - log1p(exp(log_p))) end

10634:function n_air(P, T, wavelength)     # convert to SI     P *= 133.322368421     # convert to 1/micron     wavenum = 1000. / wavelength     # refractivity is (n-1)_s for a standard air mixture     refractivity = (8342.13 + 2406030. / (130. - wavenum^2.) + 15997. / (38.9 - wavenum^2.)) * 1e-8     return ((P * refractivity) / 720.775) * ((1. + P * (0.817 - 0.0133 * T) * 1e-6) / (1. + 0.0036610 * T)) end

10686:function f_coupled(state, t, sigma, beta, rho, c_e, c, c_z, tau, S, k1, k2)     x_e, y_e, z_e, x_t, y_t, z_t, X, Y, Z = state  # Unpack state vector     dx_e = sigma * (y_e - x_e) - c_e * (S * x_t + k1)     dy_e = rho * x_e - y_e - x_e * z_e + c_e * (S * y_t + k1)     dz_e = x_e * y_e - beta * z_e     dx_t = sigma * (y_t - x_t) - c * (S * X + k2) - c_e * (S * x_e + k1)     dy_t = rho * x_t - y_t - x_t * z_t + c * (S * Y + k2) + c_e * (S * y_e + k1)     dz_t = x_t * y_t - beta * z_t + c_z * Z     dX = tau * sigma * (Y - X) - c * (x_t + k2)     dY = tau * rho * X - tau * Y - tau * S * X * Z + c * (y_t + k2)     dZ = tau * S * X * Y - tau * beta * Z - c_z * z_t     return dx_e, dy_e, dz_e, dx_t, dy_t, dz_t, dX, dY, dZ end

10690:function bounding_box(points)     # We first need to find the lowest (resp. highest) points, as     # those will be the two extreme points on the rectangle’s     # boundary.     top_left_x, top_left_y = minimum(points)     bot_right_x, bot_right_y = maximum(points)     # We then calculate the center of the rectangle     center_x = (top_left_x + bot_right_x) / 2     center_y = (top_left_y + bot_right_y) / 2     # Finally, we calculate the width and height of the rectangle     width = bot_right_x - top_left_x     height = bot_right_y - top_left_y     # And return the result in a format suitable for drawing     return [center_x, center_y, width, height] end

10734:function getChanceAgreementFromList(l1) # ------------------------- # This function returns the probability that  # the two organisms give the same classification, # given a list L1 of binary classifications. # # L1 is a list of 1s and 0s. # For example, the list [0,0,0,1,1,1]  # corresponds to the categories  # [F,F,F,T,T,T] # # Example: # l1 = [0,0,0,1,1,1] --> categories [F,F,F,T,T,T] # ------------------------- # # We want to get p_e. # # For example, if L1 = [0,0,0,1,1,1] and #                    L2 = [1,1,1,0,0,0], # then p_e is (1/N^2) * sum(n_k1 * n_k2) for k categories (i.e. two in this case, 0 or 1). # # n_k1 is the number of organisms in category k in L1. # n_k2 is the number of organisms in category k in L2. # # For k=0, n_k1 = 3, and n_k2 = 0 # # For k=1, n_k1 = 3, and n_k2 = 3 # # Thus, p_e = (1/N^2) * (3*0 + 3*3) = (1/N^2) * 3 = (1/9) # ------------------------- # # If we want to do this for an arbitrary list of categories, # we need to sum over all k categories. # # Thus, we do this over all k in range(0,len(l1)). # ------------------------- # # Let's write a function that counts the number of zeros in L1. # -------------------------     count_zeros = 0     for j in 1:length(l1)         if l1[j] == 0             count_zeros += 1         end     end # ------------------------- # Let's write a function that counts the number of ones in L1. # -------------------------     count_ones = 0     for j in 1:length(l1)         if l1[j] == 1             count_ones += 1         end     end # ------------------------- # Let's get p_e. # -------------------------     p_e = (1/float(length(l1)^2)) * count_zeros * count_ones     return p_e end

10748:function gcd1(u, v)     shift = 0     while (u & 1) == 0 && (v & 1) == 0         shift += 1         u >>= 1         v >>= 1     end     while (u & 1) == 0         u >>= 1     end     while true         while (v & 0x1) == 0             v >>= 1         end         if u > v             u, v = v, u         end         v -= u         if v == 0             break         end     end     result = u << shift     return result end

10773:function solve_approxDP_static_homo_basic(distance_g, k)     # Use k=2 to simplify the logic.     if k == 2         return solve_approxDP_static_homo_basic_k2(distance_g)     end     # We can now assume k >= 3.     epsilon_g, delta_g = distance_g     # Compute the "best" epsilon and delta.     # For k > 2, this is *almost* always the best.     epsilon_best, delta_best = epsilon_g, delta_g     for i in 2:k         epsilon_best_i, delta_best_i = solve_approxDP_static_homo_basic_k2(distance_g, k=i)         epsilon_best = min(epsilon_best, epsilon_best_i)         delta_best = min(delta_best, delta_best_i)     end     # Return the smallest epsilon and delta that is in the union bound.     # Note that the way we pick the "best" epsilon and delta, we can avoid     # double-counting a region that is already included by the tighter     # epsilon and delta from the k=2 solution.     epsilon_best, delta_best end

10807:function relative_url(url_a::String, url_b::String)::String     parts_a = split(url_a, "/")     url_b, anchor = split(url_b, "#", limit=2)     parts_b = split(url_b, "/")     # remove common left parts     while parts_a != [] && parts_b != [] && parts_a[1] == parts_b[1]         parts_a = parts_a[2:end]         parts_b = parts_b[2:end]     end     # go up as many times as remaining a parts' depth     levels = length(parts_a)     parts_relative = repeat([".."], levels)     push!(parts_relative, parts_b...)     relative = join(parts_relative, "/")     return "$(relative)#$anchor" end

10865:function point_in_polygon(point, polygon)     n = length(polygon)     inside = false     p1 = polygon[1]     x = point[1]     y = point[2]     for i in 2:n         p2 = polygon[i]         if y > min(p1[2], p2[2])             if y ≤ max(p1[2], p2[2])                 if x ≤ max(p1[1], p2[1])                     if p1[2] != p2[2]                         xints = (y - p1[2]) * (p2[1] - p1[1]) / (p2[2] - p1[2]) + p1[1]                     end                     if p1[1] == p2[1] || x ≤ xints                         inside = !inside                     end                 end             end         end         p1 = p2     end     return inside end

10898:function qcollide(Aleft, Aright, Bleft, Bright)     # quickest rejections first;     if Aright < Bleft         return(false)     elseif Aleft > Bright         return(false)     elseif Aleft <= Bright && Aright >= Bright         return(true) # Bright point is within A, collision     elseif Aright >= Bleft && Aleft <= Bleft         return(true) # Bleft point is within A, collision.     elseif Bleft <= Aright && Bright >= Aright         return(true) # Aright point is within B, collision     elseif Bright >= Aleft && Bleft <= Aleft         return(true) # Aleft point is within B, collision.     end     #print "unhandled!"     return(false) end

10903:function get_2D_bounding_box(observations)     # given a set of observations of form [x,y]     # return bounding box as a tuple of the form (x0,y0),(x1,y1)     # note that x0 will be min(x) and y0 will be min(y)     # see: https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#min     # min(x)     x0 = minimum([o[1] for o in observations])     x1 = maximum([o[1] for o in observations])     y0 = minimum([o[2] for o in observations])     y1 = maximum([o[2] for o in observations])     return (x0,y0),(x1,y1) end

10906:function findstringpattern(strings)     stringlength = length(strings)     if stringlength == 0         return ""     end     firststring = strings[1]     if all(firststring == s for s in strings[2:end])         return firststring     end     prefix = ""     while length(strings[1]) != 0 && all(strings[1][1] == s[1] for s in strings[2:end] if length(s) != 0)         prefix = prefix * strings[1][1]         strings = [s[2:end] for s in strings]     end     suffix = ""     while length(strings[1]) != 0 && all(strings[1][end] == s[end] for s in strings[2:end] if length(s) != 0)         suffix = strings[1][end] * suffix         strings = [s[1:end-1] for s in strings]     end     prefix * "*" * suffix end
