17949:function polygon_area(points)     # Check that the number of points is at least 3.     length(points) >= 3 || error("Number of vertices must be at least 3.")     # Initialize the area to be calculated.     area = 0.0     # Store the last point.     q = points[end]     # Loop over the rest of the points.     for p in points         # Calculate the contribution of this point to the area.         area += p[1] * q[2] - p[2] * q[1]         # Store the current point.         q = p     end     return area / 2 end

This is done with a 	# for-loop. 	for grade in grade_list 		length = length + 1 	end 	# Calculate the sum of the grades. 18077:function fdr_cutoff(entries, cutoff)     #first, sort by score in descending order.     sorted_entries = sort(entries, by = x->x["score"], rev=true)     #if a peptide has multiple entries, take the one with the best score     peptides = []     unique_peptide_entries = []     for x in sorted_entries         if x["peptide"] in peptides             push!(unique_peptide_entries, x)         else             push!(peptides, x["peptide"])             push!(unique_peptide_entries, x)         end     end     num_targets = 0     num_decoys = 0     cutoff_index = -1     for i = 1:length(unique_peptide_entries)         entry = unique_peptide_entries[i]         if entry["label"] == -1             num_decoys += 1         elseif entry["label"] == 1             num_targets += 1         end         if num_targets == 0             fdr = 1.0         else             fdr = 1.0*num_decoys/num_targets         end         if fdr <= cutoff             cutoff_index = i         end     end     if cutoff_index == -1         return []     else         return filter(x->x["label"] == 1, unique_peptide_entries[1:cutoff_index])     end end

18185:function convert_LTRB2QUAD(points)     # convert coordinates to [x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, x4, y4]     # https://stackoverflow.com/questions/46462621/how-to-convert-bounding-box-coordinates-from-ltrb-to-xyxy-coordinates     # ltrb = left, top, right, bottom     # quad = [x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, x4, y4]     x1, y1, w, h = points[1], points[2], points[3] - points[1], points[4] - points[2]     x2, y2 = x1 + w, y1     x3, y3 = x1 + w, y1 + h     x4, y4 = x1, y1 + h     return [x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, x4, y4] end

18200:function trapezoid_right(x1, x2, x3, y1, y3)::Float64     if x2 == x1 || x2 > x3         return (x2 - x1) * y1     else         # Find y2 using linear interpolation and calculate the trapezoid area         w = (x3 - x2) / (x3 - x1)         y2 = y1 * w + y3 * (1 - w)         return (x2 - x1) * (y1 + y2) / 2     end end

18236:function lowest_weight(edges)     # empty list for edges, sorted by weight     weight_edges = []     for edge in edges         # append current edge to empty list if the list is empty         if length(weight_edges) == 0             push!(weight_edges, edge)         else             # check to see if edge's weight is less than the first edge in the list             if edge.data["weight"] < weight_edges[1].data["weight"]                 # if it is, replace the first edge with the current edge                 weight_edges[1] = edge             elseif edge.data["weight"] < weight_edges[end].data["weight"]                 # otherwise, if it is less than the last edge in the list, append the current edge                 push!(weight_edges, edge)             else                 # otherwise, find the correct location in the list to insert the edge and insert it there                 insert!(weight_edges, findfirst(x->x.data["weight"] > edge.data["weight"], weight_edges) - 1, edge)             end         end     end     return weight_edges end

18322:function is_tissue_compatible(recv_pra, recv_id, don_id)     # Generate a random float in [0, 1).     f = rand()     # The next few lines are a simple form of feature engineering.     # We use a small amount of bit shifting and bitmasking to convert the ID to a float in [0, 1).     intval = Int(0)     if recv_pra == "High"         intval = (recv_id << 23) | (don_id >> 7)     elseif recv_pra == "Medium"         intval = (recv_id << 17) | (don_id >> 13)     else  # recv_pra == "Low"         intval = (recv_id << 11) | (don_id >> 19)     end     b = intval / (1 << 129 - 1)  # We normalize to [0, 1]     return f <= b end

18344:function calc_score(n_true_positives, n_truth, n_pred)     precision = n_true_positives / max(n_pred, 1e-5)     recall = n_true_positives / max(n_truth, 1e-5)     if precision + recall == 0         fscore = 0     else         fscore = 2* precision * recall / (precision + recall)     end     score = Dict(         "fscore" => fscore,         "precision" => precision,         "recall" => recall,     )     return score end
18345:function segment_point_distance_sq(x1, y1, x2, y2, px, py)     # Calc the dot product of the difference between the two points     # and the vector extending from x1, y1 to x2, y2     u = ((px - x1) * (x2 - x1) + (py - y1) * (y2 - y1))     # If u is less than zero the point is closer to x1, y1 than x2, y2     if u < 0         return ((x1 - px) * (x1 - px) + (y1 - py) * (y1 - py))     end     # Calculate the squared length of the vector x2, y2 extending to the     # point (px, py)     v = (x2 - x1) * (x2 - x1) + (y2 - y1) * (y2 - y1)     # If u is greater than the squared length of the vector, the point is     # closer to x2, y2 than x1, y1     if u > v         return ((x2 - px) * (x2 - px) + (y2 - py) * (y2 - py))     end     # The closest point to (px, py) is between the end points, so calculate     # that distance and return it     return ((x1 + u / v * (x2 - x1) - px) * (x1 + u / v * (x2 - x1) - px) +             (y1 + u / v * (y2 - y1) - py) * (y1 + u / v * (y2 - y1) - py)) end

18354:function reddening_correction_sfd98(extinction_r)   # Compute the reddening values using the SFD98 correction set.   # Parameters   # ----------   # extinction_r : array   #     The uncorrected extinction values in the r-band.   # Returns   # -------   # A_u : array   #     The corrected extinction values in the u-band.   # A_g : array   #     The corrected extinction values in the g-band.   # A_r : array   #     The corrected extinction values in the r-band.   # A_i : array   #     The corrected extinction values in the i-band.   # A_z : array   #     The corrected extinction values in the z-band.   # E_BV = extinction_r / 2.751   # A_u = E_BV * 5.155   # A_g = E_BV * 3.793   # A_r = E_BV * 2.751   # A_i = E_BV * 2.086   # A_z = E_BV * 1.479   # return (A_u, A_g, A_r, A_i, A_z)   return (extinction_r .* (0.9662 + 0.026 * abs.(extinction_r)) ,extinction_r .* (0.9175 + 0.041 * abs.(extinction_r)) ,extinction_r ,extinction_r .* (0.8286 + 0.045 * abs.(extinction_r)) ,extinction_r .* (0.7684 + 0.049 * abs.(extinction_r)) ) end

18361:function bezout(a, b)     r2, r1 = a, b     s2, s1 = 1, 0     t2, t1 = 0, 1     while r1 != 0         q = div(r2, r1)         r2, r1 = r1, r2 - q * r1         s2, s1 = s1, s2 - q * s1         t2, t1 = t1, t2 - q * t1     end     (s2, t2) end

18425:function insert_tag(name::String, tag::String)::String     # if name endswith tag, then we do not need to insert the tag again     if endswith(name,tag)         return name     end     # split the name into parts     name_split = split(name, '/')     # get the last position of the name     last_pos = length(name_split)     # if the last position is empty, then we do not need to insert the tag     if name_split[last_pos] == ""         return name     end     # insert the tag in the right position     name_split[last_pos] = tag * "/" * name_split[last_pos]     return join(name_split, '/') end

18467:function is_interested_source_code_file(afile)     # We only care about source code files that end with one of the following:     # - c     # - cpp     # - pl     # - tmpl     # - py     # - s     # - S     #     # We could just search for a matching suffix, but it's faster to just use the     # endswith() built-in function.     #     # We do not care about:     # - Java files, or any other language, because we aren't interested in Java.     # - The Makefile, as it's not source code.     # - The Makefile.in, as it's not source code.     # - The configure file, as it's not source code.     # - Perl files that aren't CGI scripts, since we're not interested in those.     # - CGI scripts, since we're only interested in the CGI scripts we write.     # - Files that end in any of the following:     #   - y     #   - Y     #   - L     #   - l     #   - l.c     #   - l.cc     #   - l.cpp     #   - l.m     #   - l.s     #   - l.S     #   - l.pl     #   - l.tmpl     #   - l.py     #   - l.s     #   - l.S     #   - l.java     #     # If the file is a C, C++, Perl, template or Python source code file, we return True.     # Otherwise, we return False.     if endswith(afile, ".c") ||         endswith(afile, ".cpp") ||         endswith(afile, ".pl") ||         endswith(afile, ".tmpl") ||         endswith(afile, ".py") ||         endswith(afile, ".s") ||         endswith(afile, ".S")         return true     end     return false end

18501:function get_iou(box1, box2)     # box1_tl, box1_br = box1[:2], box1[2:]     # box2_tl, box2_br = box2[:2], box2[2:]     # box1_x1, box1_y1, box1_x2, box1_y2 = box1_tl[1], box1_tl[2], box1_br[1], box1_br[2]     # box2_x1, box2_y1, box2_x2, box2_y2 = box2_tl[1], box2_tl[2], box2_br[1], box2_br[2]     # x_overlap = max(0, min(box1_x2, box2_x2) - max(box1_x1, box2_x1))     # y_overlap = max(0, min(box1_y2, box2_y2) - max(box1_y1, box2_y1))     # overlap_area = x_overlap * y_overlap     #     # box1_area = (box1_x2 - box1_x1) * (box1_y2 - box1_y1)     # box2_area = (box2_x2 - box2_x1) * (box2_y2 - box2_y1)     # return overlap_area / float(box1_area + box2_area - overlap_area)     # return overlap_area / float(box1_area + box2_area - overlap_area)     # return overlap_area / (box1_area + box2_area - overlap_area)     # return overlap_area / (box1_area + box2_area - overlap_area)     # return overlap_area / (box1_area + box2_area - overlap_area)     xA = max(box1[1], box2[1])     yA = max(box1[2], box2[2])     xB = min(box1[3], box2[3])     yB = min(box1[4], box2[4])     inter_area = max(0, xB - xA + 1) * max(0, yB - yA + 1)     box1_area = (box1[3] - box1[1] + 1) * (box1[4] - box1[2] + 1)     box2_area = (box2[3] - box2[1] + 1) * (box2[4] - box2[2] + 1)     union_area = (box1_area + box2_area) - inter_area     iou = inter_area / union_area     return iou end

18504:function jefferson(votes, seats)     allocated = zeros(length(votes))     for candidate in 1:length(votes)         remaining_seats = seats - sum(allocated)         if remaining_seats < 0             throw(ArgumentError("No seats left!"))         end         # Don't exceed available votes for a given candidate         # even if we have fewer seats than votes.         max_votes_for_candidate = min(votes[candidate], remaining_seats)         # Determine the number of seats to allocate to the current candidate         if max_votes_for_candidate == 0             continue         else             allocated[candidate] = max_votes_for_candidate         end     end     return allocated end

18510:function S_convolute_values(_data_list, _transformer)     #=     Canonical Julia Solution     Returns new data samples where values are transformed by transformer values.     For a more performant solution, see `S_convolute_values_fast`     =#     #=     Canonical Python Solution     Returns new data samples where values are transformed by transformer values.     =#     #=     Returns new data samples where values are transformed by transformer values.     Transformer values and data values must be of the same length. 18579:function B0_rel_diff(v0w, b0w, b1w, v0f, b0f, b1f, config_string, prefact, weight_b0, weight_b1)     # Left BC     if config_string == "w"         b0w_bc = b0w         b1w_bc = b1w     else         b0w_bc = b0w         b1w_bc = b1w     end     # Right BC     if config_string == "f"         b0f_bc = b0f         b1f_bc = b1f     else         b0f_bc = b0f         b1f_bc = b1f     end     if weight_b0 == weight_b1         # If b0 and b1 are evenly weighted, then only the mean is needed         b0_rel_diff = prefact * 2 * (b0w_bc - b0f_bc) / (b0w_bc + b0f_bc)     else         # Else, the mean and the weighted average need to be used         b0_rel_diff = (prefact * 2 * (b0w_bc - b0f_bc) / (b0w_bc + b0f_bc)) + (prefact * 2 * (b1w_bc - b1f_bc) / (b1w_bc + b1f_bc))     end     return b0_rel_diff end

18597:function Sdif(M0, dM0M1, alpha) 	n = size(M0, 1) 	if n == 0 		return 0 	elseif n == 1 		return M0[1] - alpha * dM0M1[1] 	else 		# with genuine iterative methods, we may need more iterations 		# with the gained speed of "naive" unrolled computation 		return Sdif(M0[1:n-1,:], dM0M1[1:n-1,:], alpha) + 			Sdif(M0[2:n,:], dM0M1[2:n,:], alpha) + 			(M0[1] - M1[1]) * (alpha * dM0M1[1]) 	end end

18631:function fib(n::Int64)::Int64     # The first two fibonacci numbers are zero and one.     ret = 1     # This is the recursive case, where we need to recurse a given     # number of times to calculate the final answer.     if n == 0         return 0     end     if n < 2         return ret     end     # Here is the recursive case, where we are calculating the answer     # for a given value of 'n' by calling fib() with one less 'n' value     # to get the two previous fibonacci numbers.     return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2) end

18843:function minimaxDepthTLCovers(tlcovs)     # Canonical Python Solution     # xd = max(min(d_min) for (_,_,d_min,_,_) in tlcovs)     # tlcovs_xd = [(u,k,d_min,d_max,ts) for (u,k,d_min,d_max,ts) in tlcovs if min(d_min) == xd]     # return tlcovs_xd, xd     # Get the maximum of the minimum of the minima depth for the covers     xd = maximum([minimum(d_min) for (u,k,d_min,d_max,ts) in tlcovs])     # Prune the list to only contain covers at this minimum depth     tlcovs_xd = [(u,k,d_min,d_max,ts) for (u,k,d_min,d_max,ts) in tlcovs if minimum(d_min) == xd]     return tlcovs_xd, xd end

18981:function _broadcast(a, b, array1, array2)     # 1-D arrays are already broadcasted     if size(a) == (1,) || size(b) == (1,)         return (array1, array2)     end     # Shapes are incompatible     if size(a) != size(b)         error("The dimensions of the two arrays do not match")     end     # Dimensions match on 2-D arrays     if size(a, 2) == size(b, 2)         return (array1, array2)     end     # Dimensions differ on 2-D arrays     m = size(a, 1)     n = size(b, 1)     # We need to calculate the dimensions of the final result     # and the intermediate matrices that will be used in the      # multiplication     if size(a, 2) > size(b, 2)         intermediate_matrix = Array(Float64, m, size(a, 2))         result_matrix = Array(Float64, m, size(b, 2))     else         intermediate_matrix = Array(Float64, n, size(b, 2))         result_matrix = Array(Float64, n, size(a, 2))     end     # Broadcast a to match the number of rows of b     if size(a, 2) < size(b, 2)         broadcast_a = _broadcast_column(a, size(b, 2))     else         broadcast_a = a     end     # Broadcast b to match the number of columns of a     if size(b, 2) < size(a, 2)         broadcast_b = _broadcast_row(b, size(a, 2))     else         broadcast_b = b     end     # Multiply two matrices     for j in 1:size(b, 2)         intermediate_matrix[:, j] = broadcast_a * broadcast_b[:, j]     end     # Permute dimensions     if size(a, 2) > size(b, 2)         result_matrix = intermediate_matrix'     else         result_matrix = intermediate_matrix     end     # Return the result     return (result_matrix, intermediate_matrix) end

19011:function joint_card(c1, c2)     # We need to return the cardinality of a new term formed from a tuple with cardinality c1 and c2.     # This means finding the cardinality of a new term whose first child is a tuple, and the     # second child is a tuple whose cardinality is equal to c2. The cardinality of the tuple     # can be found by adding together the cardinality of the two components.     # We also need to consider the cardinality of the constant value "1".     # If c1 is (1, M, M, M) or c2 is (1, M, M, M), then the new term will be (1, M, M, M).     # Otherwise, the new term will be (1, 1, M, M).     if c1 == "(1,M,M,M)" || c2 == "(1,M,M,M)"         return c1     else         return "(1,1,M,M)"     end end

19037:function cluster_hierarchically(active_sites)     # Return a single-element list with a list of all given instances     if length(active_sites) == 1         return [active_sites]     end     # Initialize clusterings to empty list     clusterings = []     # Find the best cluster for each instance (i.e., one that maximizes the sum of     # distances between all pairs of instances)     for as in active_sites         distances = [as.distance_to(as2) for as2 in active_sites]         min_distance = minimum(distances)         min_as = active_sites[distances .== min_distance][1]         closest_clustering = find_clustering(min_as, clusterings)         if closest_clustering == nothing             push!(clusterings, [min_as])         else             push!(closest_clustering, min_as)         end     end     # Recursively cluster the clusterings     clusterings = [cluster_hierarchically(clust) for clust in clusterings]     return clusterings end
19038:function getOverlap(a, b)     # Extract the interval start and end times from a and b     aStart, aEnd = a     bStart, bEnd = b     # Ensure aEnd > aStart and bEnd > bStart     if aEnd < aStart         # Swap a and b         a, b = b, a         # Swap aStart and bStart         aStart, bStart = bStart, aStart         # Swap aEnd and bEnd         aEnd, bEnd = bEnd, aEnd     end     # Return the overlap between the two intervals     return max(0, min(aEnd, bEnd) - max(aStart, bStart)) end

19119:function intersection_over_union(box1, box2)     box1_xmin = box1[1]     box1_ymin = box1[2]     box1_xmax = box1[3]     box1_ymax = box1[4]     box2_xmin = box2[1]     box2_ymin = box2[2]     box2_xmax = box2[3]     box2_ymax = box2[4]     # compute the width and height of the bounding box     x_min_max = max(box1_xmin, box2_xmin)     y_min_max = max(box1_ymin, box2_ymin)     x_max_min = min(box1_xmax, box2_xmax)     y_max_min = min(box1_ymax, box2_ymax)     intersection_width = max(0, x_max_min - x_min_max + 1)     intersection_height = max(0, y_max_min - y_min_max + 1)     # compute the area of intersection rectangle     area_intersection = intersection_width * intersection_height     # compute the area of both the prediction and ground-truth     # rectangles     box1_area = (box1_xmax - box1_xmin + 1) * (box1_ymax - box1_ymin + 1)     box2_area = (box2_xmax - box2_xmin + 1) * (box2_ymax - box2_ymin + 1)     # compute the intersection over union by taking the intersection     # area and dividing it by the sum of prediction + ground-truth     # areas - the interesection area     return area_intersection / float(box1_area + box2_area - area_intersection) end

19222:function circle_test_nah(p1, p2, p3, p4)     @assert length(p1) == 2     @assert length(p2) == 2     @assert length(p3) == 2     @assert length(p4) == 2     x1, y1 = p1     x2, y2 = p2     x3, y3 = p3     x4, y4 = p4     # these are the equations of the lines, we want to solve for x and y     den_a = (x2 - x1)*(y3 - y1) - (y2 - y1)*(x3 - x1)     den_b = (x2 - x1)*(y4 - y1) - (y2 - y1)*(x4 - x1)     num_a = (x1 - x3)*(x4 - x3) + (y1 - y3)*(y4 - y3)     num_b = (x1 - x4)*(x2 - x4) + (y1 - y4)*(y2 - y4)     x = (den_a*num_b - den_b*num_a) / (den_a*den_b)     y = (den_a*num_a - den_b*num_b) / (den_a*den_b)     # check that x and y are in the right range     dx = x - x1     dy = y - y1     d2 = dx*dx + dy*dy     if d2 > (x2 - x1)^2         return false     end     d = sqrt(d2)     if d > (x2 - x1)         return false     end     # now we have x and y, we check that the given 4 points are on the circle     # first, we have to find the distance of each point to the circle center     r = sqrt(d2 + (x4 - x)^2 + (y4 - y)^2)     if r > (x4 - x)         return false     end     return true end

19347:function power(x, y)     # we can use @assert for debugging     # @assert is_int(x)     # @assert is_int(y)     # @assert is_positive(x)     # @assert is_positive(y)     # if y < 0     #     x = 1.0 / x     #     y = -y     # while y > 0     #     if y % 2 == 1     #         x = x * x     #     x = x * x     #     y /= 2     # return x     # x = x ^ y     # we can use this technique for inplace computation     result = 1.0     if y < 0         # we can use this technique to modify both         # the variable and the value of the variable         x, y = 1.0 / x, -y     end     while y > 0         if y % 2 == 1             result = result * x         end         x = x * x         y = div(y, 2)     end     return result end

19408:function parcours_zigzag(n) 	x = 0 	y = 0 	l = [] 	for i in 1:n 		l = vcat(l, [(x,y),]) 		if y == 0 			x += 1 		elseif x == n - 1 			y += 1 		elseif y == n - 1 			x -= 1 		elseif x == 0 			y -= 1 		end 	end 	return l end
19409:function copy_letter(letter::String, source::String, target::String)::String     # Convert letter to lower case.     low_letter = lowercase(letter)     # Result of replacing letters.     result = target     # Loop through each letter in source string.     for (idx, value) in enumerate(source)         # If the current letter is the same as the lower case of letter then         # replace it with letter.         if lowercase(value) == low_letter             result = string(result[1:idx], letter, result[idx + 1:end])         end     end     return result end
19410:function generate_graph(width, height)     num_targets = width * height     graph = Dict{Int64, Set{Int64}}()     id_to_coord = Dict{Int64, Tuple{Int64, Int64}}()     coord_to_id = Dict{Tuple{Int64, Int64}, Int64}()     function get_neighbors(i::Int64, j::Int64)         neighbors = Set{Tuple{Int64, Int64}}()         if i > 0             push!(neighbors, (i-1, j))         end         if j > 0             push!(neighbors, (i, j-1))         end         if i < width - 1             push!(neighbors, (i+1, j))         end         if j < height - 1             push!(neighbors, (i, j+1))         end         # assume we can stay at the same cell for multiple rounds         push!(neighbors, (i, j))         return neighbors     end     # create nodes     id = 0     for i in 1:width         for j in 1:height             id_to_coord[id] = (i,j)  # store coordinates for each target id             coord_to_id[(i,j)] = id             graph[id] = Set()             id += 1         end     end     # set neighbors     id = 0     for i in 1:width         for j in 1:height             # go through neighbors             neighbors = get_neighbors(i, j)             for neighbor in neighbors                 push!(graph[id], neighbor)             end             id += 1         end     end     return graph, id_to_coord, coord_to_id end

19427:function compute_prf(tp, fp, fn)     precision = 0     recall = 0     f1 = 0     if tp + fp == 0         precision = 1.0     else         precision = tp / (tp + fp)     end     if tp + fn == 0         recall = 1.0     else         recall = tp / (tp + fn)     end     if precision + recall > 0         f1 = (2 * precision * recall) / (precision + recall)     else         f1 = 0.0     end     return precision, recall, f1 end

19501:function cycle_length(k::Int64)::Int64     # remove factors of 2     while k % 2 == 0         k //= 2     end     # remove factors of 5     while k % 5 == 0         k //= 5     end     if k == 1         return 0  # this is not a repeating decimal     end     # start with x = 10 % k     x = 10 % k     d = 1     # keep increasing x until it repeats     while x != 1         x = (x*10) % k         d += 1     end     return d end

19523:function bubble_sort(array)     # set the length of the array     array_length = length(array)     # loop through the array and sort it     for i = 1:array_length         # set the flag to true         flag = true         # loop through the array again and sort it         for j = 1:array_length - i             # if the current item is greater than the adjacent item, swap the items             if array[j] > array[j + 1]                 # swap the current item with the adjacent item                 array[j], array[j + 1] = array[j + 1], array[j]                 # set the flag to false                 flag = false             end         end         # if the flag is still true, then the array is already sorted and we can break out of the loop         if flag             break         end     end     # return the sorted array     return array end

19655:function _process(proc_data)     # prepares data for indexing     # makes a copy of the list so we don't modify the original list     # prepare the data to be indexed by arxiv ID, we'll sort it later     index_data = deepcopy(proc_data)     for dict in index_data         dict[:id] = dict[:arxiv_id]     end     # create a reference lookup table that stores what paper id corresponds to     # the given paper.     paper_id_lookup = Dict{String,Int64}()     for (i, paper) in enumerate(index_data)         paper_id_lookup[paper[:arxiv_id]] = i     end     # add the citations for each paper and add the paper to the citations of     # the paper it cites. This makes the citations field a 2d vector.     for (i, paper) in enumerate(index_data)         # add paper_id to citations list.         if paper[:id] in paper[:citations]             push!(index_data[i][:citations], paper[:id])         end         # add citations to paper cited by         for cited_by_paper_id in paper[:citations]             if cited_by_paper_id in paper_id_lookup                 push!(index_data[paper_id_lookup[cited_by_paper_id]][:citations], paper[:id])             end         end     end     # add the references for each paper.     for (i, paper) in enumerate(index_data)         # add paper_id to references list.         if paper[:id] in paper[:references]             push!(index_data[i][:references], paper[:id])         end     end     return index_data end
19656:function normalize_range(original_array, original_min, original_max, new_min, new_max)     # Function to normalize data to a new range (e.g. to [-1, 1] or [1, 1])     # original_array:   input array     # original_min: current minimum (array, can be derived from a larger sample)     # original_max: current max (array, can be derived from a larger sample)     # new_min: new minimum (float)     # new_max: new maximum (float)     # normalization_constant = (new_max - new_min) / (original_max - original_min)     # normalized_array = normalization_constant * (original_array - original_min) + new_min     return (new_max - new_min) / (original_max - original_min) * (original_array - original_min) + new_min end

19668:function archimedes(q1, q2, q3) # This is the difference between the lhs and the rhs of the # TripleQuadForumula.  [MF 124 @ 2:23]. # The TQF is satisfied when this is zero. # Given: #     TQF: ((q1 + q2 + q3) ** 2) == (2 * (q1 ** 2 + q2 ** 2 + q3 ** 3)) # Define: #     A(q1, q2, q3) = ((q1 + q2 + q3) ** 2) - (2 * (q1 ** 2 + q2 ** 2 + q3 ** 3)) # Claim: #     A(q1, q2, q3) = 4 * q1 * q2 - (q1 + q2 - q3) ** 2     return 4 * q1 * q2 - (q1 + q2 - q3) ^ 2 end

19729:function _match_url_start(ref, val) 	if isnothing(ref) || isempty(ref) 		# Ref was not provided. 		return true 	end 	if !occursin(r"^https?://", ref) 		ref = "https://" * ref 	end 	# Remove a trailing slash (which is allowed by the spec) from the reference URL 	# and split on slashes into a list. 	ref_parts = strip(ref, ['/', '\\']) 	ref_parts = ref_parts == "" ? [] : split(ref_parts, '/') 	# Remove a trailing slash (which is allowed by the spec) from the value URL 	# and split on slashes into a list. 	val_parts = strip(val, ['/', '\\']) 	val_parts = val_parts == "" ? [] : split(val_parts, '/') 	# Check that the reference URL is a prefix of the value URL (or the value URL is a 	# prefix of the reference URL). 	# We check that the reference URL starts with the value URL by checking that the 	# value URL starts like the reference URL, rather than checking that the value URL 	# is equal to the reference URL. This is because the reference URL may contain 	# a trailing slash (which is allowed by the spec) and the value URL may not. 	# A URL such as "https://example.com/foo" should not match a URL such as 	# "https://example.com/foo/". 	# 	# We check that the value URL starts with the reference URL by using the 	# fact that the value URL can't start with a slash. If it did, then the reference 	# URL would have to start with a slash in order for the value URL to start with 	# the reference URL. 	# 	# Note that in this check, we don't allow the value URL to have more slashes 	# than the reference URL, because the value URL can't start with a slash. This 	# is because the reference URL can't start with a slash, and we don't want to 	# allow the reference URL to have more slashes than the value URL. If the 	# reference URL had more slashes than the value URL, then the reference URL 	# could match the value URL's prefix. 	return all([ref_parts[i] == val_parts[i] for i in 1:length(ref_parts)]) end

19758:function mul(mean1, var1, mean2, var2)     # Errors if variance is negative     if var1 < 0 || var2 < 0         throw(ArgumentError("variances must be non-negative"))     end     # Errors if variance is zero     if var1 == 0 || var2 == 0         throw(ArgumentError("variances must be non-zero"))     end     # If either mean is NaN, return NaN     if isnan(mean1) || isnan(mean2)         return (NaN, NaN)     end     # Return NaN if either variance is NaN     if isnan(var1) || isnan(var2)         return (NaN, NaN)     end     # Compute mean of product and variance     new_mean = (var1 * mean2 + var2 * mean1) / (var1 + var2)     new_var = 1 / (1 / var1 + 1 / var2)     # Return tuple of results     return (new_mean, new_var) end

19823:function _process(proc_data)     res = []     for (i, row) in enumerate(proc_data)         if i > 0             # Note, this is not a valid CSV row, so fields need to be quoted             # before using them as part of another field.             row = string(row)             row = replace(row, "\"" => "\"\"")             row = string("\"\"", row, "\"\"")             # Remove leading and trailing quotes.             row = replace(row, r"^\"|\"$" => "")             # Now, we need to split the quoted fields.             row = replace(row, "\"" => " ")             row = replace(row, r"\s+" => ", ")             row = replace(row, r"^" => "")             row = replace(row, r"$" => "")             row = replace(row, "," => ",")         end         # Set the 'id' field.         row = replace(row, ",id" => ",\"id\"")         row = replace(row, ",id" => ",\"id\"")         # Add the 'id' field.         row = string("id", row)         # Remove the leading and trailing space.         row = replace(row, r"^" => "")         row = replace(row, r"$" => "")         row = replace(row, r"^\s+|\s+$" => "")         # Add a comma before the field names.         row = string(",", row)         # Add the final newline character.         row = string(row, "\n")         push!(res, row)     end     return res end

19892:function compute_rotation_frequency(delta_exponent_b, f_rotation_b, delta_exponent_c, f_rotation_c)     # Code by <NAME>     # Translated by <NAME>     # Original equation in paper by Berti et al. (2010)     # in GBT paper: http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2010A%26A...513A.113B     # with equation from GBT: https://git.ligo.org/lscsoft/GBT/blob/master/gendata/grf.py     # Test case from GBT: https://git.ligo.org/lscsoft/GBT/blob/master/gendata/test_grf.py     return ((f_rotation_c^delta_exponent_c) / (f_rotation_b^delta_exponent_b))^(1/(delta_exponent_c-delta_exponent_b)) end
19893:function max_actions(points, action_cost, recover_cost, limit)     if points <= 0 || limit <= 0 || action_cost <= 0         return 0     end     fire_actions = 0     while fire_actions * action_cost + recover_cost <= points && fire_actions < limit         fire_actions += 1     end     if fire_actions > limit         # Shoots above capacity. Has to reload         # We need to check the number of times the weapon has to reload         reload_shots = fire_actions         if reload_shots > 1             # Adds cost to reload between shots             reload_cost = (reload_shots - 1) * recover_cost             # The cost will be averaged to each shot             reload_cost = reload_cost / reload_shots         else             # A single shot. No reload needed             reload_cost = 0         end         cost = action_cost + reload_cost         fire_actions = 0         while fire_actions * cost <= points && fire_actions < limit             fire_actions += 1         end     end     return fire_actions end

19944:function point_is_under_triangle(x, y, p0, p1, p2)     # Based on:     #    http://www.blackpawn.com/texts/pointinpoly/default.html     #    https://www.geometrictools.com/Documentation/ThePointIsOn.pdf     # Determine whether the vertical line through (x, y, 0) intersects the triangle (p0, p1, p2).     dX = x - p2[1]     dY = y - p2[2]     dX21 = p2[1] - p1[1]     dY12 = p1[2] - p2[2]     # The Barycentric coordinates of (x, y) wrt the triangle.     s = dY12 * dX + dX21 * dY     t = (p2[2] - p0[2]) * dX + (p0[1] - p2[1]) * dY     D = dY12 * (p0[1] - p2[1]) + dX21 * (p0[2] - p2[2])     if D < 0         return s <= 0 && t <= 0 && s + t >= D     end     return s >= 0 && t >= 0 && s + t <= D end

19969:function calc_iou(box1, box2)     x1, y1, x2, y2 = box1     x3, y3, x4, y4 = box2     # area of each box     area_1 = abs(x1 - x2) * abs(y1 - y2)     area_2 = abs(x3 - x4) * abs(y3 - y4)     # get intersection     intersection_x1 = max(x1, x3)     intersection_y1 = max(y1, y3)     intersection_x2 = min(x2, x4)     intersection_y2 = min(y2, y4)     # make sure intersection is not negative     intersection_x1 = max(intersection_x1, 0)     intersection_y1 = max(intersection_y1, 0)     intersection_x2 = max(intersection_x2, 0)     intersection_y2 = max(intersection_y2, 0)     # get intersection area     intersection_area = abs(intersection_x2 - intersection_x1) * abs(intersection_y2 - intersection_y1)     # make sure intersection area is not negative     intersection_area = max(intersection_area, 0)     # get union area     union_area = area_1 + area_2 - intersection_area     # make sure union area is not negative     union_area = max(union_area, 0)     # get intersection over union     iou = intersection_area / union_area     return iou end

20135:function electrolyte_TDF_base_Landesfeind2019(c_e, T, coeffs)     # Electrolyte thermodynamic factor (TDF) of LiPF6 in solvent_X as a function of     # ion concentration and temperature. The data comes from [1].     # References     # ----------     # .. [1] <NAME>. and Gasteiger, H.A., 2019. Temperature and Concentration     # Dependence of the Ionic Transport Properties of Lithium-Ion Battery Electrolytes.     # Journal of The Electrochemical Society, 166(14), pp.A3079-A3097.     # Parameters     # ----------     # c_e: :class:`pybamm.Symbol`     #     Dimensional electrolyte concentration     # T: :class:`pybamm.Symbol`     #     Dimensional temperature     # coeffs: :class:`pybamm.Symbol`     #     Fitting parameter coefficients     # Returns     # -------     # :class:`pybamm.Symbol`     #     Electrolyte thermodynamic factor     p1, p2, p3, p4, p5, p6, p7, p8, p9 = coeffs     return (         p1         + p2 * c_e         + p3 * T         + p4 * c_e^2         + p5 * c_e * T         + p6 * T^2         + p7 * c_e^3         + p8 * c_e^2 * T         + p9 * c_e * T^2     ) end

20179:function get_bit_value(val, place) 	shift = 1 << place #creates a value which is a power of 2 of the number passed in 	#shift moves the bits of the value to the right or left by that amount 	#this is essentially doing a division by 2**place, but in bits and not decimal 	#val & shift does a bitwise and with the value and shift 	#the result will be 0 if the bit is 0 and 1 if the bit is 1 	#we then compare that result to 1 	#this is essentially doing a modulus operation of val by 2**place 	return val & shift != 0 end

20220:function doublef(p, q, n, jp)     @inbounds begin         if jp == nothing             return nothing         end         x1, y1, z1, z1p2, z1p3 = jp         y1p2 = (y1 * y1) % n         a = (4 * x1 * y1p2) % n         b = (3 * x1 * x1 - p * z1p3 * z1) % n         x3 = (b * b - 2 * a) % n         y3 = (b * (a - x3) - 8 * y1p2 * y1p2) % n         z3 = (2 * y1 * z1) % n         z3p2 = (z3 * z3) % n         return x3, y3, z3, z3p2, (z3p2 * z3) % n     end end

20275:function block_renormalization(signal)     # Calculate number of blocks     N = length(signal)     K = 16     # Initialize output signal     output = Array{Float64}(undef, N)     # Calculate number of blocks     Nblocks = N ÷ (K * K)     # Calculate normalization constant     Nconst = K^2     # Loop through blocks     for i in 1:Nblocks         output[K * K * (i - 1) + 1 : K * K * i] .= signal[K * K * (i - 1) + 1 : K * K * i] ./ Nconst     end     return output end

20428:function topological_sort(graph)     # Topological Sorting     no_of_nodes = length(keys(graph))     in_degree = Dict{String, Int}()     for key in keys(graph)         in_degree[key] = 0     end     for neighbors in values(graph)         for neighbor in neighbors             in_degree[neighbor] += 1         end     end     queue = String[]     for key in keys(in_degree)         if in_degree[key] == 0             push!(queue, key)         end     end     sorted_list = String[]     while length(queue) > 0         node = pop!(queue)         push!(sorted_list, node)         for neighbor in graph[node]             in_degree[neighbor] -= 1             if in_degree[neighbor] == 0                 push!(queue, neighbor)             end         end     end     return sorted_list end

20518:function average_precision(ranked_list, ground_truth)     # Compute the number of hits.     n_hits = 0     for index in 1:length(ranked_list)         if ranked_list[index] in ground_truth             n_hits += 1         end     end     if n_hits == 0         return 0     end     # Compute the sum of the precision of the hits.     n_hits_at_k = 0     sum_precs = 0     for index in 1:length(ranked_list)         if ranked_list[index] in ground_truth             n_hits_at_k += 1             sum_precs += n_hits_at_k / index         end     end     return sum_precs / n_hits end

20619:function compareInventory(inventoryint, inventoryext)     # 1. Create a dictionary of just the missing keys from inventoryint (the feed).     # This will be used to find the difference between the two dictionaries.     diff = Dict{String, Int64}()     for k in keys(inventoryint)         if !haskey(inventoryext, k)             diff[k] = -1         end     end     # 2. Create a dictionary of sequence number differences.     # Only keys from inventoryint that are in inventoryext with a different sequence number     # will be stored in this dictionary.     diff_seq = Dict{String, Int64}()     for k in keys(inventoryint)         if haskey(inventoryext, k) && inventoryext[k] != inventoryint[k]             diff_seq[k] = inventoryint[k]         end     end     # 3. Combine the two dictionaries into a single dictionary     merge!(diff, diff_seq)     return diff end

20628:function cross_product(x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2)     # Define the three vectors     v1 = [x1, y1, z1]     v2 = [x2, y2, z2]     # Perform cross product     x = v1[2] * v2[3] - v1[3] * v2[2]     y = v1[3] * v2[1] - v1[1] * v2[3]     z = v1[1] * v2[2] - v1[2] * v2[1]     # Return unit vector     return x, y, z end

20641:function sec_to_exposure_decimation(sec)     deci_millis = round(sec * 100)     deci_s = deci_millis / 1000     deci_m = deci_s / 60     deci_h = deci_m / 60     deci_d = deci_h / 24     deci_mo = deci_d / 30     deci_y = deci_mo / 12     decimation = 1     if deci_y > 10         decimation = round(deci_y)     elseif deci_mo > 10         decimation = round(deci_mo)     elseif deci_d > 10         decimation = round(deci_d)     elseif deci_h > 10         decimation = round(deci_h)     elseif deci_m > 10         decimation = round(deci_m)     elseif deci_s > 10         decimation = round(deci_s)     end     exposure = round(deci_millis / decimation)     return exposure, decimation end

20703:function endian_swap(value)     # shift value to the left by 24 bits (0xff000000)     left_shift_24 = value << 24     # shift value to the right by 8 bits (0x00ff0000)     right_shift_8 = value >> 8     # combine both shifts     combined = left_shift_24 | right_shift_8     # shift value to the right by 8 bits (0x0000ff00)     right_shift_8 = combined >> 8     # combine both shifts     combined = combined | right_shift_8     # shift value to the right by 24 bits (0x000000ff)     right_shift_24 = combined >> 24     # combine both shifts     combined = combined | right_shift_24     # return value     return combined end

20794:function reinterpret_latin1_as_windows1252(wrongtext)     # first, try to parse in the current encoding     try         return convert(String, wrongtext)     catch err         @warn "Unable to parse $wrongtext in current encoding. Falling back to latin1."     end     # latin1 failed, try with UTF8     try         return reinterpret_latin1_as_windows1252(convert(Vector{UInt8}, wrongtext))     catch err         @warn "Unable to parse $wrongtext as latin1. Falling back to UTF8."     end     # UTF8 failed, try with Windows1252     try         return reinterpret_latin1_as_windows1252(String(wrongtext))     catch err         @warn "Unable to parse $wrongtext as UTF8. 20803:function depth_breaks(increment_mm, max_mm)     dd = increment_mm     dmax = max_mm     a = Vector{Int}(undef, 0)     b = Vector{Tuple{Int, Int}}(undef, 0)     for i in range(0, dmax, step = dd)         push!(a, i)     end     # Find positions of values in a that differ from max(a)     # These are the depths to use in the depth range     idx = findall(x -> x != maximum(a), a)     # Loop through the identified depths, and create a tuple     # of each depth range     for i in idx         push!(b, (a[i], a[i+1]))     end     return b end

20811:function XYZ_to_uv76(X, Y, Z)     # denominator = (X + (15 * Y) + (3 * Z))     # if denominator == 0.0:     #     u76, v76 = 0.0, 0.0     # else:     #     u76 = (4 * X) / denominator     #     v76 = (9 * Y) / denominator     # return u76, v76     # u', v' in CIE1976     denominator = (X + (15 * Y) + (3 * Z))     if denominator == 0         u76 = 0.0         v76 = 0.0     else         u76 = (4 * X) / denominator         v76 = (9 * Y) / denominator     end     return u76, v76     # u', v' in CIE1976 end

20819:function damerau_levenshtein(string_1, string_2)     if string_1 == string_2         return 0     end     len_1 = length(string_1)     len_2 = length(string_2)     if len_1 == 0         return len_2     end     if len_2 == 0         return len_1     end     if len_1 > len_2         string_2, string_1 = string_1, string_2         len_2, len_1 = len_1, len_2     end     prev_cost = 0     d0 = Vector{Int}(undef, len_2 + 1)     d1 = Vector{Int}(undef, len_2 + 1)     dprev = copy(d0)     s1 = string_1     s2 = string_2     for i in 1:len_1         d1[1] = i         for j in 1:len_2             cost = d0[j]             if s1[i] != s2[j]                 # substitution                 cost += 1                 # insertion                 x_cost = d1[j] + 1                 if x_cost < cost                     cost = x_cost                 end                 # deletion                 y_cost = d0[j + 1] + 1                 if y_cost < cost                     cost = y_cost                 end                 # transposition                 if i > 1 && j > 1 && s1[i] == s2[j - 1] && s1[i - 1] == s2[j]                     transp_cost = dprev[j - 1] + 1                     if transp_cost < cost                         cost = transp_cost                     end                 end             end             d1[j + 1] = cost         end         dprev, d0, d1 = d0, d1, dprev     end     return d0[end] end

20910:function _lagrange_interpolate_noprime(x, x_s, y_s)     m = length(x_s)     poly = 0.0     for i in 1:m         p = 1.0         for j in 1:m             if i != j                 x_j = x_s[j]                 x_i = x_s[i]                 p *= (x - x_j) / (x_i - x_j)             end         end         poly += p * y_s[i]     end     return poly end

20997:function max_STR_repeats(sequence::String, STR::String)::Int64     # Initialize counter and list of counters     count = 0     counters = [0 for i in 1:length(sequence)]     # Loop through each possible start of sequence     for i in 1:length(sequence)-length(STR)+1         # Check if it is a STR         if sequence[i:i+length(STR)-1] == STR             count += 1             # Update the counters             for j in i:i+length(STR)-1                 counters[j] += 1             end         end     end     # Find the maximum number of repeats     max = 0     for i in counters         if i > max             max = i         end     end     return max end

21045:function reduce_size(clauses)     if isempty(clauses)         return []     end     pos = Set{Int}()     neg = Set{Int}()     for clause in clauses         pos = union(pos, (clause[1] > 0) ? Set{Int}([clause[1]]) : Set{Int}())         neg = union(neg, (clause[1] < 0) ? Set{Int}([-clause[1]]) : Set{Int}())     end     diff = Set{Int}(union(pos, neg))     while !isempty(diff)         i = 1         while i <= length(clauses)             if abs(clauses[i][1]) in diff || abs(clauses[i][2]) in diff                 deleteat!(clauses, i)             else                 i += 1             end         end         pos = Set{Int}()         neg = Set{Int}()         for clause in clauses             pos = union(pos, (clause[1] > 0) ? Set{Int}([clause[1]]) : Set{Int}())             neg = union(neg, (clause[1] < 0) ? Set{Int}([-clause[1]]) : Set{Int}())         end         diff = Set{Int}(union(pos, neg))     end     return clauses end

XXX     # It'd be nice to figure out a more concise way to express     # this.     if docratio >= 0.125 && limitratio <= 0.25         return true     elseif docratio >= 0.0625 && limitratio <= 0.125         return true     elseif docratio >= 0.03125 && limitratio <= 0.0625         return true     elseif docratio >= 0.015625 && limitratio <= 0.03125         return true     elseif docratio >= 0.0078125 && limitratio <= 0.015625         return true     elseif docratio >= 0.00390625 && limitratio <= 0.0078125         return true     elseif docratio >= 0.001953125 && limitratio <= 0.00390625         return true     end     return false end

21183:function sphere_to_plane_car(az0, el0, az, el)     # https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_common_coordinate_transformations#From_spherical_to_planar     # x = azimuth, y = elevation, z = radius     # a = azimuth_0, b = el_0, c = radius_0     # x = a cos b cos c     # y = a cos b sin c     # z = a sin b     x = cos(el0) * cos(az0) * cos(el) + cos(az0) * sin(az) * sin(el)     y = cos(el0) * sin(az0) * cos(el) + sin(az0) * sin(az) * sin(el)     z = sin(el0) * cos(el) - cos(el0) * sin(az0) * sin(el)     return atan.(y, x), atan.(z, sqrt.(x.^2 + y.^2)) end

21255:function escape_bytes(value7_uint64be)     x = value7_uint64be     x0 = UInt64(x & 0x000000000FFFFFFF)     x1 = UInt64(x & 0x00FFFFFFF0000000)     x = x0 | (x1 << 4)     x0 = UInt64(x & 0x00003FFF00003FFF)     x1 = UInt64(x & 0x0FFFC0000FFFC000)     x = x0 | (x1 << 2)     x0 = UInt64(x & 0x007F007F007F007F)     x1 = UInt64(x & 0x3F803F803F803F80)     x = x0 | (x1 << 1) | 0x8080808080808080     return x end
21256:function numbits(num_values::Int64)::Int64     if num_values == 0         return 0     elseif num_values == 1         return 1     end     # the value (num_values - 1) is the number of different values,     # so we need to find the minimum number of bits required to encode this number.     #     # the algorithm is based on binary search. it starts with zero bits and increases     # the number of bits by one bit on each iteration until the number of bits required     # to encode num_values is reached.     #     # we use this algorithm instead of a more common algorithm with logarithmic complexity,     # such as floor(log2(num_values - 1) + 1), because this algorithm requires     # less arithmetic operations.     #     # the number of different values is limited to 2^31 - 1. the algorithm will work     # correctly also for values smaller than this limit (up to 2^31 - 2).     result = 0     while num_values > (1 << result)         result += 1     end     return result end
21257:function project_ecef_vector_onto_basis(x, y, z, xx, xy, xz, yx, yy, yz, zx, zy, zz)     # Project vector in ecef onto different basis     # Parameters     # ----------     # x : float or array-like     #     ECEF-X component of vector     # y : float or array-like     #     ECEF-Y component of vector     # z : float or array-like     #     ECEF-Z component of vector     # xx : float or array-like     #     ECEF-X component of the x unit vector of new basis     # xy : float or array-like     #     ECEF-Y component of the x unit vector of new basis     # xz : float or array-like     #     ECEF-Z component of the x unit vector of new basis     # yx : float or array-like     #     ECEF-X component of the y unit vector of new basis     # yy : float or array-like     #     ECEF-Y component of the y unit vector of new basis     # yz : float or array-like     #     ECEF-Z component of the y unit vector of new basis     # zx : float or array-like     #     ECEF-X component of the z unit vector of new basis     # zy : float or array-like     #     ECEF-Y component of the z unit vector of new basis     # zz : float or array-like     #     ECEF-Z component of the z unit vector of new basis     # Returns     # -------     # x, y, z     #     Vector projected onto new basis     # Canonical Python Solution     # out_x = x*xx + y*xy + z*xz     # out_y = x*yx + y*yy + z*yz     # out_z = x*zx + y*zy + z*zz     # return out_x, out_y, out_z     return x * xx + y * xy + z * xz, x * yx + y * yy + z * yz, x * zx + y * zy + z * zz end

21282:function depth_first_ordering(adjacency, root)     tovisit = [root]     visited = Set()     ordering = []     while length(tovisit) > 0         node = pop!(tovisit)         if node in visited             continue         end         ordering = push!(ordering, node)         visited = union!(visited, [node])         for (key, value) in adjacency             if key == node                 for k in value                     if k in visited                         continue                     end                     push!(tovisit, k)                 end             end         end     end     return ordering end

21289:function filterbox_iou(rec1, rec2)     (tl_x1, tl_y1, tl_x2, tl_y2) = rec1     (br_x1, br_y1, br_x2, br_y2) = rec2     # compute the area of each rectangle     S_rec1 = (tl_x2 - tl_x1) * (tl_y2 - tl_y1)     S_rec2 = (br_x2 - br_x1) * (br_y2 - br_y1)     sum_area = S_rec1 + S_rec2     # compute the sum_area of the intersection     left_line = max(tl_x1, br_x1)     right_line = min(tl_x2, br_x2)     top_line = max(tl_y1, br_y1)     bottom_line = min(tl_y2, br_y2)     # judge if there is an intersect     if left_line >= right_line || top_line >= bottom_line         return 0     else         intersect = (right_line - left_line) * (bottom_line - top_line)         return intersect / (sum_area - intersect)     end end

21393:function quadratic_interp(a, f, x)     if length(a) != 3 || length(f) != 3         error("Incorrect array lengths for quadratic interpolation")     end     a1 = a[1]     a2 = a[2]     a3 = a[3]     f1 = f[1]     f2 = f[2]     f3 = f[3]     answer = (x-a2)*(x-a3)/(a1-a2)/(a1-a3) * f1     answer += (x-a1)*(x-a3)/(a2-a1)/(a2-a3) * f2     answer += (x-a1)*(x-a2)/(a3-a1)/(a3-a2) * f3     return answer end

21421:function get_iou(bb1, bb2)     # determine the coordinates of the intersection rectangle     x_left = max(bb1["x1"], bb2["x1"])     y_top = max(bb1["y1"], bb2["y1"])     x_right = min(bb1["x2"], bb2["x2"])     y_bottom = min(bb1["y2"], bb2["y2"])     if x_right < x_left || y_bottom < y_top         return 0.0     end     # The intersection of two axis-aligned bounding boxes is always an     # axis-aligned bounding box     intersection_area = (x_right - x_left) * (y_bottom - y_top)     # compute the area of both AABBs     bb1_area = (bb1["x2"] - bb1["x1"]) * (bb1["y2"] - bb1["y1"])     bb2_area = (bb2["x2"] - bb2["x1"]) * (bb2["y2"] - bb2["y1"])     # compute the intersection over union by taking the intersection     # area and dividing it by the sum of prediction + ground-truth     # areas - the interesection area     iou = intersection_area / (bb1_area + bb2_area - intersection_area)     if iou >= 0.0 || iou <= 1.0         return iou     else         return 0.0     end end

21459:function haversine(lon1, lat1, lon2, lat2)     # convert decimal degrees to radians      lon1, lat1, lon2, lat2 = map(rad2deg, [lon1, lat1, lon2, lat2])     # haversine formula      dlon = lon2 - lon1      dlat = lat2 - lat1      a = sin(dlat/2)^2 + cos(lat1) * cos(lat2) * sin(dlon/2)^2     c = 2 * asin(sqrt(a))      r = 6371 # Radius of earth in kilometers. Use 3956 for miles     return c * r end

21551:function is_almost_right(a, b, c)     # Make sure a is the longest side     # because we'll need to know the lengths     # of the other two sides later     if a > b         a, b = b, a     end     if a > c         a, c = c, a     end     if b > c         b, c = c, b     end     # Compare b^2 + c^2 to a^2     if abs(b^2 + c^2 - a^2) < 1e-12         return true     end     # Compare a^2 + c^2 to b^2     if abs(a^2 + c^2 - b^2) < 1e-12         return true     end     # Compare a^2 + b^2 to c^2     if abs(a^2 + b^2 - c^2) < 1e-12         return true     end     return false end

21588:function bb_iou(boxA, boxB) 	x1A = max(boxA[1], boxB[1]) 	y1A = max(boxA[2], boxB[2]) 	x2A = min(boxA[3], boxB[3]) 	y2A = min(boxA[4], boxB[4]) 	x1B = max(boxA[1], boxB[1]) 	y1B = max(boxA[2], boxB[2]) 	x2B = min(boxA[3], boxB[3]) 	y2B = min(boxA[4], boxB[4]) 	interArea = max(0, x2A - x1A + 1) * max(0, y2A - y1A + 1) 	boxAArea = (boxA[3] - boxA[1] + 1) * (boxA[4] - boxA[2] + 1) 	boxBArea = (boxB[3] - boxB[1] + 1) * (boxB[4] - boxB[2] + 1) 	iou = interArea / (boxAArea + boxBArea - interArea) 	return iou end

21655:function popcount(x)     # the number of set bits in a 64-bit integer     # (the hamming weight of `x`)     x = x - ((x >> 1) & 0x5555555555555555)     # count the number of set bits in the low half of `x`     x = (x & 0x3333333333333333) + ((x >> 2) & 0x3333333333333333)     # count the number of set bits in the low half of `x`     x = (x + (x >> 4)) & 0x0f0f0f0f0f0f0f0f     # count the number of set bits in the low half of `x`     x = x + (x >> 8)     # count the number of set bits in the low half of `x`     x = x + (x >> 16)     # return the total number of bits in `x`     return x & 0x7f end

21670:function isPower2(n)     # Base 2 is binary number system, 2^0 is 1, 2^1 is 2 and so on.     # So for a number to be a power of 2, the only allowed binary     # representation is 1 followed by 0s.     # In the above example 101 is the binary representation of 5.     # All power of 2 numbers will have a binary representation of the form 100...0.     # The rightmost bit of the binary representation of the number is always 1.     # So we can get the rightmost bit of the binary representation of the number by doing a     # bitwise AND operation with the number and the number - 1.     # If the result is 0, then we know that the number is a power of 2, because in this case     # the only allowed binary representation is 1 followed by 0s.     # If the result is not 0, then we know that the number is not a power of 2, because in this case     # the only allowed binary representation is 1 followed by a sequence of 1s.     return ((n & (n - 1)) == 0) && n > 0 end

21688:function sort_and_count_split_inversions(left, right)     inversions = 0     result = []     while length(left) > 0 || length(right) > 0         if length(left) > 0 && length(right) > 0             if left[1] <= right[1]                 push!(result, left[1])                 left = left[2:end]             else                 push!(result, right[1])                 right = right[2:end]                 inversions += length(left)             end         elseif length(left) > 0             push!(result, left[1])             left = left[2:end]         else             push!(result, right[1])             right = right[2:end]         end     end     return [result, inversions] end

21749:function calculate_same_padding(kernel_size, dilation, stride)     # Why is this necessary?  The simple calculation:     #     return ((stride - 1) + dilation * (kernel_size - 1)) // 2     # is not correct.     #     # Explanation:     #     # If the kernel size is even and the dilation is odd, we want to pad only on one side.  That's why we add a     # half-dilation to the stride before dividing by two.  If the kernel size is odd and the dilation is even, we     # want to pad equally on both sides.  That's why we subtract a half-dilation from the stride before dividing by     # two.     if (kernel_size % 2 == 0 && dilation % 2 == 1) || (kernel_size % 2 == 1 && dilation % 2 == 0)         half_dilation = (dilation - 1) ÷ 2     else         half_dilation = 0     end     padding = ((stride - 1) + half_dilation + dilation * (kernel_size - 1)) ÷ 2     return padding end

21851:function calculate_ir(p, q, vr, vj)     @assert length(p) == length(q)     @assert length(vr) == length(vj)     length(vr) == 1 || length(vr) == length(p)     length(vj) == 1 || length(vj) == length(q)     if length(vr) == 1 && length(vj) == 1         ir = (q * vj + p * vr) / (vj^2 + vr^2)         return ir     else         # Calculate the ir vector         ir = zeros(length(vr))         for i in eachindex(vr)             ir[i] = (q[i] * vj[i] + p[i] * vr[i]) / (vj[i]^2 + vr[i]^2)         end         return ir     end end

21858:function roman_to_num(string) 	#define a dictionary of roman numerals and the corresponding values in arabic numerals 	roman_dic = Dict('I' => 1, 'V' => 5, 'X' => 10, 'L' => 50, 'C' => 100, 'D' => 500, 'M' => 1000) 	#keep a running total of the values 	total = 0 	for i in 1:length(string)-1 #loop through the string, keeping the index 		if string[i] in keys(roman_dic) && string[i+1] in keys(roman_dic) #if the next two values are roman numerals 			if roman_dic[string[i]] < roman_dic[string[i+1]] #if the first value is smaller than the second 				total -= roman_dic[string[i]] #subtract the first value from the total 			else #if the first value is larger than the second 				total += roman_dic[string[i]] #add the first value to the total 			end 		end 	end 	total += roman_dic[string[end]] #add the last value in the string to the total 	return total #return the total end
21859:function temp_depression(ua_per_ft2, balance_point, outdoor_temp, doors_open)     # Assumptions:     # * Bedrooms are adjacent to the main space     # * The main space is heated directly by the heating system     # * There is no heat loss from the building envelope to the bedrooms     # r_to_bedroom = 0.424 if doors_open else 1.42     # temp_delta = balance_point - outdoor_temp     # temp_depress = temp_delta * r_to_bedroom / (r_to_bedroom + 1.0/ua_per_ft2)     # return temp_depress     # r_to_bedroom = 1.42 * doors_open + 0.424 * (1-doors_open)     # temp_delta = balance_point - outdoor_temp     # temp_depress = temp_delta * r_to_bedroom / (r_to_bedroom + 1.0/ua_per_ft2)     # return temp_depress     r_to_bedroom = (1.42 * doors_open + 0.424 * (1 - doors_open)) * (0.424 / 1.42)     temp_delta = balance_point - outdoor_temp     temp_depress = temp_delta * r_to_bedroom / (r_to_bedroom + 1.0 / ua_per_ft2)     return temp_depress end

21919:function build_tos(precedence::Int64, lowdelay::Bool, throughput::Bool, reliability::Bool, lowcost::Bool)::Int64     # ensure that precedence is in the valid range [0b000, 0b111]     precedence = min(max(precedence, 0), 0b111)     # shift the precedence 4 bits to the left     precedence <<= 4     # bitwise OR the precedence with lowdelay, throughputs, reliabilities, and lowcost     tos = precedence | (Int64(lowdelay) << 3) | (Int64(throughput) << 2) | (Int64(reliability) << 1) | (Int64(lowcost))     return tos end

21925:function karatsuba(a, b, n)     # Handle simple cases.     if n == 1         return [a[1]*b[1], 0]     end     # Break into half.     n2 = n >> 1     a0 = a[1:n2]     a1 = a[n2+1:n]     b0 = b[1:n2]     b1 = b[n2+1:n]     ax = [a0[i]+a1[i] for i in 1:n2]     bx = [b0[i]+b1[i] for i in 1:n2]     # Calculate products.     a0b0 = karatsuba(a0, b0, n2)     a1b1 = karatsuba(a1, b1, n2)     axbx = karatsuba(ax, bx, n2)     # Accumulate products.     for i in 1:n         axbx[i] -= (a0b0[i] + a1b1[i])     end     ab = [0 for _ in 1:n*2]     for i in 1:n         ab[i] += a0b0[i]         ab[i+n] += a1b1[i]         ab[i+n2] += axbx[i]     end     return ab end

21964:function validate_PEM(cert::String)::Bool     # Trust that the certificate is formatted correctly     # We need it to be formatted correctly, since our goal is to check its validity.     # First, check that the certificate begins with '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----' and ends with '-----END CERTIFICATE-----'     # We'll check these manually.  We won't use any regular expressions.     startsWith = startswith(cert, "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n")     endsWith = endswith(cert, "\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----")     if !startsWith || !endsWith         return false     end     # We'll also need to check that the certificate begins and ends with a newline.     # The end check may be handled by the 'endsWith' check, but the start check requires     # a bit more.  We'll check that it's not the first and last characters of the string.     startsWithNewline = length(cert) > 1 && cert[1] == '\n'     endsWithNewline = length(cert) > 1 && cert[end] == '\n'     return startsWithNewline && endsWithNewline end

22030:function as_snake_case(text::String)::String     output = ""     for i in eachindex(text)         char = text[i]         if char == 'I' && i != 1 && text[i-1] == 'D'             # preserve _id             continue         end         if char == 'D' && i != 1 && text[i-1] == 'I'             # preserve _id             continue         end         if isuppercase(char) && i != 1             # preserve _id             if !(char == 'D' && text[i-1] == 'I')                 output *= "_"             end         end         output *= lowercase(char)     end     return output end

22067:function christmas_log(ingredients::String, mix::Int64)::String 	# Your code here 	split_ingredients = split(ingredients, " ") 	# Running through the ingredients and add them to a new array 	# using the length of the array as the index so that the 	# ingredients are added in the correct order 	new_ingredients = String[] 	for i in 1:length(split_ingredients) 		push!(new_ingredients, split_ingredients[i]) 	end 	# Now we are going to add the ingredients to the log 	for i in 1:mix 		# Take the last ingredient and add it to the top of the log 		# Also remove it from the array 		push!(new_ingredients, pop!(new_ingredients)) 	end 	# Now we have added the ingredients to the log in the 	# correct order, we can simply return them joined by spaces 	return join(new_ingredients, " ") end

22220:function bb_intersection_over_union(box_a, box_b)     # determine the (x, y)-coordinates of the intersection rectangle     xA = max(box_a[1], box_b[1])     yA = max(box_a[2], box_b[2])     xB = min(box_a[3], box_b[3])     yB = min(box_a[4], box_b[4])     # compute the area of intersection rectangle     inter_area = max(0, xB - xA + 1) * max(0, yB - yA + 1)     # compute the area of both the prediction and ground-truth     # rectangles     bbox_a_area = (box_a[3] - box_a[1] + 1) * (box_a[4] - box_a[2] + 1)     bbox_b_area = (box_b[3] - box_b[1] + 1) * (box_b[4] - box_b[2] + 1)     # compute the intersection over union by taking the intersection     # area and dividing it by the sum of prediction + ground-truth     # areas - the interesection area     iou = inter_area / float(bbox_a_area + bbox_b_area - inter_area)     # return the intersection over union value     return iou # ### **5.2.2 Intersection over Union (IoU) Loss** # # Next, we will define a loss function to train our object detector. IoU Loss is used for multi-class object detection problems. In this problem we have two classes, so we are interested in the intersection over the union of our predicted bounding box and ground-truth bounding box. The smaller this value is, the better our prediction is. We will use the focal loss for this. # # # ![](https://github.com/aditya270520/100DaysofDeepLearning/blob/main/Images/IoULoss.PNG?raw=true) # # # # 1. The IoU is the intersection over the union (IOU) of two boxes. The IOU ranges from zero to one, where zero means that there is no overlap and one means that the two boxes are exactly the same. # 2. We have two bounding boxes: A and B. # 3. The area of A is A' and the area of B is B'. # 4. The union of the two boxes is the area of the two boxes combined, U = A' + B' # 5. Intersection of the two boxes is the area where the boxes overlap, I = A' * B' # 6. The IOU is calculated as # 7. IOU = I / U = (A' * B') / (A' + B') # # # # If A is the ground-truth box, then we want our IOU to be 100% since it exactly matches the ground-truth. If it's the prediction, then we want it to be as close to 1 as possible. To do this, we will take the logarithm of the IOU, which will give us a number between -∞ and 0. This number is then multiplied by the ground-truth class, which is 1 for our ground-truth box, and 0 for our prediction. This number is then multiplied by α, which is a weight that adjusts the relative contribution of the positive and negative examples. α is typically set to 0.25. # # # ![](https://github.com/aditya270520/100DaysofDeepLearning/blob/main/Images/FocalLoss.PNG?raw=true) # # # # The Focal Loss is implemented in TensorFlow as: # # # # ```python # def focal_loss(y_true, y_pred, alpha=0.25, gamma=2.0): # 	 # 	# compute the focal loss for each entry # 	losses = K.binary_crossentropy(y_true, y_pred) # 	# apply the alpha weight to the loss for positive examples # 	alpha_weight = alpha * K.ones_like(losses) # 	alpha_weight *= (1 - y_true) # 	# apply the negative weights # 	alpha_weight *= K.pow((1 - y_pred), gamma) # 	# compute the end

22259:function compare_version_part(a_part, b_part)     if a_part == "" && b_part == ""         return 0     elseif a_part == ""         return 1     elseif b_part == ""         return -1     end     try         a_bits = split(a_part, "-")         b_bits = split(b_part, "-")         version_difference = parse(Int, a_bits[1]) - parse(Int, b_bits[1])         if version_difference != 0 || (length(a_bits) == 1 && length(b_bits) == 1)             return version_difference         end         if length(a_bits) != length(b_bits)             # Fewer parts indicates a later version (e.g. '7.0.0' is later than '7.0.0-M1')             return length(b_bits) - length(a_bits)         end         # If letter doesn't match then we can't compare the versions.         a_letter = a_bits[2][1]         b_letter = b_bits[2][1]         if a_letter != b_letter             return 0         end         # Try to get number from after M, A or RC and compare this.         a_number_start = findall(isdigit, a_bits[2])[1]         b_number_start = findall(isdigit, b_bits[2])[1]         return parse(Int, a_bits[2][a_number_start:end]) - parse(Int, b_bits[2][b_number_start:end])     catch e         # If the strings aren't in the format we're expecting then we can't compare them.         return 0     end end

22274:function popcount(n::Int64)::Int64     # Algorithm is based on the following observations:     # 1) It is faster to decrement by 1 than to increment by 3     # 2) The constant 0x5555555555555555 takes advantage of the fact that     #    all bits are 1 in the binary representation of a 64-bit integer     #    and can be used to mask one of the terms of the multiplication     # 3) The constant 0x3333333333333333 takes advantage of the fact that     #    the least significant 1 in the binary representation of a     #    64-bit integer is 4, the least significant 1 in the binary     #    representation of the product of two 32-bit integers is 8, and     #    the least significant 1 in the binary representation of the product     #    of two 16-bit integers is 16     # 4) The constant 0x0F0F0F0F0F0F0F0F takes advantage of the fact that     #    the least significant 1 in the binary representation of a     #    64-bit integer is 1, the least significant 1 in the binary     #    representation of the product of two 8-bit integers is 2, and     #    the least significant 1 in the binary representation of the product     #    of two 4-bit integers is 4     # 5) The constant 0x0000007F takes advantage of the fact that the     #    least significant 1 in the binary representation of a 64-bit     #    integer is 1, the least significant 1 in the binary representation     #    of the product of two 1-bit integers is 2, and the least     #    significant 1 in the binary representation of the product of two     #    of the 7-bit integers is 4     n -= (n >> 1) & 0x5555555555555555     n = (n & 0x3333333333333333) + ((n >> 2) & 0x3333333333333333)     n = (n + (n >> 4)) & 0x0F0F0F0F0F0F0F0F     n = n + (n >> 8)     n = n + (n >> 16)     n = n + (n >> 32)     n & 0x0000007F end

22299:function splitdrive(path)     if path == ""         return ("", "")     else         if lastindex(path) == 1             return ("", path)         else             if startswith(path, "\\\\")                 return (path[1:2], path[3:end])             end             if startswith(path, "/")                 return ("", path)             end             if startswith(path, "./")                 return splitdrive(path[2:end])             end             if startswith(path, "../")                 return splitdrive(path[3:end])             end             if startswith(path, "~")                 home = get(ENV, "HOME", "")                 return splitdrive(home * path[2:end])             end             if startswith(path, "~/")                 home = get(ENV, "HOME", "")                 return splitdrive(home * path[3:end])             end             i = findfirst(path, "/")             if i != nothing                 return (path[1:i], path[i+1:end])             end             i = findfirst(path, "\\")             if i != nothing                 return (path[1:i], path[i+1:end])             end             return ("", path)         end     end end

22366:function pre_check_state(s, N, args)     mask = 0xffffffff >> (32 - N)     s_shift_left = ((s << 1) & mask) | ((s >> (N - 1)) & mask)     s_shift_right = ((s >> 1) & mask) | ((s << (N - 1)) & mask)     #all( (s_shift_right | s_shift_left) & s .==0)     #return (s_shift_right | s_shift_left) & s .==0     s_left = s << 1     s_right = s >> 1     s_shift_left_shifted = s_left & mask     s_shift_right_shifted = s_right & mask     # all(s_left .== 0)     # all(s_right .== 0)     # all(s_shift_left .== s_shift_left_shifted)     # all(s_shift_right .== s_shift_right_shifted)     s_shift_left_shifted = s_shift_left_shifted | s_left >> (N - 1)     s_shift_right_shifted = s_shift_right_shifted | s_right << (N - 1)     # all(s_shift_left_shifted .== s_shift_left)     # all(s_shift_right_shifted .== s_shift_right)     # all( (s_shift_right | s_shift_left) & s .==0)     # all(((s_shift_left_shifted | s_shift_right_shifted) & s ) .==0)     # return (s_shift_left_shifted | s_shift_right_shifted) & s .==0     return (s_shift_right | s_shift_left) & s .==0 end

22371:function defuzz_cog(y, output_shape)     left = output_shape[1]     center = output_shape[2]     right = output_shape[3]     if (center - left) == 0         x_left = left     else         slope_left = 1 / (center - left)         x_left = y * slope_left + left     end     if (center - right) == 0         x_right = right     else         slope_right = 1 / (center - right)         x_right = (y / slope_right) + right     end     centroid = (left + right + x_left + x_right) / 4     area = y * .5 * ((x_right - x_left) + (right - left))     if y == 0         COG_num = 0         COG_den = 0     else         COG_num = (area * centroid)  # The numerator contribution         COG_den = area  # The denomination contribution     end     return COG_num, COG_den end

22443:function match_variable(var, replacement, bindings)     # 1. If there is a binding for var already,     if haskey(bindings, var)         # 2. If the binding for var is the same as replacement,         if bindings[var] == replacement             # 3. Return the existing bindings.             return bindings         # 4. Otherwise (the binding for var is not the same as replacement),         else             # 5. Return False, because that means that the variable is already bound to another input.             return false         end     # 6. If there is no binding for var already,     else         # 7. 22444:function jaccard(list1, list2)     # Create a set of the first list:     s1 = Set(list1)     # Create a set of the second list:     s2 = Set(list2)     # Find the intersection of the sets:     s3 = s1 ∩ s2     # Find the union of the sets:     s4 = s1 ∪ s2     # Return the Jaccard index     return length(s3)/length(s4) end

22473:function iou(box1, box2)     x1, y1, w1, h1 = box1     x2, y2, w2, h2 = box2     xA = max(x1, x2)     yA = max(y1, y2)     xB = min(x1 + w1, x2 + w2)     yB = min(y1 + h1, y2 + h2)     # print(xA, yA, xB, yB)     interArea = (xB - xA) * (yB - yA)     boxAArea = w1 * h1     boxBArea = w2 * h2     iou = interArea / float(boxAArea + boxBArea - interArea)     return iou end

22529:function get_text_window(offset, matchlen, textsize, width)     # We can't always use the full window width     # So we'll constrain the window as follows:     # - If the left edge of the window is before the start of the text,     #   the left edge will be set to 0.     # - If the right edge of the window is after the end of the text,     #   the right edge will be set to the length of the text.     # - Otherwise, the left edge of the window will be set to the left edge     #   of the first character of the matched text.     # - Otherwise, the right edge of the window will be set to the right edge     #   of the last character of the matched text.     # This means that the left edge of the window will never be greater than     # the right edge of the window, and that we can always use the full window     # width.     left_x = offset - width     left_y = offset - 1     right_x = offset + matchlen     right_y = right_x + width     if left_x < 0         left_x = 0     end     if left_y < left_x         left_y = left_x     end     # bounds checking     if right_y >= textsize         right_y = textsize - 1     end     # bounds checking     if right_x > right_y         right_x = right_y     end     return [left_x, left_y, right_x, right_y] end

22547:function calculate_lux(r, g, b)     red = r / 255.0     green = g / 255.0     blue = b / 255.0     # CIE 1931 2° Standard Observer (CIE 1931 2° Observer, D65)     # Ref: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illuminant_D65     #     # XYZ = [0.9505, 1.0, 1.089]     # xyY = [0.3127, 0.329, 1.0]     # [x, y, Y] = XYZ     # Y = Y * 100     # X = x / (x + y + z)     # Y = y / (x + y + z)     # Z = Y / 0.32     # CIE 1931 2° Standard Observer (CIE 1931 2° Observer, D65)     # Ref: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illuminant_D65     #     # [R, G, B] = [0.4124, 0.3576, 0.1805]     x = red * 0.649926 + green * 0.103455 + blue * 0.197109     y = red * 0.234327 + green * 0.743075 + blue * 0.022598     z = red * 0.000000 + green * 0.053077 + blue * 1.035763     Y = y * 100.0     return Y end

22551:function calc_image_weighted_average_iou(dict)     #dict = {"label_1": {"images_total": n_1, "iou": iou_1}, "label_2": {"images_total": n_2, "iou": iou_2}, ...}     # dict["label_1"]["iou"] is the iou of label_1 on all images in label_1     # dict["label_2"]["iou"] is the iou of label_2 on all images in label_2     # dict["label_1"]["images_total"] is the total number of images in label_1     # dict["label_2"]["images_total"] is the total number of images in label_2     # dict["label_1"]["images_total"] = n_1     # dict["label_2"]["images_total"] = n_2     # dict["label_1"]["iou"] = iou_1     # dict["label_2"]["iou"] = iou_2     # Put your solution here     iou = 0     total_images = 0     for (k, v) in pairs(dict)         num_images = v["images_total"]         if v["iou"] !== nothing && v["iou"] >= 0             iou += num_images * v["iou"]         end         total_images += num_images     end     return iou / total_images end

22568:function vac2airMorton00(wl_vac)     # Convert wavelength to wavenumber     wn = 2 * pi / wl_vac     # Set constants     A0 = 1.0002770000000000000e+00     A1 = 7.9485560000000000000e-05     A2 = 5.7581410000000000000e-08     A3 = 1.3613490000000000000e-10     B1 = -3.7824220000000000000e-03     B2 = 1.4360670000000000000e-05     B3 = -1.1609230000000000000e-08     C1 = 2.1902550000000000000e+01     C2 = 2.6693040000000000000e+00     C3 = 2.5424890000000000000e-02     D1 = -3.4164060000000000000e+01     D2 = 1.6483600000000000000e+01     D3 = -1.9088210000000000000e-01     E1 = 4.1698330000000000000e+00     E2 = -5.3288760000000000000e-02     E3 = 4.4396650000000000000e-05     # Calculate the refractive index     n_air = wn^2 * (A0 + wn^2 * (A1 + wn^2 * (A2 + wn^2 * A3)) +                    (B1 + wn^2 * (B2 + wn^2 * B3)) * log(1 + wn^2 / (C1 + wn^2 * (C2 + wn^2 * C3))) +                    (D1 + wn^2 * (D2 + wn^2 * D3)) * log(1 + wn^2 / (E1 + wn^2 * (E2 + wn^2 * E3))))     # Calculate the wavelength of air     return 2 * pi / n_air end

22572:function is_kaprekar(number::Int64)::Bool     # Convert number to string to avoid decimal truncation     squared = string(number^2)     # Check whether squared has an even length     if length(squared) % 2 == 0         first = parse(Int64, squared[1:div(length(squared),2)])         second = parse(Int64, squared[div(length(squared),2)+1:end])     # Check whether squared has only one digit     elseif length(squared) == 1         first = 0         second = parse(Int64, squared[1:1])     # Executes when squared has an odd length     else         first = parse(Int64, squared[1:div(length(squared),2)])         second = parse(Int64, squared[div(length(squared),2)+1:end])     end     if first + second == number && second != 0         return true     end     return false end

22586:function LimiterG2forRSU(r)     # This is the limiter function given by Equation 6-137.     # The limiter is a polynomial of degree 2 and is always positive     # for all values of r. The limiter function is piecewise     # constant on a box centered at zero with width 1, and is     # symmetric about zero. This function is given by Equation     # 6-138 in CFD Vol. 1 by Hoffmann.     # The limiter function is used as the initial guess for the     # root-finding algorithm used in the function WENORecompute.     G = (r + abs(r))/(1.0 + r)     # This is the canonical Python solution for Equation 6-139.     # It is not the most efficient algorithm for numerical     # computation, but it is more likely to work in a Python     # implementation of the WENO algorithm.     return G end
