22638:function lRGB_ACEScg(lRGB)     # sRGB     X = lRGB[1] * 0.664511 + lRGB[2] * 0.154324 + lRGB[3] * 0.162028     Y = lRGB[1] * 0.283881 + lRGB[2] * 0.668433 + lRGB[3] * 0.047685     Z = lRGB[1] * 0.000088 + lRGB[2] * 0.072310 + lRGB[3] * 0.986039     # XYZ to LMS     L =  116.047852 * Y - 16.0 * X - 16.0 * Z     M = 500.000000 * (X - Y)     S = 200.000000 * (Y - Z)     # LMS to LMS_ACEScg     L_A = L * 1.0018755368     M_A = M * 0.3582500025     S_A = S * 0.0716750017     # LMS_ACEScg to RG_ACEScg     R_A = L_A * 0.6370825265 + M_A * -0.0636372230 + S_A * 0.0174834731     G_A = L_A * -0.0168755823 + M_A * 0.8916380106 + S_A * -0.0107276683     # RG_ACEScg to RGB_ACEScg     R = R_A * 3.24045422265 + G_A * -1.53713851270 +  G_A * -0.49853140955     G = R_A * -0.96926603050 + G_A * 1.87601084544 + G_A * 0.04155601750     B = R_A * 0.05564343096 + G_A * -0.20402591350 + G_A * 1.05722518821     # Normalize to the [0,1] range     RGB_ACEScg = [         (R <= 0.0031308) ? 12.92 * R : 1.055 * R^(1/2.4) - 0.055,         (G <= 0.0031308) ? 12.92 * G : 1.055 * G^(1/2.4) - 0.055,         (B <= 0.0031308) ? 12.92 * B : 1.055 * B^(1/2.4) - 0.055     ]     return RGB_ACEScg end

22705:function frohner_cor_3rd_order(sig1, sig2, sig3, n1, n2, n3)     numer1 = (n1 * sig2 - n2 * sig1) * (n3^2 - n1^2 - (n1 - n3) / (n1 - n2) * (n2^2 - n1^2))     numer2 = (n1 * n2^2 - n1^2 * n2) * (sig3 - sig2 - (n1 - n3) / (n1 - n2) * (sig2 - sig1))     denom = (n1 - n2) * (n3^2 - n1^2) - (n1 - n3) * (n2^2 - n1^2)     return (numer1 - numer2) / denom end

22798:function calc_iou(box1, box2)     # box 1 coordinates     x1 = box1[1]     y1 = box1[2]     x2 = box1[3]     y2 = box1[4]     # box 2 coordinates     x3 = box2[1]     y3 = box2[2]     x4 = box2[3]     y4 = box2[4]     # calculate the coordinates of the intersection rectangle     x5 = max(x1, x3)     y5 = max(y1, y3)     x6 = min(x2, x4)     y6 = min(y2, y4)     # intersection area     inter_area = max(x6 - x5 + 1, 0) * max(y6 - y5 + 1, 0)     # calculate the area of the bounding boxes     box1_area = (x2 - x1 + 1) * (y2 - y1 + 1)     box2_area = (x4 - x3 + 1) * (y4 - y3 + 1)     # union area     union_area = (box1_area + box2_area) - inter_area     # calculate the intersection over union value     iou = inter_area / union_area     return iou end

22874:function build_tos(precedence::Int64, lowdelay::Bool, throughput::Bool, reliability::Bool, lowcost::Bool)::Int64     # maximizing the precedence by 32 (0b11110000) to fit in the     # 5 bits available     #     # 0b11110000 == 0xF0     # 0b11111111 == 0xFF     #     # (0xF0 << 5) | 0x0F == 0xF00F     #     # 0xF00F == 61440     # 0xF000 == 61440     #     # 0b00011110 == 0x1E == 30     # 0b00011111 == 0x1F == 31     #     # (0x1E << 5) | 0x1F == 150     # (0x1E << 5) | 0x1E == 148     return ((precedence << 5) | (lowdelay << 4) | (throughput << 3) | (reliability << 2) | (lowcost << 1)) end

22915:function compute_iou(boxA, boxB) 	xA = max(boxA[1], boxB[1]) 	yA = max(boxA[2], boxB[2]) 	xB = min(boxA[3], boxB[3]) 	yB = min(boxA[4], boxB[4]) 	interArea = max(0, xB - xA + 1) * max(0, yB - yA + 1) 	boxAArea = (boxA[3] - boxA[1] + 1) * (boxA[4] - boxA[2] + 1) 	boxBArea = (boxB[3] - boxB[1] + 1) * (boxB[4] - boxB[2] + 1) 	iou = interArea / float(boxAArea + boxBArea - interArea) 	return iou end

23041:function td_lambda(rewards, n_step, gamma)     T = length(rewards)     V = zeros(T)     # V[1:n_step] = rewards[1:n_step]     # for t = n_step+1:T     #     V[t] = rewards[t] + gamma * V[t-1]     # end     # return V     # V[1:n_step] = rewards[1:n_step]     # for t = n_step+1:T     #     V[t] = rewards[t] + gamma * V[t-1]     # end     # return V     for t = 1:T         for i = t:min(t+n_step-1, T)             V[t] += rewards[i] * gamma^-(i-t)         end     end     return V end

23049:function is_git_sha(text)     if length(text) ∈ (40, 7)         try             parse(Int, text, base=16)             return true         catch e             # Ok, maybe it was a partial sha and we can get a little             # closer to something with a full sha.             #             # The first 7 characters are guaranteed to be valid, so             # we just need to see if we can parse 7 characters             # starting at any position.             for i ∈ 1:length(text)-6                 try                     parse(Int, text[i:i+7], base=16)                     return true                 catch e                     # Not good. This character isn't good.                     # We move on to the next.                     continue                 end             end         end     end     return false end

23094:function target_glucose_value(percent_effect_duration, min_value, max_value)     # The inflection point in time: before it we use minValue,     # after it we linearly blend from minValue to maxValue     use_min_value_until_percent = 0.5     if percent_effect_duration <= use_min_value_until_percent         return min_value     end     if percent_effect_duration >= 1         return max_value     end     slope = (         (max_value - min_value) /         (1 - use_min_value_until_percent)         )     return min_value + slope * (percent_effect_duration                                 - use_min_value_until_percent                                 ) end

23152:function solve(c, n, p, w)   tables = 0   # w is less than c so we don't need any chips   if w < c     return 0   end   # leading_ps = w / p   leading_ps = w // p   # zeroes_available = n - (leading_ps + 1)   zeroes_available = n - (leading_ps + 1)   # if w % p == 0   if w % p == 0     zeroes_available += 1   end   while zeroes_available > 0     # number_of_zeroes_filled = min(w // c,  zeroes_available)     number_of_zeroes_filled = min(w ÷ c, zeroes_available)     # w % p     chips_used = number_of_zeroes_filled * c     # first chip drawn from the non-zero entry if exists.     chips_used -= (w % p)     w -= number_of_zeroes_filled * c     tables += number_of_zeroes_filled     if number_of_zeroes_filled < zeroes_available       return tables     end     zeroes_available = 1 + chips_used ÷ p   end   # now assume no zeroes available already.   return tables end
23153:function bitcount(num)     # Count of each 2 bits in num     num = num - ((num >> 1) & 0x5555555555555555)     # Count of each 4 bits in num     num = (num & 0x3333333333333333) + ((num >> 2) & 0x3333333333333333)     # Count of each 8 bits in num     num = (num + (num >> 4)) & 0x0f0f0f0f0f0f0f0f     # Count of each 16 bits in num     num = (num * 0x0101010101010101) >> 56     return num end

23168:function calc_jac_titles(title1, title2)     # empty set to store the set of words in each title     title_set1 = Set{String}()     title_set2 = Set{String}()     # tokenize titles by splitting on the " " character     # and then append each word to the appropriate set     for word in split(title1, " ")         push!(title_set1, word)     end     for word in split(title2, " ")         push!(title_set2, word)     end     # initialize variables to count the intersections and unions     # between title_set1 and title_set2     intersection_count = 0     union_count = 0     # loop through every element in the first set     for word in title_set1         if word in title_set2             intersection_count += 1         end         union_count += 1     end     # loop through every element in the second set     for word in title_set2         if word in title_set1             intersection_count += 1         end         union_count += 1     end     # return the ratio of the intersection over the union     return intersection_count / union_count end

23187:function iou(box1, box2)     b1_x1, b1_y1, b1_x2, b1_y2 = box1[1], box1[2], box1[3], box1[4]     b2_x1, b2_y1, b2_x2, b2_y2 = box2[1], box2[2], box2[3], box2[4]     # get the overlap rectangle     overlap_x1 = max(b1_x1, b2_x1)     overlap_y1 = max(b1_y1, b2_y1)     overlap_x2 = min(b1_x2, b2_x2)     overlap_y2 = min(b1_y2, b2_y2)     # check if there is an overlap     if overlap_x1 >= overlap_x2 || overlap_y1 >= overlap_y2         return 0.0     end     # if yes, calculate the ratio of the overlap to each ROI size and the unified size     overlap_size = (overlap_x2 - overlap_x1) * (overlap_y2 - overlap_y1)     b1_size = (b1_x2 - b1_x1) * (b1_y2 - b1_y1)     b2_size = (b2_x2 - b2_x1) * (b2_y2 - b2_y1)     return overlap_size / float(b1_size + b2_size - overlap_size) end
23188:function get_threshold_multiplier(total_nobs, nob_limits, multiplier_values)     if length(nob_limits) != length(multiplier_values)         throw(DimensionMismatch("length of input lists are different"))     end     if minimum(multiplier_values) <= 0.0         throw(ArgumentError("multiplier value less than or equal to zero"))     end     if minimum(nob_limits) < 0.0         throw(ArgumentError("nob_limit of less than zero given"))     end     if nob_limits[1] != 0         throw(ArgumentError("lowest nob_limit not equal to zero"))     end     if length(nob_limits) > 1         for i in 2:length(nob_limits)             if nob_limits[i] <= nob_limits[i-1]                 throw(ArgumentError("nob_limits not in ascending order"))             end         end     end     multiplier = -1.0     if total_nobs == 0         multiplier = 4.0     end     for i in 1:length(nob_limits)         if total_nobs > nob_limits[i]             multiplier = multiplier_values[i]         end     end     if multiplier <= 0.0         throw(ArgumentError("output multiplier less than or equal to zero"))     end     return multiplier end

23198:function kochanekBartelsInterpolator(v0, v1, v2, v3, alpha, tension, continuity, bias)     alpha2 = alpha * alpha     alpha3 = alpha2 * alpha     m0 = ((v1 - v0) * (1 - tension)) * (1 + continuity) * (1 + bias) / 2.0     m0 += ((v2 - v1) * (1 - tension)) * (1 - continuity) * (1 - bias) / 2.0     m1 = ((v2 - v1) * (1 - tension)) * (1 - continuity) * (1 + bias) / 2.0     m1 += ((v3 - v2) * (1 - tension)) * (1 + continuity) * (1 - bias) / 2.0     a0 = 2 * alpha3 - 3 * alpha2 + 1     a1 = alpha3 - 2 * alpha2 + alpha     a2 = alpha3 - alpha2     a3 = -2 * alpha3 + 3 * alpha2     return a0 * v1 + a1 * m0 + a2 * m1 + a3 * v2 end

23229:function mod_inverse(a, n)     if gcd(a, n) != 1         return 0     end     b = n     if b == 1         return 1     end     x1, x2, y1, y2 = 0, 1, 1, 0     while b > 0         q, r = divrem(a, b)         x = x2 - q*x1         y = y2 - q*y1         a, b, x2, x1, y2, y1 = b, r, x1, x, y1, y     end     if x2 < 0         return x2 + n     else         return x2     end end

23438:function _get_jobs_names(jobs, deps)     all_dest = []     for (k,v) in deps         push!(all_dest, v...)     end     all_dest = sort(unique(all_dest))     starting_jobs = []     for job in jobs         job_id = job["id"]         if !(job_id in all_dest)             push!(starting_jobs, job_id)         end     end     count = 0     new_ids = Dict()     while !isempty(starting_jobs)         next_step_jobs = []         for job_id in starting_jobs             if !(job_id in keys(new_ids))                 new_ids[job_id] = "S" * string(count)                 count += 1                 if job_id in keys(deps)                     append!(next_step_jobs, deps[job_id])                 end             end         end         next_step_jobs = sort(unique(next_step_jobs))         starting_jobs = next_step_jobs     end     return new_ids end

23471:function arabic_to_roman(number::Int64)::String     if number > 3999         throw(ArgumentError("Number can not be represented with roman numerals: " * string(number)))     end     roman_number = ""     for index = 1:4         if number == 0             continue         end         digit = number % 10         number = number ÷ 10         if index == 1             first = "I"             fifth = "V"             tenth = "X"         elseif index == 2             first = "X"             fifth = "L"             tenth = "C"         elseif index == 3             first = "C"             fifth = "D"             tenth = "M"         elseif index == 4             first = "M"             fifth = ""             tenth = ""         else             throw(ArgumentError("Invalid input: $(number)"))         end         if digit == 0             continue         elseif digit == 1             roman_number = first * roman_number         elseif digit == 2             roman_number = first^2 * roman_number         elseif digit == 3             roman_number = first^3 * roman_number         elseif digit == 4             roman_number = first * fifth * roman_number         elseif digit == 5             roman_number = fifth * roman_number         elseif digit == 6             roman_number = fifth * first * roman_number         elseif digit == 7             roman_number = fifth * first^2 * roman_number         elseif digit == 8             roman_number = fifth * first^3 * roman_number         elseif digit == 9             roman_number = first * tenth * roman_number         end     end     return roman_number end

23481:function compute_chi_of_U(Z)     # Define constants     T_N2 = 298.15     T_O2 = 255.58     T_He = 373.15     T_Ar = 154.46     T_Arp = 142.20     chi = 8.7e+4 * Z     if Z == 70.0         # Compute the reduced pressure         Pr_N2 = 0.56 * (T_N2 / 3.7)         Pr_O2 = 0.05 * (T_O2 / 2.5)         Pr_He = 0.33 * (T_He / 11.2)         Pr_Ar = 0.53 * (T_Ar / 20.3)         Pr_Arp = 0.1 * (T_Arp / 15.4)         chi = 0.35 * chi + 1e+4 * (Pr_N2 + Pr_O2 + Pr_He + Pr_Ar + Pr_Arp)     end     return chi end

23489:function kahan_sum(list_of_floating_point_numbers)     suma = 0.0     c = 0.0     for y in list_of_floating_point_numbers         t = suma + y         c = (t - suma) - y         suma = t     end     return suma end

23497:function unmangle(name::String)::String 	name = replace(name, r"_\d+$" => "") 	name = replace(name, r"\b\d+$" => "") 	name = replace(name, r"'\d+$" => "") 	name = replace(name, r"_\d+::" => "::") 	name = replace(name, r"\b\d+::" => "::") 	name = replace(name, r"'\d+::" => "::") 	name = replace(name, r"_\d+\$" => "") 	name = replace(name, r"\b\d+\$" => "") 	name = replace(name, r"'\d+\$" => "") 	name = replace(name, r"_\d+" => "") 	name = replace(name, r"\b\d+" => "") 	name = replace(name, r"'\d+" => "") 	return name end

23565:function _sabr_implied_vol_hagan_A11_fprime_by_strike(underlying, strike, maturity, alpha, beta, rho, nu)     if underlying <= 0.0 || strike <= 0.0 || maturity <= 0.0 || alpha < 0.0 || alpha > 1.0 || beta <= 0.0 || rho < -1.0 || rho > 1.0 || nu <= 0.0         return zero(typeof(underlying))     end     # Normalization constant.     b_N = 4.0 * (1 - rho * rho) * nu * nu     A = 1.0 / (b_N * maturity * maturity)     # numerator     numerator = 2 * nu * nu * (underlying - strike) * (alpha - rho * beta)     # denominator     denominator = 2 * b_N * underlying * alpha     # fprime = numerator / denominator     return numerator / denominator end

23578:function cubic_bezier_point(p0, p1, p2, p3, t)     x = ((1.0 - t)^3) * p0["x"] + 3 * t * ((1.0 - t)^2) * p1["x"] + 3 * t^2 * (1.0 - t) * p2["x"] + t^3 * p3["x"]     y = ((1.0 - t)^3) * p0["y"] + 3 * t * ((1.0 - t)^2) * p1["y"] + 3 * t^2 * (1.0 - t) * p2["y"] + t^3 * p3["y"]     return Dict("x"=>x, "y"=>y) end

23592:function calculate_pizzas_recursive(participants, n_pizza_types, pizza_types)     # Base Case     # Return 0, None if there is no possible solution     if n_pizza_types <= 0 || participants <= 0         return 0, nothing     end     # If weight of the nth item is more than Knapsack of capacity     # W, then this item cannot be included in the optimal solution     if pizza_types[end] > participants         return calculate_pizzas_recursive(participants,                                           n_pizza_types - 1,                                           pizza_types[1:end-1])     end     # If it fits: Always do a binary split to include it or not     # By doing so, the case where no element at all is a solution is checked,     # which seems quite senseless     # A lot of stuff is calculated way to often by doing so     temp, temp_idx = calculate_pizzas_recursive(participants - pizza_types[end],                                                   n_pizza_types - 1,                                                   pizza_types[1:end-1])     last_element_included = pizza_types[end] + temp     last_element_not_included, _ = calculate_pizzas_recursive(participants,                                                               n_pizza_types - 1,                                                               pizza_types[1:end-1])     # Return the maximum of both cases because:     # The maximum can never be exceed, so this is save, but the higher     # the closer the addition until the maximum worked then     if last_element_included >= last_element_not_included         return last_element_included, n_pizza_types - 1     else         return last_element_not_included, nothing     end end

23595:function csc_cumsum_i(p, c, n)     if n < 1         throw(ArgumentError("csc_cumsum_i: n is negative or zero"))     elseif n == 1         c[1] = p[1]     elseif n == 2         c[1] = p[1]         c[2] = p[2]     else         c[1] = p[1]         c[2] = p[2] - p[1]         for i in 3:n             c[i] = p[i] - p[i-1]         end     end     return p[n] end

23669:function calc_levels(ply_order, n_plies_in_groups, n_groups)     levels_in_groups = [Vector{Int}() for i in 1:n_groups]     # Loop through the plies in the order in which they are to be optimised     for ind_all_plies in ply_order         # Loop through the ply groups to assign the ply to one of the groups         for ind_group in 1:n_groups             # Check whether the number of plies in the group has not yet been             # filled, i.e. if the current group has not already reached the             # maximum number of plies             if length(levels_in_groups[ind_group]) < n_plies_in_groups[ind_group]                 # Assign the ply to the current group                 push!(levels_in_groups[ind_group], ind_all_plies)                 # Break the loop, as the ply has been assigned to a group                 break             end         end     end     return levels_in_groups end

23687:function get_iou(bb1, bb2)     # determine the coordinates of the intersection rectangle     xmin = max(bb1[1], bb2[1])     ymin = max(bb1[2], bb2[2])     xmax = min(bb1[3], bb2[3])     ymax = min(bb1[4], bb2[4])     # if the boxes do not intersect     if xmax < xmin || ymax < ymin         return 0.0     end     # otherwise, compute the area of intersection rectangle     intersection_area = (xmax - xmin) * (ymax - ymin)     # compute the area of both the prediction and ground-truth     # rectangles     bb1_area = (bb1[3] - bb1[1]) * (bb1[4] - bb1[2])     bb2_area = (bb2[3] - bb2[1]) * (bb2[4] - bb2[2])     # compute the intersection over union     iou = intersection_area / (bb1_area + bb2_area - intersection_area)     return iou end
23688:function compute_agreement_score(arcs1, arcs2, method, average)     n = length(arcs1)     if length(arcs2) != n         error("Incompatible arguments: arcs1 and arcs2 must have the same length")     end     if method == "joint"         score = length(Set(arcs1) ∩ Set(arcs2))     elseif method == "independent"         score = 0.0         dep2head1 = Dict(d => (h, r) for (h, d, r) in arcs1)         dep2head2 = Dict(d => (h, r) for (h, d, r) in arcs2)         for dep in keys(dep2head1)             (head1, rel1) = dep2head1[dep]             (head2, rel2) = dep2head2[dep]             if head1 == head2                 score += 0.5                 if rel1 == rel2                     score += 0.5                 end             end         end     else         error("Unknown method: $method")     end     if average         score = score / n     end     return score end

23732:function lens_rotation(alpha0, s0, dalpha, ds, t, tb) # current values for a given date (t) # - alpha and separation # linear development # - alpha : alpha0 + (t - tb) * dalpha # - separation : s0 + (t - tb) * ds # transform t in days (Julian year) t_days = t - tb # compute angular velocity alpha alpha = alpha0 + (t_days) * dalpha # compute separation s = s0 + (t_days) * ds return alpha, s end

23735:function MD5_f3(b, c, d)     b = b & 0xFFFFFFFF     c = c & 0xFFFFFFFF     d = d & 0xFFFFFFFF     bc = (b & c) << 1     bc = bc & 0xFFFFFFFF     cd = (c & d) << 1     cd = cd & 0xFFFFFFFF     bd = (b & d) << 1     bd = bd & 0xFFFFFFFF     a = b + bc + d + cd     a = a & 0xFFFFFFFF     return a end

23746:function fwhm(fwhm_now, lambda_now, secz_now, lambda_next, secz_next)     #Predict the fwhm.     #Parameters:     #-----------     #fwhm_now    : The fwhm value of the current exposure     #lambda_now  : The wavelength of the current exposure     #secz_now    : The airmass of the current exposure     #lambda_next : The wavelength of the next exposure     #secz_next   : The airmass of the next exposure     #Returns:     #--------     #fwhm_next   : The predicted fwhm of the next exposure     lambda_now, secz_now = map(float,[lambda_now, secz_now])     lambda_next, secz_next = map(float,[lambda_next, secz_next])     fwhm_next = fwhm_now * (lambda_next/lambda_now)^(-0.2) * (secz_next/secz_now)^(0.6)     return fwhm_next end

23759:function get_matching_connections(cxs_1, cxs_2)     # return sorted([c1 for c1 in cxs_1 if c1.innovation in [c2.innovation for c2 in cxs_2]],     #                 key=lambda x: x.innovation),\     #                 sorted([c2 for c2 in cxs_2 if c2.innovation in [c1.innovation for c1 in cxs_1]],     #                 key=lambda x: x.innovation)     if length(cxs_1) > 1 && length(cxs_2) > 1         @inbounds cxs_1_sorted = sort(cxs_1, by=x -> x.innovation)         @inbounds cxs_2_sorted = sort(cxs_2, by=x -> x.innovation)     elseif length(cxs_1) > 1         @inbounds cxs_1_sorted = cxs_1         @inbounds cxs_2_sorted = sort(cxs_2, by=x -> x.innovation)     elseif length(cxs_2) > 1         @inbounds cxs_1_sorted = sort(cxs_1, by=x -> x.innovation)         @inbounds cxs_2_sorted = cxs_2     else         @inbounds return cxs_1, cxs_2     end     i1, i2 = 1, 1     cxs_1_out = Array{Connection}(undef, length(cxs_1))     cxs_2_out = Array{Connection}(undef, length(cxs_2))     while i1 <= length(cxs_1) && i2 <= length(cxs_2)         if cxs_1_sorted[i1].innovation == cxs_2_sorted[i2].innovation             cxs_1_out[i1] = cxs_1_sorted[i1]             cxs_2_out[i2] = cxs_2_sorted[i2]             i1 += 1             i2 += 1         elseif cxs_1_sorted[i1].innovation < cxs_2_sorted[i2].innovation             cxs_1_out[i1] = cxs_1_sorted[i1]             i1 += 1         else             cxs_2_out[i2] = cxs_2_sorted[i2]             i2 += 1         end     end     # fill in the rest of the output arrays with zeros     while i1 <= length(cxs_1)         cxs_1_out[i1] = Connection()         i1 += 1     end     while i2 <= length(cxs_2)         cxs_2_out[i2] = Connection()         i2 += 1     end     cxs_1_out, cxs_2_out end

23761:function get_voxel_coord(index, s)     # Squared lateral size of the 3D neighborhood     s_squared = s^2     # Index of the 3D array (where the voxel is located)     z = div(index, s_squared)     # Remainder of the index divided by the squared lateral size of the 3D neighborhood     remainder = index - (z * s_squared)     # Lateral coordinate of the voxel     y = div(remainder, s)     # Horizontal coordinate of the voxel     x = remainder - (y * s)     # Return the voxel coordinates     return x, y, z end

23788:function compute_fans(shape)   dims = length(shape)   if dims < 1     throw(ArgumentError("Fan in and fan out can not be computed " *                         "for tensor with fewer than 1 dimension"))   elseif dims == 1     fan_in = fan_out = shape[1]   elseif dims == 2     fan_in = shape[1]     fan_out = shape[2]   else     receptive_field_size = 1     for dim = 1:dims-2       receptive_field_size *= shape[dim]     end     fan_in = shape[end-1] * receptive_field_size     fan_out = shape[end] * receptive_field_size   end   return fan_in, fan_out end

23815:function internal_params_1D(pixels_per_clock::Int64, window_width::Int64, image_size::Int64, output_stride::Int64, origin::Int64)     if pixels_per_clock % window_width != 0         error("pixels_per_clock should be a multiple of window_width. In this case, image_size = $(image_size), window_width = $(window_width)")     end     # Total number of windows outputted.     window_count = image_size//output_stride     # Number of parallel window outputs.     parallelism = pixels_per_clock//window_width     if parallelism == 0         parallelism = 1     else         if parallelism*window_width != pixels_per_clock             error("Expected integer throughput (stride evenly dividing px/clk).")         end     end     # Number of times valid should be asserted.     valid_count = window_count//parallelism     if valid_count * parallelism != window_count         error("Expected window count (img/stride) to be divisible by parallelism (px/clk / stride).")     end     return window_count, parallelism, valid_count end

23836:function Dadgostar_Shaw_terms(similarity_variable)     # t1 = similarity_variable * similarity_variable     # t2 = similarity_variable * t1     # t3 = t1 * t1     # t4 = t2 * t2     # t5 = t1 * t3     # t6 = t2 * t4     # t7 = t3 * t4     # First term     # term1 = (t1*(2*t1 - 1) + t2*(t2 - 2) + t3*(1 - 2*t1)) * 3*R*(theta/T)**2*exp(theta/T)/(exp(theta/T)-1)**2     term1 = (similarity_variable*(2*similarity_variable - 1) + similarity_variable^2*(similarity_variable^2 - 2) + similarity_variable^3*(1 - 2*similarity_variable)) * 24.5     # Second term     # term2 = t5*(t6 + 2*t5 + t7) * R * theta / T     term2 = similarity_variable^3*(similarity_variable^4 + 2*similarity_variable^3 + similarity_variable^5) * 8.314 * 298.15     # Third term     # term3 = t6*(t5 + 2*t6 + t7) * R * theta / T**2     term3 = similarity_variable^4*(similarity_variable^3 + 2*similarity_variable^4 + similarity_variable^5) * 8.314 * 298.15^2     return term1, term2, term3 end

The idea is to find the best-fitting crop box at the "peak" of the histogram. This is one of the challenges of manual image cropping.You can also experiment with different values for `margin`. If the value is too small, the image will be cropped with a lot of whitespace. If the value is too large, the image will be cropped with a lot of empty space. A good strategy to find the best value is to manually crop a few images with different values for `margin`, and then use the histogram to find the "peak" of the histogram. The histogram of a cropped image should not have a lot of peaks, because pixels outside the image are not included. 23866:function xgcd(b, n)     u, v, s, t = 1, 0, 0, 1     while n != 0         q, b, n = div(b, n), n, b % n         u, s = s, u - q * s         v, t = t, v - q * t     end     return b, u, v end

23905:function expression_matter(a, b, c)   # Write your code here.   max_val = 0   for operator in ['+', '*', '(', ')']     if operator == '+'       max_val = max(max_val, a + b + c)     end     if operator == '*'       max_val = max(max_val, a * (b + c))       max_val = max(max_val, (a + b) * c)       max_val = max(max_val, a * b * c)       max_val = max(max_val, a + b * c)       max_val = max(max_val, a + b + c)     end     if operator == '('       max_val = max(max_val, (a + b + c))       max_val = max(max_val, a * (b + c))       max_val = max(max_val, (a + b) * c)       max_val = max(max_val, a * b * c)       max_val = max(max_val, a + b * c)       max_val = max(max_val, a + b + c)     end     if operator == ')'       max_val = max(max_val, a + b + c)       max_val = max(max_val, a * b + c)       max_val = max(max_val, a * b + c)       max_val = max(max_val, a * b * c)       max_val = max(max_val, a + b * c)       max_val = max(max_val, a + b + c)     end   end   return max_val end

23920:function memory2int(memory)     if memory == nothing         return 0     end     if !contains(memory, "Ki") && !contains(memory, "Mi") && !contains(memory, "Gi")         return 0     end     m = match(r"([0-9]+)(Ki|Mi|Gi)", memory)     if m === nothing         return 0     end     memory = parse(Int, m[1])     if m[2] == "Ki"         memory *= 1024     elseif m[2] == "Mi"         memory *= 1024^2     elseif m[2] == "Gi"         memory *= 1024^3     end     return memory end
23921:function combineTwice(dataI, dataI_2)     for key in keys(dataI_2)         if key ∉ keys(dataI)             dataI[key] = Dict()             dataI[key]["f"] = dataI_2[key]["f"]             dataI[key]["records"] = dataI_2[key]["records"]         else             ds = Set()             for r in dataI[key]["records"]                 t = [r[1], r[2], r[4], r[5]]                 push!(ds, t)             end             for r in dataI_2[key]["records"]                 t = [r[1], r[2], r[4], r[5]]                 if !(t in ds)                     push!(dataI[key]["records"], r)                 end             end         end     end     return dataI end
23922:function replace0(x)     # solution from https://discourse.julialang.org/t/round-to-nearest-multiple-of-10/53208/4     if x isa AbstractString         for i in 1:length(x)             c = x[i]             if c == '.'                 if i != length(x)                     c2 = x[i+1]                     if c2 != '0'                         return(x)                     end                 else                     return(x)                 end             elseif !isdigit(c)                 return(x)             end         end         return(x[1:end-2] * '0' * x[end])     else         return(x)     end end

23925:function realtime_format(seconds)     # sec = int(seconds)     # years, sec = sec/29030400, sec % 29030400     # months, sec = sec/2419200, sec % 2419200     # weeks, sec = sec/604800, sec % 604800     # days, sec = sec/86400, sec % 86400     # hours, sec = sec/3600, sec % 3600     # minutes, sec = sec/60, sec % 60     # return (years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, sec)     seconds = floor(seconds)     minutes = seconds ÷ 60     seconds = seconds % 60     hours = minutes ÷ 60     minutes = minutes % 60     days = hours ÷ 24     hours = hours % 24     weeks = days ÷ 7     days = days % 7     months = weeks ÷ 4     weeks = weeks % 4     years = months ÷ 12     months = months % 12     return years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds end

23937:function _binomial_coefficients(n)     res = Dict{Tuple{Int, Int}, Int}()     res[(0, n)] = 1     res[(n, 0)] = 1     temp = 1     for k in 1:div(n, 2)         temp = (temp * (n - k + 1)) ÷ k         res[k, n - k] = res[n - k, k] = temp     end     res end

23958:function wdrvire(b5, b7, alpha)     # t1 = (alpha * b7 - b5) / (alpha * b7 + b5)     t1 = (alpha .* b7 .- b5) ./ (alpha .* b7 .+ b5)     # WDRVIRE = t1 + ((1 - alpha) / (1 + alpha))     WDRVIRE = t1 .+ ((1 .- alpha) ./ (1 .+ alpha))     return WDRVIRE end

23969:function merge_index_boundaries(indices)     # init     indices_len = length(indices)     if indices_len == 0         return []     end     # initialise the merged_indices array with the first index     merged_indices = [indices[1]]     # main loop     # after one iteration, the boundary of the current merged span will be indices[j][1]     for j = 2:indices_len         curr_start, curr_end = indices[j]         # if the current span's start index is the same as the previous's end index,         # merge the current span into the previous one         if curr_start == merged_indices[end][2]             merged_indices[end] = (merged_indices[end][1], curr_end)         else # otherwise, add the current span to the list of merged indices             push!(merged_indices, (curr_start, curr_end))         end     end     return merged_indices end

24027:function follows(anno_prev, anno)     # Find the type of this annotation.     if length(anno_prev) > 8         type_prev = anno_prev[9]     else         type_prev = ""     end     if length(anno) > 8         type = anno[9]     else         type = ""     end     # Canonicalize the types for comparison.     type_prev = strip(lowercase(type_prev))     type = strip(lowercase(type))     # Only merge text annotations of the same type.     if !in(["text", "string", "url", "email"], type_prev) ||        !in(["text", "string", "url", "email"], type) ||        type_prev != type         return false     end     # Canonicalize token start and end indices.     sent_token_start_prev = parse(Int, anno_prev[6])     sent_token_end_prev = parse(Int, anno_prev[7])     doc_token_start_prev = parse(Int, anno_prev[8])     doc_token_end_prev = parse(Int, anno_prev[9])     sent_token_start = parse(Int, anno[6])     sent_token_end = parse(Int, anno[7])     doc_token_start = parse(Int, anno[8])     doc_token_end = parse(Int, anno[9])     # If the annotations are already consecutive, return false.     if sent_token_start_prev == sent_token_end + 1 &&        doc_token_start_prev == doc_token_end + 1 &&        sent_token_start == sent_token_end_prev + 1 &&        doc_token_start == doc_token_end_prev + 1         return false     end     # Merge is possible only if the next token in the text annotation starts     # at the same position in the document.     if doc_token_end_prev + 1 != doc_token_start         return false     end     # Merge is possible only if the previous token in the text annotation ends     # at the same position in the document.     if doc_token_end + 1 != doc_token_start_prev         return false     end     # Merge is possible only if the next token in the sentence annotation starts     # at the same position in the sentence.     if sent_token_end_prev + 1 != sent_token_start         return false     end     # Merge is possible only if the previous token in the sentence annotation ends     # at the same position in the sentence.     if sent_token_end + 1 != sent_token_start_prev         return false     end     return true end

To do so, the user will need to     #   compute the total number of sequences N and the number of K and R     #   states for all aligned sequences.     #     #   You are provided with two default implementations:     #     #   - Python     #   - MATLAB     #     #   You can modify these implementations as needed, but you must return     #   the same output as the default implementations.     #     #   The default implementations are in the file:     #     #     src/algorithms/sequencealignment.py     #     #   A description of the input and output is provided there. You can also     #   find examples of how to call this function in the file:     #     #     src/algorithms/sequencealignment.py     #     #   You will be asked to write your own implementations in Python and MATLAB     #   in the files:     #     #     src/algorithms/sequencealignment_python.py     #     src/algorithms/sequencealignment_matlab.m     #     #   The user will provide the name of the algorithm that they want to use     #   by specifying the name of the function to call when running a     #   benchmark. To do so, add the following line to the configuration     #   file:     #     #     function=sequencealignment_python     #     #   or     #     #     function=sequencealignment_matlab     #     #   The default implementations are imported from the file:     #     #     src/algorithms/sequencealignment.py     #     #   You can change this as needed. You should use the following format     #   for your implementations:     #     #   def GetKRStateFraction(alignedSeqList):     #       return (cnt_K, cnt_R,  per_K, per_R)     #     # Your code here     n = length(alignedSeqList)     lengthAlignment = length(alignedSeqList[1])     cnt_K = [0 for i in 1:lengthAlignment]     cnt_R = [0 for i in 1:lengthAlignment]     for i in 1:n         alignedSeq = alignedSeqList[i]         for j in 1:lengthAlignment             s = alignedSeq[j]             if s == 'K'                 cnt_K[j] += 1             elseif s == 'R'                 cnt_R[j] += 1             end         end     end     per_K = [0.0 for i in 1:lengthAlignment]     per_R = [0.0 for i in 1:lengthAlignment]     numSeq_float = Float64(n)     for j in 1:lengthAlignment         per_K[j] = cnt_K[j] / numSeq_float         per_R[j] = cnt_R[j] / numSeq_float     end     return cnt_K, cnt_R, per_K, per_R end

24063:function sequence_frame_number(scene_frame, mode, start, duration, offset)     frame = scene_frame - start + 1     if mode == "CLIP"         if frame < 1 || frame > duration             return nothing         end     elseif mode == "EXTEND"         frame = min(max(frame, 1), duration)     elseif mode == "REPEAT"         frame %= duration         if frame < 0             frame += duration         end         if frame == 0             frame = duration         end     else  # mode == "PING_PONG"         pingpong_duration = duration * 2 - 2         frame %= pingpong_duration         if frame < 0             frame += pingpong_duration         end         if frame == 0             frame = pingpong_duration         end         if frame > duration             frame = duration * 2 - frame         end     end     frame += offset     return frame end

24065:function distance_calc(s1, s2)     # If either string is empty, the distance is the length of the other string     if s1 == ""         return length(s2)     elseif s2 == ""         return length(s1)     end     # Initialize distance matrix     n, m = length(s1), length(s2)     d = zeros(Int, n + 1, m + 1)     # Populate distance matrix for deletion, insertion and substitution     for i in 1:n, j in 1:m         cost = 1         if s1[i] == s2[j]             cost = 0         end         d[i + 1, j + 1] = min(d[i, j + 1] + 1, d[i + 1, j] + 1, d[i, j] + cost)     end     # Final distance will be the value in the bottom right     return d[n + 1, m + 1] end

24074:function resonator_from_qubit(qubit, g, bare_res)     delta = bare_res - qubit     push = g^2 / delta     return bare_res + push # - # # 4. Phase Calibration # # The noise in the system affects our ability to determine the frequency of the resonator. For example, if we do not calibrate the phase of the signal, we can lose sensitivity to the resonance peak if it crosses over the measured threshold. # # We can measure the phase shift of the signal relative to a reference signal by looking for the ratio of the difference between the signals when measured as a function of frequency. # # $$R = \frac{V_\text{signal} - V_\text{reference}}{V_\text{signal} + V_\text{reference}}$$ # # $R$ is the **relative phase**, with a maximum value of 1 and minimum value of -1. # # We can use a graphical representation of the phase to calibrate the resonator frequency. This graphical representation is called a **phase plot**. # # <img src="images/phase-calibration.svg" width="40%"> # # The phase plot shows the amount of phase shift as a function of frequency for two signals: the original signal and the reference signal. The relative phase, $R$, is a function of frequency in this plot and is equal to the slope of the line fit to the points on the plot. The slope of the line fit is equal to $R$. # # In the previous section, we showed that the estimated resonator position is given by # # $$R = \frac{V_\text{signal} - V_\text{reference}}{V_\text{signal} + V_\text{reference}}$$ # # $$R = \frac{V_\text{signal} - V_\text{reference}}{V_\text{signal} - I_\text{signal} R}$$ # # Using the [detector equation](https://docs.microsoft.com/learn/modules/calibrate-qubit-readout-amplitude/4-detector-equation), we can rewrite the relative phase as # # $$R = \frac{V_\text{signal} - V_\text{reference}}{V_\text{signal} - (V_\text{signal} - I_\text{signal} R)}$$ # # This is equivalent to # # $$R = \frac{V_\text{signal}^2 - V_\text{reference}^2}{V_\text{signal}^2 + (V_\text{signal} - I_\text{signal} R)^2}$$ # # Solving for $R$, we get # # $$R = \frac{1}{1 + \frac{V_\text{signal}^2 - V_\text{reference}^2}{(V_\text{signal} - I_\text{signal} R)^2}}$$ # # Now we are ready to measure $V_\text{signal}$ and $I_\text{signal}$ at different frequencies to build a phase plot. The calibration steps are as follows. # # 1. Make a list of frequencies that you want to measure. Each frequency should be a multiple of the qubit frequency, and it should start at the qubit frequency and end at the qubit frequency + 20 GHz. In the example below, the qubit is 5.2 GHz, so we want to measure frequencies from 5.2 GHz to 7.2 GHz in steps of 1 GHz. # 2. For each frequency, determine the signal voltage and the current through the signal. # 3. Use the equation to calculate the relative phase $R$. # 4. Plot the points $(f, R)$ from the previous step. # ## Task 5.1. Calibrating the Phase # # You are given two signal lists that contain voltage and current measurements at different frequencies. Your task is to calibrate the phase shift of the signal relative to a reference signal. # + # Calibrating the phase qubit = 5 end

24077:function point_in_area(line1, line2, x, y, width1, width2)     # Check that x, y, width1 and width2 are numbers     try         is_number(x) && is_number(y) && is_number(width1) && is_number(width2)     catch e         @error "One or more input values are not numbers."         return false     end     # Calculate coordinates for the two lines     # x1, x2, x3, x4 = line1[0][0], line1[1][0], line2[0][0], line2[1][0]     # y1, y2, y3, y4 = line1[0][1], line1[1][1], line2[0][1], line2[1][1]     #     # Calculate width and height of the lines     # w1 = (x2 - x1) * (y3 - y4)     # w2 = (x4 - x3) * (y1 - y2)     # w = w1 - w2     # h1 = (x3 - x2) * (y4 - y1)     # h2 = (x1 - x4) * (y2 - y3)     # h = h1 - h2     w1 = width1 * (line1[2] - line1[1])     w2 = width2 * (line2[2] - line2[1])     w = w1 - w2     h1 = width1 * (line1[3] - line1[2])     h2 = width2 * (line2[3] - line2[2])     h = h1 - h2     x1, x2, x3, x4 = line1[1][1], line1[2][1], line2[1][1], line2[2][1]     y1, y2, y3, y4 = line1[1][2], line1[2][2], line2[1][2], line2[2][2]     # Calculate the intersection point     x = (w * (y3 - y4) - h * (x3 - x4)) / (h * (x2 - x1) - w * (y2 - y1))     y = (h * (x1 - x2) - w * (y1 - y2)) / (w * (x4 - x3) - h * (y4 - y3))     # Check if intersection point is on defined area     x_max = max(x1, x2)     x_min = min(x3, x4)     y_max = max(y1, y2)     y_min = min(y3, y4)     (x_min <= x <= x_max) && (y_min <= y <= y_max) end

24096:function get_sample_type(sample, sample_mapping)     sample_types = keys(sample_mapping)     # find the sample type that has a match     matching_sample_type = nothing     for sample_type in sample_types         for sample_name_base in sample_mapping[sample_type]             if startswith(sample, sample_name_base)                 if isnothing(matching_sample_type)                     matching_sample_type = sample_type                 elseif sample_type < matching_sample_type                     matching_sample_type = sample_type                 end             end         end     end     # return nothing if no sample type matched the sample     if isnothing(matching_sample_type)         return nothing     end     # return the sample type if it's unique     if length(unique(sample_mapping[matching_sample_type])) == 1         return matching_sample_type     end     # if two sample types include a sample name base in their sample name list that match     # the start of sample, then return the one matching sample more specificically, i.e.     # that with the longest match     longest_matching_sample_type = nothing     for sample_type in sample_types         for sample_name_base in sample_mapping[sample_type]             if startswith(sample, sample_name_base)                 if isnothing(longest_matching_sample_type)                     longest_matching_sample_type = sample_type                 elseif sample_type > longest_matching_sample_type                     longest_matching_sample_type = sample_type                 end             end         end     end     return longest_matching_sample_type end

24120:function min_max_scale(X)     num = length(X[1])     # find max     max_vec = zeros(num)     for row in X         for i in 1:num             if row[i] > max_vec[i]                 max_vec[i] = row[i]             end         end     end     # find min     min_vec = zeros(num)     for row in X         for i in 1:num             if row[i] < min_vec[i]                 min_vec[i] = row[i]             end         end     end     scaled_X = []     for row in X         tmp = []         for i in 1:num             tmp = append!(tmp, (row[i] - min_vec[i]) / (max_vec[i] - min_vec[i]))         end         push!(scaled_X, tmp)     end     return scaled_X end

24154:function get_version_substitute(version_str::String)     lower_case_str = lowercase(version_str)     # Substitute "edit" and "edition" with "version".     if occursin("edition", lower_case_str) || occursin("edit", lower_case_str)         lower_case_str = replace(lower_case_str, " edition" => " version")         lower_case_str = replace(lower_case_str, " edit " => " version")     end     # Remove "the".     if startswith(lower_case_str, "the ")         lower_case_str = split(lower_case_str, "the ")[2]     end     # Substitute "radio mix" with "radio version".     if occursin("radio mix", lower_case_str)         lower_case_str = "radio version"     end     # Substitute "video mix" with "video version".     if occursin("video mix", lower_case_str)         lower_case_str = "video version"     end     # Substitute "spanglish" and "spanish" with "spanish version".     if occursin("spanglish", lower_case_str) || occursin("spanish", lower_case_str)         lower_case_str = "spanish version"     end     # Substitute "remaster" with "remaster" and "remastered" with "remaster".     if endswith(lower_case_str, "remaster")         lower_case_str = "remaster"     elseif endswith(lower_case_str, "remastered")         lower_case_str = "remaster"     end     # Remove extra white space.     lower_case_str = replace(lower_case_str, r"\s+" => " ")     return strip(lower_case_str) end

We still need to wrap/unwrap         # tensors so that the implementation can be written in terms         # of Tensors and Variables.         return "use_type"     end end

24182:function sentihood_macro_F1(y_true, y_pred)     # Calculate number of true and predicted aspects     # The number of true aspects is collected in "true_positive"     # The number of predicted aspects is collected in "predicted_positive"     true_positive = length(findall(y_pred .> 0))     predicted_positive = length(findall(y_true .> 0))     # Calculate Precision, Recall, and Macro-F1 score     precision = true_positive / predicted_positive     recall = true_positive / true_positive     macro_F1 = 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)     return macro_F1 end

24232:function abbrev(name)     # initialize a string for the abbreviation     abbr = ""     # get the index of any parenthesis     paren_index = findfirst("(", name)     # append the portion of the name before the first parenthesis     # to the abbreviation string     if paren_index !== nothing         abbr = abbr * name[1:paren_index[1] - 1]         # get the index of any closing parenthesis         close_paren_index = findfirst(")", name)         # append '...' to the abbreviation string if a closing         # parenthesis is found         if close_paren_index !== nothing             abbr = abbr * "..."             # append the portion of the name after the closing             # parenthesis to the abbreviation string             abbr = abbr * name[close_paren_index[1] + 1:end]         else             # append the entire name to the abbreviation string             # if no closing parenthesis is found             abbr = abbr * name         end     else         # append the entire name if no parenthesis is found         abbr = abbr * name     end     return abbr end

24244:function extended_euclidean_algorithm(a, b)     s, old_s = 0, 1     t, old_t = 1, 0     r, old_r = b, a     while r != 0         q = old_r ÷ r         old_r, r = r, old_r - q*r         old_s, s = s, old_s - q*s         old_t, t = t, old_t - q*t     end     return old_r, old_s, old_t end

24272:function ipow(a, b)     if b == 0         return 1     elseif a == 0         return 0     elseif a == 1         return 1     elseif a == -1         if b % 2 == 1             return -1         else             return 1         end     elseif b < 0         throw(ArgumentError("ipow not defined for negative exponent and |base|>1"))     end     val = 1     while true         b,bit = divrem(b,2)         if bit == 1             val = val * a   # no *= to allow cost calculation         end         if b == 0             break         end         a = a * a   # no *= to allow cost calculation     end     return val end

24283:function hyphen_range(s) 	if isempty(s) || (s[1]=='-' && isempty(s[2:end])) 		throw(ArgumentError("hyphen_range is given its arguement as " * s * " which seems not correctly formated.")) 	end 	result = Set{Int}() 	for r in split(s,",") 		if '-' in r 			r_split = split(r,'-') 			length(r_split) != 2 && throw(ArgumentError("hyphen_range is given its arguement as " * s * " which seems not correctly formated.")) 			r_start = parse(Int, r_split[1]) 			r_end = parse(Int, r_split[2]) 			r_end < r_start && throw(ArgumentError("hyphen_range is given its arguement as " * s * " which seems not correctly formated.")) 			for i in r_start:r_end 				push!(result,i) 			end 		else 			r = parse(Int, r) 			push!(result,r) 		end 	end 	return sort(collect(result)) end

24311:function clamp(n, smallest, largest)     # We know that smallest <= largest, so it's possible that n is larger     # than largest.  If so, the smaller of n and largest must be returned.     # If n is smaller than smallest, it's possible that it's less than     # smallest but larger than largest.  If so, the larger of n and smallest     # must be returned.  This is why we need to use max and min.     return max(smallest, min(n, largest)) end

24324:function get_x_scale(xcoordinatemin, xcoordinatemax, xpixelmin, xpixelmax)   # A function that returns the scaling from pixels to x axis units. Can also be used for the y scaling, with all 'x'   # in input variables replaced with their 'y' counterparts   # Inputs:   #  - xcoordinatemin: number, minimum x (or y) value (from input image)   #  - xcoordinatemax: number, maximum x ( or y) value (from input image)   #  - xpixelmin: int, minimum pixel location along the x (or y) axis   #  - xpixelmax: int, maximum pixel location along the x ( or y) axis   # Outputs:   #  - x_scale: a value with units (pixels/coordinate unit) used to scale distances along the x (or y) axis   pixel_range = xpixelmax - xpixelmin   coordinate_range = xcoordinatemax - xcoordinatemin   x_scale = pixel_range / coordinate_range   return x_scale end

24379:function hsl_to_rgb(hue, saturation, lightness)     saturation /= 100     lightness /= 100     c = (1 - abs(2 * lightness - 1)) * saturation     x = c * (1 - abs(((hue / 60) % 2) - 1))     m = lightness - c / 2     if hue < 60         (r, g, b) = (c, x, 0)     elseif hue < 120         (r, g, b) = (x, c, 0)     elseif hue < 180         (r, g, b) = (0, c, x)     elseif hue < 240         (r, g, b) = (0, x, c)     elseif hue < 300         (r, g, b) = (x, 0, c)     else         (r, g, b) = (c, 0, x)     end     return (r+m, g+m, b+m) end

24435:function jacobi(numerator::Int64, denominator::Int64)::Int64     if denominator <= 0 || denominator & 1 == 0         throw(DomainError(denominator, "Jacobi parameters are out of function domain"))     end     j_symbol = 1     numerator %= denominator     while numerator != 0         while numerator & 1 == 0             numerator >>= 1             if denominator % 8 in (3, 5)                 j_symbol *= -1             end         end         numerator, denominator = denominator, numerator         if numerator % 4 == denominator % 4 == 3             j_symbol *= -1         end         numerator %= denominator     end     if denominator == 1         return j_symbol     end     return 0 end

24458:function topological_sort(unsorted_dict)     sorted_list = []     sorted_set = Set()     found = true     unconnected_dict = deepcopy(unsorted_dict)     while found         found = false         for pid = keys(unconnected_dict)             obsoletes_pid = unconnected_dict[pid]             if obsoletes_pid === nothing || obsoletes_pid in sorted_set                 found = true                 push!(sorted_list, pid)                 push!(sorted_set, pid)                 delete!(unconnected_dict, pid)             end         end     end     return sorted_list, unconnected_dict end

24480:function transform_s1zs2z_chi_eff_chi_a(mass1, mass2, spin1z, spin2z)     spin1 = spin1z     spin2 = spin2z     if spin1 != 0 && spin2 != 0         spin1 /= 2         spin2 /= 2     end     if spin1z >= 0         spin1 += 1     else         spin2 += 1     end     if spin1 == 0 || spin2 == 0         chi_eff = 0         chi_a = 0     else         # In the following, we are multiplying by the average mass of the                              # two particles, which is not necessarily equal to the sum of the two         # particle masses.         chi_eff = 2 * (spin1 * mass1 + spin2 * mass2) / (mass1 + mass2)         chi_a = 2 * (spin2 * mass2 - spin1 * mass1) / (mass2 + mass1)         chi_eff /= 2         chi_a /= 2     end     return chi_eff,chi_a end

24518:function calc_iou(box1, box2) # box1[0], box1[1] = [x1, y1, x2, y2] # box2[0], box2[1] = [x1, y1, x2, y2] # a = area of box1 # b = area of box2 # c = area of box1 intersection with box2 # d = area of box1 union with box2 x11, y11, x12, y12 = box1 x21, y21, x22, y22 = box2 x11 = max(x11, x21) y11 = max(y11, y21) x12 = min(x12, x22) y12 = min(y12, y22) w = max(x12 - x11, 0) h = max(y12 - y11, 0) inter_area = w * h a1 = (x12 - x11) * (y12 - y11) a2 = (x22 - x21) * (y22 - y21) union_area = a1 + a2 - inter_area iou = inter_area / union_area end

24534:function compute_reward_walk(state, action, next_state)     state_vec = state[1:2]     next_state_vec = next_state[1:2]     forward_vel = state_vec - next_state_vec     # REWARD FUNCTION     reward = 0.0     if action == 1 # forward         reward = -1.0     elseif action == 2 # right         reward = -0.5     elseif action == 3 # left         reward = -0.5     elseif action == 4 # stop         reward = 0.0     end     reward += 1.0 * forward_vel[1] # reward for moving forward     reward += 0.01 * abs(forward_vel[1]) # punish for moving backward     return reward end

24549:function sol(arr, n)     ltr = Array{Int}(undef, n)     rtl = Array{Int}(undef, n)     ltr[1] = arr[1]     for i in 2:n         ltr[i] = max(ltr[i-1], arr[i])     end     rtl[n] = arr[n]     for i in n-1:-1:1         rtl[i] = min(rtl[i+1], arr[i])     end     for i in 1:n         if ltr[i] == rtl[i] && i != 1 && i != n             return arr[i]         end     end     return -1 end

24690:function d_stp(t_ref, t_in_situ, ds)     muw = (4.2844324477E-05 + 1 / (1.5700386464E-01 * (t_in_situ + 6.4992620050E+01)^2 + -9.1296496657E+01))     C = 1.5409136040E+00 + 1.9981117208E-02 * t_in_situ + -9.5203865864E-05 * t_in_situ^2     D = 7.9739318223E+00 + -7.5614568881E-02 * t_in_situ + 4.7237011074E-04 * t_in_situ^2     vis = muw * (1 + C*0.035 + D*0.035^2)     muwd = (4.2844324477E-05 +             1 /             (1.5700386464E-01 * (t_ref + 6.4992620050E+01)^2 + -9.1296496657E+01))     A = 1.5409136040E+00 + 1.9981117208E-02 * t_ref + -9.5203865864E-05 * t_ref^2     B = 7.9739318223E+00 + -7.5614568881E-02 * t_ref + 4.7237011074E-04 * t_ref^2     visd = muwd * (1 + A*0.035 + B*0.035^2)     t_in_situ = t_in_situ + 273.15     t_ref = t_ref + 273.15     return t_in_situ / vis * visd * ds / t_ref end

24723:function sentitel_strict_acc(y_true, y_pred)     # 5 for aspect, 5 for polarity     # total_cases=int(len(y_true)/5)     # true_cases=0     # for i in range(total_cases):     #     if y_true[i*5]!=y_pred[i*5]:continue     #     if y_true[i*5+1]!=y_pred[i*5+1]:continue     #     if y_true[i*5+2]!=y_pred[i*5+2]:continue     #     if y_true[i*5+3]!=y_pred[i*5+3]:continue     #     if y_true[i*5+4]!=y_pred[i*5+4]:continue     #     true_cases+=1     # aspect_strict_Acc = true_cases/total_cases     # return aspect_strict_Acc     # Ref: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/24648080/how-to-check-for-equality-of-two-values-in-a-array     total_cases = length(y_true) ÷ 5     true_cases = 0     for i in 1:total_cases         if y_true[i * 5 - 4] == y_pred[i * 5 - 4]             if y_true[i * 5 - 3] == y_pred[i * 5 - 3]                 if y_true[i * 5 - 2] == y_pred[i * 5 - 2]                     if y_true[i * 5 - 1] == y_pred[i * 5 - 1]                         if y_true[i * 5] == y_pred[i * 5]                             true_cases += 1                         end                     end                 end             end         end     end     aspect_strict_Acc = true_cases / total_cases     return aspect_strict_Acc end

24725:function to_page_count(n_entries, entries_per_page) :: Int64     if n_entries == 0         return 0     end     # How this works:     # Say the number of entries per page was 10. Thus we'd want entries 1-10     # to appear on page 1, 11-20 to appear on page 2, and so on. Naively, the     # number of pages is `n_entries / entries_per_page`, but as we're using     # integer arithmetic, this rounds down, so we need to adjust it up one.     # Also, if the number of entries is divisible by the number of page, (e.g.     # there are ten entries), the naive arithmetic will end up stating there     # are two pages, not just one. Thus to compensate for that, we subtract     # one from the number of entries before dividing.     return (n_entries - 1) ÷ entries_per_page + 1 end

24764:function compare_versions(v1::String, v2::String)::Int64     # Basic: create arrays of integers from the version strings     parts1 = parse.(Int, split(v1, "."))     parts2 = parse.(Int, split(v2, "."))     # Zero-fill the parts to the same length     length_difference = abs(length(parts1) - length(parts2))     if length_difference > 0         if length(parts1) < length(parts2)             append!(parts1, zeros(Int, length_difference))         elseif length(parts2) < length(parts1)             append!(parts2, zeros(Int, length_difference))         end     end     # Compare each part     for (part1, part2) in zip(parts1, parts2)         if part1 < part2             return -1         elseif part1 > part2             return 1         end     end     return 0 end

24789:function linear_cell_to_tuple(c1, repeat_units)     c1 = Int(c1)     c1x = c1 % repeat_units[1]     c1y = div((c1 - c1x), repeat_units[1]) % repeat_units[2]     c1z = div((c1 - c1x - c1y * repeat_units[1]), (repeat_units[1] * repeat_units[2]))     return (c1x, c1y, c1z) end

24797:function detectsubstitutions(args)     # Initialise variables.     sub = Dict{String, Any}()     removelist = String[]     # Search for -var and -v flags, and set the corresponding values.     # FIXME: This is a little unusual, we could use regex to find -var and -v     # without needing to specify the actual flags.     for index in 1:length(args)         if args[index] == "-var" || args[index] == "-v"             sub[args[index + 1]] = args[index + 2]             removelist = push!(removelist, args[index])             removelist = push!(removelist, args[index + 1])             removelist = push!(removelist, args[index + 2])             index += 2         end     end     # Remove the flags from the argument list.     for item in removelist         args = filter(i -> i != item, args)     end     # Return the dictionary containing the substitutions.     return sub end
24798:function gcd(p, q)     # p and q must be of the same type     if typeof(p) != typeof(q)         error("p and q must be of the same type")     end     # Ensure p is larger than q     if p < q         (p, q) = (q, p)     end     # Continue to divide q by p until we find the remainder of 0     while q != 0         (p, q) = (q, p % q)     end     # Return the gcd of p and q     return p end

24813:function max_digit(n, d, r)     if d == 0         throw(ArgumentError("d cannot be zero"))     end     if n == 0         return 0     end     # Implementation from     # http://rosettacode.org/wiki/Find_digits_of_an_integer#Julia     n = abs(n)     digit_max = -1     while n >= 10         digit = n % 10         n = n // 10         if digit % d == r && digit > digit_max             digit_max = digit         end     end     digit = n     if digit % d == r && digit > digit_max         digit_max = digit     end     if digit_max < 0         throw(ArgumentError("There isn't a digit of `n` that gives a         remainder `r` on division by `d`."))     else         return "The maximum digit of `n` with remainder `r` on division by `d` is ", digit_max     end end

25024:function running_var(bar, series, period, asma, apowsumavg)     if !isa(period, Int)         throw(ArgumentError("period must be Int"))     end     if period < 1         throw(ArgumentError("period must be 1 or greater"))     end     if !isa(bar, Int)         throw(ArgumentError("bar must be Int"))     end     if bar <= 0         return 0.0     end     if asma == nothing         throw(ArgumentError("asma of nothing invalid when bar > 0"))     end     if apowsumavg == nothing         throw(ArgumentError("powsumavg of nothing invalid when bar > 0"))     end     windowsize = bar + 1.0     if windowsize >= period         windowsize = period     end     return (apowsumavg * windowsize - windowsize * asma * asma) / windowsize end

25041:function _paradox_temp_table_keyword_args(cfg, eng)     #     #     # We are using the "insert into tmp" technique here.     #     # The insert syntax is:     #     # INSERT INTO destination SELECT ... FROM source WHERE ...;     #     # Insert into an empty temporary table     #     # In SQL Server, you can use a temporary table for this.     #     # In Oracle, you can also use a temporary table but only in a subquery     # inside the insert statement.     #     # In MySQL, there is no temporary table, so you can't do this.     #     # In SQLite, you can use a temporary table for this.     #     # As a shortcut, you can create a temporary view and then drop it.     #     # The Python DB-API requires you to use a temporary table.     #     # For other SQL engines, I believe you can use a temporary table as well.     #     #     # The tests will fail if you use a temporary table.     #     # To do this, you need to create a table with a name that is unique across all     # tests. This should be done using a decorator.     #     # For this purpose, you can use a random string or a hash of the test name.     #     # Make sure that the temporary table or view is created at the right scope.     #     # For example, if you create a temporary table in the module scope, the     # database connection might be already closed.     #     # The tests will then fail.     #     #     # In the tests, you can then use a prefix argument like this:     #     #     insert_into(table, **paradox_temp_table_keyword_args)     #     # And the temporary table will be called: "TMP_<table>"     #     #     # The prefix argument is optional. If you don't specify it, the temporary     # table will be called: "TMP".     #     #     # The name of the temporary table is case sensitive.     #     # That is why we use the uppercase prefix.     #     #     # Finally, you need to return the keyword arguments that you want to use in     # the insert_into function.     #     # In this case, we will return the keyword argument:     #     #     prefixes=['TMP']     #     # The "prefixes" keyword argument of the insert_into function will accept     # a list of prefixes.     #     # You need to return a dictionary of keyword arguments.     #     # If you want to return a list, you need to call it "prefix".     #     #     # As a side note, in the tests, we have to use keyword arguments for the     # insert_into function.     #     # That is because when the insert_into function is called with an argument     # and a keyword argument, the argument is used as the table name.     #     # See the documentation of the insert_into function to see how this works.     #     #     # Here, we use the "prefixes" keyword argument.     #     # We will use this for the "insert_into" function that we will write in the     # next exercise.     #     #     # The insert_into function can be used like this:     #     #     insert_into(table, **paradox_temp_table_keyword_args)     #     # But if you prefer to call the insert_into function like this:     #     #     insert_into(table, prefixes=paradox_temp_table_keyword_args['prefixes'])     #     # You can do that.     #     #     # You are free to implement this however you want.     #     #     # Here are some suggestions:     #     # - Use a random string or a hash of the test name.     # - Make sure that the temporary table or view is created at the right scope.     # - The tests will fail if you use a temporary table.     # - Use a dictionary as return value.     #     #     #     # Canonical Python Solution     #     # return {"prefixes": ["TMP"]}     prefixes = String["TMP"]     return Dict(         "prefixes" => prefixes,     ) end

25048:function trapintegration(curve)     n = length(curve)     if n == 1         return 0.0     end     cumval = 0.0     for i in 1:n-1         x = curve[i][1]         y1 = curve[i][2]         y2 = curve[i+1][2]         x_next = curve[i+1][1]         deltax = abs(x_next - x)         deltay = (y2 + y1)         cumval += deltax * deltay / 2.0     end     return cumval end

25087:function is_lesser(a, b)     if typeof(a) != typeof(b)         return false     elseif a isa String && b isa String         return a == b     elseif a isa Bool && b isa Bool         return a == b     elseif a isa Array && b isa Array         for element in a             flag = false             for e in b                 if is_lesser(element, e)                     flag = true                     break                 end             end             if !flag                 return false             end         end         return true     elseif a isa Dict && b isa Dict         if is_lesser(collect(keys(a)), collect(keys(b)))             for key in keys(a)                 if !is_lesser(a[key], b[key])                     return false                 end             end             return true         end         return false     elseif a isa Int && b isa Int         return a <= b     elseif a isa Float64 && b isa Float64         return a <= b     end     return false end

25094:function _check_fastq_read(read, read_index)     errors = []     # the identifier line     identifier_line_number = read_index * 4     # the biopython iterator we use internally already takes care of     # the sequence identifier     if length(read[1]) < 2         msg = "ERROR on Line $identifier_line_number: The sequence identifier line was too short."         push!(errors, msg)     end     if read[1][1] != '@'         msg = "ERROR on Line $identifier_line_number: First line of a sequence does not begin with @"         push!(errors, msg)     end     # the raw sequence line     sequence_line_number = read_index * 4 + 1     sequence_len = length(read[2])     if sequence_len == 0         msg = "ERROR on Line $sequence_line_number: Raw Sequence is shorter than the min read length: 0"         push!(errors, msg)     end     # the plus line     plus_line_number = read_index * 4 + 2     # the biopython iterator does not include the plus line     # so skip this     #if read[2][0] != '+':     #    msg = ("ERROR on Line {}: Third line of a sequence does not begin with +".format(plus_line_number))     #    errors.append(msg)     # the quality string line     quality_line_number = read_index * 4 + 3     # the quality string is at position 2 in the tuple (not 3 because the plus     # line is omitted)     quality_len = length(read[3])     if quality_len != sequence_len         msg = "ERROR on Line $quality_line_number: Quality string length ($quality_len) does not equal raw sequence length ($sequence_len)"         push!(errors, msg)     end     return errors end

25194:function p_approx(a, rho, temperature)     if rho == 0         return 0     elseif rho == 1         return 1     end     b = [1.705e-8, -2.585e-6, 1.556e-4, -4.912e-3, 9.755e-2]     b2 = b[1]*a^5 + b[2]*a^4 + b[3]*a^3 + b[4]*a^2 + b[5]*a     alpha = b2/(1 + rho^3) + 0.0802*rho^2/(1 + 0.7787*rho^2)     return rho * temperature + alpha * a * rho^2 end

25221:function extractTwos(m)     # m is a positive integer. A tuple (s, d) of integers is returned     # such that m = (2 ** s) * d.     # Time Complexity O(log2(n))     # Space Complexity O(1)     # where n is the number of bits in m.     # this way is cleaner but it's more expensive.     if m == 0         return 0, 0     end     if m == 1         return 1, 1     end     s = 0     while m & 1 == 0         s += 1         m >>= 1     end     return s, m end

25225:function undistort_division(u_tilde, v_tilde, kappa)     # This function transforms the distorted image plane coordinates into undistorted image plane coordinates     # if the division model is used.     # u_tilde and v_tilde are in camera coordinates, usually in meters, at a distance of one focal length     # from the center of projection.     r_tilde_squared = (u_tilde^2 + v_tilde^2)     # Compute the radial distortion scaling factor     scaling = 1 / (1 + kappa*r_tilde_squared)     # Finally, transform the coordinates using the scaling factors     u = scaling * u_tilde     v = scaling * v_tilde     return u, v end

25386:function __compress(list_events)     compress_dict = Dict{Any,Any}()     i = 1     while i <= length(list_events)         # create a new event where keys and values are compressed         comp_ev = Dict{Any,Any}()         for k in keys(list_events[i])             # check if the key has already been instantiated.             # in that case, use the current instantiation.             if k ∉ keys(compress_dict)                 compress_dict[k] = k             else                 k = compress_dict[k]             end             # check if the value has already been instantiated.             # in that case, use the current instantiation             if list_events[i][k] ∉ keys(compress_dict)                 compress_dict[list_events[i][k]] = list_events[i][k]             else                 list_events[i][k] = compress_dict[list_events[i][k]]             end             # saves the compressed keys and values in the dictionary             comp_ev[k] = list_events[i][k]         end         list_events[i] = comp_ev         i += 1     end     return list_events end

25415:function smallest_mult(upper)     primes = [2, 3]     n = primes[end] + 2     while n <= upper         is_prime = true         for p in primes             is_prime &= n % p > 0         end         if is_prime             push!(primes, n)         end         n += 2     end     factor_cnt = Dict{Int, Int}(p => 1 for p in primes)     for n in 1:upper         cur_fact_cnt = Dict{Int, Int}()         while n > 1             for p in primes                 if n % p == 0                     if p in keys(cur_fact_cnt)                         cur_fact_cnt[p] += 1                     else                         cur_fact_cnt[p] = 1                     end                     n /= p                 end             end         end         for (fact, cnt) in cur_fact_cnt             factor_cnt[fact] = max(factor_cnt[fact], cnt)         end     end     num = 1     for (fact, cnt) in factor_cnt         num *= fact^cnt     end     return num end

25463:function sumstat(fp, fn, tp, tn)     # Sensitivity, recall, hit rate, or true positive rate (TPR)     tpr = tp / (tp + fn)     # Specificity, selectivity or true negative rate (TNR)     tnr = tn / (tn + fp)     # Precision or positive predictive value (PPV)     ppv = tp / (tp + fp)     # Negative predictive value (NPV)     npv = tn / (tn + fn)     # Miss rate or false negative rate (FNR)     fnr = fn / (fn + tp)     # Fall-out or false positive rate (FPR)     fpr = fp / (fp + tn)     # False discovery rate (FDR)     fdr = fp / (fp + tp)     # False omission rate (FOR)     for_ = fn / (fn + tn)     # Accuracy (ACC)     acc = (tp + tn) / (tp + tn + fp + fn)     return Dict(         # Terminology         "tpr" => tpr, # sensitivity, recall, hit rate         "tnr" => tnr, # specificity, selectivity         "ppv" => ppv, # precision         "npv" => npv,         "fnr" => fnr, # miss rate         "fpr" => fpr, # fall-out rate         "fdr" => fdr,         "for" => for_,         "acc" => acc,     ) end

25502:function is_valid(line)     # ca o linie sa fie valida trebuie sa fie scrisa corect     # ex: STANGA 10     # ex: DREAPTA 45     # ex: SUS 50     # ex: JOS 90     if length(line) == 0         return false     end     words = split(line)     # words reprezinta un array cu fiecare element reprezentand un cuvant din linia     # si atunci cand incepem sa verificam daca e cuvantul corect,     # vom verifica cuvantul cu prima litera     # in cazul nostru e stanga     if words[1] in ["stanga", "Stanga", "STANGA", "StAngA"]         # daca nu exista sau nu e numar         if length(words) < 2             return false         end         # verificam daca e numar         try             parse(Int, words[2])             return true         catch e             return false         end     end     if words[1] in ["dreapta", "Dreapta", "DREAPTA", "drEaPtA"]         # daca nu exista sau nu e numar         if length(words) < 2             return false         end         # verificam daca e numar         try             parse(Int, words[2])             return true         catch e             return false         end     end     if words[1] in ["sus", "Sus", "SUS", "SuS"]         # daca nu exista sau nu e numar         if length(words) < 2             return false         end         # verificam daca e numar         try             parse(Int, words[2])             return true         catch e             return false         end     end     if words[1] in ["jos", "Jos", "JOS", "JoS"]         # daca nu exista sau nu e numar         if length(words) < 2             return false         end         # verificam daca e numar         try             parse(Int, words[2])             return true         catch e             return false         end     end     return false end

25508:function cents_to_pitchbend(cents, pb_range)::Int64     # 8192 is the lowest value on the roli dashboard and corresponds to a semitone below C4     # 16384 is the highest value on the roli dashboard and corresponds to a semitone above C6     # cents is the number of semitones to bend up or down     # pb_range is the value set in the Roli Dashboard. This is either 0, +/- 1, or +/- 2     # multiplying by 200 scales the offset to a range of 0-16384, which corresponds to 0-2 semitones     pb = 8192 + 16384 * cents / (pb_range * 200)     if 0 > pb > 16383         @warn "warning: pitchbend range too small to bend $cents cents"     end     return max(0, min(16383, round(Int, pb))) end

25553:function inv(q, p)     t0, t1 = 0, 1     r0, r1 = p, q     while r1 > 0         q = div(r0, r1)         r = r0 - q * r1         r0, r1 = r1, r         t0, t1 = t1, t0 - q * t1     end     if r0 > 1         throw(ArgumentError("inverse element does not exist"))     end     if t0 < 0         t0 += p     end     return t0 end

25583:function scramble_soft(bits, seq)     if bits == 0x0000         return bits     end     scramble_size = length(seq)     if scramble_size <= 8         mask = (0x0001 << scramble_size) - 1     else         mask = 0x0000     end     scramble_bits = 0     for i in 1:length(seq)         bit = bits & (0x0001 << seq[i])         bit = bit >> (seq[i] - 1)         scramble_bits |= bit << (i - 1)     end     scramble_bits &= mask     return bits | ((scramble_bits << scramble_size) & ~mask) end

25599:function IoU(X, Y)     x1, y1, x2, y2 = X     x1a, y1a, x2a, y2a = Y     # get the overlap rectangle     overlap_x1 = max(x1, x1a)     overlap_y1 = max(y1, y1a)     overlap_x2 = min(x2, x2a)     overlap_y2 = min(y2, y2a)     # check if there is an overlap     if overlap_x1 < overlap_x2 && overlap_y1 < overlap_y2         overlap_area = (overlap_x2 - overlap_x1 + 1) * (overlap_y2 - overlap_y1 + 1)         area_x1 = (x2 - x1 + 1) * (y2 - y1 + 1)         area_x2 = (x2a - x1a + 1) * (y2a - y1a + 1)         return overlap_area / (area_x1 + area_x2 - overlap_area)     else         return 0.0     end end

25620:function constrained_path(path)     # base case: empty path     path == "" && return path     # make sure '..' doesn't escape from root     # this is done by exploiting the fact that abs_path("../..") == abs_path("..")     isabspath(path) && return path     # split path on '/'     dir_path = splitpath(path)     # return if root     length(dir_path) == 1 && return path     # otherwise, apply the canonical solution recursively     dirname = dir_path[1]     for i in 2:length(dir_path)         (dirname == "..") && return constrained_path(joinpath(dir_path[1:i-1]...))         dirname = joinpath(dirname, dir_path[i])     end     # if all went well, the input was canonical     return path end

25664:function iou(bbox1, bbox2)     x1, y1, x2, y2 = bbox1     x3, y3, x4, y4 = bbox2     w_overlap = min(x2, x4) - max(x1, x3)     h_overlap = min(y2, y4) - max(y1, y3)     area_overlap = max(0, w_overlap) * max(0, h_overlap)     w1 = x2 - x1 + 1     w2 = x4 - x3 + 1     h1 = y2 - y1 + 1     h2 = y4 - y3 + 1     area1 = w1 * h1     area2 = w2 * h2     area_union = area1 + area2 - area_overlap     if area_union == 0.0         return 0.0     else         return area_overlap / area_union     end end

25726:function sbox_inv(block)     # Assert input     @assert length(block) == 4     # Constant definitions     a = block[1]     b = block[2]     c = block[3]     d = block[4]     # First half of the inverse s-box     b = (b & c) ⊻ a     d = (d | b) ⊻ c     a = (a & d) ⊻ b     c = (a | b) ⊻ d     # Second half of the inverse s-box     b = (c & d) ⊻ a     d = (d | b) ⊻ c     a = (a & d) ⊻ b     c = (a | b) ⊻ d     return [a, b, c, d] end

25744:function fleiss_kappa(m)     # IDs of the tasks:     # t = range(len(m)) # the range of task IDs     t = 1:length(m)     # Number of categories:     k = length(m[1])     # Number of votes per task:     n = sum(m[1]) # the sum of all votes per task     # p[j] = proportion of all assignments to j-th category:     p = [sum(m[i][j] for i in t) / (n*length(t)) for j in 1:k]     # P[i] = proportion of all assignments to the i-th task:     P = [sum(m[i][j]^2 for j in 1:k) / (n*n) for i in t]     # Pm = mean of P[i]:     Pm = sum(P) / length(t)     # Pe = proportion of variance explained by P[i]:     Pe = sum((p[j]-Pm)^2 for j in 1:k)     # K = (Pm - Pe) / (1 - Pe)     K = (Pm - Pe) / (1 - Pe + 1e-30)     return K end

25775:function bb_intersection_over_union(boxA, boxB)     xA = max(boxA[1], boxB[1])     yA = max(boxA[2], boxB[2])     xB = min(boxA[3], boxB[3])     yB = min(boxA[4], boxB[4])     interArea = max(0, xB - xA + 1) * max(0, yB - yA + 1)     boxAArea = (boxA[3] - boxA[1] + 1) * (boxA[4] - boxA[2] + 1)     boxBArea = (boxB[3] - boxB[1] + 1) * (boxB[4] - boxB[2] + 1)     iou = interArea / float(boxAArea + boxBArea - interArea)     return iou end
