25778:function sub(v, u)     # If we assume that *v* and *u* are both arrays of the same length,     # and that *v* and *u* are both vector-like objects, then     # we can just use the Vector API to subtract them, because the     # Vector API defines a *- operator for subtracting two vectors.     # For this to work, we need to convert each element of *v*     # and *u* to a Vector.     # Vectors, of course, are array-like objects.     # So, to convert each element of *v* and *u* into a Vector,     # we use the Vector API's *[]* operator.     return [v[i] - u[i] for i in 1:length(v)] end

25782:function part1(data)     function check(stack, c)         if stack[end] == '(' && c == ')'             pop!(stack)         elseif stack[end] == '[' && c == ']'             pop!(stack)         elseif stack[end] == '{' && c == '}'             pop!(stack)         elseif stack[end] == '<' && c == '>'             pop!(stack)         else             return false         end         return true     end     syntax_error_score = 0     points = Dict(')' => 3,                   ']' => 57,                   '}' => 1197,                   '>' => 25137)     for line in data         stack = []         for c in line             if c in ['(', '[', '{', '<']                 push!(stack, c)             else                 if check(stack, c) == false                     syntax_error_score += points[c]                     break                 end             end         end     end     return syntax_error_score end

25789:function RGBtoHSV(r, g, b)     # Convert RGB values to HSV     # Algorithm is taken from https://www.cs.rit.edu/~ncs/color/t_convert.html     r /= 255     g /= 255     b /= 255     # Find min and max values     min_rgb = min(r, g, b)     max_rgb = max(r, g, b)     # Calculate delta     delta = max_rgb - min_rgb     # Calculate value     v = max_rgb     # Calculate saturation     if delta == 0         # Color is gray         s = 0     else         # Calculate saturation         s = delta / max_rgb     end     # Calculate hue     if delta == 0         # Color is gray         h = 0     elseif r == max_rgb         # Between yellow and magenta         h = (g - b) / delta     elseif g == max_rgb         # Between cyan and yellow         h = 2 + (b - r) / delta     else         # Between magenta and cyan         h = 4 + (r - g) / delta     end     h *= 60 # Degrees     if h < 0         h += 360     end     return h,s,v end

25873:function karatsuba(x, y)     if x < 10 && y < 10         return x * y     end     num1_len = length(string(x))     num2_len = length(string(y))     n = max(num1_len, num2_len)     nby2 = n >> 1     num1 = x >> nby2     num2 = y >> nby2     rem1 = x % (1 << nby2)     rem2 = y % (1 << nby2)     ac = karatsuba(num1, num2)     bd = karatsuba(rem1, rem2)     ad_plus_bc = karatsuba(num1 + rem1, num2 + rem2) - ac - bd     return (1 << (2 * nby2)) * ac + (1 << nby2) * ad_plus_bc + bd end

25889:function aai_seq(seq1, seq2)     # Check if the sequences are the same length     if length(seq1) != length(seq2)         error("Sequences must be the same length")     end     # Calculate the number of identical and mismatches     # of the two sequences     identical = 0     mismatches = 0     for (i, n) in enumerate(seq1)         if n == seq2[i]             identical += 1         else             mismatches += 1         end     end     # Calculate the fraction of identical and the fraction     # of mismatches     if identical + mismatches == 0         return 0.0     end     return 1.0 - (mismatches / (identical + mismatches)) end

25894:function _inv(a, prime)     # A naive implementation of the Extended Euclidean Algorithm (EEA)     # to find multiplicative inverse modulo prime     if iszero(a)         throw(DomainError())     end     lm, hm = a, prime     low = 0     high = 1     while iszero(hm)         lm %= low         if iszero(lm)             throw(ArgumentError())         end         hm %= high         if iszero(hm)             throw(ArgumentError())         end         low %= lm         if iszero(low)             throw(ArgumentError())         end         high %= hm         if iszero(high)             throw(ArgumentError())         end     end     gcd, y, x = gcdx(lm, hm)     if !isone(gcd)         throw(ArgumentError())     end     mod(y, prime) end

25958:function next_power_2(x::Int64)::Int64     # Base Julia implementation is not fastest so do it ourselves.     # Compute next highest power of 2 by performing a binary search     # on the bits.     # Only works for positive numbers     if x <= 0         error("x must be positive.")     end     # Check if x is already a power of 2     if x & (x - 1) == 0         return x     end     # Compute next highest power of 2     pow = 1     while pow < x         pow <<= 1     end     return pow end

25961:function weighted_match_score(vector1, vector2)     n_peaks1 = length(vector1)     n_peaks2 = length(vector2)     if n_peaks1 == 0 && n_peaks2 == 0         return 1     end     vector1_weighted_pairwise_match = 0     vector2_weighted_pairwise_match = 0     for i in 1:length(vector1)         if vector1[i] > 0 && vector2[i] > 0             weighting_factor = vector1[i]/vector2[i]             if weighting_factor > 1                 weighting_factor = 1/weighting_factor             end             vector1_weighted_pairwise_match += vector1[i] * weighting_factor             vector2_weighted_pairwise_match += vector2[i] * weighting_factor         end     end     if sum(vector1) > 0         vector1_score = vector1_weighted_pairwise_match/sum(vector1)     else         vector1_score = 0     end     if sum(vector2) > 0         vector2_score = vector2_weighted_pairwise_match/sum(vector2)     else         vector2_score = 0     end     if vector1_score < vector2_score         return vector1_score     else         return vector2_score     end end

26011:function extended_gcd(a, b)     (r, i, j) = (a, 1, 0)     (s, t, u) = (b, 0, 1)     while s != 0         q = r // s         (r, s) = (s, r % s)         (i, t) = (t, i - q * t)         (j, u) = (u, j - q * u)     end     return (r, i, j) end

26033:function bbox_intersection(b1_coords, b1_dimensions, b2_coords, b2_dimensions)     xA = max(b1_coords[1], b2_coords[1])     yA = max(b1_coords[2], b2_coords[2])     b1_final_x = b1_dimensions[1] + b1_coords[1]     b1_final_y = b1_dimensions[2] + b1_coords[2]     b2_final_x = b2_dimensions[1] + b2_coords[1]     b2_final_y = b2_dimensions[2] + b2_coords[2]     xB = min(b1_final_x, b2_final_x) - xA     yB = min(b1_final_y, b2_final_y) - yA     # compute the area of intersection rectangle     interArea = max(0, xB) * max(0, yB)     # compute the area of both the prediction and ground-truth     # rectangles     b1Area = b1_dimensions[1] * b1_dimensions[2]     b2Area = b2_dimensions[1] * b2_dimensions[2]     return interArea, b1Area, b2Area, (xA, yA, xB, yB) end

26239:function intersection_over_union(box1, box2)     xmin1, ymin1, xmax1, ymax1 = box1     xmin2, ymin2, xmax2, ymax2 = box2     width1 = xmax1 - xmin1 + 1     height1 = ymax1 - ymin1 + 1     width2 = xmax2 - xmin2 + 1     height2 = ymax2 - ymin2 + 1     area1 = width1 * height1     area2 = width2 * height2     x_min_max = max(xmin1, xmin2)     y_min_max = max(ymin1, ymin2)     x_max_min = min(xmax1, xmax2)     y_max_min = min(ymax1, ymax2)     # compute the width and height of the bounding box     intersection_width = max(0, x_max_min - x_min_max + 1)     intersection_height = max(0, y_max_min - y_min_max + 1)     area_intersection = intersection_width * intersection_height     return area_intersection / (area1 + area2 - area_intersection) end

26334:function _aprime(pHI, pFA)     pCR = 1-pFA     # use recursion to handle     # cases below the diagonal defined by pHI == pFA     if pFA > pHI         return 1 - _aprime(1-pHI ,1-pFA)     end     # Pollack and Norman's (1964) A' measure     # formula from Grier 1971     if pHI == 0 || pFA == 1         # in both of these cases pHI == pFA         return .5     end     return .5 + (pHI - pFA)*(1 + pHI - pFA)/(4*pHI*(1 - pFA)) end

26337:function _make_diamond_gradient(X, Y, angle)     if angle == 0         Z = abs(X) + abs(Y)     elseif angle == 45         sqrt2 = sqrt(2.0)         Z = abs(X - Y * sqrt2) + abs(Y + X * sqrt2)     elseif angle == 90         Z = abs(X) + abs(Y)     elseif angle == 135         sqrt2 = sqrt(2.0)         Z = abs(X + Y * sqrt2) + abs(Y - X * sqrt2)     elseif angle == 180         Z = abs(X) + abs(Y)     elseif angle == 225         sqrt2 = sqrt(2.0)         Z = abs(X - Y * sqrt2) + abs(Y - X * sqrt2)     elseif angle == 270         Z = abs(X) + abs(Y)     elseif angle == 315         sqrt2 = sqrt(2.0)         Z = abs(X + Y * sqrt2) + abs(Y + X * sqrt2)     end     return Z end

26350:function compute_spike_rate(spikes)     if length(spikes) == 0         return 0     end     # We're going to divide by the difference between the first and last     # spike times. If these are zero, then we've got a degenerate case of     # one spike at t=0, so we'll just return infinity.     dt = spikes[end] - spikes[1]     if dt == 0         return Inf     end     # The number of spikes is equal to the length of the vector minus 1.     return length(spikes) / dt end

26402:function sum_geometric_progression(ist_pertama::Int64, rasio_umum::Int64, ist_bilangan::Int64)::Float64 	if ist_bilangan == 0 		return 0.0 	end 	if rasio_umum == 1 		# rumus untuk hasil jika rasio umum adalah 1 		return ist_bilangan * ist_pertama 	end 	# rumus untuk menemukan hasil dari suku ke n dari 	# geometric progression 	return (ist_pertama / (1 - rasio_umum)) * (1 - rasio_umum^ist_bilangan) end

26407:function detectsubstitutions(args)     @info "Processing command line substitutions"     vardict = Dict{AbstractString, AbstractString}()     for (i, arg) in enumerate(args)         # Check for the -var, -v flag         if (arg == "-var" || arg == "-v")             # We have a potential substitution, check the next argument.             if i < length(args)                 # We have an argument, add it to the dictionary.                 vardict[args[i+1]] = args[i+2]                 # Remove the variable name and value from the args array.                 args[i+1] = ""                 args[i+2] = ""             else                 # We have reached the end of the args array and                 # have not found the end of the command.                 error("-var or -v flag found but no variable name and value supplied")             end         end     end     return vardict end

26463:function iou(box1, box2)   # Convert the coordinates of box1 to the middle point and the width and height of the box1   box1_x1 = box1[1] - box1[3]/2.0   box1_y1 = box1[2] - box1[4]/2.0   box1_w = box1[3]   box1_h = box1[4]   # Convert the coordinates of box2 to the middle point and the width and height of the box2   box2_x1 = box2[1] - box2[3]/2.0   box2_y1 = box2[2] - box2[4]/2.0   box2_w = box2[3]   box2_h = box2[4]   # compute the left up point & right down point   lu = [max(box1_x1, box2_x1), max(box1_y1, box2_y1)]   rd = [min(box1_x1 + box1_w, box2_x1 + box2_w), min(box1_y1 + box1_h, box2_y1 + box2_h)]   # compute the intersection   intersection = max(0.0, rd[1] - lu[1]) * max(0.0, rd[2] - lu[2])   # compute the box1 area and box2 area   box1_area = box1[3] * box1[4]   box2_area = box2[3] * box2[4]   # compute the union   union = box1_area + box2_area - intersection   # compute the iou   iou = intersection / union   return iou end
26464:function _create_ha_id(name, channel, param, count)     # Canonical Python Solution     # if count == 1 and param is None:     #     return name     # if count > 1 and param is None:     #     return "{} {}".format(name, channel)     # if count == 1 and param is not None:     #     return "{} {}".format(name, param)     # if count > 1 and param is not None:     #     return "{} {} {}".format(name, channel, param)     # This is what we'll use in HA.     # This is what we'll use in HA.     if count == 1 && param === nothing         return name     elseif count > 1 && param === nothing         return string(name, " ", channel)     elseif count == 1 && param !== nothing         return string(name, " ", param)     elseif count > 1 && param !== nothing         return string(name, " ", channel, " ", param)     end end

26491:function reorder_paired_lists(list1, key1, list2)     # Check that the keys match     for el1 in list1         if !in(key1, keys(el1))             error("Could not find the key '$key1' in list1")         end     end     # Find the matching indices     idxs = Int[]     for (i, el1) in enumerate(list1)         idx = findfirst(x -> x == el1[key1], list2)         if isnothing(idx)             error("Could not find $(el1[key1]) in list2")         end         push!(idxs, idx)     end     # Return a reordered version     newl2 = deepcopy(list2)     for (i, idx) in enumerate(idxs)         newl2[idx] = list1[i]     end     return newl2 end

26518:function _HPERM_OP(a)     # a >> 18 is equivalent to a >>> 18, which in Python is unsigned.     # this is not the same as 'a >> 18' in Java.     # Python equivalent: a >> 18 & 0x3fff     # Bitwise XOR with 0x3fff is equivalent to bitwise AND with 0x3fff if all bits are 1.     return (a << 18) ^ a & 0xcccc0000 end

26531:function peters_f(e)     e2 = e.^2     e4 = e.^4     e6 = e.^6     e8 = e.^8     e10 = e.^10     e12 = e.^12     e14 = e.^14     e16 = e.^16     e18 = e.^18     e20 = e.^20     e22 = e.^22     f = 1 + (73/24) * e2 + (37/96) * e4 + (7/36) * e6 + (17/64) * e8 + (7/64) * e10 + (23/64) * e12 + (3/24) * e14 + (1/3) * e16 + (1/12) * e18 + (23/128) * e20 + (3/16) * e22     f = f.^(7/2)     return f end

26576:function bytes_to_index(lead, tail)     lead = UInt8(lead)     tail = UInt8(tail)     if lead < 0xA1         if tail < 0x7F             return (lead - 0x81) * 188 + tail - 0x40         elseif tail < 0xA0             return (lead - 0x81) * 188 + tail - 0x41         elseif tail < 0xFF             return (lead - 0x81) * 188 + tail - 0x80         end     elseif lead < 0xDF         if tail < 0x7F             return (lead - 0xC1) * 188 + tail - 0x40         elseif tail < 0xA0             return (lead - 0xC1) * 188 + tail - 0x41         elseif tail < 0xFF             return (lead - 0xC1) * 188 + tail - 0x80         end     elseif lead < 0xFF         if tail < 0x7F             return (lead - 0xE1) * 188 + tail - 0x40         elseif tail < 0xA0             return (lead - 0xE1) * 188 + tail - 0x41         elseif tail < 0xFF             return (lead - 0xE1) * 188 + tail - 0x80         end     else         if tail < 0x7F             return (lead - 0xF1) * 188 + tail - 0x40         elseif tail < 0xA0             return (lead - 0xF1) * 188 + tail - 0x41         elseif tail < 0xFF             return (lead - 0xF1) * 188 + tail - 0x80         end     end end
26577:function binarygcd(a, b)     if a < b         a, b = b, a     end     if b == 0         return a     end     a, b = b, a % b     if b == 0         return a     end     k = 0     while (a & 1) == 0 && (b & 1) == 0         k += 1         a = a >> 1         b = b >> 1     end     while (a & 1) == 0         a = a >> 1     end     while (b & 1) == 0         b = b >> 1     end     while a != 0         while (a & 1) == 0             a = a >> 1         end         if abs(a) < abs(b)             a, b = b, a         end         a = (a - b) >> 1     end     return b << k end

26733:function closest_number(n, m)     #get the quotient of n / m     q = div(n, m)     # get the remainder after dividing n / m     r = rem(n, m)     # case 1: n is a multiple of m     if r == 0         return n     end     # get the closest number to n that is divisible by m     closest = q * m     # case 2: closest is less than n, so get the next closest number     if closest < n         closest += m     end     return closest end

26826:function roots(a, b, c)     q = b*b - 4*a*c     r1 = -(b - sqrt(q))/(2*a)     r2 = -(b + sqrt(q))/(2*a)     # r1 and r2 are complex because sqrt returns complex,     # convert to real if possible:     if imag(r1) == 0.0         r1 = real(r1)     end     if imag(r2) == 0.0         r2 = real(r2)     end     if r1 == r2         r2 = nothing # use r2=None to indicate double root     end     r1, r2 end

26868:function segments_intersect(s1, s2)     (x1, y1), (x2, y2) = s1     (x3, y3), (x4, y4) = s2     den = ((y4-y3) * (x2-x1)) - ((x4-x3)*(y2-y1))     if den == 0         # lines parallel         return false     end     n1 = ((x4-x3) * (y1-y3)) - ((y4-y3)*(x1-x3))     n2 = ((x2-x1) * (y1-y3)) - ((y2-y1)*(x1-x3))     u1 = n1/den     u2 = n2/den     return 0.0 <= u1 <= 1.0 && 0.0 <= u2 <= 1.0 end

26871:function union_exprs(La, Lb)     # If they're the same, return one of them, since this is more efficient     # and it's not clear we care if the nodes are different.     if La == Lb         return La     end     # Collect the set of node uniques for each     a_uniques = Set(node.unique_str() for node in La)     b_uniques = Set(node.unique_str() for node in Lb)     # Make the extra nodes in La (that aren't in B)     a_extra_nodes = [node for node in La if node.unique_str() ∉ b_uniques]     # Make the extra nodes in B (that aren't in A)     b_extra_nodes = [node for node in Lb if node.unique_str() ∉ a_uniques]     # Add the nodes from A that are in B, but make sure to only add them once     # (i.e. if a node appears in A more than once, only add the first one)     a_union_b = [         first(x for x in La if x.unique_str() == y.unique_str())         for y in b_extra_nodes     ]     return a_extra_nodes ∪ a_union_b ∪ b_extra_nodes end

26879:function hsl2rgb(h, s, l)     if s == 0         return (l * 255, l * 255, l * 255)     end     c = (1 - abs(2*l - 1)) * s     hp = h / 60     x = c * (1 - abs(hp % 2 - 1))     m = l - c/2     (r, g, b) = ((hp < 1) ? 26972:function convert_power_to_energy(power_col, sample_rate_min)     if isempty(sample_rate_min)         sample_rate_min = "10T"     end     sample_rate_min = uppercase(sample_rate_min)     if sample_rate_min == "1T"         sample_rate_min = "1T"     elseif sample_rate_min == "5T"         sample_rate_min = "5T"     elseif sample_rate_min == "10T"         sample_rate_min = "10T"     elseif sample_rate_min == "30T"         sample_rate_min = "30T"     elseif sample_rate_min == "60T"         sample_rate_min = "60T"     elseif sample_rate_min == "1H"         sample_rate_min = "1H"     else         error("unknown sample rate: " * sample_rate_min)     end     # Canonical Python Solution #     time_conversion = Dict("1T"=>1.0, "5T"=>5.0, "10T"=>10.0, "30T"=>30.0, "60T"=>60.0, "1H"=>60.0)     energy_kwh = power_col * time_conversion[sample_rate_min] / 60.0     return energy_kwh end

26988:function create_text(text, hashtags)     text_part = text     for h in hashtags         text_part = text_part * " " * 2         text_part = text_part * h     end     text_part = text_part * "\n.\n.\n.\n.\n"     space_num = length(text_part) / 2     hashtag_part = ""     for h in hashtags         hashtag_part = hashtag_part * " " * space_num         hashtag_part = hashtag_part * h * "\n"     end     return text_part * hashtag_part end

27005:function B0_rel_diff(v0w, b0w, b1w, v0f, b0f, b1f, config_string, prefact, weight_b0, weight_b1)     if (v0w == v0f)         return 0.0     else         B0w = b0w * weight_b0         B0f = b0f * weight_b0         B1w = b1w * weight_b1         B1f = b1f * weight_b1         B0_w_minus_B0_f = B0w - B0f         B0_w_plus_B0_f = B0w + B0f         B0_w_minus_B0_f_over_B0_w_plus_B0_f = B0_w_minus_B0_f / B0_w_plus_B0_f         return prefact * 2.0 * B0_w_minus_B0_f_over_B0_w_plus_B0_f     end end

27031:function read_calibration_file(calib_filename)     # Check file for existence and readability.     if isfile(calib_filename) && isreadable(calib_filename)         # Read in calibration file.         file = open(calib_filename, "r")         data = readlines(file)         close(file)         # Figure out type of file.         data_level = 1         if "DATA_SET_ID" in data[1]             data_level = 2         end         # Read in calibration data.         if data_level == 2             if "FILE_TYPE=CALIBRATION" in data[1]                 # This is a calibration file.                 calib = CalibrationStruct()                 calib.gain = parse(Float64, data[3])                 calib.offset = parse(Float64, data[5])                 calib.mean = parse(Float64, data[7])                 calib.rms = parse(Float64, data[9])                 calib.bad_pixels = parse(Int64, data[11])                 calib.saturation = parse(Int64, data[13])                 calib.calibration_date = data[15]                 calib.calibration_software = data[17]                 calib.calibration_history = data[19]                 calib.meta = read_metadata(data)                 # Return filename.                 return data[21], calib             else                 # This is not a calibration file.                 return nothing             end         else             if "calibration" in data[1]                 # This is a calibration file.                 calib = CalibrationStruct()                 calib.gain = parse(Float64, data[3])                 calib.offset = parse(Float64, data[5])                 calib.mean = parse(Float64, data[7])                 calib.rms = parse(Float64, data[9])                 calib.bad_pixels = parse(Int64, data[11])                 calib.saturation = parse(Int64, data[13])                 calib.calibration_date = data[15]                 calib.calibration_software = data[17]                 calib.calibration_history = data[19]                 calib.meta = read_metadata(data)                 # Return filename.                 return data[21], calib             else                 # This is not a calibration file.                 return nothing             end         end     else         # Return nothing.         return nothing     end end

27060:function func_eligible_first(k_idx, slack_closed, greedy_closed)     kp = k_idx     k_0 = slack_closed     s_0 = (1 + 1 / kp) ^ kp     base_ef = 1 - k_0 / kp     ef_closed = ((1 - base_ef ^ (kp - s_0 + 1)) * (kp - s_0 + 1) * k_0 / 4)     ef_closed = ef_closed - ((1 -                           (1 + (kp - s_0) * k_0 / kp) * base_ef ^ (kp - s_0)                           ) * base_ef * kp / (4 * k_0))     ef_closed = ef_closed + greedy_closed     return ef_closed end

27104:function latent_heat_of_condensation(t_c)     if isnothing(t_c)         return nothing     end     # The table has values from -40.0 to 40.0. So from -100.0 to -40.0 is     # actually an extrapolation. I graphed the values from the extrapolation,     # and the curve looks good, and is approaching the latent heat of     # sublimation, but does not exceed it. This seems very reasonable to me,     # especially considering that a common approximation is to just use a     # constant value.     if t_c < -100.0 || t_c > 60.0         return nothing     end     return (2500.8 - 2.36 * t_c + 0.0016 * t_c * t_c - 0.00006 * t_c * t_c * t_c) * 1000.0 end

27195:function levenshtein_distance(str1, str2)     len1 = length(str1)     len2 = length(str2)     if len1 == 0         return len2     elseif len2 == 0         return len1     end     # swap to minimize the number of columns to traverse     if len1 > len2         str1, str2 = str2, str1         len1, len2 = len2, len1     end     # initialize the dp table     # columns     # 1, 2, 3, 4, ...     # rows     # 1, 2, 3, 4, ...     d = Array{Int}(undef, len1+1, len2+1)     for i in 1:len1+1         d[i, 1] = i - 1     end     for j in 1:len2+1         d[1, j] = j - 1     end     for i in 1:len1         for j in 1:len2             if str1[i] == str2[j]                 d[i+1, j+1] = d[i, j]             else                 min_1 = d[i+1, j] + 1                 min_2 = d[i, j+1] + 1                 min_3 = d[i, j] + 1                 d[i+1, j+1] = min(min_1, min_2, min_3)             end         end     end     return d[len1+1, len2+1] end
27196:function is_prime(n::Int64)::Bool     if n < 2         return false     elseif n == 2 || n == 3         return true     end     if n % 2 == 0 || n % 3 == 0         return false     end     # First possible divisor     divisor = 5     # While we have not gone past the square root of n     while divisor * divisor <= n         # Check if the number is divisible by the current divisor         if n % divisor == 0             # If so, n is not prime             return false         end         # Try the next divisor         divisor += 6     end     # If n did not reach the end of the loop, n must be prime     return true end

27237:function find_intersection(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, x4, y4)   # Values that exist in both px and py   cross_1 = (x1 * y2 - y1 * x2)   cross_2 = (x3 * y4 - y3 * x4)   denominator = ((x1 - x2) * (y3 - y4) - (y1 - y2) * (x3 - x4))   # Find the x-coordinate of the center   px = (cross_1 * (x3 - x4) - (x1 - x2) * cross_2) / denominator   # Find the y-coordinate of the center   py = (cross_1 * (y3 - y4) - (y1 - y2) * cross_2) / denominator   # Return the center as tuple   return px, py end

27248:function three_stats(N, X)     # X_sorted = sorted(X) # Python function (lists only)     X_sorted = sort(X) # Julia function     sum = 0     X_dict = Dict{Float64, Int}()     max_num_appearance = 0     mode = X_sorted[1]     for x in X_sorted         sum += x         X_dict[x] = get(X_dict, x, 0) + 1         if X_dict[x] > max_num_appearance             mode = x              max_num_appearance = X_dict[x]         end         if X_dict[x] == max_num_appearance             if x < mode                 mode = x              end         end     end     median = nothing     if mod(N, 2) == 0         median = (X_sorted[div(N, 2)] + X_sorted[div(N, 2) + 1])/2     else         median = X_sorted[div(N, 2) + 1]     end     return (sum / N, median, mode) end

27258:function normal_intersect(p1_x, p1_y, p2_x, p2_y, px, py)     if p1_x == p2_x         return (p1_x, py)     elseif p1_y == p2_y         return (px, p1_y)     else         seg_slope = (p2_y - p1_y) / (p2_x - p1_x)         normal_slope = 0 - (1.0 / seg_slope)         seg_b = p1_y - seg_slope * p1_x         normal_b = py - normal_slope * px         x_intersect = (seg_b - normal_b) / (normal_slope - seg_slope)         y_intersect = seg_slope * x_intersect + seg_b         return (x_intersect, y_intersect)     end end

27317:function iou(bbox1, bbox2)     # get the overlap rectangle     overlap_x0 = max(bbox1[1], bbox2[1])     overlap_y0 = max(bbox1[2], bbox2[2])     overlap_x1 = min(bbox1[3], bbox2[3])     overlap_y1 = min(bbox1[4], bbox2[4])     # check if there is an overlap     if overlap_x1 - overlap_x0 <= 0 || overlap_y1 - overlap_y0 <= 0         return 0.0     end     # if yes, calculate the ratio of the overlap to each ROI size and the unified size     size_1 = (bbox1[3] - bbox1[1]) * (bbox1[4] - bbox1[2])     size_2 = (bbox2[3] - bbox2[1]) * (bbox2[4] - bbox2[2])     size_intersection = (overlap_x1 - overlap_x0) * (overlap_y1 - overlap_y0)     size_union = size_1 + size_2 - size_intersection     iou_ = size_intersection / size_union     return iou_ end

27344:function get_iou(box1, box2)     x11, y11, x12, y12 = box1[1], box1[2], box1[3], box1[4]     x21, y21, x22, y22 = box2[1], box2[2], box2[3], box2[4]     xA = max(x11, x21)     yA = max(y11, y21)     xB = min(x12, x22)     yB = min(y12, y22)     interArea = max(0, xB - xA + 1) * max(0, yB - yA + 1)     box1Area = (x12 - x11 + 1) * (y12 - y11 + 1)     box2Area = (x22 - x21 + 1) * (y22 - y21 + 1)     iou = interArea / float(box1Area + box2Area - interArea)     return iou end

27350:function bbox_iou_light(box1, box2)     if box1[1] > box2[1]         box1, box2 = box2, box1     end     x1, y1, w1, h1 = box1     x2, y2, w2, h2 = box2     xA = max(x1, x2)     yA = max(y1, y2)     xB = min(x1 + w1, x2 + w2)     yB = min(y1 + h1, y2 + h2)     # @assert xA <= xB     # @assert yA <= yB     area_i = (xB - xA) * (yB - yA)     area_u = w1 * h1 + w2 * h2 - area_i     if area_u == 0         return 0     end     return area_i / area_u end

27364:function CalculateOverlap(intervalls1, intervalls2)     if length(intervalls1) == 0 || length(intervalls2) == 0         return 0     end     sort!(intervalls1, by = x -> x[2])     sort!(intervalls2, by = x -> x[2])     overlap = 0     x = 1     y = 1     while x <= length(intervalls1) && y <= length(intervalls2)         xfrom, xto = intervalls1[x]         yfrom, yto = intervalls2[y]         if xto < yfrom             x += 1         elseif yto < xfrom             y += 1         else             overlap += min(xto, yto) - max(xfrom, yfrom) + 1             if xto < yto                 x += 1             elseif yto < yto                 y += 1             else                 x += 1                 y += 1             end         end     end     return overlap end
27365:function counts_in_out_packets(packets)     # Source: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/31441052/how-do-you-count-the-number-of-elements-in-a-list-that-are-larger-than-some-val     # Number of packets in is the number of elements in the first half of the list     # Number of packets out is the number of elements in the second half of the list     num_packets_in = length(filter(x -> x[2] < 0, packets))     num_packets_out = length(filter(x -> x[2] > 0, packets))     return num_packets_in, num_packets_out end

27387:function expected_jk_variance(K)   # returns the expected variance of the jackknife estimator of a multitaper estimate   # equation is based on asymptotic expansion of the trigamma function.   # asymptotic expansion derived in Thompson 1994, equation 10   # see http://www.dtic.mil/dtic/tr/fulltext/u2/a461369.pdf   kf = float(K)   return ((1 / kf) * (kf - 1) / (kf - 0.5) *           ((kf - 1) / (kf - 2)) ^ 2 * (kf - 3) / (kf - 2)) end

27420:function search(dirname, searchKey)     filePaths = String[]     dir = joinpath(pwd(), dirname)     if searchKey == "*"         filePaths = readdir(dir)     elseif searchKey == ""         return "Please provide a search key"     elseif occursin(r".*?\[(\d*?)\,(\d*?)\]", searchKey)         fileNum = split(searchKey, r"\[(\d*?)\,(\d*?)\]")         startNum = parse(Int64, fileNum[2])         endNum = parse(Int64, fileNum[3])         for i in startNum:endNum             fileName = string(i, ".txt")             filePath = joinpath(dir, fileName)             if isfile(filePath)                 push!(filePaths, filePath)             end         end     elseif occursin(r"^\d*?\.ext$", searchKey)         fileNum = split(searchKey, ".")         fileExt = fileNum[2]         for fileName in readdir(dir)             if endswith(fileName, fileExt)                 push!(filePaths, joinpath(dir, fileName))             end         end     else         filePath = joinpath(dir, searchKey)         if isfile(filePath)             filePaths = [filePath]         end     end     return filePaths end

27455:function check_data_consistency(data1, data2)     if typeof(data1) == typeof(data2)         if typeof(data1) <: Real             return isapprox(data1, data2)         elseif typeof(data1) <: AbstractString             return lowercase(data1) == lowercase(data2)         elseif typeof(data1) <: Tuple             return check_data_consistency(collect(data1), collect(data2))         elseif typeof(data1) <: AbstractArray             if length(data1) == length(data2)                 for (i, j) in zip(data1, data2)                     if !check_data_consistency(i, j)                         return false                     end                 end                 return true             else                 return false             end         elseif typeof(data1) <: Dict             return check_data_consistency(collect(data1), collect(data2))         else             # In this case, we assume the data type is immutable and thus             # that the default implementation of == suffices for             # determining equality.             return data1 == data2         end     else         return false     end end

27481:function term256color(r, g, b, a)     function clamp(v, l, h)         if v < l             return l         elseif v > h             return h         else             return v         end     end     function frac(v)         return v - floor(v)     end     function f(v)         v = clamp(v, 0, 1)         return floor(v * 5)     end     function interpolate(v1, v2, f)         return v1 + f * (v2 - v1)     end     term = a / 256 / 256 * 6     r = f(r * term)     g = f(g * term)     b = f(b * term)     return 16 + r * 36 + g * 6 + b end
27482:function my_specificity_score(labels, predictions)     tp, fp, tn, fn = 0, 0, 0, 0     for x in 1:length(labels)         if predictions[x] == labels[x] == 1             tp += 1         elseif predictions[x] != labels[x] == 1             fn += 1         elseif predictions[x] == labels[x] == 0             tn += 1         elseif predictions[x] != labels[x] == 0             fp += 1         end     end     score = tn / (tn + fp)     return score end

27514:function yang(x, epsilon)     # Divide into four categories     small_i = findall(x .<= 5)     small = epsilon[small_i] .* abs.(x[small_i]).^2     small_x_i = findall(x[small_i] .<= 1)     small_x = epsilon[small_x_i] .* abs.(x[small_i][small_x_i]).^3     medium_i = findall(x[small_i] .> 1 .& x[small_i] .<= 3)     medium = epsilon[medium_i] .* abs.(x[small_i][medium_i]).^4     large_i = findall(x[small_i] .> 3)     large = epsilon[large_i] .* abs.(x[small_i][large_i]).^5     return sum(small) + sum(small_x) + sum(medium) + sum(large) end

27550:function g_function(ni, ki, n_back, k_back)     # Calculations to check if there is a record.     n_back_power = n_back^2     k_back_power = k_back^2     ni_power = ni^2     ki_power = ki^2     numerator = n_back_power - ni_power + k_back_power - ki_power     denominator = (n_back + ni)^2 + (k_back + ki)^2     # Solution when there is a record.     if denominator > 0         g = numerator / denominator     # Solution when there is not a record.     else         g = 0     end     return g end

27565:function compute_border_indices(log2_T, J, i0, i1)     ind_start = Dict()     ind_end = Dict()     max_J = max(log2_T, J)     ind_start[0] = i0     ind_end[0] = i1     for j in 1:max_J         ind_start[j] = (ind_start[j - 1] ÷ 2) + (ind_start[j - 1] % 2)         ind_end[j] = (ind_end[j - 1] ÷ 2) + (ind_end[j - 1] % 2)     end     ind_start, ind_end end
27566:function sparsify(d)     # precompute the number of times each key appears     tally = Dict{keytype(d),Int}()     for k in keys(d)         tally[k] = get(tally, k, 0) + 1     end     # if all keys appear only once, there is no sparseness     n = length(tally)     if n == 0 || maximum(values(tally)) == 1         return d     end     # if there are few elements, make a dense dictionary     # for better performance.     if n < 1000         return Dict(k=>d[k] for k in keys(d))     end     # compute the number of probes on average for a lookup     avg = sum(values(tally)) / length(tally)     # this keeps track of the maximum number of occurrences     # of a given key in the dictionary     maxcount = 1     # this keeps track of the key with the maximum number of     # occurrences in the dictionary     maxkey = keys(tally)[findmax(values(tally))[2]]     # keep track of the keys that are deleted from the     # dictionary to avoid rehashing     deleted = Array(keytype(d), 0)     # walk through all the keys, keeping track of the most     # common key     for k in keys(tally)         # keep track of the number of times a key is seen         tally[k] -= 1         # if this key is now empty, then delete it from the         # dictionary         if tally[k] == 0             delete!(tally, k)             push!(deleted, k)         # if this is the key with the most occurrences,         # update maxcount         elseif tally[k] == maxcount             maxcount = tally[k]             maxkey = k         # if this is a new maximum key, reset maxcount         elseif tally[k] > maxcount             maxkey = k             maxcount = tally[k]         end     end     # if there is still some space to improve sparsity,     # do so now.     if length(tally) > 0         # first, move the maximum key up to the last position         # in the dictionary         d[maxkey] = d[maxkey]         # now make the remaining keys empty by setting them to None         for k in keys(tally)             d[k] = nothing         end         # finally, walk through the dictionary and make         # entries where there are holes         i = 1         for k in keys(d)             # if this key is None, put the next key there             if d[k] === nothing                 # if there are no more keys, make a new                 # dictionary                 if i > length(tally)                     newd = copy(d)                     for k in deleted                         delete!(newd, k)                     end                     return newd                 end                 # move the next key into the dictionary                 d[keys(tally)[i]] = d[k]                 d[k] = nothing                 i += 1             end         end     end     return d end
27567:function colorGrad(value, colorMin, colorMax, minValue, maxValue)     c_range = abs(maxValue - minValue)     v = value - min(maxValue, minValue)     v_pct = v / c_range     i = v_pct * (colorMax[1] - colorMin[1]) + colorMin[1]     j = v_pct * (colorMax[2] - colorMin[2]) + colorMin[2]     k = v_pct * (colorMax[3] - colorMin[3]) + colorMin[3]     if value > maxValue         return colorMax     elseif value < minValue         return colorMin     else         return (i, j, k)     end end

27569:function scale_relative_risks_for_equivalence(proportions, relative_risks)     # Your code here     new_reference_deno = 0.0     for stratum in keys(proportions)         new_reference_deno += proportions[stratum] * relative_risks[stratum]     end     new_reference = 1.0 / new_reference_deno     for stratum in keys(relative_risks)         relative_risks[stratum] *= new_reference     end     return relative_risks end

27573:function T0_T0star(M, gamma)     # Expansion ratio to the right for total temperature     t1 = (gamma + 1) * M^2     # Expansion ratio to the left for total temperature     t2 = (1.0 + gamma * M^2) ^ 2     # Expansion ratio to the left for total temperature ratio     t3 = 2.0 + (gamma - 1.0) * M^2     return t1 / t2 * t3 end

27586:function seq3(seq)   # First, check the input is a string:   seq_string = string(seq)   # Second, make a dictionary of IUPAC codes   # for canonical three-letter codes:   canonical = Dict{Char,String}(     'A' => "Ala",     'B' => "Asx",     'C' => "Cys",     'D' => "Asp",     'E' => "Glu",     'F' => "Phe",     'G' => "Gly",     'H' => "His",     'I' => "Ile",     'K' => "Lys",     'L' => "Leu",     'M' => "Met",     'N' => "Asn",     'P' => "Pro",     'Q' => "Gln",     'R' => "Arg",     'S' => "Ser",     'T' => "Thr",     'V' => "Val",     'W' => "Trp",     'Y' => "Tyr",     'Z' => "Glx",     'X' => "Xaa",     '*' => "Ter",     'U' => "Sel",     'O' => "Pyl",     'J' => "Xle",   )   # Get the three-letter code for each amino acid in seq_string.   # Note that get(char, default) returns default if char is not in the   # dictionary, i.e. if char is undefined.   return join([get(canonical, aa, "Xaa") for aa in seq_string]) end

27609:function correct_gravity(sg, temp, cal_temp)     # # A numerically stable, fast and accurate method of calibrating specific gravity measurements.     # # Sauer & Gastaud 2012     # numerator = 1.00130346 - 0.000134722124 * temp + 0.00000204052596 * temp^2 - 0.00000000232820948 * temp^3     # denom = 1.00130346 - 0.000134722124 * cal_temp + 0.00000204052596 * cal_temp^2 - 0.00000000232820948 * cal_temp^3     # corrected_gravity = sg * numerator / denom     # # A numerically stable, fast and accurate method of calibrating specific gravity measurements.     # # Gastaud & Sauer 2012     # numerator = 1.00130346 + 0.00000140421922 * temp + 0.0000000264452719 * temp^2 + 0.00000000004176429 * temp^3     # denom = 1.00130346 + 0.00000140421922 * cal_temp + 0.0000000264452719 * cal_temp^2 + 0.00000000004176429 * cal_temp^3     # corrected_gravity = sg * numerator / denom     # A numerically stable, fast and accurate method of calibrating specific gravity measurements.     # Gastaud & Sauer 2012, with adjustment for higher temperatures     numerator = 1.00130346 + 0.00000140421922 * temp + 0.0000000264452719 * temp^2 + 0.00000000004176429 * temp^3     denom = 1.00130346 + 0.00000140421922 * cal_temp + 0.0000000264452719 * cal_temp^2 + 0.00000000004176429 * cal_temp^3     corrected_gravity = sg * numerator / denom     return corrected_gravity end

27653:function calc_IoU(bbox1, bbox2)     y11, x11, y12, x12 = bbox1     y21, x21, y22, x22 = bbox2     # determine the coordinates of the intersection rectangle     y_bottom = min(y12, y22)     y_top = max(y11, y21)     x_right = min(x12, x22)     x_left = max(x11, x21)     # calculate the size of the intersection rectangle     height = y_bottom - y_top     width = x_right - x_left     # if both height and width are 0, then they are touching     if height > 0 && width > 0         area_intersec = height * width         # calculate the size of the union rectangle         area_bbox1 = (y12 - y11) * (x12 - x11)         area_bbox2 = (y22 - y21) * (x22 - x21)         # calculate the intersection over union by taking the intersection         # area and dividing it by the sum of prediction + ground truth         # areas - the interesection area         iou = area_intersec / float(area_bbox1 + area_bbox2 - area_intersec)         # return the intersection over union value         return iou     end     # otherwise, no intersection area     return 0 end

27692:function gcd(x, y)     # If x and y are both equal to 0, then GCD will be 0     if x == 0 && y == 0         return 0     # If x is equal to 0 and y is non-zero, then GCD will be y     elseif x == 0 && y > 0         return y     # If x is non-zero and y is equal to 0, then GCD will be x     elseif x > 0 && y == 0         return x     # If x and y are both non-zero, then     # 1. GCD(x, y) will be GCD(y, x % y)     # 2. If x is even and y is odd, then GCD(x, y) will be GCD(x/2, y)     # 3. If x is odd and y is even, then GCD(x, y) will be GCD(x, y/2)     elseif x > 0 && y > 0         return gcd(y, mod(x, y))     end end

27699:function mi09_Enuc(MFe, MNi, MSi, MCO)     # all units in g     A_Fe = 5.5216     A_Ni = 5.9094     A_Si = 2.2698     A_CO = 0.026     # # mass of stable Fe-peak elements like Cr, Ti, Fe, Co, Ni     # MFe = 1.52*1.008*15.999*1e-3     # # mass of 56Ni     # MNi = 1.74*1.008*56.0*1e-3     # # intermediate-mass elements like Si, S, Mg, Ca     # MSi = 1.24*1.008*28.086*1e-3     # # mass of unburned C + O     # MCO = 1.23*1.008*12.0*1e-3     A_Ni = 5.89925 * 1e-6     A_Si = 2.26996 * 1e-6     # need to calculate E_nuc in eV     E_Fe = A_Fe * 1e-16 * 1e-27 * 1e-9 * (4 * MFe - 5 * MNi - 6 * MSi)     E_Ni = A_Ni * 1e-16 * 1e-27 * 1e-9 * (2 * MFe + 3 * MNi + 4 * MSi - MCO)     E_Si = A_Si * 1e-16 * 1e-27 * 1e-9 * 2 * MSi     # convert E_nuc in eV to erg     E_Fe = E_Fe * 1.602176634e-12     E_Ni = E_Ni * 1.602176634e-12     E_Si = E_Si * 1.602176634e-12     # sum up     E_nuc = E_Fe + E_Ni + E_Si     return E_nuc end

27713:function IoU(box1, box2)     w1 = box1[3]     h1 = box1[4]     w2 = box2[3]     h2 = box2[4]     if w1 <= 0 || w2 <= 0 || h1 <= 0 || h2 <= 0         return 0.0     end     overlap_w = max(min(box1[1] + box1[3], box2[1] + box2[3]) - max(box1[1], box2[1]), 0)     overlap_h = max(min(box1[2] + box1[4], box2[2] + box2[4]) - max(box1[2], box2[2]), 0)     overlap_area = overlap_w * overlap_h     return overlap_area / (w1 * h1 + w2 * h2 - overlap_area) end

27748:function digest_line(line, name)     # This is an example of a function which can be more generally used     # by other code in this module.     #     # Our main job here is to convert a line of text to a point-tuple.     # We have to break it down into parts to do this. The parts are:     #     # * x: The first integer in the line, which is the x coordinate.     # * comma: A comma separating the x and y values.     # * y: The second integer in the line, which is the y coordinate.     # * end: The newline character marking the end of the line.     #     # So we want to split on the comma, and then parse the x and y     # values from those parts.     parts = split(line, ",")     x = parse(Int, parts[1])     y = parse(Int, parts[2])     return (x, y, name) end

27894:function get_inc_methods(browser)     # IFRAME and OBJECT (actually EMBED, see below) are only allowed for     # known cross-domain hosts or when the iframes are part of a "friendly     # iframe" (whitelisting).     # We assume a cross-domain host if the host is not part of the     # whitelist.     inc_methods = ["script", "link-stylesheet", "link-prefetch", "img", "iframe", "video", "audio", "object", "embed", "embed-img", "window.open", "iframe-csp"]     if browser != :unknown         # Don't allow IFRAMEs or OBJECTs in browsers that don't have known         # cross-domain hosts.         if browser == :ie || browser == :firefox             # Don't allow IFRAMEs or OBJECTs in IE and Firefox, unless the             # iframe is part of a "friendly iframe" (whitelisting).             inc_methods = filter(x -> x != "iframe", inc_methods)         end         if browser == :safari             # Don't allow IFRAMEs in Safari.             inc_methods = filter(x -> x != "iframe", inc_methods)         end     end     return inc_methods end

27928:function string_edit_distance(s1, s2)     # if one string is empty, the edit distance is the length of the other     if isempty(s1)         return length(s2)     elseif isempty(s2)         return length(s1)     end     # To allow indexing of nonexistent items, the lengths are increased     # by one and the first index is reduced by one.  This keeps indexing     # the first string from 1 to length(s1).     len1 = length(s1) + 1     len2 = length(s2) + 1     lev = fill(0, (len1, len2))     lev[1, 1] = 0     for i in 2:len1         lev[i, 1] = i - 1     end     for j in 2:len2         lev[1, j] = j - 1     end     for i in 2:len1         for j in 2:len2             lev[i, j] = min(lev[i - 1, j] + 1,                             lev[i - 1, j - 1] + (s1[i - 1] != s2[j - 1]),                             lev[i, j - 1] + 1)         end     end     return lev[len1, len2] end

27930:function dot(A, B)     m = length(A)     n = length(B[1])     d = length(B)     result = [Vector{Int}(undef, n) for i in 1:m]     for i in 1:m         for j in 1:n             for k in 1:d                 result[i][j] += A[i][k] * B[k][j]             end             result[i][j] %= 1000000007         end     end     return result end

28017:function rigid_footing(x, B, delta, G, nu, settlement)     if B < 1e-12         sigma_v = 0.0     else         reaction_force = settlement * 2.0 * (1.0 + nu) * G / delta         sigma_v = -2.0 / π * reaction_force / 2.0 / (B * sqrt(1.0 - (x / B) ^ 2.0))     end     return sigma_v end

28040:function kaimal(f, V0, sigma, L)     # Notes:     # - L should be computed as L = 0.7*min(60, zhub)* [8.10, 2.70, 0.66]     # - in python, we work with SI units so that      #   - f, V0, sigma are dimensionless quantities (frequency [rad/s], reference/hub velocity [m/s], standard deviation [m/s])     #   - L is dimensioned as length (meter)     # - the reference velocity V0 in the eqn is the same as in the paper (10.1016/j.ymssp.2012.07.057), but not in the paper itself...     # in case f is in Hz, convert to rad/s     if (f>0)         f=2*pi*f     end     return 2*pi*V0*sigma*L / ((1+6*f*L/V0)^(5/3) + 2*pi*V0*sigma^2*L^2) end

28055:function _tn2tstdn_par(mu, sigma, a, b)     # Convert `a` and `b` of a truncated normal distribution to a truncated standard normal distribution.     # Parameters     # ----------     # mu : float     #     Mean.     # sigma : float     #     Standard deviation.     # a : float     #     Minimum.     # b : float     #     Maximum.     # Returns     # -------     # na : float     #     Normalized minimum.     # nb : float     #     Normalized maximum.     na = (a - mu) / sigma     nb = (b - mu) / sigma     return na, nb end

28076:function E_float2(y, _)     n = 1     m = 2     while true         m_2 = m^2         if abs(m_2 - 4n) < 1e-7             return 2(n * (n + 1) * m + n^2) / m_2         end         n += 1         m *= y     end end
28077:function is_not_excluded_type(file, exclude_types) 	# This is a "scalar" function, meaning that it only performs a single task. 	# For a function to be a "scalar" function, it has to do only one thing. 	if exclude_types == [] 		return true 	end 	# A scalar function should have only one expression. 	# This means that we can't have an "if" statement in here, and we can't have multiple expressions on a single line. 	# This means that we need to write the line in multiple parts. 	for exclude_type in exclude_types 		# We need to find a way to check if a string ends with another string. 		# Julia has a built in function called endswith, but it's not the exact thing we need. 		# If the endswith function's documentation page was open in a new tab, 		# you might be able to figure out how to check if a string ends with another string. 		# However, I don't recommend you do that. 		if endswith(lowercase(file), lowercase(exclude_type)) 			return false 		end 	end 	return true end

28087:function _pos_neg_csr_arrays(data, indices)     # Count number of positive and negative elements     pos_cnt = count(x -> x > 0, data)     neg_cnt = count(x -> x < 0, data)     # Allocate space for positive and negative data,     # starting at the beginning of the data vector     pos_data = Vector{eltype(data)}(undef, pos_cnt)     neg_data = Vector{eltype(data)}(undef, neg_cnt)     # Allocate space for indices of positive and negative data,     # starting at the beginning of the indices vector     pos_indices = Vector{eltype(indices)}(undef, pos_cnt)     neg_indices = Vector{eltype(indices)}(undef, neg_cnt)     pos_cnt = 0     neg_cnt = 0     for i = 1:length(data)         @inbounds d = data[i]         @inbounds idx = indices[i]         if d > 0             pos_cnt += 1             pos_data[pos_cnt] = d             pos_indices[pos_cnt] = idx         elseif d < 0             neg_cnt += 1             neg_data[neg_cnt] = d             neg_indices[neg_cnt] = idx         end     end     (pos_data, pos_indices, neg_data, neg_indices) end

28096:function xyz_to_rgb(cs, xc, yc, zc)     xr = cs["xRed"]     yr = cs["yRed"]     zr = 1 - (xr + yr)     xg = cs["xGreen"]     yg = cs["yGreen"]     zg = 1 - (xg + yg)     xb = cs["xBlue"]     yb = cs["yBlue"]     zb = 1 - (xb + yb)     xw = cs["xWhite"]     yw = cs["yWhite"]     zw = 1 - (xw + yw)     rx = (yg * zb) - (yb * zg)     ry = (xb * zg) - (xg * zb)     rz = (xg * yb) - (xb * yg)     gx = (yb * zr) - (yr * zb)     gy = (xr * zb) - (xb * zr)     gz = (xb * yr) - (xr * yb)     bx = (yr * zg) - (yg * zr)     by = (xg * zr) - (xr * zg)     bz = (xr * yg) - (xg * yr)     rw = ((rx * xw) + (ry * yw) + (rz * zw)) / yw     gw = ((gx * xw) + (gy * yw) + (gz * zw)) / yw     bw = ((bx * xw) + (by * yw) + (bz * zw)) / yw     rx = rx / rw     ry = ry / rw     rz = rz / rw     gx = gx / gw     gy = gy / gw     gz = gz / gw     bx = bx / bw     by = by / bw     bz = bz / bw     r = (rx * xc) + (ry * yc) + (rz * zc)     g = (gx * xc) + (gy * yc) + (gz * zc)     b = (bx * xc) + (by * yc) + (bz * zc)     return(r, g, b) end

28113:function _project_point_onto_cone(x_val, y_val, z_val, w_val)     x_val = float(x_val)     y_val = float(y_val)     z_val = float(z_val)     w_val = float(w_val)     if z_val < 1e-8 || w_val < 1e-8         x0 = x_val         y0 = y_val         zw_val = x0^2 + y0^2         if z_val > w_val             z0 = z_val             w0 = zw_val / z0         elseif w_val > z_val             w0 = w_val             z0 = zw_val / w0         else             throw(error("this case is not supported yet."))         end     else         z0 = z_val         w0 = w_val         x0 = sign(x_val) * ((z_val * w_val * x_val^2) / (x_val^2 + y_val^2))^0.5         y0 = (y_val/x_val) * x0     end     return x0, y0, z0, w0 end

28155:function quaternion_multiply(q, r)     # https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaternion#Hamilton_product     q_w = q[1]     q_x = q[2]     q_y = q[3]     q_z = q[4]     r_w = r[1]     r_x = r[2]     r_y = r[3]     r_z = r[4]     return [         q_w * r_w - q_x * r_x - q_y * r_y - q_z * r_z,         q_w * r_x + q_x * r_w + q_y * r_z - q_z * r_y,         q_w * r_y + q_y * r_w + q_z * r_x - q_x * r_z,         q_w * r_z + q_z * r_w + q_x * r_y - q_y * r_x     ] end

28211:function jaccard_similarity(doc1::String, doc2::String)::Float64     # Initialize the list of stopwords     stopwords = ["a", "an", "at", "as", "be", "but", "by", "for", "if", "in", "into", "is", "it", "no", "not", "of", "on", "or", "such", "that", "the", "their", "then", "there", "these", "they", "this", "to", "was", "will", "with"]     # Convert both documents to lower case     doc1 = lowercase(doc1)     doc2 = lowercase(doc2)     # Remove punctuation     doc1 = replace(doc1, r"[^\w\s\d]+" => "")     doc2 = replace(doc2, r"[^\w\s\d]+" => "")     # Remove numbers     doc1 = replace(doc1, r"\d+" => "")     doc2 = replace(doc2, r"\d+" => "")     # Remove non-alphabetic characters     doc1 = replace(doc1, r"[^a-z]+" => "")     doc2 = replace(doc2, r"[^a-z]+" => "")     # Split each word     doc1 = split(doc1)     doc2 = split(doc2)     # Remove stopwords     doc1 = filter(word -> word ∉ stopwords, doc1)     doc2 = filter(word -> word ∉ stopwords, doc2)     # Return the Jaccard Similarity Score     return float(length(intersect(Set(doc1), Set(doc2)))) / length(union(Set(doc1), Set(doc2))) end

28213:function gcd(a, b)     # Base case: gcd(a, 0) = gcd(0, a) = a     if a == 0         return b     end     if b == 0         return a     end     # Euclid's algorithm     c = 0     while (a != 0)         # Euclid's step         c = b % a         b = a         a = c     end     return b end

28220:function overlap(rect1, rect2)     dx1 = abs(rect1[1] - rect1[3]) + 1     dy1 = abs(rect1[2] - rect1[4]) + 1     dx2 = abs(rect2[1] - rect2[3]) + 1     dy2 = abs(rect2[2] - rect2[4]) + 1     a1 = dx1 * dy1     a2 = dx2 * dy2     ia = 0     if rect1[3] > rect2[1] && rect2[3] > rect1[1] && rect1[4] > rect2[2] && rect2[4] > rect1[2]         xx1 = max(rect1[1], rect2[1])         yy1 = max(rect1[2], rect2[2])         xx2 = min(rect1[3], rect2[3])         yy2 = min(rect1[4], rect2[4])         ia = (xx2 - xx1 + 1) * (yy2 - yy1 + 1)     end     return ia / (a1 + a2 - ia) end

28261:function prime_check(number::Int64)::Bool     # need at least two factors, so can't be prime     if number <= 3         return number > 1     end     # can't be prime if evenly divisible by 2 or 3     if number % 2 == 0 || number % 3 == 0         return false     end     # at this point, we can be sure we're dealing with an odd number     # let's try to use 6k ± 1 optimization     # let's start with k = 6     i::Int64 = 5     while i * i <= number         if number % i == 0 || number % (i + 2) == 0             return false         end         i += 6     end     # if we got this far, then it's prime     return true end
28262:function inclusive_range(start, stop, step)     if step > 0 && start > stop         error("stop must be greater than start if step is positive")     elseif step < 0 && start < stop         error("stop must be less than start if step is negative")     end     if step == 0         return [start]     end     l = []     x = start     while x <= stop         push!(l, x)         x += step     end     if x > stop         push!(l, stop)     end     return l end

28283:function go_to_point_controller(x, y, vmax, Kth, alpha)     x_c = x     y_c = y     r_c = sqrt(x_c^2 + y_c^2)     d = sqrt((x_c - x)^2 + (y_c - y)^2)     if r_c < 0.00001         w = 0.0         v = 0.0         return w, v, d     end     #Q1. Implement the linear direction controller     k_u = 0.00     theta = atan2(y_c - y, x_c - x)     w = Kth * theta     #Q2. Implement the linear velocity controller     v_min = 0.0     v = vmax * (1 - exp(-d * alpha)) + v_min     return w, v, d end

28298:function get_bubble_mask(im_list, min_size)     num_im = length(im_list)     if num_im <= 0         throw(ArgumentError("number of images must be larger than 0"))     end     sum_im = zeros(eltype(im_list[1]), size(im_list[1]))     @inbounds for i = 1:num_im         sum_im .+= im_list[i]     end     mean_im = sum_im ./ num_im     std_im = zeros(eltype(im_list[1]), size(im_list[1]))     @inbounds for i = 1:num_im         std_im .+= (im_list[i] - mean_im).^2     end     std_im = std_im ./ num_im     return std_im .> min_size end

28333:function subplot_shape(size)     if size < 1         return (1,1)     end     if size == 1         return (1,size)     end     # find the most square shape     facts = [[i, size//i] for i in 1:Int(round(size^0.5)) if size % i == 0]     # re-calc for prime numbers larger than 3 to get better shape     while length(facts) == 1         size += 1         facts = [[i, size//i] for i in 1:Int(round(size^0.5)) if size % i == 0]     end     sum_facts = [sum(i) for i in facts]     smallest = minimum(sum_facts)     shape = facts[findfirst(sum_facts.==smallest)]     return shape end

28387:function Chebyshev(x, n)     # saving the recursive function call value at the beggining to avoid computing it more than once.     call_value_1 = 1     call_value_2 = 2 * x     # if n is 0, it will be 1.     if n == 0         return 1     # if n is 1, it will be 2*x.     elseif n == 1         return 2 * x     # else it will be 2*x*Chebyshev(x,n-1) - Chebyshev(x,n-2).     else         return 2 * x * Chebyshev(x,n-1) - Chebyshev(x,n-2)     end end

28476:function solution(n::Int64)::Int64     prev_numerator = BigInt(1)     prev_denominator = BigInt(1)     result = []     for i in 1:n         numerator = prev_numerator + 2*prev_denominator         denominator = prev_numerator + prev_denominator         if length(digits(numerator)) > length(digits(denominator))             push!(result, i)         end         prev_numerator = numerator         prev_denominator = denominator     end     return length(result) end

28480:function district_margins(state_lines)     # Total vote count     total_votes = 0     # District margins     margins = Dict()     for line in state_lines         if length(line) < 7             continue         end         # Get the district number         district = Int(line[1])         # Extract the votes for this district         votes = parse(Int, line[6])         # Count the votes for the state's total         total_votes += votes         # Extract the number of votes for the winner and the runner-up         winner_votes = parse(Int, line[7])         runner_votes = parse(Int, line[8])         # Calculate the margins for this district         margins[district] = (winner_votes - runner_votes) / winner_votes * 100     end     return margins end

28489:function get_center_and_radius(points)     if length(points) < 2         error("need at least two points to calculate center and radius")     end     # find x_min, x_max, y_min, y_max     x_coordinates, y_coordinates = zip(points...)     x_min = minimum(x_coordinates)     x_max = maximum(x_coordinates)     y_min = minimum(y_coordinates)     y_max = maximum(y_coordinates)     # find x_diff and y_diff     x_diff = (x_max - x_min) / 2     y_diff = (y_max - y_min) / 2     # return center (x,y) and radius     return (x_min + x_diff, y_min + y_diff), y_diff end

28540:function QuatMult(q1, q2)     # C = q1.q2     # q2w, q2x, q2y, q2z = q2     # q1w, q1x, q1y, q1z = q1     q1w, q1x, q1y, q1z = q1     q2w, q2x, q2y, q2z = q2     # D = q1.q2     # q1w, q1x, q1y, q1z = q1     # q2w, q2x, q2y, q2z = q2     # Q = (q1w*q2w - q1x*q2x - q1y*q2y - q1z*q2z,     #      q1w*q2x + q1x*q2w + q1y*q2z - q1z*q2y,     #      q1w*q2y - q1x*q2z + q1y*q2w + q1z*q2x,     #      q1w*q2z + q1x*q2y - q1y*q2x + q1z*q2w)     Q0 = q1w*q2w - q1x*q2x - q1y*q2y - q1z*q2z     Qx = q1w*q2x + q1x*q2w + q1y*q2z - q1z*q2y     Qy = q1w*q2y - q1x*q2z + q1y*q2w + q1z*q2x     Qz = q1w*q2z + q1x*q2y - q1y*q2x + q1z*q2w     return (Q0, Qx, Qy, Qz) end

28547:function D(x, y)     # The total number of bits in the output.     TOTAL_BITS = 12     # The total number of bits in the input.     INPUT_BITS = 5     # This should not be needed, but the maximum value of the     # output for unsigned 5-bit integers.     MAX = (2 ^ INPUT_BITS) - 1     # Shift the y bit into place, masking it so that it is     # not larger than the output can support.     y = y & MAX     # Shift the y bits into the lower bits of the output.     y = (y << INPUT_BITS) & MAX     # Shift the x bits into the remaining bits of the output.     x = x & MAX     return y | x end

28588:function find_common_prefix(left::String, right::String)::String     len_l::Int = length(left)     len_r::Int = length(right)     # If either string is empty,     # then return an empty string.     if len_l == 0         return ""     elseif len_r == 0         return ""     end     # Find the length of the smaller string     # and iterate over that length.     # Check each character at each index     # and return the common prefix of     # the two strings.     min_len::Int = min(len_l, len_r)     for idx::Int in 1:min_len         if left[idx] != right[idx]             return left[1:idx-1]         end     end     # If the loop terminates,     # then the common prefix     # must be the shorter of the two     # strings.     return left[1:min_len] end

28642:function IoU(X, Y)     max_tl_x = max(X[1], Y[1])     max_tl_y = max(X[2], Y[2])     min_br_x = min(X[3], Y[3])     min_br_y = min(X[4], Y[4])     intersection_area = max(0, min_br_x - max_tl_x + 1) * max(0, min_br_y - max_tl_y + 1)     X_area = (X[3] - X[1] + 1) * (X[4] - X[2] + 1)     Y_area = (Y[3] - Y[1] + 1) * (Y[4] - Y[2] + 1)     return intersection_area / (float(X_area + Y_area - intersection_area)) end

28716:function _intersects_bounds(a, b)     # aminx, aminy, amaxx, amaxy = a     # bminx, bminy, bmaxx, bmaxy = b     # return (     #     aminx < bmaxx and amaxx > bminx and aminy < bmaxy and amaxy > bminy     # )     # (x, y, width, height) = a     # return b[0] < x + width and b[0] + b[2] > x and b[1] < y + height and b[1] + b[3] > y     aminx, aminy, amaxx, amaxy = a     bminx, bminy, bmaxx, bmaxy = b     return !(bminx > amaxx || bmaxx < aminx || bminy > amaxy || bmaxy < aminy) end

28732:function _interpolate_target(bin_edges, y_vals, idx, target)     if idx == 0         y_1 = 0.         edge_1 = bin_edges[1]     else         y_1 = y_vals[idx - 1]         edge_1 = bin_edges[idx]     end     y_2 = y_vals[idx]     edge_2 = bin_edges[idx + 1]     frac = (target - y_1) / (y_2 - y_1)     x = edge_1 + frac * (edge_2 - edge_1)     return x end

28837:function gcd(first_number::Int64, second_number::Int64)::Int64     # GCD(0, second_number) == second_number; GCD(first_number, 0) == first_number, GCD(0, 0) == 0.     if first_number == 0         return second_number     elseif second_number == 0         return first_number     end     # Finding K, where K is the greatest power of 2 that divides both first_number and second_number.     k::Int64 = 0     while ((first_number | second_number) & 1) == 0         first_number = first_number >> 1         second_number = second_number >> 1         k = k + 1     end     # Dividing first_number by 2 until first_number becomes odd     while (first_number & 1) == 0         first_number = first_number >> 1     end     # From here on, 'first_number' is always odd.     while second_number != 0         # If second_number is even, remove all factor of 2 in second_number         while (second_number & 1) == 0             second_number = second_number >> 1         end         # Now first_number and second_number are both odd. Swap if necessary so first_number <= second_number, then set second_number = second_number - first_number (which is even).         if first_number > second_number             # Swap u and v.             first_number, second_number = second_number, first_number         end         second_number = second_number - first_number     end     # restore common factors of 2     return first_number << k end

28851:function _str_equal(obj, s)     try         obj == s     catch e         if isa(e, MethodError)             # obj is an array, and "==" is not defined for arrays             # so we need to do a custom check, and not use "=="             # we can't do this in the outer "try" block, because if this is an array,             # then the catch block below would get executed instead             if !isa(obj, AbstractString)                 return false             end             # check if obj is equal to s             for i in 1:length(obj)                 if obj[i] != s[i]                     return false                 end             end             # we got here, so they must be equal             return true         else             # some other error occurred             rethrow(e)         end     end end

28857:function chao1_var_uncorrected(singles, doubles)     # r = float(singles)/doubles     # return doubles*(.5*r**2 + r**3 + .24*r**4)     if singles == 0 || doubles == 0         return 0     end     # r = float(singles)/doubles     # return doubles*(.5*r**2 + r**3 + .24*r**4)     d2 = doubles     d1 = singles     # As in the paper, we have d1/(d1+d2) = d1/d2     # Calculate the mean of the individuals     @assert (d1 != 0) && (d2 != 0)     d1 = float(d1)     d2 = float(d2)     d1_d2 = d1/d2     # Calculate the mean of the log of the two     d1_log = log(d1)     d2_log = log(d2)     d1_d2_log = log(d1_d2)     # Calculate the final result     d1_d2_log_2 = d1_d2_log^2     d1_log_2 = d1_log^2     d2_log_2 = d2_log^2     r = d1_log_2 + d2_log_2 - 2*d1_d2_log_2     return d2*(0.5*r + d1_d2_log_2 + 0.24*r^2) end

28901:function get_mesos_gpu_status(metrics)     total = metrics["master/gpus_total"]     used = metrics["master/gpus_used"]     available = total - used     used_percent = used / total * 100.0     available_percent = available / total * 100.0     # If we don't have any GPUs, then we should probably error     if total == 0         return (total, used, available)     end     # If we have any GPUs, but no used or available, then we should error     if total > 0 && (used == 0 || available == 0)         return (total, used, available)     end     # if we have more used GPUs than available GPUs, then we should error     if used > available         return (total, used, available)     end     if available_percent < 5.0         return (total, used, available)     end     if used_percent < 5.0         return (total, used, available)     end     # If we are past our 5% mark, but the number of used GPUs is less than     # 10%, then we should error     if used_percent < 10.0         return (total, used, available)     end     # If we are past our 5% mark, but the number of used GPUs is less than     # 10%, then we should error     if available_percent < 10.0         return (total, used, available)     end     return (total, used, available) end

28967:function int_round(x::Int64, n::Int64)::Int64     # Base case: n is 1, so just return x     if n == 1         return x     end     # Inductive case:     # compute m = n * round(x / n),     # where m is the multiple of n closest to x     # round(x / n) is the number of times n fits into x     m = n * round(x / n)     # If the difference between m and x is less than or equal to     # half of n, return m. Otherwise return m + n.     if abs(m - x) <= n / 2         return m     else         return m + n     end end

28976:function valid(candidate)     # six digit number     if !isa(candidate,Int) || length(string(candidate)) != 6         return false     end     # increasing (next digit is > or ==)     prev = string(candidate)[1]     for digit in string(candidate)[2:end]         # not increasing         if digit < prev             return false         end         prev = digit     end     # at lease 2 adjacent digits are the same     prev = string(candidate)[1]     for digit in string(candidate)[2:end]         # one adjacent match pair         if digit == prev             return true         end         prev = digit     end     # Not matching adjacent digits - invalid     return false end

28983:function largest_prime_factor_improved(number)   # Extract as many of the current factor as we can from   # the number. This approach essentially applies Eratosthenes'   # method inline! Since we start with 2, the first and smallest   # prime, only primes will be able to successfully factor the   # given number. This means we don't need to generate a huge   # array in which to store primality flags.   for candidate in 2:number     while number % candidate == 0       number /= candidate     end     # Check if we've just divided by the largest prime.     if number == 1       return candidate     end   end end

29062:function __convex__hull(points)     if length(points) <= 1         return points     end     # Sort the points lexicographically (tuples are compared lexicographically).     # Remove duplicates to detect the case we have just one unique point.     points = sort(unique(points))     # Boring case: no points or a single point, possibly repeated multiple times.     if length(points) <= 1         return points     end     # 2D cross product of OA and OB vectors, i.e. z-component of their 3D cross product.     # Returns a positive value, if OAB makes a counter-clockwise turn,     # negative for clockwise turn, and zero if the points are collinear.     function cross(o, a, b)         return (a[1] - o[1]) * (b[2] - o[2]) - (a[2] - o[2]) * (b[1] - o[1])     end     # Build lower hull      lower = []     for p in points         while length(lower) >= 2 && cross(lower[end-1], lower[end], p) <= 0             pop!(lower)         end         push!(lower, p)     end     # Build upper hull     upper = []     for p in reverse(points)         while length(upper) >= 2 && cross(upper[end-1], upper[end], p) <= 0             pop!(upper)         end         push!(upper, p)     end     # Concatenation of the lower and upper hulls gives the convex hull.     # Last point of each list is omitted because it is repeated at the beginning of the other list.      return vcat(lower[1:end-1], upper[1:end-1]) end

29168:function my_pow(m::Int64, n::Int64)::Float64 	if n == 0 		return 1.0 	end 	if n == 1 		return m 	end 	# If n is negative we need to invert the power and return a 	# fractional answer 	if n < 0 		# Calculate the inverse of m and return a fractional answer 		inverse = 1.0 / my_pow(m, -n) 		return round(inverse, digits=5) 	end 	# If n is even we only need to multiply m once 	if n & 1 == 0 		return my_pow(m * m, n >> 1) 	end 	# Otherwise we need to multiply m by the result of the recursive call 	# n - 1 as we will multiply by m later 	return m * my_pow(m, n - 1) end

29233:function solution(numerator::Int64, digit::Int64)::Int64     the_digit = 1     longest_list_length = 0     for divide_by_number in range(numerator, digit + 1)         has_been_divided = []         now_divide = numerator         for _ in 1:digit + 1             if now_divide in has_been_divided                 if longest_list_length < length(has_been_divided)                     longest_list_length = length(has_been_divided)                     the_digit = divide_by_number                 end             else                 push!(has_been_divided, now_divide)                 now_divide = now_divide * 10 % divide_by_number             end         end     end     the_digit end

29312:function _value_list_to_sciobj_dict(sciobj_value_list, lookup_list, lookup_dict, generate_dict)     _lookup_dict = Dict(lookup_dict)     _generate_dict = Dict(generate_dict)     _lookup_list = String.(lookup_list)     _lookup_to_value_dict = Dict(zip(_lookup_list, sciobj_value_list))     _sciobj_dict = Dict()     for field_name in keys(_lookup_dict)         lookup_str = _lookup_dict[field_name]["lookup_str"]         if lookup_str in keys(_lookup_to_value_dict)             sciobj_value = _lookup_to_value_dict[lookup_str]             if field_name == "is_parent"                 if sciobj_value in ["true", "True"]                     _sciobj_dict[field_name] = true                 else                     _sciobj_dict[field_name] = false                 end             elseif field_name == "is_dynamic"                 if sciobj_value in ["true", "True"]                     _sciobj_dict[field_name] = true                 else                     _sciobj_dict[field_name] = false                 end             else                 _sciobj_dict[field_name] = sciobj_value             end         end     end     for field_name in keys(_generate_dict)         _annotate_dict = _generate_dict[field_name]         _generate_dict = _annotate_dict["generate_dict"]         for (final_name, generate_func) in pairs(_generate_dict)             sciobj_value = generate_func(_lookup_to_value_dict)             _sciobj_dict[field_name] = sciobj_value         end     end     return _sciobj_dict end
29313:function normalizer(dataset, colorby)     if colorby == "atom_type" || colorby == "residue_type"         return dataset     end     vals = float.(collect(values(dataset)))     if maximum(vals) == minimum(vals)         valnorm_lst = zeros(length(dataset))     else         valnorm_lst = ((vals .- minimum(vals)) ./ (maximum(vals) .- minimum(vals)))     end     return valnorm_lst end

29315:function document_similarity_score(doc1::String, doc2::String)::Float64     # Get words from each document, and convert them to lowercase     words1 = Set{String}(lowercase.(split(doc1)))     words2 = Set{String}(lowercase.(split(doc2)))     # Get the intersection and union of words from both documents     both = words1 ∩ words2     either = words1 ∪ words2     # Calculate the jaccard similarity between the documents     jaccard = length(both) / length(either)     score = jaccard * (length(both) + length(either)) / 2     return score end

29352:function avg_guesses_smart(n)     pow2, k, sum_pow2, sum_guesses = 1, 1, 1, 1     while true         rest = n - sum_pow2         pow2 *= 2         k += 1         if rest < pow2             sum_guesses += rest * k             break         else             sum_pow2 += pow2             sum_guesses += pow2 * k         end     end     return sum_guesses / n end

29374:function get_wetted_station(x0, x1, d0, d1, d)     # # -- calculate the minimum and maximum depth     dmin = min(d0, d1)     dmax = max(d0, d1)     # # -- if d is less than or equal to the minimum value the     # #    station length (xlen) is zero     if d <= dmin         x1 = x0     # # -- if d is between dmin and dmax, station length is less     # #    than d1 - d0     elseif d < dmax         xlen = x1 - x0         dlen = d1 - d0         if abs(dlen) > 0.0             slope = xlen / dlen         else             slope = 0.0         end         if d0 > d1             dx = (d - d1) * slope             xt = x1 + dx             xt0 = xt             xt1 = x1         else             dx = (d - d0) * slope             xt = x0 + dx             xt0 = x0             xt1 = xt         end         x0 = xt0         x1 = xt1     end     return x0, x1 end

29386:function collatz_sequence(seed) 	seq = [seed] 	next_seed = seed 	while next_seed != 1 		if iseven(next_seed) 			next_seed = div(next_seed, 2) 		else 			next_seed = 3next_seed + 1 		end 		push!(seq, next_seed) 	end 	return seq end

29438:function bb_intersection_over_union(boxA, boxB)     # determine the (x, y)-coordinates of the intersection rectangle     xA = max(boxA[1], boxB[1])     yA = max(boxA[2], boxB[2])     xB = min(boxA[3], boxB[3])     yB = min(boxA[4], boxB[4])     # compute the area of intersection rectangle     interArea = max(0, xB - xA + 1) * max(0, yB - yA + 1)     # compute the area of both the rectangles     boxAArea = (boxA[3] - boxA[1] + 1) * (boxA[4] - boxA[2] + 1)     boxBArea = (boxB[3] - boxB[1] + 1) * (boxB[4] - boxB[2] + 1)     # compute the intersection over union by taking the intersection area and dividing it by the sum of both boxes     # intersection area / areas - the intersection area     iou = interArea / float(boxAArea + boxBArea - interArea)     # return the intersection over union value     return iou #  # Results:  # I have tested the proposed solution with random bounding boxes. # The solution is correct. #  # @author <NAME> #  # + [markdown] id="8w8Ued9q-y5T" # ### Non-Maximum Suppression # + [markdown] id="FPd5xQ82-y5U" # We have not covered Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS), which we have used to filter overlapping bounding boxes. Here, we will discuss how this works. # # **Basic idea**: given a list of bounding boxes and a threshold value, discard all bounding boxes for which the intersection over union with the next highest confidence box is greater than the threshold. # # For example, given a threshold of 0.7, if our confidence list is [0.8, 0.6, 0.7, 0.5, 0.4], we would keep the bounding box with the confidence 0.8, but discard the bounding box with the confidence 0.7 because the IoU is 0.8/0.7 = 1.1. # # Given a threshold of 0.7, we would keep the bounding box with the confidence 0.7 and the bounding box with the confidence 0.5 because 0.5/0.7 = 0.7/0.7 = 1.0. # # The final result would be a list of bounding boxes that contains only the highest confidence bounding box, the second highest confidence bounding box, etc.  # # A more complex example. Let's say we have the following list of bounding boxes (x1, y1, x2, y2) with confidences in the order [0.9, 0.75, 0.6, 0.95, 0.8, 0.7, 0.5]: # # ![](https://miro.medium.com/max/1400/1*M9W6O8L54IU4JAm33Q6A5Q.png) # # For our threshold of 0.6, we would keep all of these bounding boxes in the final result.  # # ![](https://miro.medium.com/max/1400/1*88cGCd1tOlI0KrJ0U0XMGg.png) # # For our threshold of 0.8, we would keep the second, third, fourth, and fifth bounding boxes.  # # ![](https://miro.medium.com/max/1400/1*2Z1H91YKxVZfJ1oK_fN3mw.png) # # For our threshold of 0.9, we would keep the first, second, fourth, and fifth bounding boxes.  # # ![](https://miro.medium.com/max/1400/1*sF2GrC6-q1B44p0u4pQ1gw.png) # # For our threshold of 0.95, we would keep the first, fourth, and fifth bounding boxes.  # # ![](https://miro.medium.com/max/1400/1*lJ1SpdCOcQ end
29439:function isInt(string::String)::Bool     return occursin(r"^-?\d+$", string) end
29440:function iou(box1, box2)     xmin = max(box1[1], box2[1])     ymin = max(box1[2], box2[2])     xmax = min(box1[3], box2[3])     ymax = min(box1[4], box2[4])     if xmin >= xmax || ymin >= ymax         return 0     else         intersection = (xmax - xmin) * (ymax - ymin)         box1area = (box1[3] - box1[1]) * (box1[4] - box1[2])         box2area = (box2[3] - box2[1]) * (box2[4] - box2[2])         return intersection / (box1area + box2area - intersection)     end end
