29460:function color_distance(c1, c2) 	@assert(length(c1) == 3) 	@assert(length(c2) == 3) 	# Convert to linear space 	r1, g1, b1 = c1 	r2, g2, b2 = c2 	# Convert to linear space 	r1_lin = r1^2.2 	g1_lin = g1^2.2 	b1_lin = b1^2.2 	r2_lin = r2^2.2 	g2_lin = g2^2.2 	b2_lin = b2^2.2 	# Convert to u'v' 	U = (r1_lin + g1_lin + b1_lin) / 3.0 	V = (r2_lin + g2_lin + b2_lin) / 3.0 	# Compute difference 	u_diff = r1_lin - r2_lin 	v_diff = g1_lin - g2_lin 	w_diff = b1_lin - b2_lin 	# Compute distance 	distance = u_diff * u_diff + v_diff * v_diff + w_diff * w_diff 	distance = sqrt(distance) 	# Convert from u'v' to L*a*b* 	distance = distance * 3.5355339059327377 	return distance end

29474:function score(slides, photos)     total_score = 0     for (prev, curr) in zip(slides, slides[1:end])         prev_tags = Set{String}()         for phot_id in prev             for tag in photos[phot_id]["tags"]                 push!(prev_tags, tag)             end         end         curr_tags = Set{String}()         for phot_id in curr             for tag in photos[phot_id]["tags"]                 push!(curr_tags, tag)             end         end         common_tags = intersect(prev_tags, curr_tags)         prev_curr = setdiff(prev_tags, common_tags)         curr_prev = setdiff(curr_tags, common_tags)         total_score += min(length(common_tags), length(prev_curr), length(curr_prev))     end     return total_score end

29543:function semifact2(n::Int64)::Int64 #=  This is the standard, straightforward Julia solution.  Notice the use of the 'return' keyword, which  indicates a value to be returned from the function  when the function completes. 29551:function _left_rotate(n, b)     # Ensure the type of b is integer     b = b % 32     # This makes sure that the original number is not affected by the shift     # >>> a = 0x00000001     # >>> a << 32     # 0     # >>> a >> 32     # 0     # >>> a |= 0xFFFFFFFF << 32     # 1     # >>> a     # 1     n = n | (n >> (32 - b))     return ((n << b) | (n >> (32 - b))) & 0xFFFFFFFF # Testing # >>> _left_rotate(0x00000001, 32) # 0x00000001 # >>> _left_rotate(0x00000001, 31) # 0x80000000 # >>> _left_rotate(0x00000001, 1) # 0x00000002 # >>> _left_rotate(0x00000001, 0) # 0x00000001 # >>> _left_rotate(0xFFFFFFFF, 0) # 0xFFFFFFFF # >>> _left_rotate(0xFFFFFFFF, 1) # 0xFFFFFFFE # >>> _left_rotate(0xFFFFFFFF, 31) # 0x7FFFFFFF # >>> _left_rotate(0xFFFFFFFF, 32) # 0xFFFFFFFF # >>> _left_rotate(0xFFFFFFFF, 33) # 0xFFFFFFFE # >>> _left_rotate(0x00000000, 1) # 0x00000000 # >>> _left_rotate(0x00000000, 0) # 0x00000000 end

29625:function iou(bbox1, bbox2)   x0_1 = bbox1[1]   y0_1 = bbox1[2]   x1_1 = bbox1[3]   y1_1 = bbox1[4]   x0_2 = bbox2[1]   y0_2 = bbox2[2]   x1_2 = bbox2[3]   y1_2 = bbox2[4]   #get the overlap rectangle   overlap_x0 = max(x0_1, x0_2)   overlap_y0 = max(y0_1, y0_2)   overlap_x1 = min(x1_1, x1_2)   overlap_y1 = min(y1_1, y1_2)   #check if there is an overlap   if overlap_x1 - overlap_x0 <= 0 || overlap_y1 - overlap_y0 <= 0     return 0   end   #if yes, calculate the ratio of the overlap to each ROI size and the unified size   size_1 = (x1_1 - x0_1)*(y1_1 - y0_1)   size_2 = (x1_2 - x0_2)*(y1_2 - y0_2)   size_intersection = (overlap_x1 - overlap_x0)*(overlap_y1 - overlap_y0)   size_union = size_1 + size_2 - size_intersection   return size_intersection / size_union end

29705:function head2pres(head, z, rref, grav, psurf)     # if z is not an array of length 1, i.e. it is not a meshgrid     if length(z) > 1         # compute z values of each row         z = z[:]         # compute z values of each column         z = z[:,:]     end     # Compute reference head values for each row of the array     href = z * grav * rref     # Compute the difference between head and reference head     dif = head - href     # Compute the pressure     pres = (psurf + dif * rref * grav) * 10^-6     return pres end

29822:function rgb2hsv(rgb)     r, g, b = rgb     maximum = max(r, g, b)     minimum = min(r, g, b)     delta = maximum - minimum     if maximum == 0         h = nothing         s = 0     else         s = delta / maximum         if delta == 0             h = nothing         else             if r == maximum                 h = (g - b) / delta             elseif g == maximum                 h = 2 + (b - r) / delta             else                 h = 4 + (r - g) / delta             end             h *= 60 # degrees             if h < 0                 h += 360             end         end     end     return (h, s, maximum) end
29823:function get_varinfo_from_table(discipline, parmcat, parmnum)     # This is a function to return the GRIB2 variable information given values of     # discipline, parmcat, and parmnum. This functions allows for all arguments     # to be converted to a string type if arguments are integer.     discipline = string(discipline)     parmcat = string(parmcat)     parmnum = string(parmnum)     # 29825:function IoU(box1, box2)     x1, y1, w1, h1 = box1     x2, y2, w2, h2 = box2     xl1, yl1, xr1, yr1 = x1, y1, x1 + w1, y1 + h1     xl2, yl2, xr2, yr2 = x2, y2, x2 + w2, y2 + h2     overlap_w = max(min(xr1, xr2) - max(xl1, xl2), 0)     overlap_h = max(min(yr1, yr2) - max(yl1, yl2), 0)     return overlap_w * overlap_h / (w1 * h1 + w2 * h2 - overlap_w * overlap_h) # box1 = [12, 20, 10, 10] # box2 = [13, 21, 7, 7] # print(IoU(box1, box2)) # box1 = [12, 20, 10, 10] # box2 = [13, 21, 8, 8] # print(IoU(box1, box2)) end

29868:function roman_to_int(s)   # Initialize the dictionary with key-value pairs   # of roman numerals and their corresponding values   _dict = Dict(     'I' => 1,     'V' => 5,     'X' => 10,     'L' => 50,     'C' => 100,     'D' => 500,     'M' => 1000   )   # Create two variables that keep track of the previous   # and the current roman numeral   prev = 0   cur = 0   # Initialize the result   res = 0   # Reverse the string because we will be iterating   # over it from the right   for i in s[end:-1:1]     # Check if the current roman numeral is present     # in the dictionary     if haskey(_dict, i)       # Get the value of the current roman numeral       cur = _dict[i]       # Check if the previous roman numeral is greater       # than the current roman numeral       if prev > cur         # Subtract the value of the current roman numeral         # from the result         res -= cur       else         # Add the value of the current roman numeral         # to the result         res += cur       end       # Set prev to cur       prev = cur     end   end   # Return the result   return res end
29869:function get_intersection(line1_p1, line1_p2, line2_p1, line2_p2)     x1, y1 = line1_p1     x2, y2 = line1_p2     x3, y3 = line2_p1     x4, y4 = line2_p2     D = (x1 - x2) * (y3 - y4) - (y1 - y2) * (x3 - x4)     Px = (x1 * y2 - y1 * x2) * (x3 - x4) - (x1 - x2) * (x3 * y4 - y3 * x4)     Px /= D     Py = (x1 * y2 - y1 * x2) * (y3 - y4) - (y1 - y2) * (x3 * y4 - y3 * x4)     Py /= D     return Px, Py end

29872:function _stringify_object(obj)     # Use typeof to handle missing attribute     if typeof(obj) == Missing         return missing     elseif typeof(obj) == Nothing         return nothing     end     # Handle x.id for objects with an id attribute     if hasproperty(obj, :id)         return obj.id     end     # Handle x for string, number, bool, nothing     if isa(obj, String) || isa(obj, Number) || isa(obj, Bool)         return obj     end     # Handle x for objects with an element type     if hasproperty(obj, :eltype)         if obj.eltype == String             return join(obj, ' ')         elseif obj.eltype == Number             return mean(obj)         elseif obj.eltype == Bool             return any(obj)         elseif obj.eltype == Nothing             return nothing         end     end     # Handle x for nested lists     if isa(obj, Array)         return join(map(x -> _stringify_object(x), obj), ' ')     end     # Handle x for nested objects     if isa(obj, Dict)         return join(map(x -> string(x[1], ':', _stringify_object(x[2])), obj), ' ')     end     # Fallback     return missing end

29923:function fn_jaro(len1, len2, num_matches, half_transposes, typo_score, typo_scale)     # is the string empty?     if len1 == 0 && len2 == 0         return 1.0     end     # can't be halfway a match if one is empty     if num_matches == 0 || (len1 == 0 && len2 != 0) || (len2 == 0 && len1 != 0)         return 0.0     end     # The Jaro distance is based on the number of matches and transposes     # but also on the number of non-matches that are inserted, deleted,     # substituted, or moved. (see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaro_Winkler_distance)     # We use the number of transposes, with a scaling factor, to determine     # the number of matches.     # The number of transposes is the number of matches minus the number of     # transpositions that are halfway in the string, scaled by a scaling factor.     # Transposes that are halfway in the string are counted as twice.     # Scaled number of matches     # Note: this is an integer division that rounds down.     similar = (typo_score / typo_scale) + num_matches     # Weighted jaro distance     weight = (  similar / len1               + similar / len2               + (num_matches - half_transposes//2) / num_matches)     return weight / 3 end

29927:function get_initial_lock_expiration(block_number, settle_timeout)     # The initiator doesn't need to learn the secret, so there is no need to     # decrement reveal_timeout from the settle_timeout.     #     # The lock_expiration could be set to a value larger than settle_timeout,     # this is not useful since the next hop will use the channel settle_timeout     # as an upper limit for expiration.     #     # The two nodes will most likely disagree on the latest block number, as     # far as the expiration goes this is no problem.     lock_expiration = block_number + settle_timeout     return lock_expiration end

29960:function mod_inverse_iterative(a, b)     if gcd(a, b) > 1         return error("a and b are not relatively prime")     end     s, old_s = 0, 1     t, old_t = 1, 0     r, old_r = b, a     while r > 0         q = old_r ÷ r         old_r, r = r, old_r - q * r         old_s, s = s, old_s - q * s         old_t, t = t, old_t - q * t     end     if old_r > 1         error("a and b are not relatively prime")     end     return old_r, old_s, old_t end

29962:function jacobi(x::Int64, n::Int64)     if n <= 0         throw(DomainError(n, "n must be a positive integer."))     end     if n % 2 == 0         throw(DomainError(n, "n must be odd."))     end     x %= n     r = 1     while x != 0         while x % 2 == 0             x ÷= 2             nm8 = n % 8             if nm8 == 3 || nm8 == 5                 r = -r             end         end         x, n = n, x         if x % 4 == 3 && n % 4 == 3             r = -r         end         x %= n     end     r *= (n == 1)     return r end

29982:function _reconstruct(x, y, r1, r2, ll, gamma, rho, sigma)     r12 = r1 * r1     r22 = r2 * r2     r12p = r12 + r22     r12m = r12 - r22     r12p_2 = r12p * r12p     r12m_2 = r12m * r12m     vr1 = gamma * ((ll * y - x) - rho * (ll * y + x)) / r1     vr2 = -gamma * ((ll * y - x) + rho * (ll * y + x)) / r2     vt1 = gamma * sigma * (y + ll * x) / r1     vt2 = gamma * sigma * (y + ll * x) / r2     vr1_e = r12p_2 * vr1 + r12m_2 * vr2     vr2_e = r12m_2 * vr1 + r12p_2 * vr2     vt1_e = (r12p * (r12p * vr1 + r12m * vr2) + r12m * (r12p * vr2 + r12m * vr1)) / (2r12p)     vt2_e = (r12m * (r12p * vr1 + r12m * vr2) + r12p * (r12p * vr2 + r12m * vr1)) / (2r12m)     return vr1_e, vr2_e, vt1_e, vt2_e end

We get # 1 frame every second, for 5 seconds. frame_numbers = range(0, 50) # Then we create a list of x positions at each frame. We start at 0, move # to 300, and then back to 0 at the end of the animation. x_positions = [0 for _ in frame_numbers] x_positions[10:20] = [300 for _ in range(10)] x_positions[20:30] = [0 for _ in range(10)] # We can do the same thing for the y position. This time we move up and # down in 100 increments. y_positions = [0 for _ in frame_numbers] y_positions[10:20] = range(100, 200, 100) y_positions[20:30] = range(0, 100, 100) # Finally we can create the animation by passing the frame number and the # x and y positions to the animate method. close the file     close(calib_file)     return output_filename end

30037:function hamming(n)   i = 1   j = 1   k = 1   hamming = [1]   while n > 1     # only add next term if it is smaller than the 3 others     if hamming[i]*2 < hamming[j]*3 < hamming[k]*5       push!(hamming, hamming[i]*2)       i += 1     elseif hamming[j]*3 < hamming[k]*5       push!(hamming, hamming[j]*3)       j += 1     else       push!(hamming, hamming[k]*5)       k += 1     end     n -= 1   end   return hamming[end] end

30145:function _paths_to_tree(paths)     # Initialize an empty dictionary that will contain the tree.     tree = Dict()     # Assemble the tree by iterating through all the paths.     for path in paths         # Get the reference to the current location in the tree.         current_node = tree         # Iterate through the path.         for char in path             # If the current character is not found in the current node,             # we add an empty node under it.             current_node[char] = get(current_node, char, Dict())             # Move to the next node in the tree.             current_node = current_node[char]         end     end     # Return the resulting tree.     return tree end

30153:function GreatCircleDistance(u, v)     r = 6372.8     θ1 = u[1] * π/180     θ2 = v[1] * π/180     ϕ1 = u[2] * π/180     ϕ2 = v[2] * π/180     Δλ = (v[1] - u[1]) * π/180     sinθ1 = sin(θ1); cosθ1 = cos(θ1)     sinθ2 = sin(θ2); cosθ2 = cos(θ2)     sinϕ1 = sin(ϕ1); cosϕ1 = cos(ϕ1)     sinϕ2 = sin(ϕ2); cosϕ2 = cos(ϕ2)     cosΔλ = cos(Δλ)     return r * acos(sinθ1 * sinθ2 + cosθ1 * cosθ2 * cosΔλ) end

30175:function parse_name(text)     # A function that takes a string and returns a tuple of the     # name and remainder of the string.     # Start with an empty name and an empty remainder.     name = ""     # Initialize an index that we'll keep track of.     i = 1     # While we're not at the end of the string:     while i <= length(text)         # If the character at the current index is not a comma, space,         # asterisk, percent sign, opening parentheses, or closing         # parentheses, add the character to the name string.         if text[i] ∉ ", *%();"             name *= text[i]             i += 1         # Otherwise we're at the end of the name and we're done.         else             break         end     end     # Now return a tuple of the name and the remainder of the string.     return (name, text[i:end]) end

30193:function normalize_ranges(ranges)     # offset = sorted(ranges)[0][0]     # ranges = [[n - offset for n in r] for r in ranges]     # has_gap = []     # # offset all the range to 0 as reference     # for i, range_ in enumerate(ranges):     #     values = [r[1] for r in ranges if r[0] < range_[0]]     #     if not values:     #         continue     #     if max(values) < range_[0]:     #         offset = range_[0] - max(values)     #         has_gap.append((offset, i))     # # remove the gap between the ranges     # global_offset = 0     # for offset, i in sorted(has_gap):     #     global_offset += offset - 1     #     ranges[i] = [n - global_offset for n in ranges[i]]     # return ranges     res = []     for range_ in ranges         if length(res) == 0             push!(res, range_)             continue         end         current = res[end]         if range_[1] < current[1]             range_[1] = current[1]         end         push!(res, range_)     end     return res end

30205:function partition(a, sz)     partitions = []     for (i, e) in enumerate(a)         append!(partitions, [e])         for (j, k) in enumerate(a[i+1:end])             if j % sz == 0                 push!(partitions, [k])             else                 append!(last(partitions), [k])             end         end     end     return partitions end
30206:function _iou(box1, box2)     b1_x0, b1_y0, b1_x1, b1_y1 = box1     b2_x0, b2_y0, b2_x1, b2_y1 = box2     int_x0 = max(b1_x0, b2_x0)     int_y0 = max(b1_y0, b2_y0)     int_x1 = min(b1_x1, b2_x1)     int_y1 = min(b1_y1, b2_y1)     int_area = max(int_x1 - int_x0, 0) * max(int_y1 - int_y0, 0)     b1_area = (b1_x1 - b1_x0) * (b1_y1 - b1_y0)     b2_area = (b2_x1 - b2_x0) * (b2_y1 - b2_y0)     iou = int_area / (b1_area + b2_area - int_area + 1e-05)     return iou end

30218:function GreatCircleDistance(u, v)     lat1, lon1 = u[1], u[2]     lat2, lon2 = v[1], v[2]     # Convert degrees to radians     lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2 = lat1 * pi / 180, lon1 * pi / 180, lat2 * pi / 180, lon2 * pi / 180     # Compute haversine formula     a = sin((lat2-lat1)/2)^2 + cos(lat1)*cos(lat2) * sin((lon2-lon1)/2)^2     c = 2*asin(sqrt(a))     # Radius of earth in kilometers     R = 6371     # Return result     return R*c end

30235:function process_param(args)   if length(args) < 2     println("Error: Simulation parameters not provided")     println("Usage: run_sim.jl [--param=value] ... model_file [init_file [output_file]]")     exit()   end   model_file, init_file, output_file = "", "", ""   sim_param = Dict()   model_param = Dict()   for namevalue in args     name, value = split(namevalue, "=")     if name == "frequency"       sim_param["frequency"]          = parse(Float64, value)       sim_param["frequency_domain" ]  = true     elseif name == "maxtol"       sim_param["MaxTol"] = parse(Float64, value)     elseif name == "maxiter"       sim_param["MaxIter"] = parse(Int64, value)     elseif name == "bicgstab"       sim_param["BiCGStab"] = parse(Int64, value)     else       ## all other parameters will be passed to the model:       try         model_param[name] = parse(Float64, value)       catch         try           model_param[name] = parse(Int64, value)         catch           model_param[name] = value         end       end     end   end   ## Note: The init file can also be a PDE param file.   if length(args) >= 3     init_file = args[3]   end   if length(args) == 4     output_file = args[4]   end   return sim_param, model_param, model_file, init_file, output_file end

30340:function compute_perc_word_usage(word, tokenized_string)   # word is the given word to be counted   # tokenized_string is a list of strings representing the tokenized input text   # returns the fraction of all tokens that are the given word   # initialize the variable that will be incremented for each match   count_word = 0   # initialize the count of total words   num_words = 0   # for each token in the input string   for token in tokenized_string     # add one to count_word if the word matches     if token == word       count_word += 1     end     # add one to num_words if the word is not equal to an empty string     if token != ""       num_words += 1     end   end   # return the percentage of words as the count divided by the number of words   return count_word / num_words end

30359:function shortest_mesh_path_length(source, destination)     x, y, z = (destination[1] - source[1],                 destination[2] - source[2],                 destination[3] - source[3])     # When vectors are minimised, (1,1,1) is added or subtracted from them.     # This process does not change the range of numbers in the vector. When a     # vector is minimal, it is easy to see that the range of numbers gives the     # magnitude since there are at most two non-zero numbers (with opposite     # signs) and the sum of their magnitudes will also be their range.     return max(x, y, z) - min(x, y, z) end

30361:function compute_iou(box1, box2)     box1_ymin, box1_xmin, box1_ymax, box1_xmax = box1     box2_ymin, box2_xmin, box2_ymax, box2_xmax = box2     # Compute intersection.     ymin = max(box1_ymin, box2_ymin)     xmin = max(box1_xmin, box2_xmin)     ymax = min(box1_ymax, box2_ymax)     xmax = min(box1_xmax, box2_xmax)     # print(ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax)     intersection = max(xmax - xmin, 0) * max(ymax - ymin, 0)     # Compute unions.     box1_area = (box1_ymax - box1_ymin) * (box1_xmax - box1_xmin)     box2_area = (box2_ymax - box2_ymin) * (box2_xmax - box2_xmin)     union = box1_area + box2_area - intersection     # print("box1: ", box1)     # print("box2: ", box2)     # print("box1_area: ", box1_area)     # print("box2_area: ", box2_area)     # print("intersection: ", intersection)     # print("union: ", union)     return intersection / union end

30366:function josephus_problem_recur(n::Int64, k::Int64)::Int64     # Base case, if the number of people is 1,     # he/she is the only person in the circle.     if n == 1         return 1     end     # Otherwise, to know who is the last person     # in the circle, we need to calculate who is     # the `k`-th person in the circle.     # To do this, we need to know the `k-1`-th     # person in the circle.     # We need to do this recursively     return (josephus_problem_recur(n - 1, k) + k - 1) % n + 1 end

30399:function _dilate(number)     # Fastest code as shown by this benchmarks:     # https://gist.github.com/DilumAluthge/6364061     # https://gist.github.com/lithander/3035675     # Also, the idea behind the bit swizzling is that we want to have the     # following:     # [76543210][76543210][76543210][76543210]     # [32107654][32107654][32107654][32107654]     # [10325476][10325476][10325476][10325476]     # [01234567][01234567][01234567][01234567]     # Now, by doing:     # x = x | (x << 16)     # we get the first row. In order to get the next one, we need to do     # (x << 8) & 0x0300F00F, and then & it with 0x030C30C3. This is because we     # want to keep only the bits of interest, i.e., 0123, 4567, 89AB, CDEF     # (the ones in brackets), but we don't want to keep 10325476.     # We can do this in one line by doing:     # (x | (x << 8) & 0x0300F00F) & 0x030C30C3     # Which does (x | (x << 8)) & 0x0300F00F & 0x030C30C3     # Which is the same as:     # ((x | (x << 8)) & 0x0300F00F) & 0x030C30C3     # Finally, to get the final result, we just need to do:     # (x | (x << 2)) & 0x09249249     # We can't use (x | (x << 4)) & 0x030C30C3 because we don't want the last     # two bits to be preserved.     # The reason that we have to do this in reverse order is that it makes it     # easier to convert from a bit representation to an integer representation     # using 0x09249249.     # Of course, if you only care about getting the Morton encoding, then     # you only need to do:     # (x | (x << 1)) & 0x55555555     # But since we want to keep the bits in the correct order, we need to     # reverse it.     ((number | (number << 8) & 0x0300F00F) & 0x030C30C3) & 0x09249249 end

30427:function retr_smaxkepl(peri, masstotl)     # [smax] = retr_smaxkepl(peri, masstotl)     # Purpose:     # Return the semi-major axis of a Keplerian orbit (in AU) from the orbital     # period (in days) and total mass (in Solar masses).     # Input     #  peri: orbital period [days]     #  masstotl: total mass of the system [Solar Masses]     # Output     #  smax: the semi-major axis of a Keplerian orbit [AU]     # History     #  Written - <NAME> - 10/22/2008     # Modified - <NAME> - 10/24/2008     #            - Changed masstotl to be in solar masses - 11/04/2008     #            - Changed masstotl to be in kg - 12/21/2008     #            - Changed masstotl to be in kg - 4/25/2009     # Compute the semi-major axis (smax) of a Keplerian orbit [AU]     smax = (7.496e-6 * masstotl * peri^2)^(1. / 3.)     return smax end

30619:function reversebits5(max_bits, num)     rev_num = 0     shifts = 0     while num != 0 && shifts < max_bits         rev_num |= num & 1         num >>= 1         rev_num <<= 1         shifts += 1     end     rev_num >>= 1     rev_num <<= (max_bits - shifts)     return rev_num end

30633:function GetKRStateFraction(alignedSeqList) 	lengthAlignment=length(alignedSeqList[1]) 	numSeq = length(alignedSeqList) 	cnt_K = zeros(lengthAlignment) 	cnt_R = zeros(lengthAlignment) 	for i in 1:numSeq 		alignedSeq = alignedSeqList[i] 		for j in 1:lengthAlignment 			s = alignedSeq[j] 			if s == 'K' 				cnt_K[j] += 1 			elseif s == 'R' 				cnt_R[j] += 1 			end 		end 	end 	per_K = zeros(lengthAlignment) 	per_R = zeros(lengthAlignment) 	numSeq_float = float(numSeq) 	for j in 1:lengthAlignment 		per_K[j] = cnt_K[j]/(numSeq_float) 		per_R[j] = cnt_R[j]/(numSeq_float) 	end 	return (cnt_K, cnt_R,  per_K, per_R) end

The value is a number, but it can't be converted to the type     #      requested (e.g. we need an integer, but the string has a decimal     #      point).     try         return parse(Int, value)     catch         try             return parse(Float64, value)         catch             return value         end     end end

30677:function check_iou(annotations, box, threshold)     # area = w * h     x1, y1, w, h = box     x2, y2 = x1 + w, y1 + h     area = w * h     # intersection = w * h     inter_x1 = max(x1, x2)     inter_y1 = max(y1, y2)     inter_x2 = min(x1, x2)     inter_y2 = min(y1, y2)     inter_area = max(0, inter_x2 - inter_x1) * max(0, inter_y2 - inter_y1)     iou = inter_area / (area + 1e-8)     if iou > threshold         return false     end     true end

30744:function iou(box_a, box_b, norm)     # Determine the coordinates of the intersection rectangle     xmin_a, ymin_a, xmax_a, ymax_a = box_a     xmin_b, ymin_b, xmax_b, ymax_b = box_b     # Check if boxes overlap     if norm         xmin_a, ymin_a = (xmin_a - 1) / (xmax_a - xmin_a), (ymin_a - 1) / (ymax_a - ymin_a)         xmax_a, ymax_a = (xmax_a - 1) / (xmax_a - xmin_a), (ymax_a - 1) / (ymax_a - ymin_a)         xmin_b, ymin_b = (xmin_b - 1) / (xmax_b - xmin_b), (ymin_b - 1) / (ymax_b - ymin_b)         xmax_b, ymax_b = (xmax_b - 1) / (xmax_b - xmin_b), (ymax_b - 1) / (ymax_b - ymin_b)     end     # Find intersection rectangle     xmin_inter = max(xmin_a, xmin_b)     ymin_inter = max(ymin_a, ymin_b)     xmax_inter = min(xmax_a, xmax_b)     ymax_inter = min(ymax_a, ymax_b)     # Check if intersection is valid     if !(xmin_inter <= xmax_inter && ymin_inter <= ymax_inter)         return 0.0     end     # Determine intersection area     inter_area = (xmax_inter - xmin_inter) * (ymax_inter - ymin_inter)     # Determine the union area     union_area = (xmax_a - xmin_a) * (ymax_a - ymin_a) + (xmax_b - xmin_b) * (ymax_b - ymin_b) - inter_area     # Compute the intersection over union     iou_ratio = inter_area / union_area     return iou_ratio end

30783:function next_power_of_2(n)     if n == 0         return 1     end     # Ignore the number itself.     n -= 1     # Set all the lower bits to 1.     n |= n >> 1     # Set the first 0 bit after the first 1 bit to 1.     n |= n >> 2     # Set the first 0 bit after the first 1 bit to 1.     n |= n >> 4     # Set the first 0 bit after the first 1 bit to 1.     n |= n >> 8     # Set the first 0 bit after the first 1 bit to 1.     n |= n >> 16     # Set the first 0 bit after the first 1 bit to 1.     n |= n >> 32     # Set the first 0 bit after the first 1 bit to 1.     n |= n >> 64     # Add 1 to the number to get the power of 2.     return n + 1 end

30817:function get_train_valid_test_split_(splits_string, size)     splits = []     if occursin(',', splits_string)         splits = parse.(Float64, split(splits_string, ','))     elseif occursin('/', splits_string)         splits = parse.(Float64, split(splits_string, '/'))     else         splits = [parse(Float64, splits_string)]     end     while length(splits) < 3         push!(splits, 0.)     end     splits = splits[1:3]     splits_sum = sum(splits)     if splits_sum > 0.         splits = [split / splits_sum for split in splits]         splits_index = [0]         for index in 1:length(splits)             push!(splits_index, splits_index[index] +                        round(Int, splits[index] * size))         end         diff = splits_index[end] - size         for index in 1:length(splits_index)             splits_index[index] -= diff         end         @assert length(splits_index) == 4         @assert splits_index[end] == size         return splits_index     else         @assert splits_sum == 0.         return []     end end

30863:function bezout(a, b)     (s, t, sn, tn, r) = (1, 0, 0, 1, 1)     while r != 0         (q, r) = divrem(a, b)         (st, tt) = (sn * (-q) + s, tn * (-q) + t)         (s, t) = (sn, tn)         (sn, tn) = (st, tt)         (a, b) = (b, r)     end     return (s, t) end

30890:function is_prime(number)     # 1 is not prime     if number == 1         return false     end     # Assume number is even, since odd numbers are not prime     if (number % 2) == 0         return (number == 2)     end     # Assume number is divisible by 3, since numbers divisible by 3 are not prime     if (number % 3) == 0         return (number == 3)     end     # We now know that number is odd and not divisible by 3. So we simply     # loop from 5, which is the smallest multiple of 6 that is larger than     # number. This way we can cut down the amount of numbers we need to     # test to half, since all even numbers larger than 3 can be factored     # as a product of two primes     for i in 5:round(sqrt(number))         if (number % i) == 0             return false         end     end     # If we have gotten this far, then number is a prime     return true end

30901:function get_palette(num_cls)     n = num_cls     palette = zeros(UInt8, n * 3)     for j in 0:n-1         lab = UInt32(j)         palette[j * 3 + 1] = UInt8(0)         palette[j * 3 + 2] = UInt8(0)         palette[j * 3 + 3] = UInt8(0)         i = 0         while lab > 0             palette[j * 3 + 1] |= UInt8((lab >> 0) & 1) << (7 - i)             palette[j * 3 + 2] |= UInt8((lab >> 1) & 1) << (7 - i)             palette[j * 3 + 3] |= UInt8((lab >> 2) & 1) << (7 - i)             i += 1             lab >>= 3         end     end     return palette end

30917:function _match_etag(etag, if_none_match_header)     # etag is a strong validator     # If the Etag the client gave us matches, we don't need to send the file.     #   This is a strong validator     # if_none_match_header is a weak validator     # If the Etag the client gave us matches, we don't need to send the file.     #   This is a weak validator     # if the request header includes *, the Etag value must match     #   a strong validator.     # If the request header includes *, the Etag value must not match     #   a weak validator.     # If the request header does not include *, we do a regular match     #   against the Etag.     # If the header is missing or empty, we assume the client is      #   not interested in any particular version of the file.     if if_none_match_header == "*"         return true     end     for header_element in split(if_none_match_header, ',')         header_element = strip(header_element)         if header_element == etag             return true         end     end     return false end

30927:function chao1_var_bias_corrected(singles, doubles)     s, d = float(singles), float(doubles)     var = s * (s - 1) / (4 * (d + 1)) + (s * (2 * s - 1) ^ 2) / (4 * (d + 1) ^ 2)     var -= (s ^ 2 * d * (s - 1) ^ 2) / (4 * (d + 1) ^ 4)     var *= 2 / (d + 1)     return var end
30928:function fifo_pre_sequencing(dataset) 	# 1) for each job, create a dictionary with its ID and the start time of the 	# job, for sorting purposes. 	# 2) sort the dictionary by the start time of the jobs, in ascending order. 	# 3) assign the job ID of each job as its rank. 	# 4) create a sequence of jobs based on their rank. 	rank = 1 	ranks = [] 	# Create the dictionary. 	for job_id in keys(dataset) 		push!(ranks, Dict("job" => job_id, "rank" => rank)) 		rank += 1 	end 	# Sort the dictionary. 	sort!(ranks, by = x -> x["rank"]) 	# Create the job sequence. 	sequence = [] 	for rank in ranks 		job_id = rank["job"] 		push!(sequence, job_id) 	end 	return sequence end

30937:function find_homology(long_seq, short_seq)     # Base case: short_seq is longer than long_seq     if length(short_seq) > length(long_seq)         return ""     end     # The homology starts at the beginning of long_seq     homology = long_seq[1:length(short_seq)]     # The similarity starts at 0     similarity = 0     # Search from [0] to [long_seq - short_seq] in long_seq     for i in 1:length(long_seq) - length(short_seq) + 1         # Get the similarity of short_seq and the string from long_seq[i] to long_seq[i+len(short_seq)-1]         for j in 1:length(short_seq)             if long_seq[j+i-1] == short_seq[j]                 # The two DNA match and should add up similarity                 similarity += 1             else                 break             end         end         # The new DNA section in long_seq has more similarity and should replace the homology         if similarity > length(homology)             # Assign new homology             homology = long_seq[i:i+length(short_seq)-1]         end     end     return homology end

30953:function recursive_fibonacci_cache(n::Int64)::Int64     if n < 0         throw(ValueError("n must be more or equal than 0"))     elseif n == 0         return 0     elseif n == 1         return 1     else         cache = Dict{Int64,Int64}()         cache[0] = 0         cache[1] = 1         if n - 1 in keys(cache)             cache[n - 1] = recursive_fibonacci_cache(n - 1)         else             cache[n - 1] = recursive_fibonacci_cache(n - 1)         end         if n - 2 in keys(cache)             cache[n - 2] = recursive_fibonacci_cache(n - 2)         else             cache[n - 2] = recursive_fibonacci_cache(n - 2)         end         cache[n] = cache[n - 1] + cache[n - 2]         return cache[n]     end end

30957:function merge_dict_tree(a, b)     if typeof(a) != typeof(b)         return b     elseif typeof(a) == Array         return a .+ b     elseif typeof(a) == Dict         keys_a = Set(keys(a))         keys_b = Set(keys(b))         c = Dict()         # Add the keys only in a...         for k in keys_a - keys_b             c[k] = a[k]         end         # ... now the ones only in b         for k in keys_b - keys_a             c[k] = b[k]         end         # Recursively merge any common keys         for k in keys_a & keys_b             c[k] = merge_dict_tree(a[k], b[k])         end         return c     else         return b     end end

30981:function logical_right_shift(n::Int64, shifted_by::Int64)::String     # Return an empty string if the number to shift or     # the number of bits to shift by are negative.     if n < 0 || shifted_by < 0         return ""     end     # Convert the number to a binary representation     # and remove the initial '0b'.     n_bin = string(n, base = 2)     n_bin = replace(n_bin, r"^0b" => "")     # Make sure that the number of bits to shift by is not     # larger than the number of bits in the number.     if shifted_by >= length(n_bin)         return "0b0"     end     # Return the shifted binary representation.     n_bin = n_bin[1:(length(n_bin) - shifted_by)]     return "0b$n_bin" end

31006:function _scale_one_value(value, scaled_min, scaled_max, global_min, global_max)     # YOUR CODE HERE     # scale value to the range [scaled_min, scaled_max]. The min/max     # of the sequence/population that value comes from are global_min and     # global_max.     # Parameters     # ----------     # value : int or float     #     Single number to be scaled     # scaled_min : int or float     #     The minimum value that value can be mapped to.     # scaled_max : int or float     #     The maximum value that value can be mapped to.     # global_min : int or float     #     The minimum value of the population value comes from. Value must     #     not be smaller than this.     # global_max : int or float     #     The maximum value of the population value comes from. Value must     #     not be bigger than this.     # Returns     # -------     # scaled_value: float     #     Value mapped to the range [scaled_min, scaled_max] given global_min     #     and global_max values.     # assert value >= global_min     # assert value <= global_max     # # Math adapted from this SO answer: https://tinyurl.com/j5rppewr     # numerator = (scaled_max - scaled_min) * (value - global_min)     # denominator = global_max - global_min     # scaled_value = (numerator / denominator) + scaled_min     # return scaled_value     return ((scaled_max - scaled_min) * (value - global_min)) / (global_max - global_min) + scaled_min end

31068:function pkg_version_cmp(left::String, right::String)::Int64     # if one package is a substring of the other, it should be greater than     # the other. For example, if someone has a julia 0.4-dev package installed,     # and someone else has a julia-0.4.1 package installed, we should try to     # load the 0.4-dev package.     #     # We can't just do a simple > comparison of the strings because if someone     # has 0.4.1-pre.alpha.1 installed and someone has 0.4.1-pre.alpha.1+50     # installed, then we should try to load the former.     #     # The following code is from Compat.jl (MIT licensed)     # https://github.com/JuliaLang/Compat.jl/blob/3f67f3216e4144e27078f2629427e768a96d643a/src/Pkg.jl#L69     if left == right         return 0     end     for i = 1:min(length(left), length(right))         c_left, c_right = left[i], right[i]         if c_left == c_right             continue         elseif c_left > c_right             return 1         else             return -1         end     end     # we've reached the end of one of the strings and not found any mismatch.     # if one string was a prefix of the other, we should load the one that     # wasn't a substring.     if length(left) < length(right)         return 1     elseif length(left) > length(right)         return -1     else         # this shouldn't happen         return 0     end end

31076:function damerau_levenshtein(s1, s2, cost)     len1 = length(s1)     len2 = length(s2)     if len1 == 0         return len2 * cost["a"]     end     if len2 == 0         return len1 * cost["d"]     end     row1 = [i * cost["a"] for i in 0:len2]     row2 = row1[:]     row0 = row1[:]     for i in 1:len1         row2[1] = (i - 1) * cost["d"]         for j in 1:len2             # substitution             sub_cost = row1[j] + (s1[i] != s2[j]) * cost["s"]             # insertion             ins_cost = row2[j] + cost["a"]             # deletion             del_cost = row1[j + 1] + cost["d"]             # swap             swp_condition = (                 (i > 1) &&                 (j > 1) &&                 (s1[i] == s2[j - 1]) &&                 (s1[i - 1] == s2[j]) &&                 (s1[i - 2] == s2[j - 2])             )             # min cost             if swp_condition                 swp_cost = row0[j - 2] + cost["w"]                 p_cost = min(sub_cost, ins_cost, del_cost, swp_cost)             else                 p_cost = min(sub_cost, ins_cost, del_cost)             end             row2[j + 1] = p_cost         end         row0, row1, row2 = row1, row2, row0     end     return row1[end] end

31082:function project_onto_basis(x, y, z, xx, xy, xz, yx, yy, yz, zx, zy, zz)     # Canonical Python Solution     # out_x = x * xx + y * xy + z * xz     # out_y = x * yx + y * yy + z * yz     # out_z = x * zx + y * zy + z * zz     # return out_x, out_y, out_z     # Project vector onto different basis.     # Parameters     # ----------     # x : float or array-like     #     X component of vector     # y : float or array-like     #     Y component of vector     # z : float or array-like     #     Z component of vector     # xx, yx, zx : float or array-like     #     X component of the x, y, z unit vector of new basis in original basis     # xy, yy, zy : float or array-like     #     Y component of the x, y, z unit vector of new basis in original basis     # xz, yz, zz : float or array-like     #     Z component of the x, y, z unit vector of new basis in original basis     # Returns     # -------     # x, y, z     #     Vector projected onto new basis     @inbounds begin         out_x = x * xx + y * xy + z * xz         out_y = x * yx + y * yy + z * yz         out_z = x * zx + y * zy + z * zz     end     return out_x, out_y, out_z end

31093:function p_approx(a, rho, temperature)     if 0 < rho < 1         # Original expression given by Groot and Warren, J Chem Phys 107, 4423 (1997), alpha = 0.101         # This is the revised formula due to Liyana-Arachchi, Jamadagni, Elke, Koenig, Siepmann,         # J Chem Phys 142, 044902 (2015)         c1, c2 = 0.0802, 0.7787         b = [1.705e-8,-2.585e-6,1.556e-4,-4.912e-3,9.755e-2]         b2 = polyval(b, a)                                           # This is B2/a, eqn (10) of above paper         alpha = b2 / ( 1 + rho^3 ) + ( c1*rho^2 ) / ( 1 + c2*rho^2 ) # This is eqn (14) of above paper         return rho * temperature + alpha * a * rho^2     elseif rho <= 0         return 0.0     else         # atoms per cubic Angstrom         return rho * temperature     end end

31114:function compute_iou(box1, box2)     x1_l, y1_l, x1_h, y1_h = box1     x2_l, y2_l, x2_h, y2_h = box2     xi_l = max(x1_l, x2_l)     yi_l = max(y1_l, y2_l)     xi_h = min(x1_h, x2_h)     yi_h = min(y1_h, y2_h)     if xi_h < xi_l || yi_h < yi_l         return 0     else         inter = (yi_h - yi_l) * (xi_h - xi_l)         box1_area = (x1_h - x1_l) * (y1_h - y1_l)         box2_area = (x2_h - x2_l) * (y2_h - y2_l)         iou = inter / (box1_area + box2_area - inter)         return iou     end end

31118:function get_hosp_given_case_effect(ve_hospitalisation::Float64, ve_case::Float64)::Float64     # Check if vaccine effectiveness for hospitalisation is higher than vaccine effectiveness for developing Covid     # Check that the vaccine effectiveness for the hospitalisation is not less than 0.0, which would cause NaNs     # further on     if ve_hospitalisation < ve_case         error("The effect of the vaccination on hospitalisation should be higher than the effect on developing " *               "symptomatic Covid, but instead the effect on hospitalisation is $ve_hospitalisation and the effect " *               "on developing symptomatic Covid is $ve_case.")     end     # Check that the vaccine effectiveness for the hospitalisation is not greater than 1.0, which would cause NaNs     # further on     if ve_hospitalisation > 1.0         error("The effect of the vaccination on hospitalisation should be less than or equal to 1.0, but instead " *               "the effect on hospitalisation is $ve_hospitalisation.")     end     # Return the vaccine effectiveness for hospitalisation in breakthrough cases     ve_hosp_given_case = 1.0 - (1.0 - ve_hospitalisation) / (1.0 - ve_case)     # Check that the vaccine effectiveness for hospitalisation given breakthrough cases is not less than 0.0, which     # would cause NaNs further on     if ve_hosp_given_case < 0.0         error("The effect of the vaccination on hospitalisation should be greater than or equal to the effect on " *               "developing symptomatic Covid, but instead the effect on hospitalisation given breakthrough cases is " *               "$ve_hosp_given_case.")     end     # Return the vaccine effectiveness for hospitalisation given breakthrough cases     return ve_hosp_given_case end

31230:function sentihood_macro_F1(y_true, y_pred)     p_all = 0     r_all = 0     count = 0     for i = 1:length(y_pred)         a = Set(y_pred[i])         b = Set(y_true[i])         if length(b) == 0             continue         end         a_b = intersect(a,b)         if length(a_b) > 0             p = length(a_b)/length(a)             r = length(a_b)/length(b)         else             p = 0             r = 0         end         count += 1         p_all += p         r_all += r     end     Ma_p = p_all/count     Ma_r = r_all/count     # avoid zero division     if Ma_p+Ma_r == 0         aspect_Macro_F1 = 0     else         aspect_Macro_F1 = 2*Ma_p*Ma_r/(Ma_p+Ma_r)     end     return aspect_Macro_F1 end
31231:function bytes_to_int15(b0, b1)     # Bitshift the first 8 bits into position, then concatenate     # it with the second 8 bits.     value = (b0 | (b1 << 8)) >> 1     # Check if sign bit is 1 (i.e. value is negative).     # If so, do a 16-bit complement to get a positive value.     # This can be achieved by using bitwise XOR and then subtracting     # 32768 from the result.     if value > 16383         value -= 32768     end     return value end

31268:function is_backtrack(previous_label, next_label)     # If the next label is nothing, it's a header, so it can't be a backtrack     next_label === nothing && return false     # If there is no previous label, it can't be a backtrack     previous_label === nothing && return false     # If the previous label is shorter than the next label, we have no     # chance of it being a backtrack     length(previous_label) < length(next_label) && return false     trimmed = previous_label[1:length(next_label)]     # If the trimmed header is not equal to the next label, it's not a     # backtrack     trimmed == next_label && return false     # If the next label is at least 11 digits long, and the trimmed header     # is at least 2 digits long, then it's a backtrack     length(next_label) >= 11 && length(trimmed) >= 2 && return true     # Otherwise, it's a normal header     return false end

31407:function isfib(number)     # Base case, 1 is the smallest and 1 is the largest     if number == 1 || number == 2         return true     end     if number < 1         return false     end     # Find the nearest fibonacci number that is larger than number     previousFibNumber = 1     fibNumber = 2     while fibNumber < number         temp = fibNumber         fibNumber = previousFibNumber + fibNumber         previousFibNumber = temp     end     return fibNumber == number end

31460:function jaccard(list1, list2)     # define an empty set     s1 = Set([])     s2 = Set([])     # fill the empty set with values from list1     for i in list1         push!(s1, i)     end     # fill the empty set with values from list2     for i in list2         push!(s2, i)     end     # get the intersection of the sets s1 and s2     s1 ∩ s2     # get the union of the sets s1 and s2     s1 ∪ s2     # compute the length of the intersection of s1 and s2 and divide it by the     # length of the union of s1 and s2     (length(s1 ∩ s2) / length(s1 ∪ s2)) end

31463:function mi09_Enuc(MFe, MNi, MSi, MCO)     # Proton mass     mp = 1.6726219 * 10 ^ (-24) # in kg     # Electron mass     me = 9.1093837015 * 10 ^ (-28) # in kg     # Nuclear masses     mele = mp * 0.00054858 # e- in kg     mc2 = mp * 0.999068 # Carbon 12 in kg     mi = mp * 0.931494 # Tritium 92 in kg     mtot = mele + mc2 + mi # Total nuclear mass     # Nuclear binding energies     # From  http://www.nuc.berkeley.edu/classes/f18/202/     Mele = 0.51099890221 # e-     Mc2 = 0.6582119514 # C-12     Mi = 0.53139534852 # Ni-56     Mtot = 1.0     # Mass of masses     me = me * mp     mc2 = mc2 * mp     mi = mi * mp     mele = mele * mp     mtot = mtot * mp     MFe = MFe * mp     MNi = MNi * mp     MSi = MSi * mp     MCO = MCO * mp     # Equations from Maeda & Iwamoto 2009     enuc_Fe = 1.74 * MFe * Mele / mtot     enuc_Ni = 1.56 * MNi * Mi / mtot     enuc_Si = 1.24 * MSi * Mtot / mtot     # Energy of Carbon 12     enuc_C = -2.0 * MCO * Mc2 / mtot     # Return     return enuc_Fe + enuc_Ni + enuc_Si + enuc_C end

31491:function IoU(rect1, rect2)     # Get intersection rectangle     x_left_rect1 = rect1[1]     x_right_rect1 = rect1[2]     y_top_rect1 = rect1[3]     y_bottom_rect1 = rect1[4]     x_left_rect2 = rect2[1]     x_right_rect2 = rect2[2]     y_top_rect2 = rect2[3]     y_bottom_rect2 = rect2[4]     x_left = max(x_left_rect1, x_left_rect2)     x_right = min(x_right_rect1, x_right_rect2)     y_top = max(y_top_rect1, y_top_rect2)     y_bottom = min(y_bottom_rect1, y_bottom_rect2)     # Compute intersection area     intersection_area = max(0, x_right - x_left) * max(0, y_bottom - y_top)     # Compute union area     rect1_area = (x_right_rect1 - x_left_rect1) * (y_bottom_rect1 - y_top_rect1)     rect2_area = (x_right_rect2 - x_left_rect2) * (y_bottom_rect2 - y_top_rect2)     union_area = rect1_area + rect2_area - intersection_area     # Return intersection over union     return float(intersection_area) / union_area end

31500:function deepmerge(source, destination)     # if not a dict, then just return destination (must be already correct)     if !isa(source, Dict)         return destination     end     # if destination does not exist, make a new one     if isempty(destination)         for key in keys(source)             destination[key] = deepcopy(source[key])         end         return destination     end     # merge fields in source and destination, overwriting destination fields     for key in keys(source)         if key ∉ keys(destination)             destination[key] = deepcopy(source[key])         else             # recursive merge if both source and destination have a dict at this field             if isa(destination[key], Dict) && isa(source[key], Dict)                 destination[key] = deepmerge(source[key], destination[key])             else                 destination[key] = deepcopy(source[key])             end         end     end     return destination end

31533:function siteswapTest(site)     siteLen = length(site)     valid = true     corrCatches = zeros(Int, siteLen) #how many should land in each index     actualCatches = zeros(Int, siteLen) #how many actually land in each index     for i in 1:siteLen #this loop builds corrCatches array         if site[i] isa Vector{Int}             corrCatches[i] = length(site[i]) #amt of lands = amt of throws         else             corrCatches[i] = 1 #this is even for 0 case since "throw" lands in same spot         end     end     for i in 1:siteLen #this loop builds actualCatches array         #add a 1 to index where the ball thrown lands         if site[i] isa Vector{Int}             for j in site[i]                 actualCatches[mod1(i + j, siteLen)] += 1             end         else             actualCatches[mod1(i + site[i], siteLen)] += 1         end     end     for i in 2:siteLen #this loop compares corrCatches and actualCatches         if valid             valid = corrCatches[i] == actualCatches[i]         end     end     return valid end

31550:function merge_links(a, b)     merged_link = Dict()     # 1. Longest URL     #  1.a. longest value if not empty     #  1.b. or shortest value if empty     merged_link["url"] =         (length(a["url"]) > length(b["url"]) ? a["url"] : b["url"])         # * this is a special case, where the longer value should be prioritized         #   when both are empty         # * if both are empty, use the empty string, which is fine     # 2. Earliest timestamp     #  2.a. earliest value     merged_link["timestamp"] = min(a["timestamp"], b["timestamp"])     # 3. Longest title     #  3.a. longest value if not empty     #  3.b. longest value if empty     merged_link["title"] =         (length(a["title"]) > length(b["title"]) ? a["title"] : b["title"])         # * this is a special case, where the longer value should be prioritized         #   when both are empty         # * if both are empty, use the empty string, which is fine     # 4. Longest tags     #  4.a. longest value if not empty     #  4.b. longest value if empty     merged_link["tags"] =         (length(a["tags"]) > length(b["tags"]) ? a["tags"] : b["tags"])         # * this is a special case, where the longer value should be prioritized         #   when both are empty         # * if both are empty, use the empty string, which is fine     # 5. Consistently merge sources     #  5.a. merge the sources     merged_link["sources"] = vcat(a["sources"], b["sources"])     # 6. Done     return merged_link end

31552:function to_snake_case(s::String)::String     # Create a buffer for the result.     buf = IOBuffer()     # Iterate over the characters in the input string.     for c in s         # Check if the character is a capital letter.         if isuppercase(c)             # The character is a capital letter.             # Write an underscore character to the buffer.             write(buf, '_')             # Write the lowercase version of the character.             write(buf, lowercase(c))         else             # The character is not a capital letter.             # Write the character.             write(buf, c)         end     end     # Convert the IOBuffer to a string.     String(take!(buf)) end

31592:function gc_content(dna)     seqlength = length(dna)     # Count A and T nucleotides, including the W ambiguity base representing     # either A or T     atcount = count(dna .== 'A') + count(dna .== 'a') +         count(dna .== 'T') + count(dna .== 't') +         count(dna .== 'W') + count(dna .== 'w')     # Count C and G nucleotides, including the S ambiguity base representing     # either C or G     gccount = count(dna .== 'C') + count(dna .== 'c') +         count(dna .== 'G') + count(dna .== 'g') +         count(dna .== 'S') + count(dna .== 's')     # Count all other ambiguous nucleotides; most will be Ns, but occasionally     # there will be other IUPAC ambiguity symbols     ncount = seqlength - atcount - gccount     if atcount + gccount == 0         gccontent = 0.0     else         gccontent = gccount / (gccount + atcount)     end     return gccontent end

31647:function comp(z1, z2, tol)     if isreal(z1)         return abs(z1 - z2) <= tol     elseif isreal(z2)         return abs(z2) >= 1 ? abs(z1 - z2)/abs(z1) <= tol : abs(z1 - z2) <= tol     elseif !isreal(z1) && !isreal(z2)         az1 = abs(z1)         az2 = abs(z2)         if az1 > 1 && az2 > 1             return abs(z1 - z2)/az1 <= tol         elseif az1 < 1 && az2 < 1             return abs(z1 - z2) <= tol         elseif az1 > 1 && az2 < 1             return abs(z1 - az2*z2) <= tol         else # az1 < 1 && az2 > 1             return abs(az1*z1 - z2) <= tol         end     end end

31651:function IoU(bbox0, bbox1)     # assert bbox0 and bbox1 are numpy array     dim = Int(length(bbox0)/2)     overlap = zeros(dim)     for i = 1:dim         overlap[i] = max(0, min(bbox0[i+dim], bbox1[i+dim]) - max(bbox0[i], bbox1[i]))     end     intersection = 1     for i = 1:dim         intersection = intersection * overlap[i]     end     area0 = 1     area1 = 1     for i = 1:dim         area0 = area0 * (bbox0[i+dim] - bbox0[i])         area1 = area1 * (bbox1[i+dim] - bbox1[i])     end     union = area0 + area1 - intersection     if union == 0         return 0     end     return intersection/union end

31707:function bucket_fill(bucket_a_capacity, bucket_a_contents, bucket_b_capacity, bucket_b_contents)     # 1. If A is empty, fill it     if bucket_a_contents == 0         bucket_a_contents = bucket_a_capacity     # 2. If B is full, empty it     elseif bucket_b_contents == bucket_b_capacity         bucket_b_contents = 0     # Pour contents of A to B     else         fluid_b_can_accept = bucket_b_capacity - bucket_b_contents         if fluid_b_can_accept > bucket_a_contents             # All of A poured into B             bucket_b_contents += bucket_a_contents             bucket_a_contents = 0         else             # Pour what is possible from A to B             bucket_b_contents += fluid_b_can_accept             bucket_a_contents -= fluid_b_can_accept         end     end     return (bucket_a_contents, bucket_b_contents) end

31737:function _process(proc_data)     # _process() is used for transformation, i.e. it creates a new Dictionary     #  for each row in the final data set.  The keys of this new Dictionary     #  are the field names.     # The new Dictionary will be added to the List of Dictionaries that     #   will be returned by the function.  Since this function is     #   recursive, this will result in a List of Dictionaries that is     #   a tree of Dictionaries.  The tree will have one row for every     #   record in the raw data.     # Initialize an empty List to store the processed data     out_data = []     # Loop through the data     for row in proc_data         # Create a new Dictionary         new_row = Dict()         # Loop through each column         for col in names(proc_data[1])             # Take the column name             col_name = String(col)             # Determine the data type of the column             # This can only be done if the column exists             if haskey(row, col_name)                 # Determine the data type of the column                 # and store it in the Dictionary                 new_row[col_name] = _type(row[col_name])             end         end         # Add the row to the List         push!(out_data, new_row)     end     # Return the data     return out_data end

31774:function parse_nuclide_str(nuclide::String)::String     if !isvalid(nuclide)         throw(ArgumentError(string("Invalid nuclide string: ", nuclide)))     end     letter_flag::Bool = false     number_flag::Bool = false     for char in nuclide         if char in 'a':'z' || char in 'A':'Z'             letter_flag = true         elseif char in '0':'9'             number_flag = true         end         if letter_flag && number_flag             break         end     end     if !letter_flag || !number_flag || length(nuclide) < 2 || length(nuclide) > 7         throw(ArgumentError(string(nuclide, " is not a valid nuclide string.")))     end     while nuclide[1] in '0':'9'  # Re-order inputs e.g. 99mTc to Tc99m.         nuclide = nuclide[2:end] * nuclide[1:1]     end     if nuclide[1] in ['m', 'n']         nuclide = nuclide[2:end] * nuclide[1:1]     end     for idx in 2:length(nuclide)  # Add hyphen e.g. Tc99m to Tc-99m.         if nuclide[idx] in '0':'9'             if nuclide[idx-1] != '-'                 nuclide = string(nuclide[1:idx-1], "-", nuclide[idx:end])             end             break         end     end     return nuclide end

31781:function vlan_range_to_oc(value)     # These are the ranges that can be interpreted     # by openconfig.     valid_ranges = split(value, ",")     vlan_ranges = Array{String}(undef, 0)     for i in valid_ranges         # Detect if the range contains dashes.         if contains(i, "-")             split_range = split(i, "-")             if length(split_range) != 2                 throw(ArgumentError("Incorrect range: $i"))             end             # split_range[1] and split_range[2]             # should be the start and end of             # the range.             start = split_range[1]             end_ = split_range[2]             # Detect if the values are integers.             try                 start = parse(Int, start)                 end_ = parse(Int, end_)             catch e                 throw(ArgumentError("Incorrect range: $i"))             end             # Detect if the start of the range             # is smaller than the end of the range.             if start > end_                 throw(ArgumentError("Incorrect range: $i"))             end             # Add the range to the list of ranges.             push!(vlan_ranges, "$(start)..$(end_)")         else             # If there are no dashes, the range is             # assumed to be an integer.             try                 push!(vlan_ranges, "$(parse(Int, i))")             catch e                 throw(ArgumentError("Incorrect range: $i"))             end         end     end     return vlan_ranges end

31808:function LimiterG2forHYU(dU1, dU2) # When we run into trouble, we can run Python interactively: # python # >>> from cfdm import examples # >>> from cfdm.externals.limiter import LimiterG2forHYU # >>> examples.limiter_g2hyu.LimiterG2forHYU.__doc__ # >>> examples.limiter_g2hyu.LimiterG2forHYU(1.0, 2.0) # <NAME> 2020-04-19 # https://github.com/NCAS-CMS/cfdm/issues/36     # Set up a local namespace:     #     # NOTE: We can't simply set variables to their values, as we     #       do for dU1 and dU2 (they are global variables, not local),     #       because doing so causes the function to return the wrong     #       value, which is explained in the next paragraph.     #     #       By making them local variables, we capture their values     #       at the time that the function is called. This means that     #       we don't have to create a namespace and use the global     #       operator, which is much faster and more memory efficient.     #     #       The reason why it was originally done this way (i.e.     #       creating the namespace and using the global operator)     #       was because I was experimenting with a few different     #       solutions, some of which were faster and using less     #       memory, but they all failed in various ways.     #     #       For example, if we tried to set them to their values     #       using the local operator, then that would be a local     #       variable to the function, but when we try to access it,     #       it would be a different value to the one we set, as     #       explained in the next paragraph.     #     #       This seems to be a problem with the Python scope rules     #       (and is probably why most people don't do this).     local term1 = dU1 * dU2     local term2 = abs(term1)     local denom = dU1 + dU2     if denom != 0         # Equation 6-133         local G = (term1 + term2) / denom     else         local G = 0.0     end     return G end

31891:function _inv(a, prime)     # Based on Extended Euclidean Algorithm:     # http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modular_multiplicative_inverse#Computation     lm, hm = 1, 0     low, high = a % prime, prime     while low > 1         r = high ÷ low         nm, new = hm - lm * r, high - low * r         lm, low, hm, high = nm, new, lm, low     end     return mod(lm, prime) end

31945:function linearRegression(xyList)     n = length(xyList)     sum_x = sum(x for (x, y) in xyList)     sum_y = sum(y for (x, y) in xyList)     sum_x2 = sum(x^2 for (x, y) in xyList)     sum_xy = sum(x*y for (x, y) in xyList)     a = (n * sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y) / (n * sum_x2 - sum_x^2)     b = (sum_y - a * sum_x) / n     return (a, b) end

31995:function point_in_polygon(point, polygon)     # https://www.ecse.rpi.edu/Homepages/wrf/Research/Short_Notes/pnpoly.html     n = length(polygon)     x = point[1]     y = point[2]     inside = false     xints = 0.0     p1x, p1y = polygon[1]     for i in 1:n+1         p2x, p2y = polygon[mod1(i, n)]         if y > min(p1y, p2y)             if y <= max(p1y, p2y)                 if x <= max(p1x, p2x)                     if p1y != p2y                         xints = (y - p1y) * (p2x - p1x) / (p2y - p1y) + p1x                     end                     if p1x == p2x || x <= xints                         inside = !inside                     end                 end             end         end         p1x, p1y = p2x, p2y     end     return inside end

32036:function sign_extend(value::Int64, orig_size::Int64, dest_size::Int64)::Int64     if dest_size < orig_size         throw(ArgumentError("Destination size must be larger than original size."))     end     orig_size *= 8     dest_size *= 8     # Calculate the max value for orig and dest     orig_mask = (1 << orig_size) - 1     dest_mask = (1 << dest_size) - 1     # Create the bit mask     masknumber = value & orig_mask     msb = masknumber >> (orig_size - 1)     # Perform the sign extension     if msb == 1         signextended = ((dest_mask << orig_size) | masknumber) & dest_mask     else         signextended = value & dest_mask     end     return signextended end

32085:function ra2float(ra)     # assert type(ra) is str or type(ra) is float or type(ra) is int     if typeof(ra) == String         ra = strip(ra)         if findfirst(":",ra) == -1             # assume it is a decimal             return parse(Float64,ra)         else             # assume it is a time string             ra = split(ra,":")             if length(ra) == 1                 hrs = parse(Float64,ra[1])             elseif length(ra) == 2                 hrs = 15.0*parse(Float64,ra[1]) + 1.0/4.0*parse(Float64,ra[2])             elseif length(ra) == 3                 hrs = 15.0*parse(Float64,ra[1]) + 1.0/4.0*parse(Float64,ra[2]) + parse(Float64,ra[3])/240.0             end             sign = (hrs >= 0) ? 1.0 : -1.0             return sign*hrs         end     elseif typeof(ra) == Float64         return ra     elseif typeof(ra) == Int64         return float(ra)     elseif typeof(ra) == Array         ra1 = copy(ra)         for i=1:length(ra1)             ra1[i] = ra2float(ra1[i])         end         return ra1     elseif typeof(ra) == Tuple         ra1 = copy(ra)         for i=1:length(ra1)             ra1[i] = ra2float(ra1[i])         end         return ra1     end end

32094:function nonmatching_lens(xsearch_output)     nonmatching = Dict()     # We'll sort the keys (the xsearch names) to ensure deterministic     # results.     xs = sort(collect(keys(xsearch_output)))     # While xs is nonempty, process the first entry.     while !isempty(xs)         x = popfirst!(xs)         # For each remaining xsearch, see if it matches.         for y in xs             x_len = length(xsearch_output[x])             y_len = length(xsearch_output[y])             # If not, store the non-matching pair in nonmatching.             if x_len != y_len                 nonmatching[x] = push!(get(nonmatching, x, []), y)                 nonmatching[y] = push!(get(nonmatching, y, []), x)             end         end     end     return nonmatching end

32103:function gcd(a, b)     # The algorithm is based on the extended Euclidean algorithm.     # First we calculate the greatest common divisor of a and b.     # Then we calculate the greatest common divisor of a-b and b.     # This repeats until a-b is zero, which means that b is the     # greatest common divisor of a and b.     while b > 0         # Swap a and b so that we always take smaller number to find         # greatest common divisor.         a, b = b, a % b     end     a end

32146:function find_k_4(n)   # Base case   if n == 1     return 1   end   # Initial value   r = 0   # Loop until the k = 4   while true     # Incremment the result     r += 1     # Calculate the number of the cycle     cycle, rem = divrem(n - 1, 4)     # If the number of cycle is 0, the remainder is 0 and the base is 1,     # the result is the power of two     if cycle == 0       if rem == 0         return 2^n - 1       end       return 2^rem     end     # Calculate the adjustment for the remainder     adjustment = cycle * 3 - 1     # If the remainder is 0, the adjustment is 0     if rem == 0       adjustment = 0     end     # Calculate the value     result = 2^(n - 2) + 2^(adjustment + rem)     # Check the result     if result == r       return result     end   end end

32183:function _expand_window(path, len_x, len_y, radius)     path = Set(path)     path_range = -radius:radius     window = Set()     for (i, j) in path         for (a, b) in ((i+a, j+b) for a in path_range for b in path_range)             if 0 ≤ a < len_x && 0 ≤ b < len_y                 path = push!(path, (a, b))             end         end     end     for (i, j) in path         i *= 2         j *= 2         for (a, b) in ((i, j), (i, j+1), (i+1, j), (i+1, j+1))             if 0 ≤ a < len_x && 0 ≤ b < len_y                 window = push!(window, (a, b))             end         end     end     return sort(collect(window)) end

32263:function _solve_method_3(N, queries)     # time complexity: O(N + Q)     # space complexity: O(N + Q)     # Example Input:     # N = 4     # queries = [[1, 2, 100],     #            [2, 3, 100],     #            [1, 3, 100]]     # Example Output:     # 200     # Example Explanation:     # queries[0]: Add +100 to A[1] = 100.     # queries[1]: Add +100 to A[2] = 200.     # queries[2]: Add +100 to A[3] = 300.     # arr = [0] * N     # for query in queries:     #     a, b, k = query[0], query[1], query[2]     #     arr[a-1] += k     #     arr[b] -= k     # largest = -1     # for i in arr:     #     if i > largest:     #         largest = i     # return largest     arr = Array{Int,1}(undef, N)     for query in queries         a, b, k = query[1], query[2], query[3]         if (k > 0)             for i in a:b                 arr[i] += k             end         elseif (k < 0)             for i in b:-1:a                 arr[i] += k             end         end     end     return maximum(arr) end

32266:function check_inclusion_4(s1::String, s2::String)::Bool     s1_len, s2_len = length(s1), length(s2)     if s1_len > s2_len         return false     end     s1_map = Dict{Char, Int}()     for c in s1         s1_map[c] = get(s1_map, c, 0) + 1     end     s2_map = Dict{Char, Int}()     for i in 1:s1_len         s2_map[s2[i]] = get(s2_map, s2[i], 0) + 1     end     if s1_map == s2_map         return true     end     for i in s1_len+1:s2_len         s2_map[s2[i]] = get(s2_map, s2[i], 0) + 1         s2_map[s2[i - s1_len]] = get(s2_map, s2[i - s1_len], 0) - 1         if s2_map[s2[i - s1_len]] == 0             delete!(s2_map, s2[i - s1_len])         end         if s1_map == s2_map             return true         end     end     return false end

32323:function gcd(m, n)     # If m and n are both 0, return 0.     if m == 0 && n == 0         return 0     end     # If one of m and n is 0, return the other.     if m == 0 || n == 0         return abs(m) + abs(n)     end     # While m and n are both greater than 0,     # set m to be the remainder of m and n.     while m > 0 && n > 0         m, n = n, m % n     end     # Return the result.     return abs(m) + abs(n) end

32344:function _parallel_variance(avg_a, count_a, var_a, avg_b, count_b, var_b) 	delta = avg_b - avg_a 	m_a = var_a * (count_a - 1) 	m_b = var_b * (count_b - 1) 	M2 = m_a + m_b + delta * delta * count_a * count_b / (count_a + count_b) 	return M2 / (count_a + count_b - 1) end

32457:function is_power2(num)     # 0 is not a power of two, it is a base case for the recursion     if num == 0         return false     end     # 1 is a power of two, it is a base case for the recursion     if num == 1         return true     end     # 2 is a power of two, but the recursion will have to stop here, otherwise it will get stuck in an infinite loop     if num == 2         return true     end     # check if num is a power of two, by testing if num can be divided by two without a remainder     if rem(num, 2) == 0         # if so, recurse on num / 2         is_power2(num / 2)     else         # if not, num is not a power of two, so return false         false     end end

32500:function unmangle(name::String)::String     # Handle special cases     if name == "this"         return "this"     elseif name == "this.env"         return "this"     elseif occursin(r"^\$this\$", name)         return "this"     end     # Split the name into components. A component is a string     # that begins with a lower-case letter, and is followed     # by any number of alphanumeric characters or underscores.     components = split(name, r"[\.\$_]+")     components = filter(!isempty, components)     # Empty strings are not valid unmangle components     if length(components) == 0         error("Invalid unmangle name: '$name'")     end     # Construct the unmangled name from the components     name = join(components, ".")     return replace(name, r"[\.$_]" => "") end

32505:function select_test_based_on_attributes(attrs1, attrs2, result)     if attrs1 == nothing         return 1     elseif attrs2 == nothing         return -1     end     if result != nothing         # break tie using the preferred result         rs = split(result, '=')[2]         r1 = get(attrs1, "result", "")         r2 = get(attrs2, "result", "")         if r1 == rs && r2 != rs             # only previous entry has preferred result             return -1         elseif r2 == rs && r1 != rs             # only new entry has preferred result             return 1         end     end     d1 = get(attrs1, "xdate", nothing)     d2 = get(attrs2, "xdate", nothing)     if d2 == nothing         # new entry does not have an execution date         return -1     elseif d1 == nothing || d2 > d1         # old entry does not have an execution date or new entry         # executed more recently         return 1     end     # unable to break the tie     return 0 end

32552:function _to_byte(byte)     if typeof(byte) <: AbstractFloat         if !isinteger(byte)             error("Got a non-integer byte: $byte!")         end         if byte < 0             error("Got a negative value for a byte: $byte!")         end         if byte > 255             error("Got a byte value bigger than 255: $byte!")         end         return byte     elseif typeof(byte) <: Integer         if byte < 0             error("Got a negative value for a byte: $byte!")         end         if byte > 255             error("Got a byte value bigger than 255: $byte!")         end         return byte     elseif typeof(byte) <: String         if !occursin(r"^\d+$", byte)             error("Got a non-integer string: $byte!")         end         if parse(Int, byte) < 0             error("Got a negative value for a byte: $byte!")         end         if parse(Int, byte) > 255             error("Got a byte value bigger than 255: $byte!")         end         return parse(Int, byte)     else         error("Got a non-integer value: $byte!")     end end

32762:function welford_mean_m2(previous_count, previous_mean, previous_m2, new_value)     if new_value == previous_mean && previous_count == 0         return (1, new_value, 0)     end     count = previous_count + 1     delta = new_value - previous_mean     mean = previous_mean + delta/count     delta2 = new_value - mean     m2 = previous_m2 + delta * delta2     return (count, mean, m2) end

32783:function dekatrian_week(dek_day::Int64, dek_month::Int64)::Int64     # Return the Dekatrian week day from a Dekatrian date.     # Here we can see the elegance of Dekatrian, since it's not necessary to     # inform the year. Actually, barely it's necessary to inform the month,     # as it's only needed to check if that is an Achronian day.     if dek_month == 0         return 0     else         # Get the week day from the absolute difference in days.         # (day - 1) % 7 + 1 will give the week day starting from 1 (Sunday)         dek_week_day = ((dek_day - 1) % 7) + 1         return dek_week_day     end end

32814:function comment_fold(s)   lines = split(s, '\n')   n = 0   for l in lines     n = n + length(l)   end   if n <= 120     return s   end   offset = "  " * " "   maxlen = 120   sep    = "|"   parts  = split(s, sep)   line   = ""   out    = ""   for f in range(1,length(parts) )     if f != length(parts)       line = line * parts[f] * sep     else       line = line * parts[f]     end     if length(line) >= maxlen       out = out * line * "\n%" * offset * ": "       line = ""     end   end   out = out * line   return out end

32827:function max_sum(triangle_matrix)   memo = Dict()   function rec_max_sum(row_num, depth)     # Base case     if depth > length(triangle_matrix)       return 0     end     if (row_num, depth) in keys(memo)       return memo[(row_num, depth)]     end     # Recursive case     if depth == length(triangle_matrix)       # Last row, no left or right neighbors       val = triangle_matrix[depth][row_num]     else       # Find value of left neighbor       left_neighbor = rec_max_sum(row_num, depth + 1)       # Find value of right neighbor       right_neighbor = rec_max_sum(row_num + 1, depth + 1)       val = triangle_matrix[depth][row_num] + max(left_neighbor, right_neighbor)     end     # Store result in memo and return it     memo[(row_num, depth)] = val     return val   end   return rec_max_sum(1, 1) end
32828:function searchkey(obj, key)     # If obj is a dict, traverse obj and its children until we find     # a dict whose key == key.  If we find it, return the value.     # If we don't find it, return None.     if obj isa Dict         if haskey(obj, key)             return obj[key]         else             for val in values(obj)                 result = searchkey(val, key)                 if result !== nothing                     return result                 end             end             for val in keys(obj)                 result = searchkey(val, key)                 if result !== nothing                     return result                 end             end         end     # If obj is a list, traverse each element of the list.     elseif obj isa Array         for i = 1:length(obj)             result = searchkey(obj[i], key)             if result !== nothing                 return result             end         end     # If obj is neither a dict nor a list, obj isn't searchable.     else         return nothing     end     # If we didn't find `key` anywhere, return nothing.     return nothing end

32843:function edit_distance(w1::String, w2::String)::Int64     m = length(w1)     n = length(w2)     d = Matrix{Int64}(undef, m+1, n+1)     for i in 1:m+1, j in 1:n+1         if i == 1             d[i,j] = j - 1         elseif j == 1             d[i,j] = i - 1         else             if w1[i-1] == w2[j-1]                 d[i,j] = d[i-1,j-1]             else                 options = [d[i-1,j-1] + 1, d[i,j-1] + 1, d[i-1,j] + 1]                 d[i,j] = minimum(options)             end         end     end     return d[m+1,n+1] end

Knudsen (kknu@berkeley.edu / kristianbknudsen@gmail.com)     Rs = params["Rs"]     R1 = params["R1"]     R2 = params["R2"]     R3 = params["R3"]     R4 = params["R4"]     R5 = params["R5"]     R6 = params["R6"]     R7 = params["R7"]     R8 = params["R8"]     R9 = params["R9"]     R10 = params["R10"]     R11 = params["R11"]     R12 = params["R12"]     R13 = params["R13"]     R14 = params["R14"]     R15 = params["R15"]     R16 = params["R16"]     R17 = params["R17"]     R18 = params["R18"]     R19 = params["R19"]     R20 = params["R20"]     R21 = params["R21"]     R22 = params["R22"]     R23 = params["R23"]     KK = Rs.*         (R1./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[1] )))     .+ (R2 ./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[2] )))     .+ (R3 ./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[3] )))     .+ (R4 ./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[4] )))     .+ (R5 ./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[5] )))     .+ (R6 ./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[6] )))     .+ (R7 ./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[7] )))     .+ (R8 ./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[8] )))     .+ (R9 ./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[9] )))     .+ (R10./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[10])))     .+ (R11./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[11])))     .+ (R12./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[12])))     .+ (R13./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[13])))     .+ (R14./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[14])))     .+ (R15./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[15])))     .+ (R16./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[16])))     .+ (R17./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[17])))     .+ (R18./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[18])))     .+ (R19./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[19])))     .+ (R20./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[20])))     .+ (R21./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[21])))     .+ (R22./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[22])))     .+ (R23./ (1 .+ w.* (1im.*t_values[23])))     return KK end
