40223:function _linearly_scale(inputmatrix, inputmin, inputmax, outputmin, outputmax)     # handle scalars     if (isa(inputmatrix, Number) || isa(inputmax, Number) || isa(inputmin, Number) || isa(outputmax, Number) || isa(outputmin, Number))         return (inputmatrix-inputmin) * (outputmax-outputmin) / (inputmax-inputmin) + outputmin     end     outputmatrix = zeros(eltype(inputmatrix), size(inputmatrix))     for i = 1:length(inputmatrix)         outputmatrix[i] = (inputmatrix[i]-inputmin) * (outputmax-outputmin) / (inputmax-inputmin) + outputmin     end     return outputmatrix end
40224:function matrix_n_by_n_determinant(nb_rows, nb_cols, matrix)     if nb_rows == 1         return matrix[1][1]     elseif nb_rows == 2         return matrix[1][1]*matrix[2][2]-matrix[1][2]*matrix[2][1]     else         determinant = 0         for i in 1:nb_rows             minor = [[matrix[r][j] for j in 1:nb_cols if j != i] for r in 2:nb_rows]             determinant += matrix[1][i]*matrix_n_by_n_determinant(nb_rows - 1, nb_cols - 1, minor)*(-1)^(1+i+1)         end         return determinant     end end

40251:function krishnamurti(number)::Bool 	# Initialize 	s = 0 	n = number 	a = n 	# Put the digits in an array 	digits = Int[] 	while n > 0 		push!(digits, n % 10) 		n = n ÷ 10 	end 	# Calculate the sum of digits raised to their respective power 	for digit in digits 		f = 1 		for i in 1:digit 			f *= i 		end 		s += f 	end 	# Check whether the sum is equal to the original number 	if s == a 		return true 	else 		return false 	end end

40253:function convert_25d_3d(path)     path_3d = []     push!(path_3d, path[1])     for i in 2:length(path)         previous = path[i - 1]         current = path[i]         previous_25d = [previous[1], previous[2]]         current_25d = [current[1], current[2]]         previous_3d = [             Int(round(previous_25d[1] * 1.5)),             Int(round(previous_25d[2] * 1.5)),             previous[3]         ]         current_3d = [             Int(round(current_25d[1] * 1.5)),             Int(round(current_25d[2] * 1.5)),             current[3]         ]         previous_25d_to_3d = previous_3d         current_25d_to_3d = current_3d         if previous_25d[1] < current_25d[1]             if previous_25d[2] < current_25d[2]                 # 1 1                 # 0 0                 previous_25d_to_3d = [previous_3d[1], previous_3d[2] - 1, previous[3]]                 current_25d_to_3d = [current_3d[1], current_3d[2] - 1, current[3]]             else                 # 1 0                 # 0 1                 previous_25d_to_3d = [previous_3d[1], previous_3d[2], previous[3]]                 current_25d_to_3d = [current_3d[1], current_3d[2], current[3]]             end         else             if previous_25d[2] < current_25d[2]                 # 0 1                 # 1 1                 previous_25d_to_3d = [previous_3d[1] - 1, previous_3d[2], previous[3]]                 current_25d_to_3d = [current_3d[1] - 1, current_3d[2], current[3]]             else                 # 0 0                 # 1 0                 previous_25d_to_3d = [previous_3d[1], previous_3d[2], previous[3]]                 current_25d_to_3d = [current_3d[1], current_3d[2], current[3]]             end         end         push!(path_3d, previous_25d_to_3d)         push!(path_3d, current_25d_to_3d)         push!(path_3d, current)     end     return path_3d end

40267:function compute_offset_to_first_complete_codon(offset_to_first_complete_reference_codon, n_trimmed_from_reference_sequence)     # Precondition: offset_to_first_complete_reference_codon is the offset     # to the first complete codon within the reference sequence, or is     # `nothing` if the reference sequence is incomplete.     # Precondition: n_trimmed_from_reference_sequence is the number of     # nucleotides trimmed from the beginning of the reference sequence.     # This is a non-negative integer.     # if n_trimmed_from_reference_sequence <= offset_to_first_complete_reference_codon:     #     return (     #         offset_to_first_complete_reference_codon -     #         n_trimmed_from_reference_sequence)     # else:     #     n_nucleotides_trimmed_after_first_codon = (     #         n_trimmed_from_reference_sequence -     #         offset_to_first_complete_reference_codon)     #     frame = n_nucleotides_trimmed_after_first_codon % 3     #     return (3 - frame) % 3     if isnothing(offset_to_first_complete_reference_codon)         return 0     elseif n_trimmed_from_reference_sequence <= offset_to_first_complete_reference_codon         return offset_to_first_complete_reference_codon - n_trimmed_from_reference_sequence     else         n_nucleotides_trimmed_after_first_codon = (             n_trimmed_from_reference_sequence -             offset_to_first_complete_reference_codon)         frame = n_nucleotides_trimmed_after_first_codon % 3         return (3 - frame) % 3     end end

40275:function palindrome(value::String)::Bool     # If the string is empty or only 1 character, it's a palindrome     if length(value) <= 1         return true     end     # If the first and last characters of the string are different, it's not     if value[1] != value[end]         return false     end     # Otherwise, the first and last characters match, and the rest of the string     # is a palindrome. 40329:function event_evaluation(s1, s2)     used_1 = [false for _ in 1:length(s1)]     found_1 = [false for _ in 1:length(s1)]     used_2 = [false for _ in 1:length(s2)]     found_2 = [false for _ in 1:length(s2)]     for i in 1:length(s1)         for j in 1:length(s2)             if !used_2[j]                 if (s2[j][1] >= s1[i][1] && s2[j][1] <= s1[i][2]) ||                    (s2[j][2] >= s1[i][1] && s2[j][2] <= s1[i][2]) ||                    (s2[j][1] <  s1[i][1] && s2[j][2] > s1[i][2])                     found_1[i] = true                     used_2[j] = true                 end             end         end     end     for i in 1:length(s2)         for j in 1:length(s1)             if !used_1[j]                 if (s1[j][1] >= s2[i][1] && s1[j][1] <= s2[i][2]) ||                    (s1[j][2] >= s2[i][1] && s1[j][2] <= s2[i][2]) ||                    (s1[j][1] <  s2[i][1] && s1[j][2] > s2[i][2])                     found_2[i] = true                     used_1[j] = true                 end             end         end     end     correct1 = (sum(found_1) / length(found_1))     correct2 = (sum(found_2) / length(found_2))     harmonic_mean = 2 * correct1 * correct2 / (correct1 + correct2)     return harmonic_mean end

40390:function find_closing_characters(chunk::String)::String     bracket_mapping = Dict(')' => '(', ']' => '[', '}' => '{', '>' => '<')     bracket_mapping_reversed = Dict(v => k for (k, v) in bracket_mapping)     open_brackets = ['(', '[', '{', '<']     stack = []     for char in chunk         if char in open_brackets             push!(stack, char)         else             top_char = pop!(stack)             if top_char != bracket_mapping[char]                 throw(error("unexoected illegal character in "))             end         end     end     closing_characters = [bracket_mapping_reversed[char] for char in stack]     return join([x for x in reverse(closing_characters)]) end

40422:function analytical_pulse_duration(q) 	# electron charge in [nC] 	q = q * 1e-3 	# mass of electron in [kg] 	m_e = 0.510998950e-3 	# classical electron radius in [m] 	r_e = 0.0005488e-3 	# Energy of electron in [J] 	e_e = 1.602176634e-19 	# "effective" charge of an electron in [C] 	c_e = 1.60217662e-19 	# resistance of wall in [m] 	R = 5.0e6 	# Perform calculations 	t_p = 2 * pi * R * q / (m_e * e_e) # [s] 	t_p /= (2 * pi * r_e * c_e) # [s] 	t_p /= 1e15 # [fs] 	t_p *= 1e-15 # [s] 	return t_p end

40492:function longest_common_subsequence(s_1, s_2)     m = length(s_1)     n = length(s_2)     mat = Array{Int64}(undef, m + 1, n + 1)     for i in 1:m+1         mat[i, 1] = 0     end     for j in 1:n+1         mat[1, j] = 0     end     for i in 2:m+1         for j in 2:n+1             if s_1[i-1] == s_2[j-1]                 mat[i, j] = mat[i-1, j-1] + 1             else                 mat[i, j] = max(mat[i, j-1], mat[i-1, j])             end         end     end     return mat[m+1, n+1] end

40555:function _getResponseRates(results)     # Count the total number of responses     responseEvents = filter(r -> r["decision"] == true, results)     totalResponses = length(responseEvents)     # Count the number of responses that were accepted/rejected     acceptEvents = filter(r -> r["reward"] > 0, responseEvents)     acceptCount = length(acceptEvents)     rejectEvents = filter(r -> r["reward"] < 0, responseEvents)     rejectCount = length(rejectEvents)     return (totalResponses, acceptCount, rejectCount) end
40556:function cluster_hierarchically(active_sites)     # define a distance matrix between all pairs of active sites     dist_matrix = zeros(Float64, length(active_sites), length(active_sites))     # compute the distance matrix between all active sites     for i in 1:length(active_sites)         for j in i:length(active_sites)             dist_matrix[i,j] = dist_matrix[j,i] = distance(active_sites[i], active_sites[j])         end     end     # Clustering algorithm:     # - start with each site in its own cluster     # - merge closest sites until we have only one cluster     clusters = []     while length(active_sites) > 0         # initialize the clusters         cluster = [active_sites[1]]         deleteat!(active_sites, 1)         # merge the closest sites until we have only one cluster         while length(active_sites) > 0             # compute distances from each site to all sites in clusters             distances = [distance(active_sites[i], cluster[j]) for j in 1:length(cluster), i in 1:length(active_sites)]             # get the minimum distance and its index             min_index = indmin(distances)             min_distance = distances[min_index]             # add the new site to the cluster if it's closest             if min_distance < dist_matrix[min_index]                 deleteat!(active_sites, min_index)                 cluster = vcat(cluster, active_sites[min_index])                 deleteat!(active_sites, min_index)             else                 # otherwise stop looking for more closest sites                 break             end         end         # add the new cluster to the list of clusters         push!(clusters, cluster)     end     # return the list of clusters     return clusters end

40624:function naive_derivative(xs, ys)     forward = zero(eltype(ys))     backward = zero(eltype(ys))     for i in 1:length(ys) - 1         forward += (ys[i + 1] - ys[i]) / (xs[i + 1] - xs[i])     end     for i in length(ys):-1:2         backward += (ys[i] - ys[i - 1]) / (xs[i] - xs[i - 1])     end     (forward + backward) / 2 end

40637:function count_bits_set_kernighan(n::Int64)::Int64     n -= ((n >> 1) & 0x5555555555555555)     n = (n & 0x3333333333333333) + ((n >> 2) & 0x3333333333333333)     n = (n + (n >> 4)) & 0x0f0f0f0f0f0f0f0f     n += n >> 8     n += n >> 16     n += n >> 32     return n & 0x7f end

If x is not a float,     # then we throw an exception     # Precondition: x is a float     # If x is not a float, then we throw an exception     @assert typeof(x) == Float64 "$(repr(x)) is not a float"     # Then, we want to convert the value to fahrenheit     # We do this by multiplying the value by 9     # and dividing it by 5.0     # We then add 32 to get the value in fahrenheit     # Since we are only interested in the decimal value     # we convert it to a float (type conversion)     # Postcondition: x is a float, and returned value has type float     return 9*x/5.0+32 end

40651:function find_primenum(uppernum)     if uppernum < 2         error("uppernum must be a natural number greater than 1")     end     # array that will store the prime numbers up to uppernum     primes = [2]     # loop over all the numbers from 2 to uppernum     for i = 3:uppernum         # loop over all the numbers in the list primes         is_prime = true         for j = 2:round(Int, sqrt(i))             # if i is a multiple of any number in the list,             # set is_prime to false             if i % j == 0                 is_prime = false                 break             end         end         if is_prime # if i is a prime number             push!(primes, i)         end     end     return primes end

40692:function is_even_permutation(seq1, seq2)     # Check that the sequences are permutations of each other     if sort(seq1) != sort(seq2) || length(Set(seq1)) != length(seq1)         throw(DomainError())     end     # Build the permutation of the second sequence from the first     perm = collect(1:length(seq1))     for (i, val) in enumerate(seq1)         perm[i] = findall(x -> x == val, seq2)[1]     end     # Check that the permutation is even     sgn = 1     for i in 1:length(seq1)         if perm[i] != i             sgn *= -1             swap_idx = findall(x -> x == i, perm)[1]             perm[i], perm[swap_idx] = perm[swap_idx], perm[i]         end     end     parity = (sgn == 1)     return parity end

40791:function gmof(x, sigma)     x_squared = x ^ 2     sigma_squared = sigma ^ 2     return (sigma_squared * x_squared) / (sigma_squared + x_squared)     # Numerical recipes     # return erf(x / (sigma * sqrt(2)))     # This solution from: http://www.johndcook.com/blog/python_erf/"""     #     # from math import exp, pi, sqrt     #     # def erf(x):     #     a = 8 * pi**5     #     b = 5 * pi**4     #     c = 2 * pi**3     #     c2 = c * c     #     d = pi**2     #     e = pi     #     t = 1 / (1 + 0.5 * abs(x))     #     z = t * exp(-x * x)     #     r = a * z + b * z * t + c * z * t * t + d * z * t * t * t + e * z * t * t * t * t     #     return r / c2 - t * exp(-z * z) + 1 end

40810:function average_gate_error_to_rb_decay(gate_error::Float64, dimension::Int64)     # Gate error is defined as:     # gate_error = sum(D_i)/dimension     # and     # D_i = e^{2 pi i D_i/dimension}     # so     # -2pi D_i/dimension = ln(sum(D_i)) - dimension * ln(2 pi)     # -2pi D_i/dimension = ln(sum(e^(-2pi D_i/dimension))) - dimension * ln(2 pi)     # 2pi D_i/dimension = ln(e^(dimension * ln(2 pi) + ln(sum(e^(-2pi D_i/dimension)))))     # 2pi D_i/dimension = ln(e^(dimension * ln(2 pi) + ln(e^(-2pi sum(D_i)/dimension))))     # 2pi D_i/dimension = dimension * ln(2 pi) + ln(e^(dimension * ln(2 pi) + ln(e^(-2pi sum(D_i)/dimension))))     # 2pi D_i/dimension = dimension * ln(2 pi) + dimension * ln(2 pi) - 2pi * sum(D_i)     # rb_decay = -2pi * sum(D_i) / dimension     rb_decay = -2pi * (gate_error - 1 + 1 / dimension) / (1 / dimension - 1) end

40818:function broken_fit(p, xax)     # This function will evaluate the broken power law with the parameters     # chosen for the fit     #     # Inputs:     # p - [xax_break, scale, xax_low_slope, xax_high_slope]     #     xax_break - breakpoint of the broken power law     #     scale     - scale of the broken power law     #     xax_low_slope   - slope at the left break (xax < xax_break)     #     xax_high_slope  - slope at the right break (xax >= xax_break)     # xax - x axis over which the broken power law will be evaluated     #     # Outputs:     # return - broken power law evaluated at xax     xdiff = xax - p[1]     lfit = (p[2] * xdiff + p[3]) * (xdiff < 0)     ufit = (p[3] * xdiff + p[4]) * (xdiff >= 0)     return lfit + ufit end
40819:function bbox_intersects(bbox1, bbox2)     # Compare the x and y distances between the centers of the boxes     xdist = abs((bbox1[1] + bbox1[2]) / 2.0 - (bbox2[1] + bbox2[2]) / 2.0)     ydist = abs((bbox1[3] + bbox1[4]) / 2.0 - (bbox2[3] + bbox2[4]) / 2.0)     # Compare the sizes of the boxes     xsize = (bbox1[2] - bbox1[1] + bbox2[2] - bbox2[1]) / 2.0     ysize = (bbox1[4] - bbox1[3] + bbox2[4] - bbox2[3]) / 2.0     # Compare the distances and sizes to determine whether they overlap     return (xdist <= xsize) && (ydist <= ysize) end

40826:function extract_text(pdf_list)     # Nested for loop that runs through every page of each pdf in pdf_list     # and appends each line of text to the output list of lists,     # where output is a list of lists where each inner list is a line of text.     #     # The reason we use nested for loops to iterate through all the pages     # of each pdf is because PyPDF4 does not provide a method to extract     # all the text from a pdf. Each PyPDF4.pdf.PdfFileReader object has a     # .getNumPages() method that returns the number of pages in the pdf.     # However, for some reason, this method returns 1 more page than the     # number of pages in the pdf. To get around this, we use a nested for     # loop to iterate through all the pages of each pdf.     #     # The reason we use nested for loops to iterate through all the pages     # of each pdf is because PyPDF4 does not provide a method to extract     # all the text from a pdf. Each PyPDF4.pdf.PdfFileReader object has a     # .getNumPages() method that returns the number of pages in the pdf.     # However, for some reason, this method returns 1 more page than the     # number of pages in the pdf. To get around this, we use a nested for     # loop to iterate through all the pages of each pdf.     output = []     for pdf in pdf_list         pdf_pages = [pdf.getPage(i) for i in range(0, pdf.getNumPages())]         pdf_text = [page.extractText().split('\n') for page in pdf_pages]         append!(output, pdf_text)     end     return output end

40988:function get_subsecond_component(frac_seconds, frac_seconds_exponent, subsec_component_exponent, upper_exponent_limit)     if frac_seconds_exponent <= subsec_component_exponent         return 0     end     total_subsecs = round(Int, frac_seconds * (10^(frac_seconds_exponent-subsec_component_exponent)))     # This gets the difference between the subsec_component_exponent and     # upper_exponent_limit. Note that the subsec_component_exponent is the     # exponent of the fractional second, so it is always negative and the     # upper_exponent_limit is the exponent of the upper limit.     exponent_diff = subsec_component_exponent - upper_exponent_limit     if exponent_diff == 0         # The upper limit is the same as the subsec_component_exponent, so         # subtracting them does not change anything.         return total_subsecs     elseif exponent_diff > 0         # The upper limit is lower than the subsec_component_exponent, so         # this means that we need to divide the total_subsecs by 10^abs(exponent_diff).         return total_subsecs ÷ (10^abs(exponent_diff))     else         # The upper limit is higher than the subsec_component_exponent, so         # this means that we need to multiply the total_subsecs by 10^abs(exponent_diff).         return total_subsecs * (10^abs(exponent_diff))     end end

41016:function rhosat(phi, sw, rhomin, rhow, rhohc)     #   Returns the density of a partially-saturated rock,     #   given the fraction of the particle that is saturated     #   and the resistivity of the water, brine, and hydrocarbon     #     #   inputs:     #   phi = saturated porosity [-]     #   sw  = saturation of water in the rock [-]     #   rhomin = density of mineral in rock [-]     #   rhow = density of water in rock [kg/m^3]     #   rhohc = density of hydrocarbon in rock [kg/m^3]     return rhomin * (1.0 - phi) + rhow * sw * phi + rhohc * (1.0 - sw) * phi end

41022:function parse_code(code)     if length(code) == 0         return (0, Vector{String}())     end     code_lines = split(code, '\n')     # The last line from the split has nothing in it; it's an artifact of the     # last "real" line ending in a newline. Unless, of course, it doesn't:     last_line = code_lines[end]     last_real_line_ends_in_newline = false     if length(last_line) == 0         pop!(code_lines)         last_real_line_ends_in_newline = true     end     snippet_lines = Vector{String}()     first = true     first_line_number = 1     for code_line in code_lines         number_and_snippet_line = split(code_line, ' ', limit=2)         if first             first_line_number = parse(Int, number_and_snippet_line[1])             first = false         end         snippet_line = number_and_snippet_line[2] * '\n'         push!(snippet_lines, snippet_line)     end     if !last_real_line_ends_in_newline         last_line = snippet_lines[end]         snippet_lines[end] = last_line[1:(end-1)]     end     return first_line_number, snippet_lines end

41180:function _autobitmask(val, total_size, index, size, keymap)     bitmask = 0b0     for i in 1:total_size         bitmask += Int(0b1)<<(total_size-i)     end     # The size of the bitmask should be reduced by the index of the bit to     # retrieve, and the size of the bit to retrieve should be added back     # at the end.     bitmask >>= (index+size)     bitmask <<= index     bitmask &= val     key = bitmask >> index     # Convert the key to a string to use as a dictionary key.     key = string(key)     return keymap[key] end

41240:function _next_legen_der(n, x, p0, p01, p0d, p0dd)     # Compute the next Legendre polynomial and its derivatives     # p0 is the previous polynomial, x the point where we want to evaluate the next     # one, p01 and p0d its first and first-derivative.     # This function assumes p01 and p0d are already computed and the input     # p0, p0d, p0dd are from the previous step.     # old_p0 = p0     # old_p0d = p0d     p0 = (2 * n - 1) * x * p0 - (n - 1) * p01     p0d = n * p0d + x * p0dd     p0dd = (n + 1) * p0dd + x * p0dd     return p0, p0d, p0dd end

41269:function is_crack(x, y)     crack_length = 0.3     output = 0     p1 = x     p2 = y     if x[1] > y[1]         p2 = x         p1 = y     end     # 1e-6 makes it fall one side of central line of particles     if p1[1] < 0.5 + 1e-6 && p2[1] > 0.5 + 1e-6         # draw a straight line between them         m = (p2[2] - p1[2]) / (p2[1] - p1[1])         c = p1[2] - m * p1[1]         # height a x = 0.5         height = m * 0.5 + c         if height > 0.5 * (1 - crack_length) && height < 0.5 * (1 + crack_length)             output = 1         end     end     return output end

41377:function levenshtein_distance(str1, str2)   function recursion(str1, str2, max_i, max_j)     if (max_i == 0)       return max_j     elseif (max_j == 0)       return max_i     elseif (str1[max_i] == str2[max_j])       return recursion(str1, str2, max_i - 1, max_j - 1)     else       return 1 + min(recursion(str1, str2, max_i - 1, max_j), recursion(str1, str2, max_i, max_j - 1), recursion(str1, str2, max_i - 1, max_j - 1))     end   end   recursion(str1, str2, length(str1), length(str2)) end
41378:function p_correct_given_pos(sens, fpr, b)     (sens >= 0 && sens <= 1) || throw(DomainError(sens, "sens must be in range [0,1]"))     (fpr >= 0 && fpr <= 1) || throw(DomainError(fpr, "fpr must be in range [0,1]"))     if sens == 0 && fpr == 0         throw(DomainError(sens, "sens and fpr cannot both be zero"))     elseif sens == 1 && fpr == 1         throw(DomainError(sens, "sens and fpr cannot both be one"))     elseif sens == 0 && b == 1         return 0.0     elseif sens == 1 && b == 0         return 1.0     else         return sens * b / (sens * b + fpr * (1 - b))     end end

41383:function bbox_iou_light(box1, box2)     # mx = min(box1[0]-box1[2]/2, box2[0]-box2[2]/2)     # Mx = max(box1[0]+box1[2]/2, box2[0]+box2[2]/2)     # my = min(box1[1]-box1[3]/2, box2[1]-box2[3]/2)     # My = max(box1[1]+box1[3]/2, box2[1]+box2[3]/2)     # w1 = box1[2]     # h1 = box1[3]     # w2 = box2[2]     # h2 = box2[3]     # uw = Mx - mx     # uh = My - my     # iw = w1 + w2 - uw     # ih = h1 + h2 - uh     # if iw <= 0 or ih <= 0:     #     return 0     # area1 = w1 * h1     # area2 = w2 * h2     # iarea = iw * ih     # uarea = area1 + area2 - iarea     # return iarea / uarea     # if box2[0] >= box1[0] + box1[2] or box2[1] >= box1[1] + box1[3]     #     return 0     # if box2[0] < box1[0] or box2[1] < box1[1]     #     return 0     # inter_box = [     #     max(box1[0], box2[0]),     #     max(box1[1], box2[1]),     #     min(box1[0] + box1[2], box2[0] + box2[2]),     #     min(box1[1] + box1[3], box2[1] + box2[3]),     # ]     # inter_area = (inter_box[2] - inter_box[0]) * (inter_box[3] - inter_box[1])     # box1_area = box1[2] * box1[3]     # box2_area = box2[2] * box2[3]     # return inter_area / (box1_area + box2_area - inter_area)     if isnothing(box1) || isnothing(box2)         return 0     end     inter_box = [         max(box1[1], box2[1]),         max(box1[2], box2[2]),         min(box1[1] + box1[4], box2[1] + box2[4]),         min(box1[2] + box1[3], box2[2] + box2[3]),     ]     inter_area = (inter_box[3] - inter_box[1]) * (inter_box[4] - inter_box[2])     box1_area = box1[3] * box1[4]     box2_area = box2[3] * box2[4]     return inter_area / (box1_area + box2_area - inter_area) end

41391:function cmp_version(a, b)     if length(a) == 0 && length(b) == 0         return 0     end     n_a, n_b = 0, 0     for i = 1:length(a)         n_a += (a[i] == '.')     end     for i = 1:length(b)         n_b += (b[i] == '.')     end     n_a, n_b = n_a + 1, n_b + 1     n_a, n_b = length(a) - n_a, length(b) - n_b     if n_a > n_b         return 1     elseif n_a < n_b         return -1     else         for i = 1:length(a)             if a[i] != '.'                 a1, a2 = parse(Int, a[i]), parse(Int, b[i])                 if a1 > a2                     return 1                 elseif a1 < a2                     return -1                 end             end         end     end     return 0 end

41394:function _reconstruct(x, y, r1, r2, ll, gamma, rho, sigma)     # Reconstruction algorithm from O'Neill, 1998.     # Compute internal variables.     t1 = y - (r1 * x) / r2     t2 = y + (r2 * x) / r1     # Compute the desired reconstruction.     V_r1 = gamma * ((ll * t1 - x) - rho * (ll * t1 + x)) / r1     V_r2 = -gamma * ((ll * t2 - x) + rho * (ll * t2 + x)) / r2     V_t1 = gamma * sigma * (t1 + ll * x) / r1     V_t2 = gamma * sigma * (t2 + ll * x) / r2     return [V_r1, V_r2, V_t1, V_t2] end

41412:function getrank(level::Int64)::String     # if the level is impossible, we don't need to do anything     if level >= 200         return "netherite"     end     # if the level is greater than or equal to 150, then it's diamond     if level >= 150         return "diamond"     end     # if the level is greater than or equal to 100, then it's gold     if level >= 100         return "gold"     end     # if the level is greater than or equal to 50, then it's iron     if level >= 50         return "iron"     end     # if the level is greater than or equal to 25, then it's stone     if level >= 25         return "stone"     end     # if the level is greater than or equal to 0, then it's wooden     if level >= 0         return "wooden"     end     # if the level is less than 0, then it's impossible     return "impossible" end

41429:function filter_containing_dirs_from_inputs(input_files_list)     if length(input_files_list) < 2         return input_files_list     else         filtered_input_files = []         populating_dirs = Set{String}()         for f in input_files_list             # We are checking if the directory is in the filter_out_dirs             # set and populating the populating_dirs set if it is.             # We do it here as this way we can keep the input list             # as is while populating populating_dirs with the list of             # all directories that have at least one file or dir inside them.             dir_populated = length(filter(x->x==f.dirname, filtered_input_files))>0             if !dir_populated                 populating_dirs = push!(populating_dirs, f.dirname)             end             # We are checking if the input file is a member of             # the populating_dirs set.             # We do it here as we cannot do it for the above             # condition because we are comparing f.dirname with the             # populating_dirs set which does not support indexing.             if !(f.dirname in populating_dirs)                 filtered_input_files = push!(filtered_input_files, f)             end         end         return filtered_input_files     end end

41488:function td_lambda(rewards, n_step, gamma)     n_step == 1 && return rewards     V = zeros(length(rewards))     N = zeros(length(rewards))     G = zeros(length(rewards))     lambda = 1.0     for i in n_step:-1:1         G[i] = rewards[i] + gamma * G[i+1]         V[i] = G[i] + lambda * gamma * V[i+1]         N[i] = N[i+1] + lambda * gamma * N[i+1]     end     # advice 1: use math mode     #    return list(map(     #        lambda i: sum(map(lambda t_r: t_r[1] * gamma**t_r[0], enumerate(rewards[i:i+n_step]))),     #        range(len(rewards))))     # advice 2: use power mode     return sum(map(i->rewards[i] + gamma * V[i+1], 1:length(rewards)-n_step))     # return sum(map(i->rewards[i] + gamma * (V[i+1] - N[i+1] * gamma * V[i+1]), 1:length(rewards)-n_step))     # advice 3: use divide and conquer     return sum(map(i->rewards[i] + gamma * (V[i+n_step] - N[i+n_step] * gamma * V[i+n_step]), 1:n_step:length(rewards))) end

41552:function build_tos(precedence::Int64, lowdelay::Bool, throughput::Bool, reliability::Bool, lowcost::Bool)::Int64     # bits 1-3 are for precedence; 4-5 is for lowdelay, 6-7 is for throughput, 8-9 is for reliability, 10-11 is for low cost     # http://www.networksorcery.com/enp/protocol/ip.htm     # precedence    lowdelay    throughput   reliability    lowcost     return (         (precedence << 1)         + (ifelse(lowdelay, 0b001, 0b000) << 4)         + (ifelse(throughput, 0b010, 0b000) << 6)         + (ifelse(reliability, 0b100, 0b000) << 8)         + (ifelse(lowcost, 0b1000, 0b0000) << 10)     ) end

41564:function dot_product(A, B)     # Ensure A and B are two-dimensional     if (length(size(A)) > 2 || length(size(B)) > 2)         throw(ArgumentError("A and B should be two-dimensional"))     end     # Ensure A and B have the same number of columns     if (length(size(A)) > 1 && length(size(A)) == length(size(B)))         throw(ArgumentError("A and B should have the same number of columns"))     end     # Ensure A and B have the same number of rows     if (length(size(A)) > 2 && length(size(A)) == length(size(B)))         throw(ArgumentError("A and B should have the same number of rows"))     end     # Section 1: Ensure A and B dimensions are the same     rowsA = length(A); colsA = length(A[1])     rowsB = length(B); colsB = length(B[1])     if rowsA != rowsB || colsA != colsB         throw(ArgumentError("Matrices are NOT the same size."))     end     # Section 2: Sum the products      total = 0     for i = 1:rowsA         for j = 1:colsB             total += A[i][j] * B[i][j]         end     end     return total end

41576:function split_pdb_atom_lines(lines)     properties = []     for line in lines         #line = line.rstrip()         if startswith(line, "ATOM  ") || startswith(line, "HETATM")             # Get PDB atom properties             # For ATOM lines, the index range is 1:6,             # for HETATM lines, the index range is 1:6             # To start the index range at 0, decrement all indices by 1             atype = line[0:6].strip()             index = line[6:11].strip()             atom = line[12:16].strip()             resid = line[17:20].strip()             chain = line[21:22].strip()             resseq = parse(Int, line[22:26])             icode = line[26:27].strip()             pos_x = line[30:38].strip()             pos_y = line[38:46].strip()             pos_z = line[46:54].strip()             occ = line[54:60].strip()             tfactor = line[60:66].strip()             symbol = line[76:78].strip()             charge = line[78:79].strip()             # Create dictionary for each PDB atom             dict = Dict("atype"=>atype,                         "index"=>index,                         "atom"=>atom,                         "resid"=>resid,                         "chain"=>chain,                         "resseq"=>resseq,                         "icode"=>icode,                         "pos_x"=>pos_x,                         "pos_y"=>pos_y,                         "pos_z"=>pos_z,                         "occ"=>occ,                         "tfactor"=>tfactor,                         "symbol"=>symbol,                         "charge"=>charge)             # Add each atom dictionary to the list             push!(properties, dict)         end     end     return properties end
41577:function rgb_to_hsv(rgb)     (r, g, b) = (rgb[1] / 255, rgb[2] / 255, rgb[3] / 255)     cmin = min(r, g, b)     cmax = max(r, g, b)     delta = cmax - cmin     h = 0     s = 0     v = cmax     if delta == 0         s = 0         h = 0 #undefined, maybe nan?     else         s = delta / cmax         if r == cmax             h = 60 * (g - b) / delta         elseif g == cmax             h = 120 + 60 * (b - r) / delta         else             h = 240 + 60 * (r - g) / delta         end     end     if h < 0         h += 360     end     return (h, s, v) end

41579:function _get_mul_scalar_output_quant_param(input_scale, input_zero_point, scalar)     # type: (Float32, Int64, Float32) -> (Float32, Int64)     # q_min = 0     # q_max = 255     # self_scale = input_scale     # self_zero_point = input_zero_point     # other_val = scalar     # if other_val > 0.0:     #     s_prime = other_val * self_scale     #     z_prime = self_zero_point     # elif other_val == 0.0:     #     s_prime = 1.0     #     z_prime = 0     # else:     #     s_prime = abs(other_val) * self_scale     #     z_prime = q_max - (self_zero_point - q_min)     # return s_prime, z_prime     # Note: the following code is not used for now, but can be used if we want to     # make sure that the results of get_mul_scalar_output_quant_param are same as     # the quantized::mul_scalar op     # get_mul_scalar_output_quant_param needs a scalar input     # We use randn as scalar to make the test more robust     # scalar = randn()     # input_scale = 1.2f0     # input_zero_point = 41     # other_val = 0.5f0     # s_prime, z_prime = _get_mul_scalar_output_quant_param(input_scale, input_zero_point, other_val)     # @testset "mul scalar quant test" begin     #     # @test abs(s_prime) == 0.6f0 # note: this is the same as self_scale     #     @test z_prime == 126     # end     q_min = 0     q_max = 255     self_scale = input_scale     self_zero_point = input_zero_point     other_val = scalar     if other_val > 0.0         s_prime = other_val * self_scale         z_prime = self_zero_point     elseif other_val == 0.0         s_prime = 1.0         z_prime = 0     else         s_prime = abs(other_val) * self_scale         z_prime = q_max - (self_zero_point - q_min)     end     return s_prime, z_prime end
41580:function get_iou(bb1, bb2) 	# determine the coordinates of the intersection rectangle 	xi1 = max(bb1["x1"], bb2["x1"]) 	yi1 = max(bb1["y1"], bb2["y1"]) 	xi2 = min(bb1["x2"], bb2["x2"]) 	yi2 = min(bb1["y2"], bb2["y2"]) 	# compute the area of intersection rectangle 	inter_area = abs(max((xi2 - xi1), 0) * max((yi2 - yi1), 0)) 	# compute the area of both the prediction and ground-truth 	# rectangles 	bb1_area = abs((bb1["x2"] - bb1["x1"]) * (bb1["y2"] - bb1["y1"])) 	bb2_area = abs((bb2["x2"] - bb2["x1"]) * (bb2["y2"] - bb2["y1"])) 	# compute the intersection over union by taking the intersection 	# area and dividing it by the sum of prediction + ground-truth 	# areas - the interesection area 	iou = inter_area / float(bb1_area + bb2_area - inter_area) 	# return the intersection over union value 	return iou end

41714:function neville(datax, datay, x)     n = length(datax)     p = zeros(n)     for k = 1:n         for i = 1:n-k+1             if k == 1                 p[i] = datay[i]             else                 p[i] = (x-datax[i+k-1])*p[i] + (datax[i]-x)*p[i+1]                 p[i] = p[i]/(datax[i]-datax[i+k-1])             end         end     end     return p[1] end
41715:function get_iou(pred_box, gt_box)   # 1.get the coordinate of inters   ixmin = max(pred_box[1], gt_box[1])   ixmax = min(pred_box[1] + pred_box[3], gt_box[1] + gt_box[3])   iymin = max(pred_box[2], gt_box[2])   iymax = min(pred_box[2] + pred_box[4], gt_box[2] + gt_box[4])   iw = max(ixmax - ixmin, 0.)   ih = max(iymax - iymin, 0.)   # 2. calculate the area of inters   inters = iw * ih   # 3. calculate the area of union   uni = (pred_box[3] * pred_box[4] + gt_box[3] * gt_box[4] - inters)   # 4. calculate the overlaps between pred_box and gt_box   iou = inters / float(uni)   return iou end

41732:function liangbarsky(left, top, right, bottom, x1, y1, x2, y2)     dx = x2 - x1     dy = y2 - y1     dt0, dt1 = 0, 1     xx1 = x1     yy1 = y1     if bottom > top         bottom, top = top, bottom     end     checks = ((-dx, x1 - left),               (dx, right - x1),               (-dy, y1 - bottom),               (dy, top - y1))     for (p, q) in checks         if p == 0 && q < 0             return (nothing, nothing, nothing, nothing)         end         if p != 0             dt = q / (p * 1.0)             if p < 0                 if dt > dt1                     return (nothing, nothing, nothing, nothing)                 end                 dt0 = max(dt0, dt)             else                 if dt < dt0                     return (nothing, nothing, nothing, nothing)                 end                 dt1 = min(dt1, dt)             end         end     end     if dt0 > 0         x1 += dt0 * dx         y1 += dt0 * dy     end     if dt1 < 1         x2 = xx1 + dt1 * dx         y2 = yy1 + dt1 * dy     end     return (x1, y1, x2, y2) end

41758:function EITCamount(basic_frac, phasein_rate, earnings, max_amount, phaseout_start, agi, phaseout_rate)     # quit if max amount < 0     if max_amount < 0         return 0.0     end     # quit if phaseout start < 0     if phaseout_start < 0         return 0.0     end     # quit if earnings < 0     if earnings < 0         return 0.0     end     # quit if agi < 0     if agi < 0         return 0.0     end     # quit if phaseout rate < 0     if phaseout_rate < 0         return 0.0     end     # quit if phasein rate < 0     if phasein_rate < 0         return 0.0     end     # quit if phasein rate > phaseout rate     if phasein_rate > phaseout_rate         return 0.0     end     # quit if basic_frac > 1.0     if basic_frac > 1.0         return 0.0     end     # if agi > phaseout start, quit     if agi > phaseout_start         return max_amount     end     # if earnings > phaseout start, quit     if earnings > phaseout_start         return max_amount - phaseout_rate * (max(earnings, agi) - phaseout_start)     end     # quit if max amount < phasein rate * earnings     if max_amount < phasein_rate * earnings         return 0.0     end     # return eitc amount     return min((basic_frac * max_amount +                 (1.0 - basic_frac) * phasein_rate * earnings), max_amount) end

41803:function get_hosp_given_case_effect(vacc_reduce_hosp_given_case::Float64, case_effect::Float64)::Float64     # This test is meant to ensure the argument is in fact a probability.     # This test will fail if the argument is not in fact a probability.     # This test will *not* fail if the argument is a probability but just not a probability greater than zero.     # This test will not fail if the argument is zero, because in that case the calculation of the effect     # is simply `1 - vacc_reduce_hosp_given_case / (1 - case_effect)`     #     # We first check that `vacc_reduce_hosp_given_case / (1 - case_effect) >= 0`     # We do this using the conditional version of the greater-than-or-equal-to operator     # to avoid introducing `NaN`s into the calculation.     #     # Inspired by https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chain_rule_(probability)#Inequality_conditions_for_probabilities_and_independence     if vacc_reduce_hosp_given_case / (1 - case_effect) >= 0.         # If vaccination reduces hospitalisation at least as much as becoming a case,         # then the effect of vaccination on hospitalisation given case is simply         # `1 - vacc_reduce_hosp_given_case / (1 - case_effect)`         return 1. - (1. - vacc_reduce_hosp_given_case) / (1. - case_effect)     else         # If vaccination reduces hospitalisation less than becoming a case,         # then the effect of vaccination on hospitalisation given case is just 0.         return 0.     end end

41819:function get_subverts(voxel, g, step)     # Construct the subvertices for this voxel     # The vertices are ordered in a standard fashion (clockwise when viewed from outside the voxel)     # The volume "g" contains the coordinate system for the whole volume.     # The local coordinate system for this voxel is centered at the volume origin     # and has dx,dy,dz = voxel size.     # The argument "step" is the size of a voxel in the local coordinate system     # It can be different from the volume coordinate system, which will be     # a multiple of the voxel size.     # So to calculate the position of a subvertex, first convert the local     # coordinates to the volume coordinate system. Then, calculate the voxel     # coordinates and use those to find the position.     # "voxel" is a tuple (i,j,k), the coordinates of the voxel     # "g" is a dictionary, the volume grid     # "step" is a tuple, the step size for the local coordinate system     # See "Volume Visualization with OpenGL" for more detail.     # https://web.stanford.edu/class/cs1400/projects/volumeExplorer/     i, j, k = voxel     dx, dy, dz = g["dx"], g["dy"], g["dz"]     DX, DY, DZ = step     v1_0, v1_1, v1_2 = g["xlo"] + i * dx, g["ylo"] + j * dy, g["zlo"] + k * dz     vertices = [         (v1_0, v1_1, v1_2),         (v1_0 + DX, v1_1, v1_2),         (v1_0 + DX, v1_1 + DY, v1_2),         (v1_0, v1_1 + DY, v1_2),         (v1_0, v1_1, v1_2 + DZ),         (v1_0 + DX, v1_1, v1_2 + DZ),         (v1_0 + DX, v1_1 + DY, v1_2 + DZ),         (v1_0, v1_1 + DY, v1_2 + DZ),     ]     return vertices end

41880:function safe_equals(x, y)     # Handle NULLs.     if x == "NULL"         x = 0     end     if y == "NULL"         y = 0     end     # Handle equality checks on a wildcarded file name. The     # current file name is never going to be equal to "".     if x == "CURRENT_FILE_NAME" && y == "" ||         y == "CURRENT_FILE_NAME" && x == "" ||         x == "SOME_FILE_NAME" && y == "" ||         y == "SOME_FILE_NAME" && x == ""         return false     end     # Handle wildcard matching.     wildcards = ["CURRENT_FILE_NAME", "SOME_FILE_NAME", "**MATCH ANY**"]     if x in wildcards || y in wildcards         return true     end     # Easy case first.     # pylint: disable=unidiomatic-typecheck     if x == y         return true     elseif x === nothing         return y === nothing     elseif y === nothing         return false     elseif typeof(x) == typeof(y)         return x == y     elseif (typeof(x) == Bool && typeof(y) == Int) ||         (typeof(y) == Bool && typeof(x) == Int)         return x == y     end     # Punt. Just convert things to strings and hope for the best.     return string(x) == string(y) end

41888:function stiff_b(v1v1, v0v1, v0v0, rold)     # real and imag parts of roots are returned in a list     root1 = [0.0, 0.0]     root2 = [0.0, 0.0]     r = v0v1 / v0v0     rho = abs(r)     det = v0v0 * v1v1 - v0v1^2     res = abs(det / v0v0)     rootre = det == 0.0 || (res <= 1e-6 * v1v1 &&                             abs(r - rold) <= 0.001 * rho)     if rootre         root1[1] = r     end     rold = r     return rold, rho, root1, root2, rootre end

41906:function bbox_iou_light(box1, box2)     mx = min(box1[1] - box1[3] / 2, box2[1] - box2[3] / 2)     Mx = max(box1[1] + box1[3] / 2, box2[1] + box2[3] / 2)     my = min(box1[2] - box1[4] / 2, box2[2] - box2[4] / 2)     My = max(box1[2] + box1[4] / 2, box2[2] + box2[4] / 2)     w1 = box1[3]     h1 = box1[4]     w2 = box2[3]     h2 = box2[4]     uw = Mx - mx     uh = My - my     iw = w1 + w2 - uw     ih = h1 + h2 - uh     if iw <= 0 || ih <= 0         return 0     end     area1 = w1 * h1     area2 = w2 * h2     iarea = iw * ih     uarea = area1 + area2 - iarea     return iarea / uarea end

41938:function parse_channel_info(data)     channel_list = split(data, ";")     if length(channel_list) == 0         throw(ArgumentError("Channels data is empty"))     end     default_channel_id = nothing     channels = Dict{String, Dict{String, String}}()     for channel in channel_list         channel_info = split(channel, ",")         if length(channel_info) == 3             channel_id, from_addr, api_url = channel_info             if channel_id == ""                 throw(ArgumentError("Channel id is empty"))             end             if from_addr == ""                 throw(ArgumentError("From address is empty"))             end             if api_url == ""                 throw(ArgumentError("API URL is empty"))             end             channel_id = strip(channel_id)             from_addr = strip(from_addr)             api_url = strip(api_url)             channels[channel_id] = Dict{String, String}(                 "FROM_ADDRESS" => from_addr,                 "API_URL" => api_url             )         elseif length(channel_info) == 2             if channel_info[1] == ""                 throw(ArgumentError("Channel id is empty"))             end             if channel_info[2] == ""                 throw(ArgumentError("API URL is empty"))             end             channel_id = strip(channel_info[1])             api_url = strip(channel_info[2])             if haskey(channels, channel_id)                 throw(ArgumentError("Channel ID '$channel_id' already used"))             end             channels[channel_id] = Dict{String, String}(                 "API_URL" => api_url             )         else             throw(ArgumentError("Invalid channel info: $(channel)"))         end         if default_channel_id == nothing             default_channel_id = channel_id         end     end     return default_channel_id, channels end

41951:function shortest_torus_path_length(source, destination, width, height)     (sx, sy, sz), (dx, dy, dz) = source, destination     (w, h) = width, height     # Get (non-wrapping) x, y vector from source to destination as if the     # source was at (0, 0).     (x, y, z) = (dx - sx, dy - sy, dz - sz)     (x, y) = (x - z, y - z)     # Get the length of the shortest path from source to destination as if     # the path was a vector between (0, 0) and (x, y).     return min(max(abs(x), abs(y)),                abs(x - w) + abs(y),                abs(y - h) + abs(x),                max(abs(x - w), abs(y - h))) end

41968:function get_unique_parents(entity_list)     if length(entity_list) == 0         return []     end     # get the parent of the first entity in the list     parent = get_parent(entity_list[1])     # copy the list of entities to a new list     unique_parents = copy(entity_list)     # remove the parent of the first entity from the list     deleteat!(unique_parents, 1)     # remove the parents of the rest of the entities in the list from the list     for entity in unique_parents         deleteat!(unique_parents, findfirst(unique_parents, entity))     end     # add the unique parents to the end of the list     append!(unique_parents, [parent])     # recursively call this function to add the parents of the parents     append!(unique_parents, get_unique_parents(unique_parents))     return unique_parents end

41998:function seconds_to_hhmmss(time_s) 	if typeof(time_s) == String 		time_s = parse(Float64, time_s) 	end 	hh = floor(Int, time_s/3600) 	time_s = time_s % 3600 	mm = floor(Int, time_s/60) 	ss = round(Int, time_s % 60) 	return string(hh,"h",mm,"m",ss,"s") end

42016:function tile_to_screen(pos, dims, off, p, screen_height)     # offx, offy = off     # if offx < 0:     #     offx = 0     # xpos,  ypos,  zpos  = pos  # x, y and z position     # xdims, ydims, zdims = dims # Total size of x, y and z     # xx = (xdims - 1 - xpos + ypos) * (p / 2) + offx     # # Gives top-left position of subsection     # yy = ((xdims - xpos) + (ydims - ypos)) * (p / 4) + (zpos * p) + offy + (p / 2)     # if screen_height is not None:     #     yy = screen_height - yy     # return (xx, yy)     if screen_height === nothing         screen_height = 0     end     x_off, y_off = off     x_pos, y_pos, z_pos = pos # x, y and z position     x_dims, y_dims, z_dims = dims # Total size of x, y and z     # need to invert z to screen coords     xx = (x_dims - 1 - x_pos + y_pos) * (p / 2) + x_off     # Gives top-left position of subsection     yy = ((x_dims - x_pos) + (y_dims - y_pos)) * (p / 4) + (z_dims - 1 - z_pos) * p + y_off + (p / 2)     # if screen_height is not None:     yy = screen_height - yy     return (xx, yy) end

42088:function eulerToQuaternion(pitch, roll, yaw)     cy = cos(yaw * 0.5);     sy = sin(yaw * 0.5);     cr = cos(roll * 0.5);     sr = sin(roll * 0.5);     cp = cos(pitch * 0.5);     sp = sin(pitch * 0.5);     q = [cy * cr * cp + sy * sr * sp,          cy * sr * cp - sy * cr * sp,          cy * cr * sp + sy * sr * cp,          sy * cr * cp - cy * sr * sp]     return q end

42095:function map_range(x, in_min, in_max, out_min, out_max)     in_range = in_max - in_min     in_delta = x - in_min     if in_range != 0         mapped = in_delta / in_range     elseif in_delta != 0         mapped = in_delta     else         mapped = 0.5     end     mapped = mapped * (out_max - out_min)     mapped = mapped + out_min     if out_min <= out_max         return max(min(mapped, out_max), out_min)     else         return min(max(mapped, out_max), out_min)     end end

42156:function Km(cw, R, M, L, P_phot)     return cw * R^3.1 * M^-0.22 * L^0.56 * P_phot^0.44 ## 4) Compare your results to that of Figures 3.8-4.15 in Kawaler+ 2002 ## # --- 3.8 --- # --- 3.9 --- # --- 3.10 --- # --- 3.11 --- # --- 3.12 --- # --- 3.13 --- # --- 3.14 --- # --- 3.15 --- ## 5) What are the limitations of the "effective" viscosity? ## # The effective viscosity in this example is the average over the entire  # photosphere, which is simply a measure of how much dissipation occurs  # at the photosphere. If a larger taper of the photosphere is considered,  # such as the taper formed by the dilution zone, then the effective viscosity  # is probably not a good measure of viscosity at all. ## 6) Are there any other interesting features to note? ## # There are some differences between the plots with and without the  # dipole taper. In the plots without the dipole taper, the lower density  # portion of the photosphere becomes extremely thin. ## 7) Make a plot of M vs. K. What do you see? ## # For the Sun: # # Please see the Sun data folder for your own plot. It should look similar # to Figure 3.15. # For other stars: # # Please see the default.jl file for your own plot. # --- 7.1 --- ## 8) What are the strengths and weaknesses of the tapered dipole model? ## # The weaknesses of the tapered dipole model are that it is very sensitive to # changes in the density of the photosphere. This is because the tapering # leads to a more complicated mass-radius relation, which is more sensitive to # changes in the density. # # The strengths of the tapered dipole model are that it is simple to compute, # it requires very little data, and it gives a good estimate of the viscosity # of the photosphere in the visible light. end

42169:function overlap(b1, b2)     x1 = max(b1[1], b2[1])     x2 = min(b1[3], b2[3])     y1 = max(b1[2], b2[2])     y2 = min(b1[4], b2[4])     if (x1 > x2) || (y1 > y2)         return 0.0     else         # Calculate area of intersection         a = (b1[3]- b1[1]) * (b1[4] - b1[2])         b = (b2[3]- b2[1]) * (b2[4] - b2[2])         c = (x2 - x1) * (y2 - y1)         return c / (a + b - c)     end end

42171:function convolution_of_two_uniforms(x, loc1, s1, loc2, s2)     z = x - loc1 - loc2     d = abs(s1 - s2)     s = s1 + s2     h = 2. / (d + s)     if -s/2. <= z < -d/2.         x0, y0 = -s/2, 0         x1, y1 = -d/2, h         return (y1 - y0)/(x1 - x0) * (x - x0) + y0     elseif -d/2 <= z < d/2.         return h     elseif d/2 <= z < s/2.         x0, y0 = s/2, 0         x1, y1 = d/2, h         return (y1 - y0)/(x1 - x0) * (x - x0) + y0     else         return 0.     end end

42205:function get_bboxes_intersection(roiA, roiB)     roiA_x1 = roiA[1]; roiA_y1 = roiA[2]; roiA_x2 = roiA[3]; roiA_y2 = roiA[4]     roiB_x1 = roiB[1]; roiB_y1 = roiB[2]; roiB_x2 = roiB[3]; roiB_y2 = roiB[4]     # Calculate the X-overlap     xInter = min(roiA_x2, roiB_x2) - max(roiA_x1, roiB_x1)     # Calculate the Y-overlap     yInter = min(roiA_y2, roiB_y2) - max(roiA_y1, roiB_y1)     return max(xInter, 0) * max(yInter, 0) end

42236:function deriv(y, t, Delta, beta, mu, epsilon, gamma, alpha, delta)     S, E, I, R, D = y     N = S + E + I + R     dS = Delta*N - beta*S*I/N - mu*S + delta*R     dE = beta*S*I/N - (mu + epsilon)*E     dI = epsilon*E - (gamma + mu + alpha)*I     dR = gamma*I - mu*R - delta*R     dD = alpha*I + delta*R     return [dS, dE, dI, dR, dD] end
42237:function HSVtoRGB(h, s, v)     if s == 0         # Achromatic, i.e. gray         return round(v*255), round(v*255), round(v*255)     end     # Calculate our "sectors"     h = h / 60     i = floor(h)     # A few intermediate values we may need     f = h - i     p = v * (1 - s)     q = v * (1 - s*f)     t = v * (1 - s*(1 - f))     # Figure out which "sector" of the HSV cylinder we're in and assign RGB     if i == 0         return round(v*255), round(t*255), round(p*255)     elseif i == 1         return round(q*255), round(v*255), round(p*255)     elseif i == 2         return round(p*255), round(v*255), round(t*255)     elseif i == 3         return round(p*255), round(q*255), round(v*255)     elseif i == 4         return round(t*255), round(p*255), round(v*255)     else         return round(v*255), round(p*255), round(q*255)     end end

42278:function _combine_ind_ranges(ind_ranges_to_merge)     # Sort the list of intervals to merge in non-decreasing order     ind_ranges_to_merge = sort(ind_ranges_to_merge, by=first)     # Initialize the stack     stack = []     # Initialize the result     result = []     # Iterate over the sorted intervals     for curr in ind_ranges_to_merge         # If the stack is empty, simply append the current interval         if length(stack) == 0             push!(stack, curr)         # Otherwise, check if the top interval overlaps with the current interval         elseif stack[end][end] >= curr[1]             # Pop the top interval from the stack             prev = pop!(stack)             # Combine the current and the top interval             merged = sort(union(prev, curr), by=first)             # Push the combined interval back onto the stack             push!(stack, merged)         # Otherwise, the current interval does not overlap with the top interval         else             # Push the top interval onto the result             push!(result, pop!(stack))             # Push the current interval onto the stack             push!(stack, curr)         end     end     # Push any remaining intervals onto the result     push!(result, pop!(stack))     # Return the merged intervals     return result end

42396:function mod_min(a, b)     b_abs = abs(b)     # return the remainder     r = mod(a, b)     # get the absolute difference     diff = b_abs - r     if r > diff         # take the absolute value         diff = abs(diff)         # if the remainder is > diff,         # set the remainder to -diff         r = -diff     end     return r end
42397:function get_bit(byteval, index)::Bool     # bitwise operator "&" is used to apply bitwise AND to the operands.     # so here, we are applying bitwise AND to the given byteval and a      # bitmask which has the bit at "index" position set to 1.      # By doing this, we are extracting the bit value at the specified index.     # bitwise operator ">>" is used to shift bits to the right.     # here, we are shifting the given byteval right "index" positions and      # then bitwise ANDing the result with 1.     # This effectively gives us the bit value at the specified index.     return (byteval & (1 << index)) >> index == 1 end

42454:function RGB_TO_HSB(col) 	r, g, b = col 	cmax = max(r, g, b) 	cmin = min(r, g, b) 	delta = cmax - cmin 	saturation = (cmax > 0) ? delta / cmax : 0 	brightness = cmax / 255.0 	hue = 0 	if saturation > 0 		if r == cmax 			hue = (g - b) / delta 		elseif g == cmax 			hue = 2 + (b - r) / delta 		else 			hue = 4 + (r - g) / delta 		end 		hue /= 6 		if hue < 0 			hue += 1 		end 	end 	return (hue, saturation, brightness) end

42498:function line_intersection(line1, line2)     xdiff = (line1[1][1] - line1[2][1], line2[1][1] - line2[2][1])     ydiff = (line1[1][2] - line1[2][2], line2[1][2] - line2[2][2])     function det(a, b)         return a[1] * b[2] - a[2] * b[1]     end     div = det(xdiff, ydiff)      # if lines do not intersect     if div == 0         return 0, 0     end      # Calculates intersection cord     d = (det(line1[1], line1[2]), det(line2[1], line2[2]))     x = det(d, xdiff) / div     y = det(d, ydiff) / div      # Return X and Y cords of intersection     return Int(round(x)), Int(round(y)) end

42604:function ext_euclid(a, b)     r = a;     s = 1;     t = 0;     r1 = b;     s1 = 0;     t1 = 1;     while r1 > 0         q = div(r, r1)         r2 = r - q*r1         s2 = s - q*s1         t2 = t - q*t1         r = r1         s = s1         t = t1         r1 = r2         s1 = s2         t1 = t2     end     return r, s, t end

42606:function convert_ireg_name(iregname)     # RFC 2396 permits the user and password segments of URIs     # to contain non-ASCII characters, but it doesn't define     # how to translate those characters into ASCII.     # From RFC 2396, page 17:     #     #   The ireg-name rule is the ireg-name from the     #   URI syntax specifier.     #     #   The ireg-name is defined as:     #     #      ireg-name  = 1*ireg-name-char     #      ireg-name-char = iunreserved / pct-encoded / sub-delims     #      iunreserved = ALPHA / DIGIT / "-" / "." / "_" / "~"     #      pct-encoded = "%" HEXDIG HEXDIG     #      sub-delims = "!" / "$" / "&" / "'" / "(" / ")"     #                  / "*" / "+" / "," / ";" / "="     return iregname end

42642:function compute_bitmap_representation(blade, firstIdx)     # if the tuple is empty return 0     # this is also the base case     if length(blade) == 0         return 0     end     # get the first item of the tuple     # and use that as the value in the bitmap     firstVal = first(blade)     bitmap = 1 << (firstVal - firstIdx)     # if the tuple has more than 1 value     # we need to XOR this value with the     # remaining values     if length(blade) > 1         # iterate through the remaining items         # and XOR them to the bitmap         for val in blade[2:end]             bitmap = bitmap ^ (1 << (val - firstIdx))         end     end     return bitmap end

42662:function sqrt_decimal_expansion(n::Int64, precision::Int64)::String     # break n into two-digit chunks     n_digits = []     while n > 0         n, mod = divrem(n, 100)         push!(n_digits, mod)     end     n_digits = reverse(n_digits)     expansion = []     remainder = 0     root_part = 0     f(x) = x * (20 * root_part + x)     # compute digits before decimal point     for carry in n_digits         a = 1         b = f(a)         c = remainder * 100 + carry         while b <= c             a += 1             b = f(a)         end         a -= 1         b = f(a)         remainder = c - b         root_part = root_part * 10 + a         push!(expansion, string(a))     end     push!(expansion, ".")     # compute digits after decimal point     for _ in 1:precision         a = 1         b = f(a)         c = remainder * 100         while b <= c             a += 1             b = f(a)         end         a -= 1         b = f(a)         remainder = c - b         root_part = root_part * 10 + a         push!(expansion, string(a))     end     return join(expansion) end

42802:function parse_nat_msg(msg)     dnat_in = ""     out = ""     mac = ""     src = -1     dest = -1     len_ = -1     tos = -1     proc = -1     ttl = -1     id_ = -1     proto = ""     spt = -1     dpt = -1     window = -1     res = ""     urgp = -1     words = split(msg, " ")     for w in words         if startswith(w, "DNAT_IN=")             dnat_in = w[9:end]         elseif startswith(w, "OUT=")             out = w[5:end]         elseif startswith(w, "MAC=")             mac = w[5:end]         elseif startswith(w, "SRC=")             src = w[5:end]         elseif startswith(w, "DST=")             dest = w[5:end]         elseif startswith(w, "LEN=")             len_ = w[5:end]         elseif startswith(w, "TOS=")             tos = w[5:end]         elseif startswith(w, "PREC=")             proc = w[6:end]         elseif startswith(w, "TTL=")             ttl = w[5:end]         elseif startswith(w, "ID=")             id_ = w[4:end]         elseif startswith(w, "PROTO=")             proto = w[7:end]         elseif startswith(w, "SPT=")             spt = w[5:end]         elseif startswith(w, "DPT=")             dpt = w[5:end]         elseif startswith(w, "WINDOW=")             window = w[8:end]         elseif startswith(w, "RES=")             res = w[5:end]         elseif startswith(w, "URGP=")             urgp = w[6:end]         end     end     d = Dict()     d["dnat_in"] = dnat_in     d["out"] = out     d["mac_address"] = mac     d["src_ip"] = src     d["dest_ip"] = dest     d["len"] = len_     d["tos"] = tos     d["proc"] = proc     d["ttl"] = ttl     d["id"] = id_     d["proto"] = proto     d["spt"] = spt     d["dpt"] = dpt     d["window"] = window     d["res"] = res     d["urgp"] = urgp     return d end

42809:function _process(proc_data)     # If the data is just a string, then convert it to a single row     if typeof(proc_data) == String         proc_data = [proc_data]     end     # The output array     output = []     for row in proc_data         # The row to be saved         output_row = Dict()         # Separate the data into an array of strings         row_data = split(row, "|")         # Find the seperator between the field names and values         sep = findfirst("=", row)         # Check if the line is an header row         if row_data[1] == "#"             # Split the field names             header_names = split(row_data[2], "!")             # Set the first value as a field name             output_row[header_names[1]] = row_data[3]             # For each field name, set its value             for header in header_names[2:end]                 output_row[header] = row_data[findfirst(header, row_data) + 1]             end             # Add the row to the output             push!(output, output_row)         else             # Set the field name             output_row[row_data[1:sep-1]] = row_data[sep+1:end]             # Add the row to the output             push!(output, output_row)         end     end     return output end

42818:function get_trid_isrc_full_con(tr_id, tr_exc, exid2next_dic, nexts_cisrc_dic)     isr_c, fully_con = 0, true     if tr_exc == 1         return 0, false     end     isr_c_pair = 0     for i in 1:tr_exc-1         ex_nr1 = i         ex_nr2 = i+1         ex_id1 = tr_id * "_e" * string(ex_nr1)         ex_id2 = tr_id * "_e" * string(ex_nr2)         next1 = exid2next_dic[ex_id1]         next2 = exid2next_dic[ex_id2]         nexts1 = next1 * "," * next2         nexts2 = next2 * "," * next1         nexts1_yes = false         nexts2_yes = false         if nexts1 in keys(nexts_cisrc_dic)             nexts1_yes = true         end         if nexts2 in keys(nexts_cisrc_dic)             nexts2_yes = true         end         if nexts1_yes && nexts2_yes             @assert false "NEXT ID combination appears twice in nexts_cisrc_dic ($nexts1, $nexts2)"         end         if nexts1_yes             isr_c_pair = nexts_cisrc_dic[nexts1]         elseif nexts2_yes             isr_c_pair = nexts_cisrc_dic[nexts2]         end         isr_c += isr_c_pair         if !nexts1_yes && !nexts2_yes             fully_con = false         end     end     return isr_c, fully_con end

42932:function mult(M, v)     # because we can't multiply a matrix by a vector, we first need to     # transpose the matrix M, then we can multiply M' by v' to     # get the vector product of M and v.     Mt = [t[:] for t in M]     return [sum(Mt[i][j] * v[j] for j in 1:length(v)) for i in 1:length(Mt)] end

43004:function pgcd(a, b)     #check if both numbers are positives and integers     if ((typeof(a) != Int64) || (typeof(b) != Int64))         throw(DomainError(a, "The number 'a' must be an integer"))     elseif a <= 0         throw(DomainError(a, "The number 'a' must be positive"))     elseif (typeof(b) != Int64) || b <= 0         throw(DomainError(b, "The number 'b' must be positive"))     end     # The idea is to check if b is a divisor of a, in case of true, we do not need to do anything, in case of false     # we make b the greatest divisor, by taking substraction one by one of the greatest divisor until b becomes a divisor     # of a     if (a % b == 0)         return b     end     temp = 1     while (a % b != 0)         temp = b         b = a % b         a = temp     end     return b end

43008:function is_valid_version_code(version)     if version == nothing         return false     end     # Version is valid only if it has five characters (e.g. 2018f).     if length(version) != 5         return false     end     # Get numeric part of version.     version_number = version[1:4]     # Get alphabetic part of version.     version_letter = version[5:end]     # Version number must be in the range 1990 - 2050.     version_number_int = tryparse(Int, version_number)     if version_number_int == nothing || version_number_int < 1990 || version_number_int > 2050         return false     end     # Version letter must be in the range ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f', 'g', 'h'].     for c in version_letter         if !in(c, ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f', 'g', 'h'])             return false         end     end     return true end

43011:function get_thumbnail_spec(size, height) 	size_width, size_height = size 	max_source_width = 2 * max(size_height, height) 	max_source_height = max(2 * size_width, height) 	source_width = min(size_width, max_source_width) 	source_height = min(size_height, max_source_height) 	source_left = (size_width - source_width) // 2 	source_top = 0 	result_height = min(size_height, height) 	result_width = (source_width * result_height + source_height // 2) ÷ source_height 	return ( 		(source_left, source_top, source_left + source_width, source_top + source_height), 		(result_width, result_height), 	) end

43018:function compute_bitmap_representation(blade, firstIdx)     bladeLength = length(blade)     # If there is no blade, the bitmap representation is 0     if bladeLength == 0         return 0     end     # If there is only one blade, we have the bitmap representation     # with a single 1, followed by all the 0s     if bladeLength == 1         bitmap = 1 << (blade[1] - firstIdx)         for i = 2:2^63             bitmap = bitmap ^ (1 << (i - 1))         end         return bitmap     end     # If there are two blades, we can do the following     # 1. Create the bitmap with a single 1 and all the 0s     # 2. Add a 1 to the position of the second blade     # 3. Add a 0 to the position of the first blade     # 4. Negate the bitmap     # 1. Create the bitmap with a single 1 and all the 0s     bitmap = 1 << (2^63 - 1 - firstIdx)     for i = 2:2^63         bitmap = bitmap ^ (1 << (i - 1))     end     # 2. Add a 1 to the position of the second blade     bitmap = bitmap | (1 << (blade[2] - firstIdx))     # 3. Add a 0 to the position of the first blade     bitmap = bitmap | (1 << (blade[1] - firstIdx))     # 4. Negate the bitmap     return ~bitmap end

43027:function _IBeamProperties(h_web, t_web, w_flange, t_flange, w_base, t_base) 	# Area of T cross section is sum of the two rectangles 	area_web = h_web * t_web 	area_flange = w_flange * t_flange 	area_base = w_base * t_base 	area = area_web + area_flange + area_base 	# Y-position of the center of mass (Yna) measured from the base 	y_cg = ( 		(t_base + h_web + 0.5 * t_flange) * area_flange + (t_base + 0.5 * h_web) * area_web + 0.5 * t_base * area_base 	) / area 	return area, y_cg end

43051:function is_permutation(a::String, b::String)::Bool # Check if the length of a is different from the length of b     if length(a) != length(b)         return false     end     # Check if the length of a is 0, which is a valid permutation     if length(a) == 0         return true     end     # Store the count of characters for each string in a dictionary     a_counter = Dict{Char, Int}()     for char in a         if char in keys(a_counter)             a_counter[char] += 1         else             a_counter[char] = 1         end     end     # Subtract the characters in b from the characters in a     for char in b         if char in keys(a_counter)             a_counter[char] -= 1         else             a_counter[char] = 1         end     end     # Check if the value for all the entries of the dictionary is zero     for (char, value) in a_counter         if value != 0             return false         end     end     return true end

43066:function fancy_ind(inds, shape)     #throw a type error if there's a mismatch between the length of the list     #of indices and the length of the list of dimensions     if length(inds) != length(shape)         error("Number of indices does not match number of dimensions")     end     #throw an error if the values in the list of indices are not less than the     #values in the list of dimensions     for i in 1:length(inds)         if inds[i] >= shape[i]             error("Index exceeds the size of the dimension")         end     end     #initialize the index     ind = 0     #multiply the values in the list of indices by the product of the values     #in the list of dimensions after the current value, then add them to the     #current index. This is repeated for each value in the list of indices.     for i in 1:length(inds)         mult = prod(shape[i+1:end])         ind += inds[i]*mult     end     return ind end

43145:function jaccard_word_level_similarity(y_true::String, y_pred::String)::Float64     # Create sets of lowercase words     y_true_lower = Set(lowercase.(split(y_true)))     y_pred_lower = Set(lowercase.(split(y_pred)))     # Count intersection of words between the sets     y_intersect = length(intersect(y_true_lower, y_pred_lower))     # Return ratio between intersection and union of words     return y_intersect / (length(y_true_lower) + length(y_pred_lower) - y_intersect) end
43146:function is_valid_jwt(jwt::String)::Bool   try     # Check the number of sections     sections = split(jwt, ".")     if length(sections) != 3       return false     end     # Check the signature length     jwt_body = split(sections[1], "-")[1]     jwt_body = replace(jwt_body, r"[A-Za-z\-\_\s]+"=>"")     jwt_body = replace(jwt_body, r"="=>"")     if length(jwt_body)%4 != 0       return false     end     # Check the signature     # The .payload.signature is a URLSafe base64 encoded SHA256     # of the previous string     # The .signature is a URLSafe base64 encoded SHA256     # of the previous string plus the .secret     payload_signature = replace(sections[2], r"[A-Za-z\-\_\s]+"=>"")     signature = replace(sections[3], r"[A-Za-z\-\_\s]+"=>"")     secret = "secret"     if payload_signature != base64encode(sha256(secret * jwt_body))       return false     end     if signature != base64encode(sha256(secret * jwt_body * "." * jwt_body))       return false     end     return true   catch ex     return false   end end

43158:function ignore_headers(headers_to_sign)     # Excerpts from @lsegal -     # https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-js/issues/659#issuecomment-120477258     #     #  User-Agent:     #     #      This is ignored from signing because signing this causes problems     #      with generating pre-signed URLs (that are executed by other agents)     #      or when customers pass requests through proxies, which may modify     #      the user-agent.     #     #  Content-Length:     #     #      This is ignored from signing because generating a pre-signed URL     #      should not provide a content-length constraint, specifically when     #      vending a S3 pre-signed PUT URL. The corollary to this is that when     #      sending regular requests (non-pre-signed), the signature contains     #      a checksum of the body, which implicitly validates the payload     #      length (since changing the number of bytes would change the     #      checksum) and therefore this header is not valuable in the     #      signature.     #     #  Content-Type:     #     #      Signing this header causes quite a number of problems in browser     #      environments, where browsers like to modify and normalize the     #      content-type header in different ways. There is more information     #      on this in https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-js/issues/244. Avoiding     #      this field simplifies logic and reduces the possibility of bugs.     #     #  Authorization:     #     #      Is skipped for obvious reasons     ignored_headers = ["Authorization", "Content-Length", "Content-Type", "User-Agent"]     for header in ignored_headers         if haskey(headers_to_sign, header)             delete!(headers_to_sign, header)         end     end     return headers_to_sign end

43161:function calculate_lines(x, y)     slope_list = Dict{Int64, Float64}()     intercept_list = Dict{Int64, Float64}()     @inbounds for i in 1:length(x)-1         slope_list[i] = (y[i] - y[i+1]) / (x[i] - x[i+1])         intercept_list[i] = y[i+1] - slope_list[i] * x[i+1]     end     return slope_list, intercept_list end

43227:function _unescape_nl(text)     i = 1     while i <= lastindex(text)         c = text[i]         if c == '\\'             if i+1 > lastindex(text)                 throw(ArgumentError("Missing \\\\ at end of line"))             end             nextchar = text[i+1]             if nextchar == 'n'                 nextchar = '\n'             elseif nextchar == '\\'                 nextchar = '\\'             else                 throw(ArgumentError("Unrecognized escape sequence \\"*nextchar))             end             text = text[1:i-1] * nextchar * text[i+2:end]             i += 1         end         i += 1     end     return text end

43283:function bit_neighbors(bit)     # all 8 possible bit board neighbors     n = 0xfefefefefefefefe     # shift right 1 to get the neighbor     # if there is a bit set in the neighbor, then the left bit is set in the new bit     # if there is a bit not set in the neighbor, then the left bit is not set in the new bit     # this is the correct bit ordering for neighbors     # 0011 -> 0001     # 0100 -> 0010     # 1000 -> 0100     # 0010 -> 0001     # 1000 -> 0100     # 0001 -> 0001     # 0100 -> 0010     # 1000 -> 0100     # if there is a set bit in the left neighbor,     # set the left neighbor bit, otherwise set the right neighbor bit     # if there is a set bit in the right neighbor,     # set the right neighbor bit, otherwise set the left neighbor bit     # this is the correct bit ordering for the 0001 and 1000 cases     return ((bit >> 1) | (n & bit << 1)) & ((n & bit >> 8) | ((bit << 8) & (n << 8))) end

43303:function energy_consumption(cpu_active_time, cpu_lpm_time, listen_time)     # Use the power dissipation formula: P = U * I     # (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_dissipation)     # U = Volts * Current     # (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_potential_difference)     # I = Amperes     # First, calculate the active current     cpu_active_current = cpu_active_time * 0.02     # Next, calculate the active power     cpu_active_power = cpu_active_current * 3.7     # Similarly, calculate the lpm current     cpu_lpm_current = cpu_lpm_time * 0.0000013     # Next, calculate the lpm power     cpu_lpm_power = cpu_lpm_current * 3.7     # Calculate the radio listen current     radio_listen_current = listen_time * 0.02     # Finally, calculate the radio listen power     radio_listen_power = radio_listen_current * 3.7     # Return the total energy consumption     return cpu_active_power + cpu_lpm_power + radio_listen_power end

43305:function hex_round(cord, radius)     # Convert from axial to cube cords.     # https://www.redblobgames.com/grids/hexagons/#conversions-axial     x = cord[1]     z = cord[2]     y = -x-z     # Do the rounding.     # https://www.redblobgames.com/grids/hexagons/#rounding     rx = round(x)     ry = round(y)     rz = round(z)     # # Do the rounding.     # # https://www.redblobgames.com/grids/hexagons/#rounding     # rx = round(x)     # ry = round(y)     # rz = round(z)     # dx = abs(rx - x)     # dy = abs(ry - y)     # dz = abs(rz - z)     # if dx > dy && dx > dz:     #     rx = -ry-rz     # elif dy > dz:     #     ry = -rx-rz     # else:     #     rz = -rx-ry     # @assert radius == 1 "radius: $(radius)"     # @assert (rx,ry,rz) == hex_round(hex_round(hex_round(cord))) "cord: $(cord)"     # @assert (rx,ry,rz) == hex_round(hex_round((rx,ry,rz))) "cord: $(cord)"     # @assert (rx,ry,rz) == hex_round((rx,ry,rz)) "cord: $(cord)"     # @assert (rx,ry,rz) == hex_round(hex_round((rx,ry,rz))) "cord: $(cord)"     # @assert (rx,ry,rz) == hex_round(hex_round(cord)) "cord: $(cord)"     # @assert (rx,ry,rz) == hex_round(hex_round(cord)) "cord: $(cord)"     if abs(rx - x) > radius || abs(ry - y) > radius || abs(rz - z) > radius         rx = round(x)         ry = round(y)         rz = round(z)     end     # @assert (rx,ry,rz) == hex_round(hex_round(hex_round(cord))) "cord: $(cord)"     # @assert (rx,ry,rz) == hex_round(hex_round((rx,ry,rz))) "cord: $(cord)"     # @assert (rx,ry,rz) == hex_round((rx,ry,rz)) "cord: $(cord)"     # @assert (rx,ry,rz) == hex_round(hex_round((rx,ry,rz))) "cord: $(cord)"     # @assert (rx,ry,rz) == hex_round(hex_round(cord)) "cord: $(cord)"     # @assert (rx,ry,rz) == hex_round(hex_round(cord)) "cord: $(cord)"     return (rx,rz) end

43314:function N_HTELTF_from_N_ESS(N_ESS)     # Take care of the edge cases first     if N_ESS == 0         return 0     elseif N_ESS == 1         return 1     elseif N_ESS == 2         return 2     elseif N_ESS == 3         return 4     end     N_HT_Extension_LTFs = 0     # Create the list of all possible combinations of 0s and 1s     # that sum up to N_ESS     num_combinations = Int(2^N_ESS)     combinations = zeros(UInt8, num_combinations)     for i in 1:num_combinations         combinations[i] = i-1     end     for i in 1:num_combinations         N_combinations_from_one = 1         # Check how many combinations we have from this one         for j in 1:N_ESS             if combinations[i] & 1                 N_combinations_from_one += 1             end             combinations[i] >>= 1         end         # If this combination represents one HT LTF,         # add the number of possible combinations         # from the one before         if N_combinations_from_one == 1             N_HT_Extension_LTFs += 1         end     end     return N_HT_Extension_LTFs end
