43347:function iterate_pagerank(corpus, damping_factor)   # Determine the number of pages in the corpus.   # The number of pages is the number of keys in the corpus dictionary.   num_pages = length(keys(corpus))   # Create a dictionary of "old" PageRank values, where keys   # are pages, and values are their corresponding PageRank value.   # Assign each page an initial PageRank value of 1 / num_pages.   old_ranks = Dict()   for (page, links) in corpus     old_ranks[page] = 1 / num_pages   end   # Create a dictionary of "new" PageRank values, where keys   # are pages, and values are their corresponding PageRank value.   new_ranks = Dict()   # While the "delta" between the old and new PageRank values   # is greater than some threshold, iterate.   while true     # Iterate through all the pages in the corpus.     for (page, links) in corpus       # Initialize the summation of all of the PageRank values       # that point to this page.       rank_sum = 0       # Iterate through all the pages in the corpus.       for (other_page, other_links) in corpus         # If this page links to the other page, add its PageRank value         # to the rank_sum, as we'll be dividing by the number of links         # from the current page to the other page.         if page in other_links           rank_sum += old_ranks[other_page] / length(other_links)         else           rank_sum += old_ranks[other_page] / num_pages         end       end       # Apply the damping factor to the rank_sum to create a "weighted"       # PageRank value.       rank_sum *= damping_factor       # Add the "weighted" PageRank value to the "weighted" sum of       # PageRank values for all pages.       rank_sum += (1 - damping_factor) / num_pages       # Add the "weighted" sum of PageRank values to the new dictionary.       new_ranks[page] = rank_sum     end     # Find the maximum difference between the old and new PageRank values.     # If that difference is less than some threshold, stop iterating.     difference = maximum([abs(new_ranks[page] - old_ranks[page]) for (page, links) in old_ranks])     if difference < 0.001       break     end     # Otherwise, update the old PageRank values to the new PageRank values.     old_ranks = new_ranks.copy()   end   # Return the final PageRank values.   return old_ranks end

43365:function update_parameters(params, grads, alpha)     # Retrieve each parameter from the dictionary "params"     Ws = []     bs = []     for (k, v) in params         if startswith(k, "w")             append!(Ws, v)         elseif startswith(k, "b")             append!(bs, v)         else             @warn "update_parameters: key $k not recognized!"         end     end     # Compute gradients for each parameter     dWs = []     dbs = []     for (k, v) in grads         if startswith(k, "dw")             append!(dWs, v)         elseif startswith(k, "db")             append!(dbs, v)         else             @warn "update_parameters: key $k not recognized!"         end     end     # Update rule for each parameter     @inbounds for i = 1:length(Ws)         Ws[i] = Ws[i] - alpha * dWs[i]         bs[i] = bs[i] - alpha * dbs[i]     end     # Store updated parameters in the params dictionary     for i = 1:length(Ws)         params["w$i"] = Ws[i]         params["b$i"] = bs[i]     end     return params end

43387:function two_of_three(a, b, c) 	biggest = a >= b && a >= c ? a : (b >= c ? b : c) 	if biggest == a 		other = b >= c ? b : c 	elseif biggest == b 		other = a >= c ? a : c 	else # biggest == c 		other = a >= b ? a : b 	end 	return biggest*biggest + other*other end

43417:function _get_intersection(cp1, cp2, s, e) 	dc = (cp1[1] - cp2[1], cp1[2] - cp2[2]) 	dp = (s[1] - e[1], s[2] - e[2]) 	n1 = cp1[1] * cp2[2] - cp1[2] * cp2[1] 	n2 = s[1] * e[2] - s[2] * e[1] 	n3 = 1.0 / (dc[1] * dp[2] - dc[2] * dp[1]) 	return ((n1*dp[1] - n2*dc[1]) * n3, (n1*dp[2] - n2*dc[2]) * n3) end

43438:function segments_intersect(s1, s2)     a = (s1[2][1] - s1[1][1], s1[2][2] - s1[1][2])     b = (s2[2][1] - s2[1][1], s2[2][2] - s2[1][2])     den = a[1]*b[2] - a[2]*b[1]     if den == 0         return false     else         n1 = a[1]*(s1[1][2] - s2[1][2]) - a[2]*(s1[1][1] - s2[1][1])         n2 = b[1]*(s1[1][2] - s2[1][2]) - b[2]*(s1[1][1] - s2[1][1])         u1 = n1/den         u2 = n2/den         return (0 <= u1 <= 1) && (0 <= u2 <= 1)     end end

43488:function _calculate_interconnected_value(vij, vik, vil, vkj, vkk, vkl, vlj, vlk, vll)     # calculate the intermediate value of vik     c = 1 - vkl - vlk     # calculate the intermediate value of vkj     a = 1 - vlk     # calculate the intermediate value of vlj     b = 1 - vkl     # intermediate values of vik, vkj, vlj     i1 = (vij + vkj * vil * a + vlj * vik * b) / (a * b)     i2 = (vij + vlj * vik * b + vkj * vil * a) / (a * b)     # calculate the intermediate value of vkk     d = 1 - vll     # calculate the intermediate value of vll     e = 1 - vkk     # calculate the final value of vik     vik_new = (         vij + vkj * vil * (1 - vlk) + vlj * vik * (1 - vkl) + vkj * vll * vik + vlj * vkk * vil     ) / (c * (1 - vlk) - vkk * vll)     # calculate the final value of vkj     vkj_new = (         vij + vlj * vik * (1 - vkl) + vkj * vil * (1 - vlk) + vlj * vkk * vik + vkj * vll * vil     ) / (c * (1 - vlk) - vkk * vll)     # calculate the final value of vlj     vlj_new = (         vij + vkj * vil * (1 - vlk) + vlj * vik * (1 - vkl) + vkj * vll * vil + vlj * vkk * vik     ) / (c * (1 - vlk) - vkk * vll)     # calculate the final value of vkk     vkk_new = (         vij + vkj * vil * (1 - vlk) + vlj * vik * (1 - vkl) + vkj * vll * vik + vlj * vkk * vil     ) / (c * (1 - vlk) - vkk * vll)     # calculate the final value of vll     vll_new = (         vij + vkj * vil * (1 - vlk) + vlj * vik * (1 - vkl) + vkj * vll * vil + vlj * vkk * vik     ) / (c * (1 - vlk) - vkk * vll)     # calculate the final value of vil     vil_new = vik_new * vkj_new * e + vik_new * vlj_new * d + vik_new * vkk_new * vll     # calculate the final value of vlk     vlk_new = vik_new * vkj_new * d + vik_new * vlj_new * e + vik_new * vkk_new * vll     # calculate the final value of vik     vik_new = i2 * vkk_new * vll + i2 * vlj_new * e + i2 * vkj_new * vlk     # calculate the final value of vil     vil_new = i2 * vkk_new * vlk + i2 * vlj_new * d + i2 * vkj_new * vll     # calculate the final value of vlk     vlk_new = i1 * vkk_new * vll + i1 * vlj_new * e + i1 * vkj_new * vlk     # calculate the final value of vik     vik_new = i2 * vkk_new * vlk + i2 * vlj_new * d + i2 * vkj_new * vll     # calculate the final value of vil     vil_new = i1 * vkk_new * vlk + i1 * vlj_new * d + i1 * vkj_new * vll     # calculate the final value of vlk     vlk_new = vik_new * vkj_new * vll + vik_new * vlj_new * e + vik_new * vkk_new * e     # calculate the final value of vik     vik_new = vik_new * vkj_new * vlk + vik_new * vlj_new * d + vik_new * vkk_new * d     # calculate the final value of vil     vil_new = vik_new end

43603:function calc_f1_macro(y_true, y_pred)     y_true_1_idx = findall(x -> x == 1, y_true)     y_true_0_idx = findall(x -> x == 0, y_true)     y_pred_1_idx = findall(x -> x == 1, y_pred)     y_pred_0_idx = findall(x -> x == 0, y_pred)     tp1 = length(intersect(y_true_1_idx, y_pred_1_idx))     tp0 = length(intersect(y_true_0_idx, y_pred_0_idx))     tn1 = length(intersect(setdiff(y_true_1_idx, y_pred_1_idx), setdiff(y_pred_1_idx, y_true_1_idx)))     tn0 = length(intersect(setdiff(y_true_0_idx, y_pred_0_idx), setdiff(y_pred_0_idx, y_true_0_idx)))     fp1 = length(intersect(setdiff(y_true_1_idx, y_pred_1_idx), setdiff(y_true_1_idx, y_pred_1_idx)))     fp0 = length(intersect(setdiff(y_true_0_idx, y_pred_0_idx), setdiff(y_true_0_idx, y_pred_0_idx)))     fn1 = length(intersect(setdiff(y_pred_1_idx, y_true_1_idx), setdiff(y_true_1_idx, y_pred_1_idx)))     fn0 = length(intersect(setdiff(y_pred_0_idx, y_true_0_idx), setdiff(y_true_0_idx, y_pred_0_idx)))     f1_1 = tp1 / (tp1 + 0.5 * (fp1 + fn1))     f1_0 = tp0 / (tp0 + 0.5 * (fp0 + fn0))     f1_macro = (f1_0 + f1_1) * 0.5     return f1_macro end

43655:function inverse_mod(k, p)     if k == 0         throw(ErrorException("division by zero"))     elseif k < 0         return mod(p + -k, p)     end     old_x = 0     x = 1     old_y = 1     y = 0     old_r = p     r = k     while r != 0         quotient = old_r ÷ r         old_r, r = r, old_r - quotient * r         old_x, x = x, old_x - quotient * x         old_y, y = y, old_y - quotient * y     end     gcd, x, y = old_r, old_x, old_y     if gcd != 1         throw(ErrorException("not invertible"))     end     return mod(x, p) end

43661:function is_threatening(x1::Int64, y1::Int64, x2::Int64, y2::Int64)::Bool     delta1 = min(x1, y1)     delta2 = min(x2, y2)     same_row = x1 == x2     same_col = y1 == y2     major_coords1 = (x1 - delta1, y1 - delta1)     major_coords2 = (x2 - delta2, y2 - delta2)     same_diagonal_major = major_coords1 == major_coords2     delta1 = x1     delta2 = x2     minor_coords1 = (x1 - delta1, y1 + delta1)     minor_coords2 = (x2 - delta2, y2 + delta2)     same_diagonal_minor = minor_coords1 == minor_coords2     same_diagonal = same_diagonal_major || same_diagonal_minor     return same_row || same_col || same_diagonal end

43747:function struct_size(elems)     n = length(elems)     if n == 0         return 0     end     # Assume 8 is size of 'most-aligned' data type (e. g. double).     align_values = Set([2,4,8])     member_sum = 0     most_aligned = elems[1]     for elem in elems         pad = 0         if elem in align_values             mod = member_sum % elem             if mod != 0                 pad = elem - mod                 most_aligned = max(most_aligned, elem)             end         end         member_sum = member_sum + pad + elem     end     if most_aligned in align_values         mod = member_sum % most_aligned         if mod != 0             member_sum += most_aligned - mod         end     end     return member_sum end

43768:function decode_lsi_loginfo_numbers(val)     t = (val >> 28) & 0xF     origin = (val >> 24) & 0xF     code = (val >> 16) & 0xFF     spec = val & 0xFFFF     # Following is a "manual" implementation of the above     # This is here for code review and to make it easier to follow     # Is the 12 least significant bits the loginfo number     ls12 = val & 0xFFF     # Get the upper 4 bits     upper4 = (val >> 12) & 0xF     if upper4 == 0x1         spec = ls12     elseif upper4 == 0x2         origin = ls12     elseif upper4 == 0x3         code = ls12     elseif upper4 == 0x4         t = ls12     elseif upper4 == 0x5         spec = val         origin = 0         code = 0         t = 0     elseif upper4 == 0x6         origin = val         code = 0         t = 0     elseif upper4 == 0x7         code = val         t = 0     elseif upper4 == 0x8         spec = val         origin = 0         code = 0         t = 0     elseif upper4 == 0x9         origin = val         code = 0         t = 0     elseif upper4 == 0xA         code = val         t = 0     elseif upper4 == 0xB         t = val         spec = 0         origin = 0         code = 0     elseif upper4 == 0xC         t = val         origin = 0         code = 0     elseif upper4 == 0xD         t = val         code = 0     elseif upper4 == 0xE         spec = val         origin = 0         code = 0         t = 0     elseif upper4 == 0xF         spec = val         origin = 0         code = 0         t = 0     else         println("Unknown upper 4 bits: ", upper4)     end     return (t, origin, code, spec) end

43791:function calc_iou(box1, box2)     (x11, y11, x12, y12) = box1     (x21, y21, x22, y22) = box2     # get the coordinates of the intersection rectangle     x_left = max(x11, x21)     y_top = max(y11, y21)     x_right = min(x12, x22)     y_bottom = min(y12, y22)     if x_right < x_left || y_bottom < y_top         return 0.0     else         # The intersection of two axis-aligned bounding boxes is always an         # axis-aligned bounding box         intersection_area = (x_right - x_left) * (y_bottom - y_top)         # compute the area of both AABBs         box1_area = (x12 - x11) * (y12 - y11)         box2_area = (x22 - x21) * (y22 - y21)         # compute the intersection over union by taking the intersection         # area and dividing it by the sum of prediction + ground-truth         # areas - the interesection area         iou = intersection_area / float(box1_area + box2_area - intersection_area)         return iou     end end

43889:function sort_tups(seq)     # We don't want to mess with the original sequence,     # so copy it first     sorted_seq = copy(seq)     # We need to make a sorted version of the sequence     # to sort by the string length     sort_by_length = sort!(copy(seq),by=k -> -length(k[1]))     # To do that, we need to invert the order of the     # "by" function, so that it'll be a "greater than"     # comparison     # Note that we had to use the "by" keyword argument     # in order to use a function, which we couldn't otherwise.     # Note also that we don't actually need to copy the     # sorted_seq array, since we're going to be overwriting     # it anyway.     sort!(sorted_seq,by=k -> k[1] in sort_by_length[1:end-1],rev=true)     # The last step is to return the reversed list     reverse(sorted_seq) end

43907:function check_bounds_overlap(bounds_1, bounds_2)     bounds_1 = [convert.(Float64, x) for x in bounds_1]     bounds_2 = [convert.(Float64, x) for x in bounds_2]     left_1, top_1, right_1, bottom_1 = bounds_1[1], bounds_1[2], bounds_1[3], bounds_1[4]     left_2, top_2, right_2, bottom_2 = bounds_2[1], bounds_2[2], bounds_2[3], bounds_2[4]     width_1 = right_1 - left_1     height_1 = bottom_1 - top_1     width_2 = right_2 - left_2     height_2 = bottom_2 - top_2     overlap_width = width_1 + width_2 - (max(left_1 + width_1, left_2 + width_2) - min(left_1, left_2))     overlap_height = height_1 + height_2 - (max(top_1 + height_1, top_2 + height_2) - min(top_1, top_2))     if overlap_height <= 0 || overlap_width <= 0         return false     end     overlap_area = overlap_height * overlap_width     bounds_1_area = width_1 * height_1     bounds_2_area = width_2 * height_2     ratio = overlap_area / (bounds_1_area + bounds_2_area - overlap_area)     return ratio end

44028:function oxy_ml_to_umolkg(oxy_mL_L, sigma0)     # Convert dissolved oxygen from units of mL/L to micromol/kg.     # Parameters     # ----------     # oxy_mL_L : array-like     #     Dissolved oxygen in units of [mL/L]     # sigma0 : array-like     #     Potential density anomaly (i.e. sigma - 1000) referenced to 0 dbar [kg/m^3]     # Returns     # -------     # oxy_umol_kg : array-like     #     Dissolved oxygen in units of [umol/kg]     # Notes     # -----     # Conversion value 44660 is exact for oxygen gas and derived from the ideal gas law.     # (c.f. 44052:function tetra_clean(instr::String)::Bool     # Create lookup dictionary     # keys are the ambiguity symbols, values are the nucleotides they represent     lookup = Dict{Char, String}(         'R' => "AG",         'Y' => "CT",         'K' => "GT",         'M' => "AC",         'S' => "CG",         'W' => "AT",         'B' => "CGT",         'D' => "AGT",         'H' => "ACT",         'V' => "ACG",         'N' => "ACGT"     )     # Initialize output string     output = ""     # Loop through each character in the string     for c in instr         # If the character is an ambiguity symbol         if c in keys(lookup)             # Add its representation to the output string             output = output * lookup[c]         # If the character is a valid nucleotide symbol         elseif c in "ACGT"             # Add it to the output string             output = output * c         end     end     # Return whether the output string matches the input string     return instr == output end

44070:function is_luminous(rgb) 	new_color = zeros(size(rgb)) 	for c = 1:size(rgb,1) 		if rgb[c] <= 0.03928 			new_color[c] = rgb[c] / 12.92 		else 			new_color[c] = ((rgb[c] + 0.055) / 1.055) ^ 2.4 		end 	end 	L = sum(new_color .* [0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722]) 	return L < 0.179 end

44077:function inv_sinc(arg)     # /*Can't use gsl_sf_sinc_pi because of the possibility of overflow.*/     # /*  Assumes x > -1.0e-9 */     # Convert to radians     a = arg * π     # Apply series expansion     x = a     x -= x^2 / 6.0     x -= x^2 / 120.0     x -= x^2 / 5040.0     x -= x^2 / 362880.0     x -= x^2 / 39916800.0     x -= x^2 / 6227020800.0     # Re-apply formulae     x = ((x * a) - (sin(a) / a)) / ((a * cos(a) - π * sin(a)) / (a^2))     # // Return answer     return x end

44083:function prime_factorization(n)     # your code here     dict = Dict{Int64, Int64}()     if n == 1         dict[1] = 1     end     # this loop will be iterated until the square root of n is reached     # if n is a prime number, the loop will stop after one iteration     i = 2     while i^2 <= n         if n % i == 0             dict[i] = 0             while n % i == 0                 dict[i] += 1                 n /= i             end         end         i += 1     end     if n > 1         dict[n] = 1     end     return dict end

44160:function reddening_correction_sfd98(extinction_r)     # 3.2 micron correction     f = 0.38     E_BV = extinction_r / 2.751     # 4.6 micron correction     f = 0.37     E_BV = extinction_r / 2.751     # 8.0 micron correction     f = 0.36     E_BV = extinction_r / 2.751     # 22.0 micron correction     f = 0.34     E_BV = extinction_r / 2.751     # 44.0 micron correction     f = 0.33     E_BV = extinction_r / 2.751     # 100 micron correction     f = 0.29     E_BV = extinction_r / 2.751     # E(B-V) = A(V)/A(B) * E(B-V)/A(B) = A(V)/A(B) * E(B-V)     A_u = E_BV * 5.155     A_g = E_BV * 3.793     A_r = E_BV * 2.751     A_i = E_BV * 2.086     A_z = E_BV * 1.479     return (A_u, A_g, A_r, A_i, A_z) end

44170:function get_intersection_area(box1, box2)     # we are applying the math from:     # https://github.com/cocodataset/cocoapi/blob/master/PythonAPI/pycocotools/cocoeval.py     # which is in turn based on:     # http://stackoverflow.com/questions/5266499/rectangle-intersection-in-python     # determine the (x, y)-coordinates of the intersection rectangle     xmin = max(box1[1], box2[1])     ymin = max(box1[2], box2[2])     xmax = min(box1[3], box2[3])     ymax = min(box1[4], box2[4])     # if there is no overlap, the intersection area is zero     if xmin > xmax || ymin > ymax         return 0     end     # otherwise, the area of intersection is given by the     # product of the lengths of the vertical and horizontal     # segments     return (xmax - xmin) * (ymax - ymin) end
44171:function bell_number(n)     if n < 0         error("Invalid Input")     end     bell = zeros(n+1,n+1)     bell[1,1] = 1     for i = 2:n+1         bell[i,1] = bell[i-1,i-1]         for j = 2:i             bell[i,j] = bell[i-1,j-1] + bell[i,j-1]         end     end     return bell[n+1,1] end

44384:function is_valid_orcid_id(orcid_id::String)     # make sure the ID is in all upper case     orcid_id = uppercase(orcid_id)     # check that the ORCID ID is a string of 4-6 alphanumeric characters     # the 4-digit prefix and 6-digit suffix are always all upper case     if length(orcid_id) < 9 || length(orcid_id) > 17         return false     elseif !occursin(r"^[0-9A-Z]{4}-[0-9A-Z]{6}-[0-9A-Z]{3}[0-9X]$", orcid_id)         return false     end     # convert the 4-digit prefix and 6-digit suffix from the ORCID ID     # into 4-digit numbers     orcid_prefix = parse(Int64, orcid_id[1:4])     orcid_suffix = parse(Int64, orcid_id[6:end])     # apply the modulus 11-2 checksum formula to compute the check digit     check_digit = mod(2 * mod(orcid_prefix + orcid_suffix, 11), 11)     # return true if the check digit is 1     return check_digit == 1 end

44396:function hermiteInterpolate(v0, v1, v2, v3, alpha, tension, bias)     alpha2 = alpha * alpha     alpha3 = alpha2 * alpha     m0 = (((v1 - v0) * (1 - tension)) * (1 + bias)) / 2.0     m0 += (((v2 - v1) * (1 - tension)) * (1 - bias)) / 2.0     m1 = (((v2 - v1) * (1 - tension)) * (1 + bias)) / 2.0     m1 += (((v3 - v2) * (1 - tension)) * (1 - bias)) / 2.0     a0 = 2 * alpha3 - 3 * alpha2 + 1     a1 = alpha3 - 2 * alpha2 + alpha     a2 = alpha3 - alpha2     a3 = -2 * alpha3 + 3 * alpha2     return a0 * v1 + a1 * m0 + a2 * m1 + a3 * v2 end

44432:function line(x1, y1, x2, y2) 	if abs(y2-y1) > abs(x2-x1) 		x1, y1 = y1, x1 		x2, y2 = y2, x2 		isSteep = true 	else 		isSteep = false 	end 	if x1 > x2 		x1, x2 = x2, x1 		y1, y2 = y2, y1 		isReversed = true 	else 		isReversed = false 	end 	deltax = x2 - x1 	deltay = abs(y2-y1) 	error = div(deltax, 2) 	ystep = ifelse(y1 < y2, 1, -1) 	y = y1 	points = [] 	for x in x1:x2 		if isSteep 			push!(points, (y, x)) 		else 			push!(points, (x, y)) 		end 		error -= deltay 		if error < 0 			y += ystep 			error += deltax 		end 	end 	isReversed ? reverse!(points) : points end

44434:function migrate_impl_args(argv, migrate_args)     argv_index = findall(x -> x == "--", argv)     if isempty(argv_index)         # If there is no separator, then we have nothing to migrate.         return argv     end     args = argv[1:argv_index[1]-1]     impl_args = argv[argv_index[1]:end]     impl_args_to_remove = []     for impl_arg in impl_args         split_index = findfirst(isequal('='), impl_arg)         if split_index == nothing             arg = impl_arg         else             arg = impl_arg[1:split_index[1]-1]         end         if arg in migrate_args             args = vcat(args, impl_arg)             impl_args_to_remove = vcat(impl_args_to_remove, impl_arg)         end     end     return vcat(args, filter(x -> x ∉ impl_args_to_remove, impl_args)) end

44444:function _broadcast(a, b, array1, array2)     # if a, b don't have the same number of dimensions, return nothing     if length(size(a)) != length(size(b))         return nothing     end     # if a, b have the same number of dimensions, check if they are equal     if length(size(a)) == length(size(b))         if size(a) != size(b)             return nothing         end     end     # if a, b have the same size, return     if size(a) == size(b)         return (array1, array2)     end     # if a, b are both 1-dimensional, return     if length(size(a)) == 1         return (array1, array2)     end     # check if the leading dimensions are equal     if size(a)[1] != size(b)[1]         return nothing     end     # if the leading dimensions are equal, check if the following dimensions are equal     if size(a)[2:end] == size(b)[2:end]         return (array1, array2)     end     # check if the trailing dimensions are equal     if size(a)[end] != size(b)[end]         return nothing     end     # if the trailing dimensions are equal, create new dimensions for array1, array2     # and return     new_size = []     for (x, y) in zip(size(array1), size(array2))         push!(new_size, x * y)     end     return (reshape(array1, new_size), reshape(array2, new_size)) end

44497:function error_rate(y_true, y_pred)   labels = unique(vcat(y_true, y_pred))   scores = []   for label in labels     true_positive = sum(         i == label && j == label ? 1 : 0 for (i, j) in zip(y_true, y_pred)     )     true_negative = sum(         i != label && j != label ? 1 : 0 for (i, j) in zip(y_true, y_pred)     )     false_positive = sum(         i != label && j == label ? 1 : 0 for (i, j) in zip(y_true, y_pred)     )     false_negative = sum(         i == label && j != label ? 1 : 0 for (i, j) in zip(y_true, y_pred)     )     s = true_positive + true_negative + false_positive + false_negative     push!(scores, (false_positive + false_negative) / s)   end   return sum(scores) / length(scores) end

44540:function paeth_predictor(left::Int64, above::Int64, upper_left::Int64)::Int64 # Canonical Python Solution     total = left + above - upper_left     dist_to_left = abs(total - left)     dist_to_above = abs(total - above)     dist_to_upper_left = abs(total - upper_left)     if dist_to_left <= dist_to_above && dist_to_left <= dist_to_upper_left         return left     elseif dist_to_above <= dist_to_upper_left         return above     else         return upper_left     end end

44640:function intersect(p1, p2, p3, p4)     # Trivial case -- test for p1 == p4     if p1 == p4         return intersect(p3, p4, p1, p2)     end     # Trivial case -- test for p3 == p2     if p3 == p2         return intersect(p4, p3, p1, p2)     end     # Precompute these values -- note that we're basically shifting from     #     #        p = p1 + s (p2 - p1)     #     # to     #     #         p = p1 + s d     #     # where D is a direction vector.  The solution remains the same of     # course.  We'll just be computing D once for each line rather than     # computing it a couple of times.     d21x = p2[1] - p1[1]     d21y = p2[2] - p1[2]     d43x = p4[1] - p3[1]     d43y = p4[2] - p3[2]     # Denominator     d = d21x * d43y - d21y * d43x     # Return now if the denominator is zero     if d == 0         return -1.0     end     # For our purposes, the first line segment given     # by p1 & p2 is the LONG hatch line running through     # the entire drawing.  And, p3 & p4 describe the     # usually much shorter line segment from a polygon.     # As such, we compute sb first as it's more likely     # to indicate "no intersection".  That is, sa is     # more likely to indicate an intersection with a     # much a long line containing p3 & p4.     nb = (p1[2] - p3[2]) * d21x - (p1[1] - p3[1]) * d21y     # Could first check if abs(nb) > abs(d) or if     # the signs differ.     sb = float(nb) / float(d)     if sb < 0 || sb > 1         return -1.0     end     na = (p1[2] - p3[2]) * d43x - (p1[1] - p3[1]) * d43y     sa = float(na) / float(d)     if sa < 0 || sa > 1         return -1.0     end     return sa end

44661:function fstarBen(mh, m1, f0, beta, gamma)     # Halo mass to stellar mass ratio as a function of halo mass.     # Fitting function from Moster et al. (2015).     # (f0, beta, gamma) = (0.29, -1.43, -1.26) # See Moster et al. (2015) for original values.     mstar = 2.0 * f0 * 10.0^mh / ((10.0^mh/10.0^m1)^(-beta) + (10.0^mh/10.0^m1)^gamma)     # Stellar mass to halo mass ratio as a function of halo mass.     # Fitting function from Moster et al.     fstar = mstar/10.0^mh     return fstar end

44745:function sum_dict(a, b)     # if both dictionaries are empty then return empty dictionary     if isempty(a) && isempty(b)         return Dict()     end     # if one dictionary is empty then return the non-empty one     if isempty(a)         return b     elseif isempty(b)         return a     end     # initialize the result     result = Dict()     for key in keys(a)         # if key is not present in b then add the corresponding values         if !haskey(b, key)             result[key] = a[key]         # otherwise add the values         else             result[key] = a[key] + b[key]         end     end     # for all keys in b not present in a add the values     for key in keys(b)         if !haskey(a, key)             result[key] = b[key]         end     end     return result end

44835:function prod2Gaussian(mu1, var1, mu2, var2) # #   function [mu12, var12, C12] = prod2Gaussian(mu1,var1,mu2,var2) #   %PROD2GAUSSIAN  Product of two Gaussian distributions #   %   INPUTS:  mu1 - mean value of first Gaussian distribution #   %            var1 - variance value of first Gaussian distribution #   %            mu2 - mean value of second Gaussian distribution #   %            var2 - variance value of second Gaussian distribution #   %   OUTPUTS: mu12 - mean value of product distribution #   %            var12 - variance value of product distribution #   %            C12 - covariance between the two distributions #   % #   %   Based on the formulas in "The Statistics of the Extreme" by <NAME> #   %   Ported from MATLAB Code # #   %   This is the Python translation of the Matlab code available at: #   %   http://www.mathworks.com/matlabcentral/fileexchange/24693-product-of-two-gaussian-distributions/content/prod2Gaussian.m #     mu12 = (var1*mu2 + var2*mu1) / (var1 + var2)     var12 = 1.0 / (1.0 / var1 + 1.0 / var2)     C12 = (mu2-mu1)*(mu2-mu1) / (var1+var2)     return mu12, var12, C12 end

44870:function topological_sort(graph)     node_counts = Dict{String, Int}(node => 0 for node in keys(graph))     for node in keys(graph)         for successor in graph[node]             node_counts[successor] += 1         end     end     ready = [ node for node in keys(graph) if node_counts[node] == 0 ]     result = [ ]     while !isempty(ready)         node = pop!(ready)         push!(result, node)         for successor in graph[node]             node_counts[successor] -= 1             if node_counts[successor] == 0                 push!(ready, successor)             end         end     end     result end

44898:function HSVtoRGB(HSVcol)     c = 255.0     R = 0     G = 0     B = 0     H = HSVcol[1]     S = HSVcol[2]     V = HSVcol[3]     Hi = Int((H / 60.0) % 6.0)  # residue     f = H / 60.0 - Int(H / 60)     p = V * (1.0 - S)     q = V * (1.0 - f * S)     t = V * (1.0 - (1.0 - f) * S)     if S != 0         if Hi == 0             R = V             G = t             B = p         elseif Hi == 1             R = q             G = V             B = p         elseif Hi == 2             R = p             G = V             B = t         elseif Hi == 3             R = p             G = q             B = V         elseif Hi == 4             R = t             G = p             B = V         elseif Hi == 5             R = V             G = p             B = q         end     end     R = Int(c * R)     G = Int(c * G)     B = Int(c * B)     return [R, G, B] end

44973:function chunk_str_list(fat_list, max_chars_per_list)   if typeof(fat_list) <: AbstractArray     # check that we aren't empty and that the max_chars_per_list is greater than 0     if isempty(fat_list) || max_chars_per_list < 1       throw(ArgumentError("Input is empty or max_chars_per_list is less than 1.  Returning empty list.  Please check your inputs."))     else       # get the total length of all the strings in the list       total_chars = 0       for (index, text) in enumerate(fat_list)         total_chars += length(text)       end       # set up the arrays       parent_list = []       starting_point = 1       # loop over the text array and add to lists until we are done       for (index, text) in enumerate(fat_list)         total_chars += length(text)         # check if the total characters is greater than the max_chars_per_list or if we're at the end         if total_chars > max_chars_per_list || index == length(fat_list)           push!(parent_list, fat_list[starting_point:index])           starting_point = index + 1           total_chars = 0         end       end       return parent_list     end   else     throw(ArgumentError("Input is not an array.  Please check your inputs."))   end end
44974:function is_prime(number::Int64)::Bool     # Using a set here to keep the results in memory for a small speed boost     results_set = Set{Int64}()     # Loop from 2 to the square root of the number     for i in 2:sqrt(number)         # If the number is divisible by anything in this range, then it is not prime         if number % i == 0             return false         end     end     return true end

44976:function PaethPredictor(a::Int64, b::Int64, c::Int64)::Int64     # PaethPredictor(a, b, c) is the same as PaethPredictor(b, a, c)     p = a + b - c     pa = abs(p - a)     pb = abs(p - b)     pc = abs(p - c)     if pa <= pb && pa <= pc         Pr = a     elseif pb <= pc         Pr = b     else         Pr = c     end     return Pr end

44979:function factorial_n(num) 	if isa(num, Int) && num >= 0 		product = 1 		while num > 1 			product *= num 			num -= 1 		end 		return product 	else 		return "Expected Positive integer" 	end end

45000:function linear_cell_to_tuple(c1, repeat_units)     # c1 = int(c1)     c1x = c1 % repeat_units[1]     c1y = ((c1 - c1x) // repeat_units[1]) % repeat_units[2]     c1z = (c1 - c1x - c1y * repeat_units[1]) // (repeat_units[1] * repeat_units[2])     return c1x, c1y, c1z end
